title: Unfold Daedongyeojido
description: The National Museum of Korea (Director Yoo Hong-jun) will be displaying the entire 22 volumes of 《Daedongyeojido (大東輿地圖)》 by Gosanja Kim Jeong-ho (1804?~1866?) Kim Jeong-ho (1804?~1866?) at the ‘Road of History’ on the first floor of the permanent exhibition hall from February 12, 2026 (Thursday). Exhibit. This exhibition is a special opportunity to view the entire Daedongyeojido, produced by Kim Jeong-ho in 1861 (the 12th year of King Cheoljong’s reign) at a glance. 3.8m wide, 6.7m tall... Meet the entire map of the overwhelming scale of ‘Daedongyeojido’ Daedongyeojido is a fold-and-fold map that divides Korea into 22 layers from north to south, with maps for each layer in one book. When all 22 volumes are connected, it becomes a large national map measuring about 6.7m long and 3.8m wide. The National Museum of Korea printed high-definition data from its collection of Daedongyeojido (Shinsu 19997) on traditional Korean paper, allowing visitors to appreciate its grand scale and detailed expressions at a glance. Through this, it is expected that people will be able to vividly experience the size and structure of the country as understood by people in the late Joseon Dynasty. Delicate mountain streams and streams, a road network marked every 10 ri... Daedongyeojido, created by Kim Jeong-ho, is considered the definitive map of the Joseon Dynasty and is a compilation of research results on Korea's old map production tradition. You can understand the pulse of the country through the accurately and detailed mountain ranges and watercourses, and dots are added every 10 ri on the roads to help you estimate the actual distance, adding convenience. In addition, various information about the society at the time, including administrative and defense information, economy, and transportation, was expressed in symbols. In particular, it is characteristic that a separate map table corresponding to the legend of a modern map was created so that users can easily and quickly understand a lot of geographical information. The tradition of our old maps and the achievements of Kim Jeong-ho The fact that Korea had an excellent map-making tradition can also be seen through <Honil Gangni Yeokdae National Road Map> produced in 1402 (the 2nd year of King Taejong's reign). <Donggukdaejido (東國大地圖)> produced by Jeong Sang-gi (1678-1752) during the reign of King Yeongjo using the scale of Baeknicheok, and Shin Gyeong-jun (1712-1781) produced it. 《Donggukyeojido》, etc. became the basis for the production of 《Daedongyeojido》. Prior to the production of 《Daedongyeojido》, Kim Jeong-ho compiled manuscript national maps such as 《Cheonggudo Map》 and 《Dongyeodo Dongyeodo》 and geographical books such as 『Daedongjiji』. 《Daedongyeojido》 was completed by compiling these map-making traditions. In particular, a feature of Daedongyeojido is that it was printed with woodblocks so that more people could easily carry and use the map. Yoo Hong-jun, director of the National Museum of Korea, said, “This exhibition will be a valuable opportunity to directly experience the great achievements of Kim Jeong-ho and the beauty of our country by encountering the Daedongyeojido, which was previously only available in book form, as a huge map.” He added, “I hope that you will feel pride in the excellence of our ancient maps through the Daedongyeojido, which contains the essence of science and art from the Joseon Dynasty.” The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220

description: 《The Origin》 illuminates Tao Moon’s plaster prototype as the first moment of form in his sculpture and as a complete work of art in itself. Generally, plaster prototypes are understood as an intermediate step toward the final work, but to Moon Jae-in, plaster prototypes were a condensation of the birth and creation process of a work of art, and had such special meaning that even in the last moments of his life, he requested a “Prototype Sculpture Exhibition” (June 3-July 31, 1995). These forms, which are infused with the artist's touch and time, are already filled with fullness even before they become completed sculptures. The plaster prototype is a pure white form that excludes color or material elements, and we encounter the first shape the artist conceived. In this pure and understated beauty, you can gain deep insight into his creative process and sensuously follow the depth of thought behind the shapes he pursued. The rhythm and volume of lines and surfaces flowing over the surface of the plaster, and the subtle tension created by light and shadow reveal the vitality of the work more clearly. In this way, the plaster prototype is a completed shape and at the same time a starting point for creation that allows for infinite variations, and can be said to be the source of the vibrant formative energy of the tattoo sculpture. Meanwhile, plaster prototypes require continuous preservation and management because they are greatly affected by time and the environment due to their material characteristics. In this exhibition, we will introduce examples of preservation of plaster prototypes of tattoos and examine how the works are managed after their creation and their meaning continues. This process makes you think about how the preservation of works of art connects time and memory to the present and the future. 《The Origin》 sheds new light on the meaning of plaster prototypes in the creative process of tattoos, and seeks to look deeply into his artistic world. title: How is the existence of images that never sleep celebrated?
description: This Park Seong-yeol invitation exhibition, planned by Space Tree Gallery Aurora, begins with the question, ‘How is existence celebrated?’ The author deals with memory through shapes. It is not a frozen record of the past, but is still breathing and moving. The giant faces, animals, and monumental structures that appear on the screen stand in silence while staring at the audience and asking questions. This exhibition is a place to rethink the method of ‘commemoration’ and the meaning of ‘existence.’ The figures presented in this exhibition are not complete monuments. If traditional monuments were devices that stopped time by fixing heroes and victories with stone and metal, Park Seong-yeol's figures imply states of crack, erosion, and movement. The seemingly solid face is broken somewhere, and the symbolic figures are unstable, unable to maintain their center of gravity. It is closer to a face that has withstood the weight of time rather than an expression of victory. The author chooses a wavering state instead of a firm declaration, and a question instead of a straightforward message. Animal shapes such as horses, wolves, gorillas, and lions are also major motifs. They symbolize time, instinct, and the archetype of life before humans. If the human face represents history and civilization, animals are close to life itself. When two worlds overlap within one screen, existence is not fixed to one meaning but vibrates in multiple layers. Tensions between civilization and instinct, ideals and reality intersect tightly within pictorial space. Park Seong-yeol's screens are characterized by thick matiere. He repeats the process of piling up paint, scratching it, and adding it again, pushing up the screen like a sculpture. This physical property goes beyond simple texture and reveals the accumulation of time. Instead of a smoothly organized surface, the traces left behind testify to the ‘process’ rather than the ‘completion’. The form exists in a state of being both solid and alive, and still and yet moving. Rather than conveying a specific message, the author proposes a space that evokes the memories of each audience member. The moment we come face to face with a huge face, or the moment we receive the gaze of an animal approaching us directly, we ask ourselves: What remains as a memory? What is worth celebrating? And what kind of shape will we be left with? This invitational exhibition, planned by Space Tree Gallery Aurora, shows the possibility of expansion of contemporary figurative painting and is an opportunity to think anew about commemoration, memory, and the meaning of existence. Park Seong-yeol's fierce artist spirit, which has undergone constant changes and challenges, will be revealed more clearly through this exhibition. The question ‘How is existence celebrated?’ is the starting point of the exhibition and is a question that will be left to each viewer. Exhibition name: Park Seong-yeol Invitation Exhibition <Shapes that never sleep, how is existence celebrated> Participating artist: Park Seong-yeol Exhibition period: February 25, 2026 ~ March 23, 2026 Venue: Space Namu Gallery Aurora Inquiry: 055-374-3500 The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220

What holds us back is not always what we see. It could be a structure, a relationship, a memory, or a silent tension. Both artists have explored these invisible forces in their own ways, and their work moves between space and emotion, order and anxiety, expanding the sensory realm that sculpture can reach. Information has studied architecture and sculpture together and has developed the language of sculpture with the concept of ‘space’ at the center for a long time. Through two-dimensional and three-dimensional works that visualize the rhythm or frequency of music, he demonstrates a formative language that flexibly transcends sense, technology, structure, and flow. Choi Jeong-yoon has used symbolic materials such as swords, thread, salt, and flowers to sculpt human desire, power, and traces of time. Through the act of wrapping a sword with thread or sealing it with salt, one suppresses desires, seals emotions, and embodies the aesthetics of resentment. The formative language that combines symbolism and materiality creates tension along with strong interiority. 《What Holds Us》 creates a new balance by combining different aesthetic languages ​​such as structure and seal, space and desire, abstraction and symbolism. Through the work of the two artists, viewers will encounter the question ‘What holds us back?’ and their own answers. Gallery Sejul presents the two person exhibition What Holds Us featuring artists Chung Bowon and Choi Jeongyun, on view from February 26 to April 4, 2026. Bringing together two sculptors of different generations and artistic approaches, the exhibition poses a fundamental question about the forces that sustain and bind us. Chung Bowon has developed his sculptural language around the concept of space, shaped by his background in both architecture and sculpture. His practice is characterized by an expanded spatial sensibility that embraces structure, tension, flow, and even sound as integral elements of form. *Stories that remind you of couples, lovers, and parents
*We touch your heart calmly and without exaggerated emotions.
*A play in which ‘silence’ lingers longer than dialogue
*Deep lingering effects whether seen alone or together

title: Seongjin Yoon: 2 Faces / 2 Visions
description: “When the ‘flat memory’ of sculpture and the ‘extended spatial memory’ of painting are combined, another possibility for artistic expression opens up.” ㅡSeongjin Yoon, Artist's Note 2025 Today, sculpture appears in a hybrid style with painting, installation art, performance, and video in terms of materials and expression techniques, and is expanding space and concepts through combination with other genres. Gallery JJ presents sculptor Seongjin Yoon’s solo exhibition <Seongjin Yoon: 2 Sides, 2 Perspectives>. Seongjin Yoon seeks a space beyond painting and sculpture and explores new experiences in contemporary sculpture. In a paradoxical approach that aims for a pictorial plane by minimizing the materiality and volume of traditional sculpture, the artist presents ‘2-face sculpture,’ an abstract object with two sides of a pictorial plane. It appears to combine pictorial experience with sculptural structure. This exhibition is the first to present the artist's works over the past four years since he returned to Seoul after a long period of living in Paris. It introduces new works such as <Folded Square> as well as representative 'double sculptures' of his work. The exhibition consists of about 20 standing works erected in a space and wall works using the wall surface. This exhibition highlights the unique formative methods he has thought and constructed and the uniqueness of his world of work based on the visual and perceptual experiences of visitors. Seongjin Yoon's abstract sculptures have expanded the boundaries of modern sculpture by exploring the point where the flatness of painting and the structure of sculpture meet, based on principles and formative sensibilities derived from geometric formative elements and calligraphy. His work, which has a formative structure that intersects the boundaries between painting and expression, goes beyond the physical space occupied by sculpture and raises questions about two-dimensionality and three-dimensionality by delicately revealing the spatial tension and layers of sensation that occur within the plane. The work, which the artist calls ‘painterly sculpture’ or ‘two-sided sculpture,’ is based on geometric abstract structures and moves between the genres of painting, sculpture, and installation. The method of juxtaposing two different pictorial surfaces on a single thin plate creates a tension between two-dimensional and three-dimensional, and encourages the work to be gradually completed through the viewer's movement and changes in gaze. In this way, the work goes beyond the dichotomous distinction of front and back, inside and outside, and creates another sensory space where atmospheres intersect between the two sides. Looking back, even in the past, art forms were not completely closed off from each other. Throughout the long history of Western sculpture, sculpture was not separated from and interacted with architecture and painting, but after the Renaissance, they became independent and took on autonomous forms, and over time, the competition between the forms only progressed in a way that proved itself to be a focused and powerful method. In modern art, the identity of sculpture has been constantly challenged, such as Naum Gabo, who tried to break away from the framework of traditional sculpture by minimizing mass and connecting the inside and outside with new materials, and Gwon Osang, who brought the medium of photography into sculpture and asked questions about the two-dimensional and three-dimensional aspects, which are big topics in sculpture. In the early 1990s, the artist was well known for his highly expressive works, expressing changes in values ​​and the era of chaos caused by the development of science, and denouncing the destruction of nature and the desolation of humanity. He continued the lineage of exploration of materiality in Korean art in the 1970s by cutting and combining silver aluminum plates, and his works are housed in major institutions at home and abroad, including the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art and the Metropolitan Museum of Art. Expressionist work, which emphasizes subjective sensibility and materiality, has gradually changed to the current geometric abstract form centered on balance and reason, raising curiosity about it. The reason for this seems to be found in the cultural atmosphere ingrained in Paris for nearly 20 years and the relationship between the cross-shaped formative work, the borrowing of the art history of the early 20th century, including Russian Constructivism, and, above all, the memory of the formative nature of calligraphy encountered from deep within the artist himself. — Lines, planes, space Geometrical abstract objects installed on the walls and floor of the exhibition hall continuously unfold the basic elements of form, lines and planes, not only within the plane but also as the structural form of sculpture.

title: Younghwan Park Solo Exhibition 《Immaterial: What Remains》
description: Mac Gallery is hosting artist Park Young-hwan's (b.1998-) solo exhibition 《Immaterial: What Remains》 from February 28th to March 28th. The artist, who works based on ink and Korean paper, has explored the layers of emotion, memory, and time through not only paintings but also performances and installations. This solo exhibition presents 17 new works of painting and ceramics, raising questions about the senses and states that remain after disappearance without completely disappearing.⠀ The black sphere that appears on the artist's screen is a formative unit that captures the process of life condensing, separating, and returning to flow. These shapes, arranged heterogeneously in landscapes or architectural spaces, disrupt the order of the representational landscape and visualize the multi-layered structure of life. The possibility of the spread and seepage of ink, accumulation and erasure, is in line with the sense of ‘immaterial’ that the artist focuses on, and the screen functions as a place to reveal the density of time rather than a space to reproduce objects.⠀ This exhibition unfolds at a time when the artist himself recognizes that his work is going through a transitional period. A point at which, while standing on an already formed formative language, we do not stop at repeating it but question its conditions again. The black sphere still exists on the screen, but the space in which it is placed, its density, and the way it is related are gradually changing.⠀ This exhibition asks: After the experience has passed, after the emotions have volatilized, after the work has passed one phase — what remains? And how does that remaining begin again at this moment? ⠀ GALLERY MAC is pleased to present 《Immaterial: What Remains》, a solo exhibition by Younghwan Park(b.1998-), on view from February 28 to March 28. Working primarily with ink and hanji (traditional Korean paper), the artist has explored layers of emotion, memory, and time not only through painting, but also through performance and installation. This exhibition presents 17 new works, including paintings and fired panel pieces, raising questions about sensations and states that do not entirely disappear even after vanishing.⠀ The black spheres that appear in the artist’s compositions function as formal units that embody the processes through which life condenses, separates, and flows once again. Positioned incongruously within landscapes or architectural spaces, these forms disrupt the order of representational scenery and visualize the multilayered structure of life. The spreading and permeation of ink, along with the possibilities of accumulation and erasure, resonate with the artist’s exploration of “immateriality.” Rather than serving as a site of depiction, the pictorial surface operates as a field where the density of lingering time becomes visible. description:
[Performance introduction] 

We invite you to ‘Umlaut Music Kids Classic’, a classical performance for your children!

<What is ‘Umlaut Music Kids Classic’? >
This is a classical performance for infants (preschoolers) and their families starting from the age of 0, when they are too young to go to a concert hall.
This is a performance where children can see, hear with their own ears, and feel with their bodies the vivid classical music played at the concert hall.

< My child experiences this! >
- Helps brain development by using various senses!
- Children improve concentration and become emotionally stable while listening to classical music!
- Your creativity and imagination grow as you experience various sounds!
- Have a great time immersing yourself in the music by following the rhythm and singing along to exciting children's songs and classical songs!

< What instruments do you experience? >
- Touch actual instruments such as violin, cello, and cello with the player and ask, ‘What does this sound like?’ There is time for children to make sounds themselves!

< Parents can enjoy it too! >
As children and parents experience music together, communication and bonding between family members will naturally deepen, right? This is a time when parents who are exhausted from raising children can also heal for a while with music.

title: 2026 New Artist Contest Selection Exhibition: Here and now
description: Gallery Grimson is holding an exhibition of six artists selected for the 2026 New Artist Contest: Kim Jeong-hee, Kim Hyeong-wook, Park Jeong-gyu, Min Lee, Jo Hee-ju, and Hwang Jeong-won. Every year, through a contest, we select artists who have had less than two solo exhibitions and who showcase novel and original formative artistry in their own style. This exhibition is an opportunity to see the questions and concerns of contemporary artists, as well as the world expressed in their own words, all in one place. A new perspective on the familiar, a method of expression that crosses boundaries, and a story that starts from personal experience and expands into universal sympathy are contained throughout the exhibition hall. Through this exhibition, we hope to provide a venue for artists with potential and potential to meet the audience in depth for the first time. Please join us for the moment when the new name becomes the starting point of how contemporary art will expand in the future. Artist Kim Jeong-hee uses Korean paper, which is a translucent threshold that passes light and the world through metaphor and lingering emotions, and explores the ‘other side’ between reveal and concealment, inside and outside, at that delicate boundary. Artist Kim Hyeong-wook reveals doubts about ‘complete reality’ in the uncertainty of the world created by the senses and the individual universe created by each person’s perception, and visualizes the state of energy and emptiness through the square blank space of the screen. Artist Park Jeong-gyu redefines past regrets and emotions and sublimates them into learning and memories, and through the harmony of dots and colors, he expresses his hope that they will eventually become a solid background in his work. Artist Minri explores the boundaries where inner senses intersect with external space and are revealed as forms, and works to leave room for viewers to imagine their own forms through screens where light and symbolic images interact. Artist Cho Hee-joo reinterprets disappearing spaces and childhood memories with warm colors and subjective perspectives to record ‘shapes of memories,’ and through this, conveys feelings of comfort and nostalgia. Artist Hwang Jeong-won fully embraces the moments of light, air, memory, and emotion that space evokes, and expresses the personal emotions that each space conveys through her work. title: Open Storage Center Special Exhibition 《Into the Deep, Deep Forest: Dorothy’s Wondering》
description: 《Into the Deep, Deep Forest: Dorothy's Wondering》 begins with the Salem Witch Trials* in the late 17th century. Imagining the aftermath of Dorothy Good, a four-year-old girl who lost her mother in this incident, it brings back unrecorded times and sensations. Dorothy's journey of meeting various beings in the deep forest unfolds, blurring the boundaries between reality and fantasy. ‘Wondering’ in the exhibition title is not presented as aimless wandering, but as a process of recognizing the world after loss, establishing relationships, and reconstructing oneself. This exhibition asks what artist Stella Sujin sees and wants to leave behind through the act of painting. Through this, we are able to encounter the artist's perspective and flow of thoughts accumulated in the work. * Salem Witch Trials (1692–1693): A witch trial that took place in Salem, Massachusetts, USA, in which innocent people were sacrificed in a society full of conflict and prejudice. title: Open Storage Permanent Exhibition 《DMA Collection Highlights 2026》
description: As installation works use space as part of the work, they occupy the entire exhibition space with a free installation form and overwhelming scale, and have the characteristics of interacting with visitors. However, after the exhibition ends, it inevitably goes through a dismantling process and is stored in as compressed a form as possible. At this time, the dedicated storage box for artwork used to safely transport and store the work is called a ‘crate.’ Unlike simple shipping boxes, crates go through heat treatment and fumigation processes in accordance with international standards from the manufacturing stage to block the inflow of microorganisms and pests, and function as a small-scale preservation system designed to protect works from rapid changes in temperature and humidity as well as physical shock. New media works exist as data and variable hardware, not as fixed entities. Immaterial data is stored and implemented through storage and playback media, and with technological advancements, the format of storage and playback has changed dramatically as laser discs have transitioned to DVDs and DVDs have transitioned to digital files. This transition in media leads to the challenge of how to preserve the original form of new media works amidst the flow of technological change. Storage is the site of preservation and management where works are most privately protected before they are displayed. The museum's efforts to safely preserve and accurately represent works continue behind the scenes. This exhibition transparently shares the storage site by visualizing the functional cross-section of the museum's preservation management through a crate that condenses the huge scale of installation art and a new media storage system that preserves immaterial data. title: Daesoo Kim’s solo exhibition [Luminous Sonata]
description: Daesoo Kim is a photographer who starts from questions about the essence of humanity that have persisted since his youth and works on the subject of reflection on the passage of time and my existence. Living abroad for several years in the author's life further solidified his identity as a Korean. And in his quest for his roots, he becomes fascinated by bamboo, one of the Four Gentlemen (plum, chrysanthemum, orchid, and bamboo), a material that our ancestors enjoyed using in their arts and crafts. Artist Kim Dae-su, who says that the bamboo that extends straight even though it is hollow symbolizes the spirit of scholars who do not lose their upright spirit despite any hardships, adds that this ‘scholar spirit’ is a noble spirit that exists in all Koreans, and through his work, he provides enlightenment to the society and people who forget it and live today. In addition, the formative composition, use of black and white film, and working process in his work also stimulate Korean emotions by containing meanings such as the harmony of yin and yang and the white people. We hope that you will experience the scholarly spirit conveyed by the strong vitality and spiritual power of bamboo, which he has been exploring for a long time, through artist Kim Dae-su's solo exhibition [Luminous Sonata] held at Gallery Imazoo this March. title: ‘Chunsik’s Spring’ Kim Won-geun’s solo exhibition
description: . KIM WON KEUN 2026.3.5 - 4.25 Gallery Mare, Paradise Hotel New Wing B1, 296 Haeundae Beach-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan. . Kim Won-geun’s sculpture begins with ‘laughter.’ Instead of images of grand and sophisticated sculptures, he conveys the warmth of life through ordinary people that can be found anywhere around us. His human figures, made with colorful colors on a modern material called resin epoxy, just stand quietly without any special movements, but they make the viewer smile naturally. This exhibition, Spring of Spring, tells the story of the warm days of spring that finally arrived after a long, difficult and lonely winter. The characters in the work have stout bodies, bulging bellies, somewhat clumsy expressions, and unfashionable fashion. The first impression is that it is rough and rough, but the longer you look at it, the more strange feelings and affection seep into it. This is not a flashy protagonist, but an ordinary version of ourselves who has always remained on the periphery. Kim Won-geun gives a warm look to those who are easily alienated in modern society dominated by lookism. The large head, exaggerated body proportions, intense colors, and persistent surface texture give the characters a sense of vitality and reveal their lives and emotions more clearly. The author shines a spotlight on those who remained in supporting roles, and expresses the beauty of life as they each struggle in their own way. . . The writer says: “Our lives are like boxers fighting alone in a square ring. But the images of struggling youth are infinitely more beautiful. I wanted to express ‘portrait of youth’ through the stories of ordinary people, not some heroes or great people.” Kim Won-geun's sculptures convey hope through the purity of imperfect beings. Like spring that comes after a long winter, the characters in his works offer small messages of comfort and warm support to those of us living today. . . <Spring of Spring> is ultimately the story of the day of spring that arrives for all ordinary people. 2026 Jeonbuk International Jazz Festa Season 1

DAY 1) Stella Cole

'A private gift-like concert where you can meet Stellar Cole, the star with 1.5 million followers who is attracting attention from all over the world, from a distance where you can even hear her breathing!'

<Unrivaled presence that captivated 850,000 people on TikTok and 730,000 people on Instagram>
<Judy Garland, revival of classical elegance reminiscent of Edith Piaf>
<The most notable jazz vocalist of 2026 selected by the legendary Decca>

Feel her delicate vocal control, bright energy, and positive energy conveyed through eye contact, which cannot be felt in a large concert hall, right under your nose. The romance of Old Hollywood, where time seems to have stopped, unfolds right next to you. Stella Cole's first performance in Korea, with a magical voice that makes you feel like you've turned back time! Don't miss the special opportunity to see it right before your eyes at Jeonju The Vine Hall!


DAY 2) Paul Cornish 

‘A young virtuoso chosen by Blue Note, the mecca of jazz!’
'The pinnacle of the current generation's jazz, Paul Cornish, the key pianist of the Joshua Redman Band, visits Korea for the first time!'

<The dream of jazz musicians, a new virtuoso ambitiously presented by ‘Blue Note’ in 2025>
<A unique talent chosen by maestro Joshua Redman as the pianist for his band>
<Composition of elite members of the New York jazz scene, including Joshua Crumbly (Bass) and Jonathan Pinson (Drums)>
<Overwhelming techniques ranging from the nostalgia of legendary bebop to the modern sensibility of Robert Glasper>

Witness the hottest sounds of New York, the center of world jazz, right before your eyes at The Vine Hall!

title: Back to the Nature
description: Back to the Nature The Back to the Nature exhibition by artists Jemin Kim and Kyungha Lee will be held at Cheonghwarang in March. Authors Kim Je-min and Lee Kyeong-ha have a deep love for nature and have explored the relationship between nature and humans through different perspectives and media. Artist Kim Je-min uses gouache and oil painting to personify nature and objects, and depicts moments that we tend to overlook inadvertently into witty and warm scenes. It captures the expressions and emotions of nature in everyday life and offers visitors a new perspective. Artist Kyungha Lee uses charcoal and oil paint as her main materials to capture the images of modern people living in the vast nature. The contrast between the vast landscape and the characters makes us think about the fragility of human existence and at the same time the possibility of coexistence with nature. How far have we gone from nature, and how can we get back to it? We hope that you will take the time to reconsider the meaning of nature that you have forgotten in your daily life through the two authors' honest perspectives on nature. Title: Back to the Nature: Kim Je-min and Lee Kyung-ha Period: 26. 3.10-3.28 Location: Cheonghwarang, 4 Samseong-ro 147-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul Opening hours: Tue-Fri 11-18 p.m., Sat: 11-17 p.m. Inquiries: 02 543 1663 The performance/exhibition program may change depending on the circumstances of the organizer, performer, etc. 1688-2220

title: Creative One-Act Play Festival: Horny Deul
The Last Dance with me
description: Gallery Planet will host the two-person exhibition “The Last Dance with Me” by Hana Kim and Yeju Lee from March 11 to April 10, 2026. This exhibition straddles the border between painting and three-dimensionality, focusing on the method and process by which the work is formed rather than the objects of its reproduction. Hana Kim presents a painting work that emphasizes the density and rhythm of brushstrokes, and Yeju Lee presents a three-dimensional work that reveals the physical properties of plaster and the repetitive production process. Through this, we highlight the points where the physical rhythm and work language that the two artists have built are revealed. Hana Kim considers the flatness of painting as an important condition for her work, and reveals the artist's movement and sense of time through the density and rhythm of brushstrokes accumulated on the canvas. In his work, the screen is not simply a space to reproduce objects, but functions as a surface on which the experiences and traces of the body facing the world accumulate. Yeju Lee repeats the process of molding, adding, and carving out plaster, pushing the form to the point where the material's resistance is revealed. His three-dimensional work, which develops around organic curves and masses, evokes the potential of the body rather than directly reproducing the concrete body, and the color and texture of the surface bring together the accumulation of time and a non-linear sense. 《Last Dance with Me》 shows the attitude of the two artists toward their work. Here, ‘last’ does not mean the end, but is closer to a condensation point formed after repetition and accumulation and a moment of transition that prepares for the next movement. The attitude of pushing forward with work according to one's own rhythm rather than external standards or speed, and the artist's time to choose and handle each moment on his own form an important axis of this exhibition. This attitude is in line with the perspective of this exhibition, which focuses on the process and accumulation of work rather than the finished result. Rather than viewing the completed work only as a result, this exhibition seeks to read it as a record of movements accumulated during the work process. The artist's body, emotions, speed, and energy remain as traces on materials and surfaces, and the work is revealed as a condensed state of this process of selection, repetition, and push and pull. The exhibition presents this process as a metaphor for ‘dance’ and focuses on the flow of the artist’s movements and judgments that existed before the completed form. Through this, we will provide an opportunity to look at contemporary work from the perspective of process and accumulation, following Kim Hana and Lee Yeju's unique body language and subjective rhythm. title: Jeongbin Lee's solo exhibition <The Passing, Standing By>
description: Ceramic artist Jeongbin Lee has been contemplating the two points of anxiety and well-being, and has focused on the ‘Nyangupshin’ series, which is a guardian deity work that can fit modern people living in the same era. The work is sometimes shaped using local soil or traditional techniques, which is a result of the artist going further than inheriting technical traditions and reflecting that emotional elements are important in the formation of tradition in his work. This exhibition is mainly explained around two things. It deals with the author's method of conveying the writer's well-being in response to the widespread anxiety and concerns of the times, while also conveying the perspective of Korea's misfortune and ups and downs. The artist's core series, the 'Cat Up God' series, simultaneously shows the familiarity and closeness of a cat, as well as a kind of sublimity and dignity as a guardian deity. In addition, by looking at the traditional motifs of this guardian deity, such as fortune telling and family religious aspects, we ask the question of whether our perspective on ups and downs may have changed in the present era. Lifting and flying in the exhibition title traditionally refer to the flowing or flowing out of yin and yang energy, and ‘and side’ used together refers to the place where the guardian spirit object that exists next to our living space or area is placed. In this exhibition, the object of family faith, which has been placed as a relational object rather than a symbol of coercion and authority, is interpreted in a modern way, and at the same time, it shows that the attitude of Korea's faith for blessings and fortunes is not to hope for good things or good fortune in the moment, but to let the energy flow as it is. The artist's work provides comfort and solace in the anxiety of the current era, and at the same time, it is a guardian spirit that enables us to let go of what we let go and to face the incoming energy, regardless of mere luck and wealth. Originally, well-being is not a very happy or good state, but is like a wide river. Even though the wide river is flowing, it appears to be calm and unmoving. And yet it flows within it at its own pace. I hope that while viewing this exhibition, one of the guardian spirits will be placed in your heart and become a companion to help you enjoy a peaceful and well-being. synopsis: [Chimpanzee] “Movies are like old friends.” Gwanghwamun, 2000. Godo, Momo, and Zeze become best friends because they have one thing in common: a love of movies. Three people discover a fascinating story about a chimpanzee in a used bookstore and fall in love with it. In 2025, Godo, who has become a film director, walks alone through Gwanghwamun and encounters the story of a chimpanzee again. [Naturally] “Now, comfortably and naturally! Ready…Action!” A movie filming location on a hot summer day. Child actors are performing scenes where they are running around the neighborhood and having fun. However, the director keeps telling them to act more naturally, and the actors and staff are worried. “What on earth is natural acting?” [Movie Time] “You really haven’t changed. Your face is the same as back then.” Yeonghwa, who lives in Chuncheon, visits Gwanghwamun for the first time in a long time. While walking alone through Jeong-dong and Gwanghwamun, I stumbled upon a theater and reunited with my high school classmate for the first time in decades. title: Creative cradle, subverted anatomical landscape:
description:
[Synopsis]

01 Living Machines, Mechanical Life
Living machines, mechanical life: Machines indulge in self-destructive mechanical pleasure through movements that can be repeated infinitely while in operation, and human mortality sometimes causes us to fall into the inhuman power of machines. It suggests the possibility of new life forms through the process where life forms and machines indulge and merge with each other.

02 The Intensity of Fusion
Mechanization of unstoppable impulse: The human brain and nerves have an instinctive impulse to survive, but the mechanical instinct is nothing more than simple repetition. When humans give up their nature and accept mechanical impulses,
It reminds us of the moment when metal and flesh become more deeply intertwined, and makes us imagine the possibility of a new life form being born between humans and non-living things.

03 The Mechanization of Irresistible Impulses
Violence of fusion: The moment when machines and living things collide, lusting after each other, iron and flesh, nerves and metal collide roughly. Sensation and insensibility, life and inanimateness mix together, and the possibility of a new existence arises.
This fusion is not a simple union, but a field of creation where neural explosion and mechanical pressure intersect.
At the moment when metal and skin share lustful friction, the boundary between humans and machines becomes blurred, and a new being called 'pseudo-life' exhales like a herald of birth.

04 The Birth of Artificial Life
Birth of similar life: We are aware of the new life forms or side effects that are born.
Will they live in harmony? Machines with a human scent and humans.
It suggests how we should live in the future.

title: Damien Hirst
venue: Seoul | National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Seoul
description: The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art is hosting Asia's first large-scale solo exhibition by British visual artist Damien Hirst. This exhibition encompasses the artist's entire work, from his early works to his recent works, and consists of various media such as installation, sculpture, and painting. The exhibition illuminates key themes the artist has explored, such as death and eternal life, human belief and desire in science and medicine, the value of art, and market logic, and seeks to provide a venue for broad discussion about life and values ​​in modern society. It includes representative works such as the ‹Natural History› series in which dead animals are placed in formaldehyde tanks and ‹For the Love of God› (2007), as well as unreleased latest works following the ‹Cherry Blossoms› series, providing an in-depth introduction to the world of the artist's work, which has constantly questioned the institutions and belief systems that make up society. title: 22nd Green Feel Wind Orchestra Regular Concert
venue: Dream Forest Art Center Concert Hall
description:
[Performance introduction]
This performance is a colorful stage that begins with the liveliness of the march and continues with the emotion of the movie music.

Opening the performance, First Suite for Band – Alfred Reed delightfully displays the rhythm and vitality of a wind ensemble with a work consisting of marches, rags, and gallops. The following song, Pearl Harbor, quietly depicts human emotions in the midst of war with its lyrical melody.

In the middle part, John Williams in Concert, which contains the musical world of John Williams, is played, presenting the charm of film music that is both grand and touching. Afterwards, Beauty and the Beast delivers a fairytale-like time to the audience with familiar melodies and a warm atmosphere.

Lastly, Moment for Morricone, a compilation of Ennio Morricone's famous songs, is played, ending the performance with a deep resonance.

title: Jooheon Shin Classical Guitar Invitational Recital
description:
[Performance introduction]

Classical guitarist Shin Joo-heon

Classical guitarist Shin Joo-heon, who is praised by both the music industry and the public for his creative ideas and emotional interpretation of works, majored in classical guitar and graduated from the Department of Instrumental Music, College of Music, Seoul National University.

He was recognized for his skills by winning prizes at leading domestic and international guitar competitions, including 1st place at the Korean Music Competition, 1st place at the Overseas Dispatch Competition, 2nd place at the International Music Competition Vienna, 1st place at the France Music Competition Guitar, and 4th place at the Adelaide Guitar Festival. Based on this, he has been invited to perform on major stages such as with orchestras and performances at the Seoul Arts Center, and is continuing his active international activities by giving solo recitals and invited performances in Korea, Tokyo, Japan, and Taichung, Taiwan.

He has collaborated with Seongnam Philharmonic Orchestra, Hanyang University College of Music, and Seoul Haegeum Ensemble, and has been invited as a performer to various festivals and stages to communicate with audiences, including a concert with commentary by Geum Nan-sae, Hyundai Motor Company STAGE

In addition, he served as music director for the IBK Industrial Bank of Korea's Win Class VVIP Concert and as the music general artist for Dokdo LIVE hosted by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, engaging in activities encompassing planning and performance.

Not limited to classical music, he has also been active in a wide range of popular music and content stages, such as PLAY THE GUITAR, musical performances, Nexon game music concerts, and various album production sessions, establishing himself as a performer who crosses the boundary between classical and popular music.

Recently, he has attempted to harmonize Eastern and Western music by collaborating with a number of Korean traditional music players, including duo activities with haegeum player Noh Eun-ah, and is continuously expanding his musical spectrum.

Meanwhile, his music is widely loved by the general public and music lovers at home and abroad through broadcast appearances such as SBS Amazing Competition Star King, KBS Music Room, and KBS Korean Traditional Music Festival, as well as YouTube and SNS content media.

He is currently teaching at Seoul Arts High School, Gyeonggi Arts High School, and Yewon School, and served as a conductor and music director for guitar ensemble classes at the former Armed Forces Financial Management Corps. In addition, he is striving to nurture younger students by running Shin Joo-heon's guitar class, and was awarded the Korea Guitar Association's Outstanding Leader Award.

In addition, he received the Korea Best Brand Cultural Artist Award in recognition of his musical achievements and contribution to the field of culture and arts.

Continuing his various activities, he is currently attracting attention as a next-generation guitar player, captivating the hearts of audiences with his beautiful tone and technically sophisticated performance.

title: FULL-RISE, Odd x Kurani x Blankible
Gukak Groove: Korean traditional music playing in the living room
description:
[Performance introduction]
This performance is an interpretive performance that combines Arirang, sanjo, folk songs, and popular melodies with the traditional gayageum and 25-string gayageum. It introduces the depth of traditional music and modern reinterpretation, and proposes an intimate musical experience that communicates with the audience in a salon space.

[PROGRAM]
* Two Arari 
This is a performance piece that newly arranged Jeongseon, Gangwon-do, Haeju, and Jindo Arirang into traditional gayageum and 25-string gayageum. It is a lyrical opening song that conveys the emotion of Korean folk songs through various gayageum tones.

* Kimjukparyu Gayageum Sanjo 
Kim Juk-pa is a master who established the flow of gayageum sanjo in the 20th century. Kimjukparyu Sanjo is a representative piece that shows the artistry and skills of the performer with its delicate Sigimsae, various playing techniques, and gradually faster beats.

* <A Million Roses> 
A Million Roses is widely known as Shim Soo-bong's song in Korea, but it began with the song <The Life of a Girl Given by Marinya>, which was released in Latvia in 1981. It contains a mythological story about the goddess of the earth and fate, Mara, suffering because she forgot to give happiness to her daughter. It was later rewritten into Russian and became widely known as a love song, and today's performance tells the story of how this melody traveled across borders.

* 25-string gayageum <Doraji Taryeong>
This is a performance piece that reinterprets the representative folk song of the Gangwon-Gyeonggi region, <Bolaji Taryeong>, using the wide vocal range and harmony of the 25-string gayageum.

* Memories engraved in my heart - <Cheommilmil> 
The theme song ‘Wolryang Representative Ah Jeoksim’ and ‘I’m Still Loving You’ from the movie <Cheommilmil> are played on two gayageums.

The 23rd Village Concert with Choir Music
description:
[Performance introduction]

Village with Choir Music was founded in 1996 by the first director, Lee Kang-sook (who served as the first president of Korea National University of Arts), to develop and distribute Korean choral music in the spirit of ‘bringing the beauty of the Korean language to the choir and to the world’ and to grow into a world-class choir. Currently, there are about 60 active musicians and members, including 2nd director Kun-yong Lee (former president of Korea National University of Arts), planning director Seung-chan Hong (arts management, professor at Korea National University of Arts), music director Jun-cheol Hong (former professor at Daewoo, Sungkonghoe University), and conductor Hong-soo Kim (currently professor of conducting department at Korea National University of Arts). We are striving to widely disseminate Korean choral music through a total of 22 regular performances and various collaborative and joint performances, and we plan to present composer Kim Jun-beom's cantata ‘The Missing Case of Samsinhalmae’ and various original choral pieces through the 23rd regular concert.

venue: Cheongju Art Hall old. Cheongju Citizens' Center) (Cheongju Art Hall (formerly Cheongju Citizens' Center)
description:
[Performance introduction]
Two pianists who imprinted the concept of ‘star’ in the classical world.
Peter Jablonski and Jeongwon Kim.
Appearance and charisma reminiscent of idols at the time of debut, and matching
Two artists who have charted unrivaled trajectories in their respective paths with their talent and musical depth.
Do you remember your first duo performance at the Seoul Arts Center 15 years ago?
Since then, through continued musical exchanges and friendships, he is on his way to becoming a virtuoso.
The two of them have become more mature in their interpretations and can communicate with just their eyes,
We will tell you a musical conversation that goes beyond a simple collaboration and spans the ages.

Pianists Peter Jablonsky and Jeongwon Kim debuted as star icons of the classical music world representing the 1990s and 2000s, and are performers who have received both deep musicality and wide public love. In this duo recital, Beethoven's Symphony No. 9, one of the most beloved symphonies by the public, will be presented in a special version arranged for two pianos by the ‘piano magician’ Franz Liszt.
In addition, through a colorful and fantastic program created by two pianos and four hands, the delicate sensibilities and excellent chemistry of the two performers are highlighted, and a deep musical conversation that only artists who have walked through the same era can be shared on stage.

title: Oral Play Project Jeong Joo-haeng: Marriage Proposal, and Bear
Kimchi!
synopsis: ‘Min-kyung’, who has lost her place in her heart due to retirement and separation, comes down to a small rural village and begins to spend her time quietly taking pictures. One day, an old man enters her camera, which focuses on landscapes rather than people and distance rather than emotions. ‘Deokgu’, a Vietnam veteran suffering from dementia. After losing his granddaughter in a car accident, his memory is gradually fading. Although he suffers from dementia, he sits in front of his house every morning and waves to his dead granddaughter. At the moment of taking a picture, he looks at the camera with clearer eyes than anyone else. The record that started out as a coincidence gradually becomes ‘Min-kyung’s’ day, and the time spent learning the story of Deok-gu’s family and trying to hold on to Deok-gu’s losing memories soon becomes a time to caress and heal Min-kyung’s own wounds. People who are losing their memories and people who have lost their direction in life. Two people with different wounds regain their smiles through photos and begin to share their feelings little by little. And finally, Deok-gu enters Min-kyung’s heart and says the words that resonate the brightest. “Kim~chi!” Like that one photo, the time between the two becomes clear again.

Yeongdo Culture and Arts Center OnStage, Daleum (DAL: UM): coexistence
venue: Yeongdo Culture and Arts Center Small Performance Hall (Jeolyeong Hall)
description:
[Performance introduction]
Daleum’s second regular album, “Coexistence,” is a musical work that depicts the harmony and balance created by different beings under the theme of ‘living together.’
This performance is centered around the sound of coexistence created by two traditional string instruments, the gayageum and geomungo. The program begins with ‘Dasreum’ based on traditional modes and continues through ‘Tal’, ‘dot’, ‘The Waves’, ‘Cracking’, and ‘Alive’, showing a musical narrative where tradition and modernity intersect. Each song expresses everyday emotions, cracks, recovery, and the energy of life in various ways and is structured so that the audience can comfortably immerse themselves in it. Daleum's unique performance style, which maintains the depth of traditional music while adding a modern sensibility, will provide a new experience to the audience.

[Program]
1. Dasreum

2. Tal

3.dot

4. Dodry

5.The Waves

6. Poison and Antidote

7.In the deep

8. Cracking

9. Alive

title: Gyeonggi Museum of Modern Art 20th Anniversary《Flowing and Accumulating》
venue: game | Gyeonggi Museum of Modern Art
description: The collection, which is the ‘face’ of the museum, is not limited to past art preserved in storage. The collection is living art that meets us again now and creates new meaning. In the layers of time, the collection asks the question, “What have we done and what should we do?” and makes us think about our past and future together. The 20th anniversary of the Gyeonggi Museum of Modern Art, Flowing and Accumulating, looks back on the museum's past with 125 pieces from its collection and looks at its future direction. The title “flowing and accumulating” is a metaphor for the process of our thoughts and questions accumulating and expanding over time. This encompasses the 20 years of Gyeonggi Museum of Modern Art and the meaningful moments the collection will create with visitors in the future. This exhibition does not list the past, but focuses on the moment when memories of the past are summoned to the present and acquire meaning. The collections, which were born at different times and collected in the museum, meet visitors here and now, creating new moments. This encounter leads to the museum's essential questions: “How do art and life meet?” and “How does an art museum connect visitors and art?” The exhibition unfolds the landscape where art and life meet through five questions, ranging from the fundamental beginnings of art to the scenery of our daily lives, memories of things that are forgotten, and solidarity and practice. When various ‘we’ with different backgrounds and experiences build up our own thoughts on this question, the exhibition acquires richer meaning. "Does art ( ) begin?" - About art that breaks down and expands boundaries "Do we live ( )?" - About the colorful aspects of everyday life and the trajectory of life "Do we remember ( )?" - About recalling forgotten memories to the present and remembering them together "Does art ( ) together?" - About connecting in the process and the meaning of 'together' "Do I practice ( )?" - About social practice examined through the attitude of artists The parentheses in the question are left blank. Let’s fill in the blanks and listen to the story that art tells. In particular, the last question highlights the attitude and practice adopted by an artist among members of society, focusing on the work of artist Kim Jeong-heon donated in 2024. This journey, which starts with art, discovers ‘us’, and then discovers ‘me’ again in art, does not lead to a single answer. Rather, it leads to more questions. The exhibition is completed only when the ‘now’ moment when the collection and the visitor meet, and the visitor’s thoughts are added. I hope this will be a time for you to reflect on yourself and your surroundings through the encounter with art that flows and accumulates. 3rd Seoul International Monodrama Festival, There is Morning
description:
[Synopsis]

Monday, September 4, 2001, 7:39 AM. The moment a girl takes her steps, time becomes undifferentiated and stops. The girl closes her eyes, sneezes, and floats in the air.
In that moment, a perfect rainbow at an angle of 42 degrees unfolds before your eyes. The seven-color panorama from red to purple is replaced with everyday objects such as trains, sheet music, jackets, and swimsuits, filling the stage. The seven notes of Doremi Fasolassido overlap to create a huge chord, but the girl who is the protagonist of that moment is unaware of this wonderful cosmic phenomenon.
Starting from a sneeze, time flows back and forth. People around me, friendship, dating, learning. The girl looks at the world by breaking it into small pieces, and reaches sadness and resentment within it.
So the girl sneezes, breathing and spitting out all of this with all her might.

title: 83rd Mokpo City Choir Regular Concert: B to B, Beyond (From Bach to Brahms, and to us)
venue: Mokpo Citizens Cultural & Sports Center Small Hall
description:
[Performance introduction]
Opening the most beautiful history book written in the language of music on a spring road
-The confession of the soloist becomes the sound of the choir... A special journey that continues a great legacy -

Bach, Beethoven, Brahms...and Schubert and Schumann.
The music of virtuosos whose names alone make our hearts beat has arrived in Mokpo riding the warm spring breeze.
This performance is a special stage where the beautiful 'German art song' that someone had quietly sung alone blooms again with the delicate harmony created by the Mokpo City Choir.
As we walk through the romantic forest following guest conductor Hwang Ji-hee's friendly commentary, we reach the premiere song 'Mokpo Station', where the music embodies our waiting and excitement. 
At the 'starting point of excitement' rather than the final station, please experience the scenery of the train flying into the sky and the Archipelago Sea becoming a constellation through the chorus.

title: Threshold, Kim Danbi Band Lane (來潾): A new beginning, Lane
description:
[Performance introduction]
Danbi Kim's band Lane was on stage to announce the start of [Threshold] in 2023.
Since then, the three-year threshold has moved forward with a new breath, and Lane stands at the beginning again.

<New Beginning, Lane> is a starting point for refining their respective meanings for both [Threshold] and Kim Danbi Band Lane.

Based on the experience accumulated so far, [Threshold] further improves the completeness of the performance and expands the scope of the performance by embracing various arts centered on music.

Lane redefines the meaning of the team name from 'Rain', which symbolizes comfort, to 'Rain (來潾)', which symbolizes coming clarity.

Dreaming of a place where clear sound always flows (來潾) and the sound of people visiting (來人) never ceases (來人), this performance shares the excitement and anticipation of the beginning, a little fear, and yet a cheerful heartbeat through music.

Following Kim Dan-bi's in-depth commentary and witty and witty progress, the performance and story naturally continue, and the audience crosses the time of a new beginning while listening to the music.

<New beginning, Lane>.
Sound and people meet again when I stand in front of them for the first time.

title: Creativity Center, Momo Me Salon: Adult Content
Creation Center, Choi Jin-seok: Four Pieces for Orchestra
description:
[Performance introduction]

- Modern music composer Choi Jin-seok's new orchestral work <Four Pieces for Orchestra>
- Jinseok Choi, a contemporary music composer who won third place at the Basel Composition Competition, presents a new orchestral work consisting of four chapters on the themes of waves, darkness, light, and wind.
Contemporary music composer Choi Jin-seok's new orchestral work <Four Pieces for Orchestra> consists of four pieces (chapters) on the themes of waves, darkness, light, and wind. Each chapter musically explores the different energies and states of nature, forming a continuous flow through the contrast between violence and silence, creation and extinction, and tension and relaxation. Throughout the work, the movements of nature are depicted by applying the structural principles of music that the composer considers most important. This work will be performed for the first time by the Hankyung Arte Philharmonic and conducted by Kim Yu-won.

title: Daejeon City Dance Company Special Performance Ⅰ, Fairy Tale Drawn through Dance: Pinocchio
description:
[Program]

Prologue - Wooden Child Pinocchio
The fairy who granted the father's wish for a child, “Prove that you are brave, truthful, and unselfish, and one day you will become a real person!”

Chapter 1 Village Market
In a peaceful marketplace, a greedy count tyrannizes the villagers.

Chapter 2 Grandfather returns home
Pinocchio and his grandfather's first meeting.

Chapter 3 The road to school
Pinocchio is different from ordinary children.

Chapter 4 Pinocchio's Lie
Pinocchio bravely jumps into the wandering group... His nose gets longer every time he lies, and it returns to its original state with just a word of 'truth'!

Chapter 5 Pinocchio's wrong choice
Pinocchio did not listen to his father. “You must learn to choose between right and wrong. Your ‘heart’ will give you the answer.”

Chapter 6 Inside the whale's belly...
When I found out about my father's love, I cried because I was worried and sad for my father, who was trapped inside the Pinocchio whale's stomach.

Epilogue - Pinocchio, a real person gained through ‘heart’
Something magical happened to Pinocchio, who found his ‘true heart’!!!

title: Matinee Concert Ⅰ: Author Youngha Kim’s reason for travel, and music
venue: Gangdong Arts Center Grand Theater Han River
description:
[Performance introduction]

Wednesday morning, a matinee concert with classical music.
We are waiting for four meetings in 2026. In April and May, September and October, we meet between seasons and start talking about music.
This series is co-created by writer Kim Young-ha. Every month, we present new stories and a curation of music hand-selected by the author.

Reason for music, reason for travel
Europe walked through the eyes of a novelist and remembered through the melody of music

Why do we go on a trip?
Best-selling author and storyteller of our time, Kim Young-ha, will become the host of the 2026 Matinee series and invite audiences to a romantic city in Europe.
This series is a high-quality lecture concert that combines classical music with the unfamiliar landscapes and people that the author encountered while traveling to Italy, Germany, France, and Spain, and the humanistic insights he gained there.
The brilliant sunlight, lonely contemplation, and artistic inspiration felt while traveling are vividly brought to the stage.
In a leisurely time in the morning, a combination of author Kim Young-ha's charming conversation and a performance full of local flavor will be a special rest that will remind you of the 'reason for travel' when you are tired of repetitive daily life.

Life is like a festival, the land of opera
In warm April, Italians live like the main characters on stage every day. Eat well, laugh loudly, and love passionately. It follows the cheerful and optimistic lifestyle of Italians as told by author Youngha Kim. It is the most exciting stage to fill the vitality of spring while appreciating gorgeous and dramatic opera arias and romantic Italian songs.

A lazy person turned into a cow
girl referee
synopsis: The high school girl who conquered the school with just one fist is back, this time wearing ‘sweatshirts’! ‘Minah’, who has a strong sense of chivalry and determination, is an overly righteous girl who lost her parents in an accident at a young age and grew up at her aunt’s house. Minah entered high school with the promise of ‘never fighting again’ and dreams of a new, ordinary start, but from the first day, she falls in love with her handsome and seemingly just friend ‘Mingi’. The problem is ‘Se-hyuk’, the leader of the delinquent Iljin Circle who is targeting Min-gi. Min-ah, who saw Se-hyuk's gang bullying Min-gi, couldn't bear it anymore and rescued Min-gi 'in a sweatshirt that covered her face'. After this day, the school is in an uproar trying to find the identity of the sweatshirt guy, and Mingi begins a full-fledged investigation to find the savior. Meanwhile, the triangular battle between Min-ah, Hye-ri, and Se-hyeok, with Min-gi in the middle, ignites, and Min-ah hides her identity and leads a triple life, pretending to be normal, mischievous, and in love. But is that possible for Minah, who has an explosive sense of justice and is also hot-tempered? Love becomes twisted, identity is in danger of being revealed, and the fight grows bigger...

title: HA HYUN SANG Archive Live: New Boat
Missing
description:
[Performance introduction]



Missing

Contemporary dance × Interactive media art



A record of adaptation, a body that never stops

What record will your body leave in a lost world?



What has disappeared?

Is it nature, air, or senses?

Or is it the human form we knew?



〈Missing〉 observes the human body reorganizing itself in a changed environment. In this work, the body is not the subject of expressing emotions. The body is a structure that responds to the environment and is a constantly adapting system.



What Missing refers to is not simple disappearance. The loss of familiar sensations, the previous way of breathing, the relationship with nature, and some of the forms that defined humans have been erased. However, this work does not mourn that loss. We quietly look at the body that continues to transform and adapt even after it disappears.



[Synopsis]



A body wrapped in wrap is on stage. It is not a sign of oppression, but a condition. In an environment full of dust and toxins, the body surrounds itself and redesigns its functions within limited conditions. Media art is layered on the body, and the body is distorted, transformed, and reborn.



The body faces the floor. Contact with nature and soil that remains among the artifacts. A body that reawakens at the cellular level through the skin, through movement, and through movement. The dancers' movements unfold in space in the form of waves and contours and respond in real time to interactive media.



When the environment changes, the body also changes. Where beauty standards disappear, the body creates a new balance. Physically impossible distortions of the body are visualized through the media, and traces of evolution are revealed in unfamiliar forms on stage.



Nevertheless, humans do not give up on relationships. Pushing and pulling, misaligning and intertwining, the transformed bodies adapt together. The essence of a relationship remains the same even if the environment changes.



The song flows. The body responds to the sound. In places where language cannot reach, the body instinctively moves towards nature. A body that is distorted and changed, but does not give up hope. 〈Missing〉 is not a work of restoring something that has disappeared. It is an exploration of the body that continues to transform and adapt even after it disappears. After this work is over, it is enough for the audience to be aware of their breathing and body for a moment.

title: So we,
venue: Daejeon City Yeonjeong Gugak Center small yard
description:
[Performance introduction]
<Isaenggyujangjeon> from 『Geumosinhwa』 by Kim Si-seup, a writer of the Joseon Dynasty, is a required classic for the CSAT literature subject. 
A musical with artistic and educational value by reinterpreting <Isaenggyujangjeon> in a modern way and expressing the emotions of traditional Korean music with a modern sensibility.

[Synopsis]
Choi Rang is at a flowery age with a lot of things she wants to do and a lot of curiosity.
I love the love my parents give me in a wealthy and happy home, and I always try to be a pretty daughter.
I lived. But since when? Was it because we laughed together at our friends’ love news?
The sudden wind of excitement that blooms in my heart is awkward for me, but it's not a bad thing.
It's true. I want to love too. Not the free love I've enjoyed so far, but the love I can have
First love! If I could, I would pour out my love without regret. And forever
I will protect you and be happy forever!
Life is hard like frozen ground, but I always live as I am today.
This life is lived for the happiness of today.
Although he is highly educated, he was born into a poor family. Although I live for my father's unfulfilled dream,
It's not the life I want. But I can't betray my parents' expectations. Why is it me?
Wouldn't you be interested in this? My family's first goal is my success. Before that, love was nonsense.
It happens. But today, when everything is in order, I feel strange for some reason.
When two different people meet and feel that it is a solid and perfect love, trials come...

venue: Gongju Literary Center Grand Performance Hall
description:
[Performance introduction]

Wisdom and hope instilled in dreaming children, a heartwarming masterpiece musical enjoyed by the whole family.
 
The magic of One Thousand and One Nights unfolding in the mysterious desert city of Agrabah will come to the main performance hall of the Princess Literary Center in 2026.
The children's musical <Aladdin and the Magic Lamp> is based on the famous fairy tale that has been loved by children all over the world, and is completed with upgraded attractions and solid storytelling.
A fairytale world that stimulates the imagination, a stage background with an exotic atmosphere and colorful costumes that highlight the characters' personalities were combined to bring the Agrabah seen in books to life on stage.
 
The eye-catching lighting production, the lively acting of the actors, and the lively dances and songs that make you shake your shoulders will provide enjoyment just right for children.
In 2026, we invite you to this special adventure prepared by the Gongju Literary Center so that our children can discover the jewel-like courage in their hearts.

title: NT Live, Mrs Warren's Job (film)
description:
[Performance introduction]
Between morality and survival, the price of choice that women had to bear

We present “Mrs. Warren’s Occupation” by George Bernard Shaw, a Nobel Prize winner in literature and a leading British critic, thinker, and playwright. This work sharply criticized the structural inequality of British society that economically oppresses women through the 'prostitute problem', and caused a great stir when it was published. It also attracts attention in that five-time Olivier Award winner Imelda Staunton plays mother and daughter together for the first time with her own daughter, Bessie Carter. In addition, this work is a new work in which Imelda Staunton and director Dominic Cooke have joined hands once again, and sheds a deep light on human choice and responsibility at the point where morality and self-reliance, tradition and progress collide.

[Plot]
Bibi Warren is an intelligent and independent young woman who has just graduated from college. She learns that her mother, Kitty Warren, used socially unacceptable methods to make a living in the past. Bibi questions whether her mother's choice was morally justifiable, and is conflicted as she faces the reality that it is not a thing of the past. A daughter and a father who try to live according to their beliefs

The mother's values, which had to survive in a wealthy society, clash. But what was the price of Mrs. Warren's enormous wealth?

title: National Opera, The Magic Flute
description:
[Performance introduction]
<The Magic Flute>, the last opera written by genius composer Mozart in his life, will be performed by Korea's representative National Opera. This work, which depicts the journey of a man and a woman overcoming trials and achieving love amidst the conflict between reason and emotion symbolized by night and day, has been loved by people around the world for over 200 years since its premiere in 1791. In addition to fantastic melodies, including the 'Queen of the Night' aria, the arias were performed with Korean subtitles and the lines were performed in Korean, making it easy and enjoyable for anyone to immerse themselves in. I hope the whole family can enjoy the magical feast of music presented by Mozart together.

[Plot]
This is Singsheville (a German-language opera with dialogue in the middle, like a play) that Mozart completed two months before his death.
The simple story of lovers in love and the battle between good and evil, along with Mozart's beautiful music and comical elements.
In addition, it is a work that is still loved even about 200 years after its premiere in 1791. 

In a world where the 'forces of light' ruled by Sarastro and the 'forces of darkness' ruled by the Queen of the Night are in conflict, Tamino loses his mind while being chased by a large snake, and the Queen of the Night's three maids save him. The Queen of the Night shows Tamino a portrait of her daughter Pamina and asks him to save her. The three maids give a magic flute to Tamino, who is in love with Pamina's portrait, and together with Papageno, they set off to rescue Pamina, who has been kidnapped by Sarastro. Tamino meets Pamina after many twists and turns, and they undergo Sarastro's test to confirm their love for each other and make their love come true.

title: Toetmaru Dance Company’s regular performance: Community [Daehakro]
description:
[Performance introduction]

1. <NODE>
〈NODE〉, choreographed by Jaeho Shim, explores the structure of the ‘group’ that humans have formed for survival, and the mechanism of ‘splitting’ that inevitably occurs within it. We form groups to connect with each other, but as the group expands, differences in standards become boundaries and create new separations. In the structure of human society, which becomes more connected and more finely divided at the same time, individuals begin to be defined by ‘where they belong.’

Rather than determining this structure, the work raises the question of whether a society complete as one is possible. Here, ‘node’ refers to a state in which each individual exists as a single point rather than a large one, and we want to explore through the body the relationships that coexist in invisible tension without being completely combined or broken.

2. 〈Walk and Waltz〉
Everyone walks. But how much do we look at the life hidden in those steps?

〈Walk and Waltz〉, choreographed by Kim Young-woong, is an experimental creation that uses ‘walking’, the most everyday human action, as the starting point of dance, with the theme of ‘swimming the rhythm of life’. This work seeks to capture the inner voices and life experiences that humans face in their lives through the everyday act of ‘walking.’ The dancer's steps extend beyond simple movement into a flow of emotions, and traces of daily life are reorganized into visual movements. The stage, which utilizes light, sound, and the texture of costumes, sensuously reveals the theme of ‘a body that walks through time.’

Here, ‘node’ refers to a state in which each individual exists as a single point rather than a large one, and we want to explore through the body the relationships that coexist in invisible tension without being completely combined or broken.

2. 〈Walk and Waltz〉
Everyone walks. But how much do we look at the life hidden in those steps?

〈Walk and Waltz〉, choreographed by Kim Young-woong, is an experimental creation that uses ‘walking’, the most everyday human action, as the starting point of dance, with the theme of ‘swimming the rhythm of life’. This work seeks to capture the inner voices and life experiences that humans face in their lives through the everyday act of ‘walking.’ The dancer's steps extend beyond simple movement into a flow of emotions, and traces of daily life are reorganized into visual movements. The stage, which utilizes light, sound, and the texture of costumes, sensuously reveals the theme of ‘a body that walks through time.’

title: Paul Cornish Trio's first performance in Korea
venue: Seongsu Art Hall Seongsu Culture and Welfare Center) (Seongsu Art Hall (Seongsu Culture and Welfare Center)
description:
[Performance introduction]


As a jazz album record label, Blue Note has great symbolism among jazz enthusiasts in terms of not only popular popularity but also artistic achievement. Paul Cornish, a new pianist ambitiously recruited by Blue Note, is currently playing in the band of American modern saxophone virtuoso Joshua Redman, and his debut work was released by Blue Note in 2025.

 
Many media outlets commented on his debut work <You're Exaggerating!>, saying that Blue Note once again has a keen eye for finding new artists with fresh ideas, and the Financial Times evaluated the combination of Blue Note and Paul Cornish with the headline “Blue Note strikes again.” This first performance in Korea, conducted by the original members who participated in the album, consists of a trio of Joshua Crumbley (bass) and Jonathan Pinson (drums), allowing you to experience the lively performances and energy of young performers representing the current American jazz scene.


From classic bop reminiscent of bebop greats Bud Powell and Thelonious Munch to post-bop creative jazz following the lineage of modern pianists such as Jason Moran and Robert Glasper, the Paul Cornish Trio's first performance in Korea will be a performance where you can experience the essence of 21st century jazz pianism through lyrical and powerful sound, adding your own original color to Blue Note's great legacy.



[Introducing Paul Cornish]


He was a finalist at the 2023 American Piano Awards and the Herbie Hancock International Jazz Piano Competition, and won third place. He was recognized for his youthful sense and perfect skills, and has performed extensively as a session member for Joshua Redman, Louis Cole, Mark Guiliana, etc. Turning 29 this year, he already displays the maturity of a virtuoso and the agility and creativity required for jazz interplay, and is a sensational pianist selected by Blue Note.
