description: The National Ballet's <Swan Lake>, which records sold-out performances every time, is a choreography by Yuri Grigorovich, a master of ballet choreography, and features a happy ending designed especially for the National Ballet. Act 1 Scene 1 Inside the palace. Today is the prince's 20th birthday. The prince and his friends dancing happily with the maidens of the court. At this time, the queen appears and congratulates the prince on becoming an adult and gives him a sword as a gift. After everyone leaves, Prince Siegfried, left alone, feels that some unknown force keeps leading him somewhere. Act 1, Scene 2: Guided by an unknown force, we arrive at a lake in the forest. The prince discovers swans on the lakeside that take on human form. Prince Siegfried falls in love with the most beautiful of them all, Princess Odette. She complains that they have been transformed into swans during the day and humans at night by a genius devil's curse, and says that to be freed from the spell of this curse, they must receive the unchanging love of one person. The prince swears his love and promises to announce his marriage to her at the ball the next day, and they part ways. Act 2, Scene 1, Palace Ballroom. The prince greets the guests while waiting for Odette to arrive. The prince is urged to choose a bride among the princesses invited from Poland, Russia, Spain, Hungary, and Naples, but the prince has no intention. At that time, the devil appears with his daughter Odile. The prince runs to Odile, who resembles Odette. The devil now begins to test the prince's feelings. The prince falls for the charms of Odile the Black Swan and announces his marriage to her. At this time, darkness suddenly creeps in and a vision of Odette in despair appears. Only then does the prince realize that he has been played by a trick of fate and runs to the shore of Swan Lake. Act 2, Scene 2, Lakeside. Odette delivers the sad news to the swans, saying that they will live as swans forever due to the prince's betrayal. The prince came running to ask for forgiveness. However, the devil continues to interfere in order to separate him from Odette. The prince tries to fight against fate, but the devil's power is great. At that moment, when Odette tells the prince that she forgives him, a miracle occurs in which their love overcomes the evil power of the devil. description:
[Performance introduction]

[Pre-Event 1] 

32nd Domestic Academic Conference <Records of 40 years of Korean Dance Festival and discourse for the future>

As a pre-event for the 40th anniversary of the Korean Dance Festival, a domestic academic conference <Records of 40 years of the Korean Dance Festival and Discourse for the Future> will be held as a pre-event. This academic conference, held in conjunction with the Korean Dance Research Society, an affiliated organization of the Korean Dance Association, will provide an academic overview of the trends and achievements of Korean creative dance accumulated by the Korean Dance Festival over the past 40 years, reinterpret its artistic value and contemporary meaning, and research presentations to seek future directions and discourse. A forum for discussion between Korean creative dance and academia will be held on Friday, April 3 at 1 p.m. at the Multipurpose Hall of the Artist House.

[Pre-event 2] <Charm Series - Seoul Street Dance Film>

The charming city of Seoul is captured through Korean dance. Korean dancers visit the streets and spaces of Seoul, where past, present, and future coexist and whose beauty is recognized worldwide, and express them through dance. [Synopsis]

[Opening invitation performance] The opening invitation performance begins with a performance by the honorary chairman of the Korea Dance Association and continues with meaningful projects with the board of directors and works showing the current state of Korean creative dance.

The opening invitational performance of the Korean Dance Festival will be decorated with excellent works by many artists who have come together for the Korean Dance Festival. First, <Sounds of the Night> by honorary chairman Deok-kyung Yoon, who led the Korean Dance Association as chairman for over 10 years, will be presented. <Sounds of the Night> is a solo dance piece composed by Hwang Byeong-ki, inspired by Ahn Jung-sik's oriental painting 'Seongjaesugando (聲在樹間圖)' and premiered at the '1990 Contemporary Dance Artists Exhibition'. This is a work that expresses the dense moments, the resonance amplified in silence.

A special stage that highlights this year’s Korean Dance Festival! <Dance, the Excitement> by the Korean Dance Festival 40th Anniversary Project Team will be presented. <Dance, the Excitement>, a work that can be enjoyed by people of all ages and genders, was first performed in 1982 and is a work that seeks to complete another layer created through the unity of the audience and dancers. A coexistence structure is formed through communication between the dancers, performers, and the audience in the work, and the work is maximized through visual mise-en-scène production through the combination of object performance and modern music, theatrical elements, and modern wear of traditional costumes. For this stage of <Dance, the Excitement>, 10 dance artists, including Lim Hyun-seon, Lee Ae-hyun, and Kim Yong-cheol, who are board members of the Korea Dance Association, came together for this Korean Dance Festival. In celebration of the 40th anniversary of the Korean Dance Festival, another ‘exciting’ stage will be performed by the artists of the Korea Dance Association. 

Lastly, <Resonance and Mystery>, a work by Jeon Su-hyeon of Altimeets, which won the Best Work Award in the Grand Theater category at the 39th Korean Dance Festival in 2025, will be performed. Choreographer Jeon Soo-hyun's <Resonance and Mystery> is a work that talks about the timeless resonance and rebirth of our words, music, and art. The energy of the group dance that seems to shake the ground and the resonance through the deconstruction and recombination of Korean art are presented.  The opening performance of this Korean Dance Festival, where you can experience the history, present, and new resonance of Korean dance through three works, will convey the deep emotion of dance to the audience.

[Main Performance] 2026 40th Korean Dance Festival <The Path, Trace of the Body> A new performance by 20 choreographers!

The main performance of the Korean Dance Festival will be a competition stage for works with the theme of ‘The Path, the trace of the body’. The large theater division consists of new works presented by eight choreographers at the Arko Arts Theater's main theater, while the small theater division presents experimental and unique new works by twelve choreographers at the Cotton Hall of the Performing Arts Center of Dongduk Women's University. The Korean Dance Festival, which is held in a competition format, is positioned as a dance art festival that discovers the next generation of choreographers in the Korean dance world by selecting the best and best works, expands the representative repertoire of Korean creative dance, and leads new artistic attempts.

[Closing Invitation Performance and Awards Ceremony] A closing invitation performance where you can see works that have been in sync with the revival of Korean creative dance and award-winning works with a new sense.

You can see <Yeom> by Kang Miri Hall Dance Company, which has led the revival of Korean creative dance in the Busan area through creative work since the 1980s, at the closing invitation performance. The work <Yeom (念)> is a work that deeply interprets Seungmu, and has been evaluated as ‘an experiment on the limits of Korean traditional dance, another experiment on the overflow, and an inevitable work that must be done.’ <Yeom (念)>, which solidifies the identity and position of Korean creative dance by crossing the transformation and deconstruction of traditional dance, is expected to brighten the stage of this closing invitation performance.

Following this, <Strangers> by Dance us project Kim Hyeon-seon, winner of the Excellence Award in the Grand Theater category at the 39th Korean Dance Festival in 2025, will be performed. People who cannot mix in a certain place are expressed as strangers, and contain the message that anyone can be a stranger, so differences must be acknowledged and coexist.

At the final awards ceremony, the award-winning works that graced the 2026 40th Korean Dance Festival <The Path, Trace of the Body> will be announced. Out of a total of 20 works, the Grand Prize, Excellence Award, Audience Special Award, and Best Dance Award will be selected in the large theater category, and the Grand Prize, Excellence Award for Choreography, and Special Jury Award will be selected in the small theater category. In addition, we will be awarding ‘Dance Artist of the Year’ certificates to the eight choreographers selected in the Grand Theater category and the Best Click Award, which can be said to be the popular award of the pre-event Seoul Street Dance film, so please show your interest.

Please join us for the 2026 40th Korean Dance Festival <The Path, Trace of the Body>, which unfolds the 40 layers of time that Korean creative dance has accumulated, and the new movements that will be layered on top of them.

[Performance introduction]
Cellist Kian Soltani, who has been attracting attention on the world stage for his ‘deep musicality and unique presence,’ and pianist Jaehong Park, who has rapidly expanded his presence through international competitions, will present a duo recital.
Soltani, resident artist of the Iceland Symphony Orchestra, has been described as a “remarkable cellist” by The Times and “perfection itself” by Gramophone. As an exclusive artist for Deutsche Grammophon, he has performed with world-class orchestras such as the Berlin Staatskapelle, Munich Philharmonic, and NHK Symphony.
Jaehong Park gained international fame by winning the 2021 Ferruccio Busoni International Piano Competition with four special awards, and has proven his musical capabilities by winning the Cleveland International Young Artist Piano Competition and the Gina Bakauer Competition.
On this stage, the program continues with Reza Valli, Schubert, and Rachmaninoff, naturally revealing each person's musical roots and interpretations. Soltani's cello, with its deep lyricism and sophisticated technique, and Jaehong Park's piano, with its wide tone and solid structure, form a dense ensemble in close harmony. This duo recital, completed by the combination of experience accumulated on the international stage and mature musicianship, will be a time to present the depth of sincere chamber music beyond glamour.

title: Popera tenor Lim Hyeong-ju’s New Year’s Recital: Popera Sensation!
description:
[Performance introduction]

Since the ‘King Of Popera - King of Popera’ recital commemorating the 25th anniversary of his debut, which was grandly held at the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts in Seoul in September 2023, the ‘original popera star’ Lim Hyung-joo (40, Distinguished Professor of Vocal Music at Rome City University of the Arts) is holding a paid recital in Seoul for the first time in three years!

 
Became the first Korean to receive the UN Peace Medal, completely conquered the three major halls of Carnegie Hall in the U.S. with a solo performance, signed an exclusive album distribution contract with one of the world's top four record labels, received Japan's NHK's 'Red and White Song Concert' and both the U.S. Obama & Trump Presidential Awards, was a voting member and judge of the U.S. Grammy Award, had a private audience and performance with Pope Francis, was awarded the title of FRSA for life by the Royal Society of Arts and was awarded the title of FRSA by the Royal Society of Korea, received a commendation from the President of the Republic of Korea and is the youngest recipient of the National Merit in history. Lim Hyeong-ju, a true popera legend born in Korea, including the Dongbaekjang Medal, will hold a New Year's recital with the subtitle 'Popera Sensation!' at Yeongsan Art Hall in Yeouido, Seoul at 7:30 pm on March 20th.

 
In this performance, Lim Hyeong-ju will present to the audience the elegant, gorgeous, lyrical and grand 'essence of popera', including 'Become a Thousand Winds' and 'I Hope You Are Happy (KBS Cheerful Girl Chunhyang OST)', classical music, pop music, musicals, pop songs, and even special 7080 dance songs, with the fantastic accompaniment of the Korean National Philharmonic Ensemble, of which he has served as music director for a long time.

 
There is no doubt that a lot of public attention will be paid to his beautiful and affectionate songs that are closer to his friendly appearance that removes his mysticism, such as his recent appearances in EBS's <Seo Jang-hoon's Millionaire Next Door>, KBS's <100 People's Emotional Show: The Signature>, Channel A's <Table for Four>, and TV Chosun's <Dad and Me>.


[Program]

1, Shostakovich Waltz No. 2 (orchestra performance)
Performance: Korean National Philharmonic Orchestra

 
2, Ave Maria
Popera tenor Lim Hyung-joo/Performer: Korean National Philharmonic Orchestra

 
3,Memory (Musical ‘Cats’)
Popera tenor Lim Hyung-joo/Performer: Korean National Philharmonic Orchestra

 
4,A Time For Us (Movie ‘Romeo and Juliet’)
Popera tenor Lim Hyung-joo/Performer: Korean National Philharmonic Orchestra

Performance: Korean National Philharmonic Orchestra

Popera tenor Lim Hyung-joo/Performer: Korean National Philharmonic Orchestra

Popera tenor Lim Hyung-joo/Performer: Korean National Philharmonic Orchestra

 
8, O Sole Mio (Neapolitan folk song)
Popera tenor Lim Hyung-joo/Performer: Korean National Philharmonic Orchestra



INTERMISSION

Popera tenor Lim Hyung-joo/Performer: Korean National Philharmonic Orchestra

Popera tenor Lim Hyung-joo/Performer: Korean National Philharmonic Orchestra

Popera tenor Lim Hyung-joo/Performer: Korean National Philharmonic Orchestra

title: Tenor Jin Seong-won Recital
venue: Sejong Center for the Performing Arts Sejong Chamber Hall
description:
[Synopsis]

“A lullaby for lost youth”
-Comfort shared between Schubert and the youth of the 21st century

Schubert sang of hope and despair from his sickbed in 1823. The wanderings of the water mill youth he depicts reflect our anxiety and loneliness living in 2026. It's an ironic love song of youth that's okay to fail and beautiful even if it hurts.

Jin Seong-won, a tenor with excellent interpretive skills and a warm vocal voice, trains younger students as a professor at Gachon University. His voice expresses the human agony and youth composed by Schubert with vocal depth!

Eunjoo Choi, a pianist with a distinguished and delicate touch. From the whisper of a stream to the swirling psychological changes of a young man, her accompaniment embodies the essence of Schubert's songs in piano melody!

Announcer Kim Jin-woong, a rising talent at KBS. With his captivating voice and delivery, his trustworthy commentary serves as a bridge to lower the threshold for the beautiful mill girl!

“Every night when I go to bed, I hope not to wake up again… Only works created by sadness can bring people the most joy…”
(From a letter sent by Schubert to his friend Kupelwieser in 1824)

We present to you the song “The Beautiful Mill Girl,” a record of the ‘will to live’ that Schubert left us.


[PROGRAM]

Franz Schubert (1797–1828)
The beautiful mill girl Die Schöne Mullerin D.795

I. Das Wandern
II. Wohin? where?
III. Halt! Stop!

XIV. Der Jäger Hunter

XVII. Die Böse Farbe The color I hate
XVIII. Trockne Blumen dried flower
XIX. Der Müller Und Der Bach The Mill Youth and the Stream
XX. Des Baches Wiegenlied Lullaby of the Stream

description: The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art's interdisciplinary art project «Detective Time» is a project that explores the complexity of time that modern people experience in their daily lives by comparing it to the existence of a “detective” and the “deep thoughts of a detective.” Human time, in contrast to the efficient time of artificial intelligence, resembles the thinking of a detective who wanders around looking for subtle clues, focuses on the time, and sometimes fails to arrive at a clear answer. title: Me and Grandpa [Princess]
venue: Gongju Literary Center Grand Performance Hall
description:
[Performance introduction]
A heart-warming true story of a grandfather who sets out to find an old love lost during the war, and a grandson who dreams of becoming a melodrama.
 
Filled with emotion even without fancy stage techniques, this is the power of a ‘real’ story!
The play <Me and Grandpa> is a work based on the real story of Min Jun-ho, the director and CEO of the theater company ‘Ganda Performance Delivery Service’.
This play, which is completed by 'Junhee', a performance script writer who wanted to write a great melodrama, while observing his maternal grandfather, is completed without artificial directing. 
It depicts the simple and honest scenes of our lives. “The people we call grandmother and grandfather were once youths who were passionately in love.”
It reminds us of the truth and provides deep empathy and warm comfort across all generations. 

[Synopsis]
‘Junhee’ is a passionate performance script writer who wants to write a melodrama.
As he sets out to find his grandfather's old love, he discovers true 'life'.
 
Junhee is a passionate performance script writer who wants to write a great melodrama.
His teacher asked him to observe and complete the task of his maternal grandmother and grandfather.
 
However, my grandmother suddenly collapsed before I could start writing.
Eventually, Junhee began to observe only his grandfather.
Record your grandfather's voice and listen to his past stories.
In the end, before my grandmother collapsed, she warned me, “Never help me find something.”
The grandfather's acquaintances also set out to find him.
Listening to my grandfather's story, I somehow thought it was a woman! Was this my grandfather’s first love?
 
Somehow, out of anticipation that a melodrama might be completed, I disobeyed my grandmother's words,
Jun-hee sets out to find grandmother Lim Soo-im together.
 
Will there be an interesting path that Junhee wants to take?

title: Hyeja Bang
venue: Chungbuk | National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Cheongju
description: This is an exhibition that introduces the works of Bang Hye-ja (1937-2022), who traveled back and forth between Korea and France and built an independent world of art based on the culture and arts of both countries. As one of the events commemorating the 140th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Korea and France in 2026, the exhibition introduces major works from each period by Bang Hye-ja, who showed early abstract art works as a female artist, along with French-based works that have not been introduced in Korea, including works from the collection of the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art. In this exhibition, which provides a comprehensive view of the life, worldview, and expression method of the artist who has used ‘light’ as a source of inspiration throughout his life, and explores its significance, you can examine the process of various pictorial experiments and insights. title: UNDERCITY presents, Jeremy Olander concert in Korea: Jeremy Olander When The Rain Falls album tour
description:
[Performance introduction]

Jeremy Olander, who held the Soft Opening of UNDERCITY, returns to Seongsu after a year. This time, it is not just one set, but Open to Close, which completes the flow of the night from the beginning to the end as a single narrative? The stage is filled with All Night Long Set (6 hours).

Since his debut through Eric Prydz's Pryda Friends, he has established himself as one of the most trusted producers in the melodic house and techno scenes, working on international labels such as Drumcode, Anjunadeep, and Diynamic. Detailed sound design and a set composition that designs both emotion and structure are his biggest signatures. He has also established his identity as an artist and curator through his own label, Vivrant, which he founded in 2014.

This performance is not just a simple performance in Korea, but a Vivrant Showcase and a symbolic night that opens the era of his debut album When The Rain Falls. This album, which will be released on March 13, is his most personal and introspective work, capturing years of artistic evolution and changes in life.

When The Rain Falls aims for electronic music as ‘listening music’ rather than as a functional track for clubs. This album, completed based on his own experiences and emotions, shows the direction of sound newly defined by Jeremy Olander.

The album's world view, starting with the first single 'Apollo', focuses on cinematic sound and clear emotional lines, revealing his expanded musical spectrum through various collaborations. It is a turning point that goes beyond existing progressive house and evolves into a more mature and epic sound.
This Open to Close Set, which will be held at UNDERCITY, is the moment when his career, album narrative, and Vivrant's philosophy are connected as one. This night will remain a special experience that will be remembered for a long time for fans who have grown up with his music.

title: Kenny Baron Trio concert in Korea
venue: Yonsei University Centennial Memorial Hall Concert Hall
description:
[Performance introduction]

Jazz pianist Kenny Barron is a master of modern jazz piano who has achieved lyricism, swing, and a sophisticated sense of harmony in perfect balance. He established his musical presence early on through collaboration with the greats at the center of jazz history, such as Dizzy Gillespie, Stan Getz, and Freddie Hubbard, and over the following decades, he has steadily developed his own musical world in a wide range of formats, from trios, solos, and large formations. His performances are always based on understated lyricism and deep swing, conveying the intellectual yet warm charm of jazz.

This performance has special meaning in that it is the first Korean performance of Kenny Barron's trio with bassist Alexis Cuadrado and drummer Jonathan Blake. In particular, April 30th, when the performance will be held, is Jazz Day designated by UNESCO, and will be a special stage to commemorate this special day with the 83-year-old living jazz legend.

Alexis Cuadrado is a Barcelona-born, New York-based bassist who combines the passion of flamenco with the intelligence of modern jazz. Based on her solid classical technique, she collaborated with world-renowned masters such as Angelique Kidjo and Mark Turner. Additionally, as a composer and leader, he will use epic and sophisticated performances, adding depth and dynamism to Kenny Barron's elegant pianism.

On drums is Jonathan Blake, one of the leading players in the modern jazz scene. Jonathan Blake is a drummer with both a traditional swing sense and a modern rhythm interpretation, and has been highly praised for his dynamic yet detailed playing. His drumming goes beyond simple rhythm accompaniment and plays the role of an active conversation between the piano and bass, raising the tension and energy of the entire trio.

The Kenny Barron Trio created by these three is based on the format of a classic piano trio, but will deliver a modern sound that naturally blends the individuality and experience of each player. Elaborately built harmonies, interplay that takes advantage of the blank space, and improvisation that does not miss the inspiration of the moment clearly reveal the most essential charm of trio jazz. In particular, Kenny Barron's musical insight accumulated over a long period of time on stage will shine even more deeply in close collaboration with the two performers.

This performance by the Kenny Barron Trio, held in commemoration of Jazz Day, will be more than a simple performance in Korea, but will be a valuable opportunity to directly see the highest level of perfection that a contemporary jazz trio can achieve. This stage, where you can simultaneously experience the intellectual depth and human warmth of jazz, and the vivid breathing that can only be felt on a live stage, is expected to be a special moment that will be remembered for a long time by domestic jazz fans.

Alexis Cuadrado is a Barcelona-born, New York-based bassist who combines the passion of flamenco with the intelligence of modern jazz. Based on her solid classical technique, she collaborated with world-renowned masters such as Angelique Kidjo and Mark Turner. Additionally, as a composer and leader, he will use epic and sophisticated performances, adding depth and dynamism to Kenny Barron's elegant pianism.

On drums is Jonathan Blake, one of the leading players in the modern jazz scene. Jonathan Blake is a drummer with both a traditional swing sense and a modern rhythm interpretation, and has been highly praised for his dynamic yet detailed playing. His drumming goes beyond simple rhythm accompaniment and plays the role of an active conversation between the piano and bass, raising the tension and energy of the entire trio.

The Kenny Barron Trio created by these three is based on the format of a classic piano trio, but will deliver a modern sound that naturally blends the individuality and experience of each player. Elaborately built harmonies, interplay that takes advantage of the blank space, and improvisation that does not miss the inspiration of the moment clearly reveal the most essential charm of trio jazz. In particular, Kenny Barron's musical insight accumulated over a long period of time on stage will shine even more deeply in close collaboration with the two performers.

This performance by the Kenny Barron Trio, held in commemoration of Jazz Day, will be more than a simple performance in Korea, but will be a valuable opportunity to directly see the highest level of perfection that a contemporary jazz trio can achieve. This stage, where you can simultaneously experience the intellectual depth and human warmth of jazz, and the vivid breathing that can only be felt on a live stage, is expected to be a special moment that will be remembered for a long time by domestic jazz fans.

[Performance introduction]

The best gift to give your child! ‘Happy Day’ with the musical <Al Candy>

On May 5th, Children's Day, the Gongju Literary Center is transformed into a huge dream playground for children.
The Arts Center's Children's Day special project, which started in 2025, welcomes family audiences with even more upgraded fun and emotion this year.
The stage of the main concert hall will feature the family musical “Al Candy,” based on the bestseller by writer Baek Hee-na, loved all over the world. Eat the mysterious candy and make up your mind
Through the story of Dongdong, who heard the sound, the clumsy but sincere love and courage of a family is conveyed, and a touching warmth is felt for both the child and the parents.
It is planned to be presented. The excitement continues off stage as well. Before and after the performance, a variety of side events, <Happy Day>, are held in the lobby and outdoors.
A cute ‘small theater’, exciting ‘outdoor performance’ and an eye-catching ‘magic performance’ add excitement to the festival. Also, ‘Mister Long Legs’ who will welcome children.
There is plenty of experiential events so you will never be bored. We hope that it will become the best children's day outing spot where the whole family can laugh, have fun, and make precious memories.


[Introduction to the work]

A warm story of comfort and growth told by 'Magic Candy', a voice that hears the heart's voice.
Based on the picture book <Al Candy> by world-renowned writer Baek Hee-na, the story has a solid story and beautiful music.
Various stage effects are added to embody the emotion of the picture book.
Since its premiere in 2019, it has ranked first in sales (children's and family categories) for three consecutive years.
It is a luxury family musical that has captured the hearts of not only children but also their parents.

Whose voice will be heard next?

title: Matinee Concert Ⅱ. Writer Kim Young-ha’s reason for traveling, and music
venue: Gangdong Arts Center Grand Theater Han River
description:
[Performance introduction]
Reason for music, reason for travel
Europe walked through the eyes of a novelist and remembered through the melody of music

Why do we go on a trip?
Best-selling author and storyteller of our time, Kim Young-ha, will become the host of the 2026 Matinee series and invite audiences to a romantic city in Europe.
This series is a high-quality lecture concert that combines classical music with the unfamiliar landscapes and people that the author encountered while traveling to Italy, Germany, France, and Spain, and the humanistic insights he gained there.
The brilliant sunlight, lonely contemplation, and artistic inspiration felt while traveling are vividly brought to the stage.
In a leisurely time in the morning, <Music by Kim Young-ha>, which combines author Kim Young-ha's charming conversation with a performance full of local flavor, will be a special break that will remind you of the 'reason for travel' for those who are tired of repetitive daily life.

<Germany> Deep in the forest, alone in contemplation
Germany is a great country to think about. It talks about the value of solitude found in dense forests and well-organized cities. Listen to German instrumental music that is logical yet deeply emotional and lyrical songs that touch your heart. Like walking along a forest path in fresh May, it will be a time to sort out your complicated thoughts and provide calm comfort.

description:
[Performance introduction]
Kim Seon-wook, who has had a special relationship with the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra as a soloist and debuted on the regular performance stage as a conductor in December 2022, meets the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra once again. After announcing the start of the performance with Modest Mussorgsky’s ‘One Night on a Bare Mountain’, which leaves an impressive atmosphere with its gritty music, the piece that appears is Maurice Ravel’s Piano Concerto in G major. Alice Sarah Ott, who made her name known as a child prodigy in Germany early on and has firmly established herself on the international stage with her popular moves, participates as the soloist in this concerto, which is bright at every moment. Conductor Kim Seon-wook, who decorated the second part with the work of Richard Strauss in the October 2023 performance with the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra, prepared this time for Johannes Brahms' Symphony No. 2. We look forward to seeing the Brahms that musician Kim Seon-wook will present with the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra, who has been evaluated as an outstanding Brahms player throughout his career as a pianist and has shown special affection for the composer even after beginning his full-time career as a conductor.

title: Monaco Monte Carlo Ballet, Swan Lake
description:
[Performance introduction]
A black-and-white thriller that strips away fairytale fantasy.

The Monaco Monte Carlo Ballet, which has captivated dance fans around the world by exquisitely combining the elegance of classical ballet and the unconventionality of modern dance, will captivate Korean audiences with Jean-Christophe Maillot's masterpiece [Swan Lake]. Maillot removed the fairytale fantasy of the original work and transformed ‘The Swan’ into a detailed psychological drama that delve into the inner self of humans by expressing the contrast between black and white, good and evil, purity and desire with sophisticated mise-en-scène. The newly composed music based on Tchaikovsky's original score will be performed live by the Korea Coop Orchestra, further enriching the tension and emotions of the work.

Jo Hye-ryeon
venue: Gongju Literary Center Grand Performance Hall
description:
[Performance introduction]

Broadcaster Jo Hye-ryun's first directing and starring role!
In the 1980s, a tough mother... This is the story of our mother!
 
Broadcaster Cho Hye-ryun directed and starred in the play “My Lovely Mother,” which garnered attention in the 1980s, when she lost her husband and struggled to get out of the market.
This is the story of 'Ok-hee', who sold fish and lived with only her son in mind.
It depicts the process of 'Cheoldong', a childish son who took his mother's endless sacrifice for granted, and belatedly realizes his mother's love.
The stage is filled with cheerful laughter and heartbreaking emotions that remind us of our mothers back in the day.
May, Family Month, will be a warm time for the whole family to laugh and cry together while reflecting on the love of parents they have forgotten.


[Synopsis]
 
“Oiso boiso Saiso~~”
 
A mother who sold fish alone without a husband and lived a strong life as a mother rather than a woman.
To such a mother, the son is always blunt and immature.
 
...One day, my mother was diagnosed with cancer.
 
“Mom”
 
“Wow”
 
“I’m sick… I feel like I’m going to die.”
 
“It doesn’t hit the line… It will take a little while.”
 
“Is it real?”
 
“Mom”
 
“Wow”
 
“Can I do it on my own?”
 
“Well.. whose son is this.. Mom doesn’t have to worry at all. He can do well.”
 
"......."
 
“Cheoldong... Mom, let’s go...”

title: Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra Markus Stenz and Vadim Gluzmann ①
description:
[PROGRAM]

Brahms, Violin Concerto
Brahms, Violin Concerto in D major, Op. 77

Walton, Symphony No. 1 
Walton, Symphony No. 1 in B-flat minor 

* Program and performer may change.

There are only two pieces on stage, but it couldn't be more revealing. Markus Stenz, who has been with the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra as the orchestra's chief guest conductor from 2017 to 2021, returns for the first time in a long time with major works. Part 1 is Johannes Brahms' violin concerto. Although Brahms began composing under the influence of Bruch's Violin Concerto No. 1, which swept through the times, he completed a work that was fully imbued with his unique symphonic spirit. Violinist Vadim Gluzman, who has already performed in Korea several times and met with the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra in 2019, will be the soloist of this work. William Walton's Symphony No. 1, which follows, is a work that demonstrates the power of symphony experienced in the previous Brahms work. The work, which reflects the influence of Sibelius, who first explored what a symphony can do in the 20th century, pays homage to the traditions of classical music in many places, including the contrapuntal movement seen in the last movement.

title: Sancho and Don Quixote
description:
[Performance introduction]

A living book, Don Quixote unfolding through a puppet show
The puppet show “Sancho and Don Quixote” was recreated so that even children who cannot read books can experience the message of the book “Don Quixote” in an easy and fun way.
The story begins with Sancho, a 9-year-old child, opening a ‘book’ that leads him into a world of adventure. The production using various types of puppets and pop-up books, such as joints, boards, and shadows, depicts Don Quixote's absurd adventures on stage more convincingly. The actors' humorous performances and music, including medieval dances, add romance to artistic imagination.


[Plot]

The story of Sancho going on an adventure with Don Quixote
A different adventure awaits you every time you open a book in a strange and mysterious old bookstore.
The adventure in the book waiting for you today is the story of the knight Don Quixote. An ordinary child who enters the bookstore is called ‘Sancho’ and is led by Don Quixote on a journey to become an honorable knight. As Sancho sets out on the road with Don Quixote, unimaginable events occur every time, such as a windmill giant and a black-maned lion appearing in front of Sancho... . At this time, a large dragon appeared before our eyes! What will happen to Sancho and Don Quixote in the face of a dragon that they cannot slay or avoid?

title: This is (not) conceptual art.
venue: Seoul | National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Seoul
description: «This is (not) conceptual art» is an exhibition that highlights conceptual art that focuses on concepts, language, process, and context rather than material form or visual completion in the flow of Korean contemporary art. In particular, this exhibition focuses on the linguistic turn in art and revisits works that have constantly reflected on the essence and reality of art through subtopics such as objects and language, language and behavior, measurement and guidance, and reality and institutional criticism. In addition, we hope to provide an opportunity to discuss the contemporaneity of Korean contemporary art by examining the conceptual trends of post-war art in the 1990s, which developed amidst advanced capitalism and rapid social and political changes, along with the trends of previous generations of art. description:
[Synopsis]

Park Dae-chul had no money throughout his life and died in poverty.

When the memorial service in his honor began, Park Dae-chul couldn't bear the injustice and came back to life.

In my last life, I lived and died in poverty with only loans, but in this life, I will definitely live and die as a rich person.

Park Dae-chul and the villagers come back to life, but honest people are always poor.

Bad people are angry at being rich and summon the money god.

At this time, the god of poverty tries to dissuade Park Dae-chul and the villagers, saying that money is bad.

However, Park Dae-chul and the village people do not agree and defeat the god of poverty and summon the god of money.

But a blind man dressed as a beggar appears in front of them...

title: Danny Goo Debut 10th Anniversary Recital [Princess]
venue: Gongju Literary Center Grand Performance Hall
description:
[Performance introduction]

A one-time performance to celebrate our 10th anniversary in Korea!
 
Violinist Danny Goo is loved by the entire nation for his 'positive energy' on MBC's <I Live Alone>!
He, who has been the 'busiest classical star' since his debut on the Korean stage in 2016, will hold a recital to commemorate his 10th anniversary in Korea in 2026.
This performance is a meaningful stage that looks back on the journey of the past 10 years and announces the beginning of a new ‘journey’ moving forward.
The stage opened splendidly with his favorite song, Corelli's 'La Folia', and a modern reinterpretation of the masterpiece of classical master 'Bach'.
And ‘Claude Bowling’s’ exciting suite with jazz piano trio and ‘Gershwin’s’ captivating melody!
We want to share with the audience the musical footsteps of the past 10 years and the new beginnings of the future.


[Program]

A. Corelli – La Folia
Corelli ‘La Folia’
 
J. S. Bach – Goldberg Variations
Bach Goldberg Variations (arranged version)
 
C. Bolling – Suite for Violin and Jazz Piano Trio
Claude Bolling Suite for Violin and Jazz Piano Trio
 
G. Gershwin – Gershwin Suite
Gershwin Gershwin Suite (arranged version)

title: Sancho and Don Quixote [Princess]
venue: Gongju Literary Center Grand Performance Hall
description:
[Performance introduction]

A living book, Don Quixote unfolding through a puppet show
 
The puppet show <Sancho and Don Quixote> is the story of Sancho going on an adventure with Don Quixote. This work was recreated with Sancho as a child as the main character.
Although it is different from the original novel, it still contains the message of the original, 'Tomorrow's Don Quixote is Sancho.' The puppet show <Sancho and Don Quixote> cannot read the book yet.
It was created so that even children could see it as if it were a living book.
 
A strange and mysterious old bookstore. A different adventure awaits you every time you open a book. The adventure in the book waiting for you today is the story of the knight Don Quixote.
An ordinary child who enters the bookstore is called 'Sancho' and is led by Don Quixote to set out on a journey to become an honorable knight.
Unimaginable events occur, such as fighting a windmill giant and a black-maned lion...
 
At this time, a large dragon appeared before my eyes!
What will happen to Sancho and Don Quixote when they encounter a dragon that they cannot avoid or slay?


[Synopsis]
 
Take the lead, Sancho, take out your trumpet and blow! Let's go, it's an adventure!
Now, my friend Sancho, tell me where to find the lion!
 
A different adventure awaits you every time you open a book in a strange and mysterious old bookstore.
 
The adventure in the book waiting for you today is the story of the knight Don Quixote.
 
An ordinary child who enters a bookstore is called ‘Sancho’.
Led by Don Quixote, he sets out on a journey to become an honorable knight.
 
Unimaginable events occur, such as fighting a windmill giant and a black-maned lion...
At this time, a large dragon appeared before our eyes!
 
What will happen to Sancho and Don Quixote when they encounter a dragon that they cannot escape or defeat?

description: To celebrate the 40th anniversary of the opening of the Gwacheon Museum, we are promoting a series of site-specific installation projects with the theme of ‘light’ to brighten the museum and allow visitors to experience deeper artistic immersion both inside and outside the museum. In addition to the new collection, James Turrell's “Imaginations, Wide Rectangular Curved Surface,” the museum collaborates with contemporary artists, architects, and designers at home and abroad, including Jeong-ah Koo, A-young Kim, Philippe Parreno, and Ivan Navarro, to install their works in major spaces inside and outside the museum, reinterpreting the space based on the sense of place of the Gwacheon building. Through this, we would like to propose a new sensory experience using light as a medium. In particular, taking advantage of the unique characteristics of the Gwacheon Museum as an art museum within nature, we plan to implement a space program inside and outside the museum in which art, nature, and thinking organically connect. title: Ballet with commentary, Swan Lake [Princess]
venue: Gongju Literary Center Grand Performance Hall
description:
[Performance introduction]

A friendly ballet <Swan Lake> that can be enjoyed with the ears and eyes.
 
<Swan Lake> presented by Seoul City Ballet breaks the prejudice that ballet is difficult by providing friendly commentary on the beautiful movements of the dancers.
It is a ‘tailored to eye level’ performance designed so that anyone, regardless of gender or age, can enjoy it easily and with fun. The story goes that Prince Siegfried is a wizard at a lake in the forest.
It begins with him meeting Princess Odette, the Swan Queen under Rothwald's curse, and swearing fateful love. The wizard brought out the black swan Odile and brought the two together.
It depicts a beautiful ending in which people try to separate each other, but ultimately overcome trials and regain happiness through the power of true love. Trying to understand the mime or the plot
If you follow the exciting story told by the narrator without any need, you will soon become immersed in the work. For children who are new to ballet
It will become a living fairy tale book and the best introductory performance for adult audiences to easily enjoy the depth of the classics.


[Synopsis]
 
Prologue Prince's Coming of Age Ceremony
Prince Siegfried, who had a grand coming-of-age ceremony and received a bow as a gift, saw a swan flying away.
I go hunting by the lakeside with my friends.
 
Act 1 Lakeside view
Prince Siegfried, who came to the forest chasing swans, is attacked by wolves and Rodwald at the lakeside, but overcomes them with the help of the swans.
He discovers Princess Odette, who transforms into human form, falls in love with her at first sight, and proposes to her. For the princess to be freed from the devil's spell
After hearing that he must receive the eternal love of one person, Prince Siegfried promises to swear an oath of love.
 
Act 2 Palace Ballroom
Prince Siegfried welcomes the guests while waiting for Princess Odette to arrive. Friends and ladybugs are enjoying a party together
The demon Rodwald appears with his daughter Odile, who resembles Princess Odette. Odile, brought by the devil Rodwald, becomes Princess Odette.
Prince Siegfried, deluded, announces his marriage to her and promises eternal love at Rodwald's request. At this time, his true colors were revealed.
The demon Rodwald and Odile disappear and Prince Siegfried runs into the forest in sorrow.
 
Act 3 Eternal Love
Princess Odette is forced to live as a swan forever due to Prince Siegfried's betrayal. Prince Siegfried and Odette run to receive forgiveness
Although the princesses mourn each other's fate, they defeat the demon Rodwald with the power of love and promise eternal love.

title: Daewon Lee
venue: Seoul | National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Deoksugung Hall
description: Lee Dae-won (1921-2005) is a representative artist of Korean modern and contemporary art, along with Kim Hwan-ki, Park Soo-geun, Jang Wook-jin, and Cheon Kyeong-ja. In his teens, he was already selected for the Joseon Art Exhibition three times in a row, and he held a total of 19 solo exhibitions, starting with his first at the age of 36. However, research and exhibitions that examined Lee Dae-won's world of work from an art historical perspective were insufficient. Although he was widely known as a landscape painter who mainly painted ‘orchards,’ his early painting occupies a very unique position in the Korean art world at the time. After liberation, he had a significant impact on the Korean art world as a whole, including the formation of Korean aesthetic theory, operation of the Bando Gallery, and serving as president of Hongik University. This exhibition sheds new light on Lee Dae-won's life and art in three dimensions by examining the background and historical context of his work and closely depicting the process leading up to the orchard painting, a typical example of Lee Dae-won's work. title: National Gugak Center Orchestra, Festival [Gongju]
venue: Gongju Literary Center Grand Performance Hall
description:
[Performance introduction]
When the rhythm sounds, the stage becomes a festival.
 
The orchestral music <Festival> presented by the National Gugak Center's Creative Orchestra breaks down the boundaries of Korean traditional orchestral music by reinterpreting the deep breath of tradition with a modern sense.
This is a stage where the essence of our dynamic music is displayed. In the sound of magnificent orchestral music, the delicate melodies of the daegeum, piri, and haegeum come to life and broadcast. 
From the familiar 'Frontier' of both dialects to the deep resonance of calligraphy sound, the splendid technique of the mysterious Saenghwang, and the rain rose of 'Beompi Jungryu' from Simcheongga.
In addition, it dramatically depicts the process in which Han's emotions soar powerfully into the energy of excitement. The wave-like sound created by the overlap of different breaths
The essence of Korean music is clearly revealed, and in particular, 'Pannoreum', a combination of samulnori and orchestral music at the peak of the performance, creates an overwhelming performance that unites the stage and the audience.
It will provide excitement. By adding popular trends and colorful compositions to boldly break the stereotype that “tradition is boring,” even audiences unfamiliar with Korean traditional music can enjoy it.
It will be a thrilling festival scene where you will be captivated by the dynamic energy and enjoy the excitement of our sori music with your whole body.

[Program]
Orchestral Frontier (Composition/Yang Bang-eon)
 
Calligraphy Concerto ‘Poetry of Wind, Trees and Earth’ for calligraphy sound and orchestra
 
Saenghwang Concerto Fantastic (Composer/Lee Jeong-ho)
 
Pansori Concerto Beompi Jungryu (Arrangement/Lee Yong-tak)
 
Pangut and orchestral pannoreum (composed by Lee Jun-ho)

title: Pagagnini’s performance in Korea [Princess]
venue: Gongju Literary Center Grand Performance Hall
description:
[Performance introduction]

Who said classics are boring? Beyond imagination! A comical string quartet that makes you laugh so hard!
 
The string quartet 'Pagagnini', produced by YLLANA Production, a Spanish production company specializing in performance, is a unique comical performance that breaks the mold of classical concerts, which are usually serious and solemn.
It captivates the audience with witty humor and a beautiful musical medley that stimulates emotions. In particular, it tells the story of genius musician Paganini's complex composition methods, reckless personality, and musical interpretation.
reflected in This performance is a new genre called 'classical contemporary music' presented by four outstanding performers with elegant performance skills, and will attract not only the general audience but also the general audience.
It also received praise from demanding audiences who were knowledgeable about music. It can be enjoyed by audiences from all over the world, regardless of age or nationality, and was held at the 2008 Edinburgh Fringe Festival in the UK.
Its quality was recognized by winning awards at numerous international festivals, including the 'Best Picture Award'. It was invited as the opening production of the Busan International Theater Festival and was sold out.
In 2026, we will use even more upgraded humor and irony to allow audiences to interact with the stage through laughter.


[Program]

title: Lecture Concert III. Latin classical music [Princess]
venue: Gongju Arts Center Small Performance Hall
description:
[Performance introduction]

Time to expand from listening to understanding
 
Lecture concerts are lecture-type concerts that explore various musical genres, from baroque and romantic classics to opera, musicals, Latin classical (tango), and jazz, through expert commentary and demonstrations.
The genre's birth, background, history, and composer's representative songs are explained in an easy and fun way, and it is composed mainly of popular songs so that everyone from beginners to lovers of each genre can enjoy it. 
Provides a three-dimensional experience. Four independent performances are connected organically, helping audiences understand the wide world of music as if traveling naturally, and allowing audiences to enjoy music in their daily lives.
This is a performance designed to make you feel closer. We want to present a special morning to the audience through coffee and cookies provided before the performance, as well as fun and interesting commentary and performances.


[Program]

<The Beginning of Solitude and Passion>
It explains the musical journey of Piazzolla, who attempted to combine traditional tango and classical music, and talks about the charm of the bandoneon, which is said to be the heart of tango.
Oblivion
Adios Nonino
Libertango
 
<History and evolution of tango> 
We introduce the origins of tango, which began in the slums of Argentina in the early 20th century, and its development into a global music through its golden age.
Histoire of Tango
History of Piazzolla Tango
I. Bordel 1900 (tavern of 1900)
II. Café 1930 (Café of 1930)
III. Night-club 1960 
IV. Concert d'Aujourd'hui (Concert of the Day)
 
<The golden age of Piazzolla and Nuevo Tango>
‘Invierno Porteño’ from Buenos Aires Four Seasons 
‘Winter’ among the four seasons of Bueno Aires

description: This is a large-scale solo exhibition by Korea's leading installation artist Do-ho Suh, encompassing his artistic world from early works to major works to ongoing projects, and illuminating the artist's conceptual foundation and practical expansion in a three-dimensional way. The author has been deepening the issues of spatial memory and identity, focusing on the themes of migration and residence, individuals and communities, and is further expanding the scope of his creativity based on multidisciplinary research. A voice that becomes a poem meets an orchestra.
 
The 'Special Concert' with La Poem and the Gongju City Chungnam Symphony Orchestra is a special stage that encompasses various genres such as pop, pop, and musicals.
La Poem, the world's first crossover group to include a traditional countertenor, presents a poetry-like stage to the audience with resonance and emotional expression based on vocal music.

title: Gongju, Andong Sister City Exchange Concert: Ode to Joy [Gongju]
venue: Gongju Literary Center Grand Performance Hall
description:
[Performance introduction]

The ancient princess of Baekje and Andong, the capital of spiritual culture,
An overwhelming and touching moment that transcends time and becomes one through art.
 
Beyond suffering to joy!
A message of hope from two sister cities! At the threshold of winter, a special performance will be held that will fill the stage with a magnificent sound.
This concert, organized to commemorate the sisterhood relationship between Gongju City and Andong City and to strengthen the friendship between the two cities, is the first concert in the history of classical music.
Beethoven's last symphony, 'The 9th Symphony', which is considered one of his greatest masterpieces, will be presented.
Beethoven's spirit of singing about humanity and hope even in desperate situations is harmonized with the meeting of two cities with a long history.
It conveys a deeper meaning. The elaborate and powerful performance of the Gongju City Chungnam Symphony Orchestra, which represents Gongju, and the Gongju City Choir and
The delicate and rich harmony of the Andong City Choir is expected to create explosive synergy.
The moment the 4th movement ‘Ode to Joy’ rings out, the stage and audience will feel a thrill of excitement as they become one!
The melody of peace and harmony will resonate deeply in your heart.

title: The Art of Reading: From Paper to Pixels
venue: Seoul | National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Seoul
description: This exhibition traces the history of graphic design since the introduction of horizontal Hangul writing in the printing and publishing field in the 1970s. The activities of designers who have studied the relationship between text and images in an environment transitioning from analog to digital will be reconstructed by era. The exhibition presents experimental attempts that cross the material and non-material world through the revival of phototypesetting and offset printing technology in the 1970s and 1980s, the transition to graphic tools and the web environment in the 1980s and 1990s, and today. This exhibition is an attempt to expand the base of Korean art by examining the dynamic relationship between technological development and visual culture within the flow of graphic design practice. title: stranger in paris
venue: Seoul | National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Deoksugung Hall
description: After the Korean War, many Korean artists who considered Paris the ‘capital of modern art’ moved to France. In the Paris art world, which competed with New York for the center of international art after World War II and sought to revive the glory of modernism, they interacted with artists from all over the world, experienced a variety of new contemporary art, and built their own world. This exhibition illuminates in three dimensions the art world of Korean artists who moved to Paris in the 1950s and 1970s, starting with Lee Jong-woo, who became the first Korean artist to move to Paris in 1925. The exhibition explores the diverse art world of Taoist and Buddhist artists who pursued modernization by seeking national identity in unfamiliar places, or expanded the boundaries of art through exploration of new themes and experimentation with media, and examines the meaning and value of their lives and art as strangers. 93 Museum Family Art Museum
description: 93 Museum 93 Museum, which plans and displays works by leading domestic artists, started as Gallery Focus in Cheongdam-dong, Seoul in 1990. In 2004, the People Art Museum 93 opened in Paju Heyri Art Village by compiling art pieces and various historical materials related to people, and the gallery was moved to the museum annex, where exhibitions of works by leading domestic artists are being planned and displayed. Gallery Focus in Cheongdam-dong, Seoul, exhibited contemporary art works by Korea's older and younger artists, as well as ancient works of art such as ancient paintings and ceramics, and consistently discovered and introduced works by leading Vietnamese artists. In 2007, the Seoul branch of Gallery Focus, operated in conjunction with Paju Heyri Gallery Focus, was opened in Samseong-dong and is exhibiting works by leading Korean masters, as well as works by emerging and promising artists and works by leading Vietnamese artists. 93 Museum, Gallery Focus, and Gallery Focus are demonstrating the qualities of professional art dealers by taking advantage of each other's characteristics and complementing each other.

title: AK& Giheung
description: AK & Giheung is a complex shopping mall with an area of ​​approximately 18,400 pyeong, from the 1st basement level to the 6th floor above ground. It is directly connected to exits 3, 4, and 9 of Giheung Station, where the Suin-Bundang Line and Yongin Light Rail pass, making it highly accessible. Lotte Premium Food Market is located on the first basement floor, and lifestyle brands such as fashion, beauty, and F&B and experiential content are located on each floor on the upper floors. It is characterized by strengthening kids and family stores and convenience facilities to reflect the regional characteristics of a high proportion of young couples and families living there.

title: AK Plaza Gwangmyeong
description: AK Plaza Gwangmyeong Branch is a complex shopping mall located near Gwangmyeong Station in Gwangmyeong-si, Gyeonggi-do, where you can enjoy shopping, dining, and culture all in one place. The ‘Urban Grove’ concept emphasizes the harmony between nature and the city, and Korea’s largest kinetic art installation adds visual fun. It is suitable for families as it has a variety of brands including fashion, living, food and beverages. The open playground on the 3rd floor is equipped with various facilities and programs and can be used for free, making it a great place to visit with children.

title: AK Plaza Geumjeong
description: AK Plaza Geumjeong Branch is a shopping complex that combines fashion, beauty, lifestyle, and F&B. Golf, sports, and children's stores are located on the first basement floor, and cosmetics, lifestyle brands, and Megabox are located on the first floor. The Geumjeong branch's landmark, a large hand heart bearbrick sculpture, is installed on the second floor, making it a must-see photo spot for visitors. You can also take a leisurely break at the rooftop garden and cafe.

title: AK Plaza Suwon
description: AK Plaza Suwon, located at Suwon Station, is Suwon's representative cultural complex where shopping, culture, and entertainment coexist. It is connected to Subway Line 1, the Suin Bundang Line, and the Bus Transfer Center, so it can be conveniently visited from anywhere in the country. Featuring a variety of cultural and character content, including popular fashion and beauty brands, Megabox Movie Theater, Gundam Base, and Acorn Forest, as well as large-scale dining stores such as Ashley Queens, Outback Steak House, and Cymbidium, it is loved as Suwon's representative cultural attraction where you can stay and enjoy all day with family, friends, and lovers.

title: Gariwangsan Cable Car
description: Gariwangsan Cable Car is located on Gariwangsan Mountain, which is one of the top 100 famous mountains in Korea and successfully hosted the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics. Gariwang Mountain has been renovated so that many citizens can enjoy it even after the Olympics are over. At the top of the cable car, various convenience facilities of 512.5㎡ are installed, including a 2,400㎡ ecological exploration deck road, an unmanned agricultural product store (gift shop), a VR experience center, a DID video theater, a customer rest area, a cafe 156 days, and a moonlight photo zone. People of all ages and the disabled and those with mobility issues can easily access it without any inconvenience. The cable car may close early or close without prior notice for safety reasons such as weather conditions, so it is best to check in advance before visiting.
operatingHours: 10:00~18:00 (Ticket closing 17:50) ※ Boarding deadline: Sookam Station (boarding area) 16:00 ※ Operating hours may change depending on weather and local circumstances, so please check in advance

title: Gawon Art Museum
description: Gawon Art Museum, located at the foot of Cheonggyesan Mountain, is affiliated with the Korea Watercolor Association and is an art museum specializing in watercolor painting. Opened in 2003, this museum was built as a two-story building in European style. On the first basement floor, there is the Gawon Academy and Atelier, where watercolor and oil painting classes are held. The first floor is the first exhibition room and a lounge, and the second floor is the second exhibition room, the third exhibition room, and the curator's room. There is a cafe inside the museum, and if you order a drink, you can receive a 50% discount on admission. Gawon Art Museum is also famous for its beautiful garden, as its name Gawon (佳苑, beautiful garden) suggests. Gawon Art Museum is also frequently used as a filming location for dramas, and dramas such as The Fugitive, War of the Roses, Tale of the New Gisaeng, Wild Romance, and Secret were filmed here.

title: Gail Art Museum
description: If you drive along the beautiful road along the Bukhangang River, you will find Gail Art Museum about halfway from Yangsu-ri to Cheongpyeong Lake. Kang Geon-guk, director of Gail Art Museum, the first private art museum in Gapyeong-gun, has been working as an architect and interior designer for 30 years. He opened in 2003 and has been holding regular concerts once a month at the exhibition hall or art hall as of 2020. He is planning concerts with a variety of genres, including popular music, jazz, and classical music. In addition, starting from the idea that music, along with art, is the best character education for children, we continue to hold art experience classes, especially for children in Gapyeong, a culturally underprivileged area. Gail Art Museum's exhibitions are planned as family-oriented exhibitions to differentiate themselves from large art museums. The Gail Art Museum, which means that every day of the museum's visitors will be a "beautiful day," is a complex cultural space equipped with a variety of facilities, including an art hall where domestic and foreign art works are exhibited and various performances such as chamber music and jazz are held, and an outdoor performance hall where the public can directly participate in customized concerts.
price: Adults 3,000 won / Children 2,500 won ※ Admission fees may be charged separately for special exhibitions in some cases, so please check the exhibition schedule (Exhibition Guide - Special Exhibitions)

title: Gapyeong Culture and Arts Center
description: Gapyeong Culture and Arts Center is the only theater in Gapyeong-gun and strives to satisfy the cultural needs of local residents. It was completed in 1998 with a total area of ​​4,801 m2, from the 3rd floor underground to the 2nd floor above ground. The main facilities include a large performance hall, multipurpose exhibition hall, outdoor performance hall, projection room, practice room, management office, and electrical and mechanical room. The main performance hall can accommodate 641 seats, and the outdoor performance hall can accommodate 250 people at the same time. You must arrive at the performance hall 20 minutes in advance and enter the audience 10 minutes in advance. Taking photos without prior agreement is prohibited, so be careful when viewing. The remodeling project will be promoted by the end of 2024 as the results of a precise safety diagnosis of the building and stage machinery require repairs. In particular, Gapyeong-gun plans to quickly renovate the Arts Center in preparation for it being used as a bodybuilding competition venue when Gapyeong hosts the 2025 Gyeonggi-do Sports Festival and the 2026 Gyeonggi-do Sports Festival.

title: Gapyeong Cultural Center
description: The Gapyeong Cultural Center was established to discover and foster traditional culture with residents and to promote preservation of tradition by providing cultural and artistic opportunities. Through this, it is a place where awareness of local culture is renewed and our unique culture is continuously inherited and developed. The Cultural Center not only supports cultural and arts education projects, but also supports cultural activities for multicultural families and supports projects entrusted by the national or local governments to revitalize local culture. The program implemented here incorporates the meaning of lifelong education, utilizes the leisure time of the residents, and seeks to provide an opportunity to lead a high-quality life by developing potential talents and infusing vitality into daily life through enriching hobbies. We are also contributing to promoting Gapyeong and our culture through various cultural events in the Gapyeong area. It is a place that aims for a life that is warm with culture and bright with art.

title: Gapyeong Begonia Bird Garden
description: In the clean air and nature of Gapyeong, Gyeonggi-do, the Begonia Bird Garden is a complex cultural experience space with indoor and outdoor gardens of approximately 20,000 m2, rare birds, interactive experiences, and flowers in all four seasons. The greenhouse where rare birds and flowers come together has a flower zone, an infinity zone, and a bird zone. Here, there is a begonia hill with beautiful colorful begonia flowers in full bloom, a media room, a space of infinite mirrors through the media facade, and a feast of flowers, the mirror room, the best photo zone where wisteria and hydrangeas welcome you with splendor. In the Bird Zone, you can see rare birds gliding freely, and you can also experience feeding parrots. In addition to the indoor greenhouse, there are three themed outdoor gardens: the front garden where you can see the charm of flowering plants in different seasons, the mystery garden where you can get acquainted with alpacas and Boer goats, and the water garden.

title: Ganwolam (Seosan)
description: Ganwolam is a small hermitage located in Ganwol-dori, Buseok-myeon. It is said to have been founded by Master Muhak in the early Joseon Dynasty and rebuilt by Master Song Man-gong. Unlike other hermitages, it is a mystical hermitage that is connected to the land at low tide and becomes an island at high tide. It feels like a hermitage floating on the water at high tide. The combination of the surrounding natural scenery and the ancient temple where you can feel the breath of our ancestors is attracting a number of tourists. In addition, the Gulburugigunwangje, which prays for a good harvest of oysters produced in Ganwol Island, stands in front of the Eori Oyster Monument at Ganwol-dori every year at high tide on the first full moon day. This event is held in front of the Eori Oyster Monument, where clean women who have not committed any unclean behavior wear white clothes and dance at the entrance of the village. When they arrive in front of the oyster tower, they set up offerings and offer oysters collected during the oyster bountiful prayer ceremony for tourists to taste.

title: Cutlassfish Reservoir
description: Cutlassfish Reservoir is an agricultural reservoir located in Sokdal-dong, Gunpo-si, Gyeonggi-do, and was created in 1984. The area is about 493,000㎡, the water depth is about 8m, and it is located near Beombagol, the valley of Surisan Mountain. There were a lot of reeds in the field around this area, so it was called ‘Galti’ or ‘Galchi’, and the name continued to be the name of the reservoir. There is a rest area and physical fitness equipment at the entrance, and a well-maintained deck path along the reservoir makes it great for a quiet walk.

title: Gamaksan Suspension Bridge
description: Gamaksan Mountain is one of the five peaks of Gyeonggi Province, and is called a dark blue rock mountain because black and blue lights appear simultaneously between the rocks. The suspension bridge, located at the starting point of the Gamaksan Trail, is a bridge that connects the Seolmari Valley, which was cut off by a road. The Suspension Bridge is the nation's longest 150m pillarless mountain suspension bridge and was constructed to harmonize with nature. Ungye Falls, a cute valley with Seolmaceon Stream, is the pride of Gamaksan Mountain. The waterfall, which falls almost vertically, is also used for winter ice training. At the top stands the Gamak Mountain Monument, and just below Janggunbong is the Im Keok-jeong Cave, where Im Keok-jeong hid while avoiding the pursuit of the government forces. Gamaksan Mountain is close to the ceasefire line, so when you climb to the top, you can see the Imjin River and Songaksan Mountain in Gaeseong. The pine-scented hiking trail on the ridge and the refreshing earthy scent are also excellent, so many hikers visit.

title: Gangneung Gyeongpodae
description: Gangneung Gyeongpodae is one of Gangneung's representative scenic spots and is designated as National Cultural Heritage Treasure No. 2046. It is one of the Eight Scenic Views of Gwandong that shows the culture of the Goryeo Dynasty, and is a pavilion located on a hill north of Gyeongpo Lake. Since its founding in the 13th year of the reign of King Chungsuk of the Goryeo Dynasty, most detailed records of its restoration and several renovations remain. In particular, records from before its founding remain, making it a pavilion that allows one to see in detail the process of change by era. The name ‘Gyeongpo University’ on the electronic signboard is Yu Han-ji’s handwriting, and the Haeseo font signboard is on Lee Ik-hoi’s handwriting. Inside Gyeongpodae, there are numerous writings by famous people and poets, including ‘Yesterday Poem’ written by King Sukjong, ‘Gyeongpodaebu’ written by Yulgok Yi I at the age of 10, and Sangryangmun by Jo Ha-mang. Pine and oak trees grow thickly around the pavilion, creating an elegant landscape. Gyeongpo 8 Gyeonggi and Gyeongpo Wolsam are said to be the most spectacular of the world. Tourist attractions around Gyeongpodae include Gyeongpo Lake, with its old pine forest and cherry trees, and the coastal sandbar that separates Gyeongpo Lake from the East Sea forms Gyeongpo Beach.
priceDetail: Free

title: Gangneung Solhyang Arboretum
description: Gangneung Solhyang Arboretum began construction in 2008 in the area of ​​135 Gujeong-ri, Gujeong-myeon, Gangneung-si, and opened on October 30, 2013. The arboretum is located in Yongsogol, famous for its beautiful scenery in Gangneung, at the foot of Chilseongsan Mountain, where a primeval Geumgang pine forest is preserved. Yongsogol, where the arboretum is located, was named after a dragon that ascended to the sky since ancient times. It is an area where Geumgang pine trees, the representative tree species of Gangneung, have been well maintained under the theme of ‘a meeting place in a thousand-year forest.’ This place preserves the original appearance of a natural forest, making its beauty shine even more. The arboretum, built on a total of 78.5 ha (approximately 240,000 pyeong) of land, is comprised of 220,000 plants of a total of 1,127 species along with 23 various themed spaces. Starting with the sound of water, the scent of flowers, and the scent of pine trees from the entrance, you can enjoy the scenery that changes throughout the four seasons through various exhibition gardens such as the forest ecology observation path with a colony of ginger trees and bamboo trees, the thousand-year breath healing path filled with a thousand years of waiting, the pine forest square surrounded by Geumgang pine trees, and the Bibichu Garden, Daylily Garden, Medicinal Botanical Garden, and Dye Botanical Garden where various wild flowers bloom every season. Among them, the Thousand Year Breath Healing Path, where Geumgang Pine, a native tree species, stretches straight out, is the representative walking course of the arboretum and leaves a deep impression on visitors.

title: Gangneung Jungang Market
description: Gangneung Jungang Market is a representative traditional market located in the Seongnam-dong area of ​​Gangneung City. It was registered and opened on January 18, 1980 and has been actively operated to this day. To the east is the Eastern Market and to the west, the Western Market is located. As the third market to open following these two, it is a core commercial district that faithfully performs the distribution function of Gangneung city center. Seongnam Market, which consists of individual shops, is adjacent to the market, and institutions such as livestock cooperatives, Nonghyup Mart, and Saemaeul Geumgo are concentrated, making it closely connected to the local commercial district. In particular, various stalls are formed along the roadsides and alleys, and local specialties are actively traded throughout the four seasons, allowing you to feel the liveliness of a traditional market. The biggest characteristic of Jungang Market is that it preserves the local character of the Gangneung region. It is a market visited not only by citizens living in downtown Gangneung, but also by residents of farming and fishing villages near the east coast, and has played a central role in the local economy, selling various items such as agricultural and marine products, dried fish, and Gangneung's specialty food ingredients. In particular, during the Gangneung Dano Festival, which is held every year, the Namdaecheon Dano Market area around the market is filled with a festive atmosphere, and it becomes even more lively as a traditional market centered in the Yeongdong area where various products and people from all over the country gather. If you want to experience the life and culture of Gangneung in a space where tradition and modernity come together, Jungang Market is one of the travel destinations that you should not miss.

title: Gangmun Beach
description: Gangmun Beach is located in Gangmun-dong, and there is a small port called Gangmun Port nearby, so you can taste fresh raw fish caught at dawn at a nearby raw fish restaurant. Cleanly maintained accommodations and the Gyeongpo district are nearby. At Gangmun Beach, you can anchor at a place that takes 5 to 10 minutes by boat and enjoy the excellent underwater scenery of natural rocks, sea anemones, and large fish spread out in the sea at a depth of 5 to 30 meters. This is a popular destination for scuba diving enthusiasts, and underwater diving is especially for newlyweds who want to make memories. In addition, there is Gangmun Port, so 16 fishing boats regularly catch flounder, yellowtail, octopus, clams, sea urchins, sea squirts, and sea cucumbers, as well as flounder, flatfish, and giant clams in the spring, mackerel in the summer and fall, and rockfish in the winter. Fishing enthusiasts also catch dace and wrasse at the port. ◎ Travel information to meet the charm of the Korean Wave - This is where Seong-jun from the drama “She Was Pretty” came up with the idea for a photoshoot while watching the sea with Hye-jin. The two people revealed their inner feelings to each other here and formed a romantic atmosphere. It is also a popular date course for couples as there are many photo zones where you can take pictures of your life with the East Sea in the background.
