title: Gangchon Rail Park (Kim Yu-jeong Rail Bike)
venue: Gangchon Rail Park Kim Yu-jeong Rail Bike
description: With the opening of the Gyeongchun Line double-track railway, the old Gyeongchun Line railway has now run on rail bikes instead of trains. Gangchon Rail Park Kim Yu-jeong Rail Bike departs right next to Gim Yu-jeong Station on the Gyeongchun Line. At the boarding area, there are many small things to enjoy, such as a photo zone such as a large book sculpture and a five-colored umbrella sculpture that take advantage of regional characteristics, as well as a cafe and zip wire. It is an 8.5km course that starts from the Gimyujeong Station boarding area and ends at the old Gangchon Station. The first 6km section is by rail bike, and the remaining 2.5km section is by romantic train. The rail bike section is mainly downhill, so it is not difficult, and offers idyllic scenery with mountains, fields, and rivers, and tunnels decorated with various themes. There is a section where VR (virtual reality) experience is available, and it can be used for an additional fee. The romantic train with an exotic atmosphere runs along the Bukhangang River and offers a panoramic view. After arriving at your destination, take the shuttle bus and return to the boarding area. The Gyeonggang Rail Bike, a 7.2km course departing from Gyeonggang Station, is also operated separately.

title: Ganghwa Dongmak Beach
description: Dongmak Beach is a great place to experience the mudflats, as it is considered one of the world's top five mudflats. Surrounded by a white sandy beach and a dense pine forest, it boasts a natural natural scenery. You can enjoy swimming in the sea during high tide, and observe various creatures living in the mudflats during low tide. When the water recedes, the endless mud flats are revealed, allowing you to observe various sea creatures such as black crabs, blackfish, rice-skinned whelks, and lugworms. On one side of the beach, there is a coastal walking path called ‘The Road to See Spoonbills.’ The black-faced spoonbill is a globally endangered species and is protected as a natural monument, and its breeding site has been discovered in the Ganghwa mudflats. Ganghwa mudflats and spoonbill breeding grounds have been designated as natural monuments.

title: Ganghwa Jeondeungsa Temple
description: Jeondeungsa Temple has the longest history among existing Korean temples, and is a temple that preserves its history and authority as a fundamental Buddhist doctrine that protected the country with the Buddha's covering. As recorded in ‘Sejong Annals of Geography’, Samrangseong was an ancient earthen fortress that Dangun had his three sons build, and during the Three Kingdoms period, a stone fortress was built on the site of the earthen fortress, which continues to this day. It is said that Jeondeungsa Temple was founded in 381 AD (the 11th year of King Sosurim of Goguryeo). The person who first founded Jeondeungsa Temple was Ado, who came from the Jin Dynasty. At that time, Ado is known to have introduced Buddhism to Silla via Ganghwa Island. When Ado was staying in Ganghwa Island, he built a temple at the current location of Jeondeungsa Temple, and the name at that time was ‘Jinjongsa Temple.’ Afterwards, the Goryeo royal family built a palace within Samnangseong Fortress and greatly rebuilt Jinjongsa Temple. 16 years later, during the reign of King Chungnyeol, Queen Jeonghwagungju donated sutras and jade lanterns to Jinjongsa Temple, and the name of the temple was changed to ‘Jeondeungsa Temple.’ Later, in 1614, during the reign of King Gwanghaegun of the Joseon Dynasty, the entire building was destroyed by fire. Reconstruction began under the leadership of Monk Jigyeong, and Jeondeungsa Temple was restored to its original appearance in February 1621. Jeondeungsa Temple contains Korea's treasures such as Daeungjeon, Yaksijeon, and temple bell, and Jeongjoksago, which stored the Annals of the Joseon Dynasty, is located within the precincts. Also, at the east gate, there is a monument to Monk Yangheon, which proves that Jeondeungsa Temple is the epicenter of Buddhism. It was built in 1873, the 10th year of King Gojong's reign, to commemorate the achievement of General Yang Heon-su, who defeated the French army that invaded Jeondeungsa Temple, a strategic point during the Byeonginyangyo period, and saved the country from crisis. Temple stay is available as an experience program and is divided into one-day type, experience type, and relaxation type. The one-day type is designed to allow you to experience Korean Buddhist culture in a short period of time, the experience type offers slightly different programs at each temple depending on the season or the characteristics of the participants, and the rest type is a program that literally helps you stay at the temple and rest your tired body and mind for a while.
address: 37-41 Jeondeungsa-ro, Gilsang-myeon, Ganghwa-gun, Incheon Metropolitan City

title: Ganghwa Luge (Ganghwa Seaside Resort)
description: Ganghwa Luge is a dynamic experiential leisure sports facility where you ride a specially designed cart without a special power device and go down a track using only the slope of the ground and gravity. It allows direction adjustment and braking, and is characterized by the fact that everyone from children to adults can enjoy it. The track slope is gentle, but the curved course repeats itself, so you can quickly feel the sense of speed and thrill. You can enjoy it safely while wearing protective gear. The track is the largest in Asia with a total of 2 courses (Ocean Course and Valley Course) extending 1.8km/line, and each course has a 360 º rotation course and tunnels and drop sections for each section that double the interest and fun.

title: Gallery Park Young
description: Gallery Park Young is the first gallery in the Paju Book Complex, opened in 2008. The meaning of Park Young (博英) is to cultivate talented people and embodies the founder's corporate spirit. Paju Publishing Complex was formed as a special art and culture district where various cultural contents such as book-based art, music, architecture, education, furniture, and entertainment are gathered. The current gathering of more than 300 artists is also the result of the start of Park Young-sa's Gallery Park Young, which was opened to support artists. The artist support project, which was an artist residency program, is currently continuing exhibitions with artists of various genres through an annual contest under the name Park Young The Shift, and the works of Park Young artists are being displayed. Introducing it. Gallery Park Young is a gallery that strives to expand the base of art culture by communicating with the public through meaningful exhibitions such as special exhibitions with representative Korean artists with whom the gallery has been collecting art for over 30 years and exhibitions of Park Young's collection. It is a two-story building with a total floor area of ​​1,000㎡ and is equipped with a total of three exhibition spaces, a space dedicated to digital video, and an outdoor performance hall. It also operates the ''Studio Park Young'' program, which provides studios and various support to promising artists.

title: Galleria Gwanggyo
description: As the first department store where light penetrates the entire building, Galleria Gwanggyo proposes a shopping space that offers special and new enjoyment. It was designed by world-renowned architect Rem Koolhaas, who won the Pritzker Prize, known as the Nobel Prize of architecture. The façade, reminiscent of a huge rock, and the light streaming inside through the glass roof surrounding it provide a unique spatial experience. Aqua Planet Gwanggyo, where you can see 30,000 marine and land creatures of 210 species, and the Courtyard by Marriott Hotel, which has 288 rooms, are connected. You can enjoy the encounter between nature and the city in one place by taking a walk through Suwon Convention Center and Gwanggyo Lake Park.

title: Gallery Tea
description: GALLERY:T is a brand that proposes art experiences within lifestyle, and provides curating services so that art can naturally permeate daily life. Original paintings by various artists are displayed, and curation is conducted with a focus on the philosophy and messages contained in the works, as well as the emotional connection with the audience. In addition to original works, prints, art posters, interior frames, and mini frames are presented at reasonable prices, and art goods such as postcards and mugs are also displayed and sold.

title: Gaetgol Camping Site
description: Gaetgol Camping Site is located in Siheung-si, Gyeonggi-do. Starting from Siheung City Hall, you can reach it by passing through Janghyeon Intersection and Sanggok Intersection, and it takes about 10 minutes. Although it is located in the city center, when you enter the campsite, you feel like you have entered the forest. It has 2 glamping sites and 40 camping sites. Glamping rooms prepared to accommodate a large number of people are equipped with only air conditioning and heating, so guests must bring their own cooking utensils and other necessary items. If you do not have camping equipment, you can rent it from the management office. Additionally, although electricity is available, the use of a stove is not permitted. The concession stand, open from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., sells food and drinks. Cash is not accepted, and payment is only possible by card. It also has auxiliary facilities such as a playground for children.

title: Gangmae Waterfall
description: Gangmae Falls is a waterfall located at the foot of Oknyebong (376m) in the Maebong (582m) valley of Cheonggyesan Mountain and is also called Sujong Falls. The term Gaengmae is an abbreviation for Gaengmaengi, the largest neighborhood in Makgye-ri, Gwacheon-eup, Siheung-gun, Gyeonggi-do, and was called Gaengmae Village. Gaengmaeng is a dialect of Gwangmyeong, the old name of Makgye 2-ri, and is located above the valley of Gaengmae Village, so it was naturally called Gaengmae Waterfall. Now, with the construction of Seoul Grand Park in Gwacheon, Gaengmae Village has disappeared, and the name has been changed to Makgye-dong, Gwacheon-si, Gyeonggi-do. This waterfall is 13m long and 8m wide. Water flows from Maebong Valley in Cheonggyesan Mountain, through Gaengmae Falls, and through Gwacheon Reservoir (formerly Makgye Reservoir) in Seoul Grand Park to Yangjaecheon, joins Tancheon, and reaches the Han River. It is said that old villagers called Gaengmae Falls Cheonggye Falls, Dongpo Falls, and Gaengmaengi Falls. It takes about 30 minutes on foot from Exit 2 of Grand Park Station on Metropolitan Subway Line 4.

title: Geomdansan Mountain
description: Located east of Hanam City Hall, it is 657m high and is famous as a representative mountain of Hanam City. It is said to be Seongsan (崇山) and Jinsan (鎭山) in Wiryeseong, Hanam during the Hanseong period of Baekje, and is a sacred mountain where the king performed ancestral rites to heaven. From the summit of Geomdansan Mountain, you can enjoy the scenery of Yangsu-ri and Hanam, where the Namhan River and Bukhangang River meet, as well as Seoul, the Yangpyeong area, and the surroundings of Paldang Lake, making it a popular one-day climbing course near Seoul. It is located near Seoul, has convenient transportation, has well-maintained hiking trails, and the course is not that difficult, making it a good place for a family outing as a day hike. For hiking, you can use the hiking trail toward Sangok Elementary School in Hasangok-dong and toward Aebaealmi across Paldang Dam, with the former being more convenient for transportation. In addition, there is a memorial tower hiking trail that starts from the direction of Korea Animation High School in Changwoo-dong. The hike starting from Hasangok-dong is initially very steep, but the middle of the mountain is covered with old pine trees, making it a good place to take a break. When you stand on the wide, flat summit, you can see the mountains of Bukhansan Mountain and Dobongsan Mountain in the distance. Paldang Dam is visible to the east, Yongmasan Mountain rises on the ridge extending to the south, and the Jungbu Expressway runs powerfully to the west. Originally, King Sejong's tomb was intended to be built here, but it was moved to Yeoju, and the tomb site that was cleaned up still remains, telling the history, and there is the tomb of Yu Gil-jun, who wrote 《Seoyugyeonmun》.* Origin of Geomdansan *It was called Geomdansan Mountain because the Zen master Geomdan lived in seclusion here during the Baekje period. The height is similar to Gwanaksan Mountain (629m), but the mountain's shape is so unique that it is called the true mountain of Gwangjumok in Dongguk Yeoji Seungnam (東國與地勝覽). When you pass the steep slope and climb up to the ridge, the panoramic view in all directions opens up, and the path gradually leading to the top is very diverse.

title: Joan, Namyangju, Gyeonggi (Slow City)
venue: Namyangju Gyeonggi Namyangju Joan Slow City
description: Joan, named for ‘birds nesting comfortably,’ is the first slow city in the metropolitan area to be designated in November 2010. There is a bicycle path along the Namhangang River that runs from Paldang to Yangpyeong and Daeseong-ri. Additionally, there is a Slow City road that starts from Ungilsan Station, passes through Majin Fortress, Sujongsa Temple, and Songchon Independence Park, and tours the Slow City Cultural Center. This road was selected among about 40 target sites across the country through a public contest by the Ministry of Public Administration and Security for the project to create an eco-friendly living space green road. It is made up of 12 villages with simple and beautiful names such as Jeonwon Village, Jangsu Village, Lotus Village, and Ilgigi Village. Specialties of Joan-myeon include pear pear, organic ssamchae grown through organic farming, strawberries, and crafts made with rice straw and ssari.

title: Gyeonggi-do Gugakdang
description: Gyeonggi-do Gugakdang, located near the Korean Folk Village, opened in July 2004 to widely disseminate Korean traditional arts, expand the base of Korean traditional music, realize the globalization of traditional culture, and disseminate various traditional cultures to local residents and foreign tourists. Starting with the founding of the Gyeonggi Provincial Theater Company in 1990, it was launched as the Gyeonggi Arts Center in 2004 and is an affiliated organization of the Gyeonggi Arts Center, which changed its name in 2020. Gyeonggi-do Gugakdang was built with two floors above ground and three floors above ground. The performance hall has 470 seats (including 6 disabled seats), and auxiliary facilities include a dressing room, ensemble room, classroom, instrument storage room, costume storage room, lounge, snack bar, and children's playroom. It takes about 7 minutes by car from Suwon Singal IC and about 6 minutes from Sanggal Station on the Suin Bundang Line, and there is a bus that goes there from the station. Nearby are Everland, Korean Folk Village, Korea Job World, World Cultural Heritage Yunggeonreung Royal Tomb, Mulhyanggi Arboretum, Yongin Rural Theme Park, and Deokpyeong Dinosaur Arboretum.

title: Gyeonggi Museum of Modern Art
venue: Ansan Gyeonggi Museum of Modern Art
description: The Gyeonggi Museum of Modern Art provides a variety of cultural services by operating programs such as exhibitions by domestic and foreign artists, collection of art works, research, education, and promotional projects. In particular, it has established itself as a famous place for art and culture through various special exhibitions that harmonize professionalism, artistry, locality and globality. The museum building, with the park's ecological lake in the background, is made of glass on the front, giving it a clear and pleasant feel, while also fulfilling the role of a modern art museum centered on a high-floor exhibition hall where various special exhibitions are held. The Gyeonggi Museum of Art runs [Culture Day] on the last week of every month so that anyone can easily access culture and arts in their daily lives. Curators from the Museum of Art tell stories on new and diverse topics every month, including exhibitions, works, archives, and architecture. Through this, you can enjoy art more comfortably and happily, and it is well-received as an art museum where anyone, including the general public and children, not just art experts, can appreciate and enjoy works of art.

title: Gyeonggi Ceramic Museum
description: * Gyeonggi Ceramic Museum, a museum specializing in Joseon ceramics * Gwangju Joseon Royal Court Museum is located in Gwangju, Gyeonggi-do, where the royal palaces of the Joseon Dynasty were installed and operated for over 400 years. It is a specialized ceramic museum that studies traditional Korean ceramics, including research on Joseon white porcelain, excavation of Joseon official relics, academic research projects, and education on traditional ceramic culture. In order to foster and develop traditional Korean ceramics, a traditional ceramics contest called ''Beautiful Korean Pottery Exhibition'' is held every two years, through which beautiful Korean ceramics that match today's Korean characteristics will be showcased. It consists of two large exhibition halls, a special exhibition room, and a multi-purpose room, and is equipped with auxiliary facilities such as a large-scale outdoor sculpture park, a firewood kiln, a Korean garden, a tea ceremony extension, and a ceramics shopping mall selling ceramics produced in the Gwangju area. Gwangju Joseon Official Art Museum permanently exhibits traditional ceramics produced in Joseon Dynasty official ceramics, such as pure white porcelain, blue and white porcelain, iron and white porcelain, and Buncheong porcelain, which have continued the Joseon Dynasty's 500-year history, as well as works by modern artists who have inherited that tradition. It will allow you to feel our living, breathing ceramic tradition through special exhibitions and special exhibitions that illuminate our traditional ceramic culture and history. * Discover various information about ceramics * The Gyeonggi Ceramic Museum has two floors of exhibition rooms, with a ceramic culture room and special exhibition room on the first floor and a permanent exhibition room on the second floor. The Ceramic Culture Room provides visitors with knowledge and information on ceramic concepts, history, and techniques, and the Gyeonggi Ceramic Museum holds special exhibitions that highlight the history and traditions of domestic and foreign ceramics by theme at least twice a year. Special exhibitions held in various spaces, including the first floor special exhibition room as well as the second floor exhibition room, provide new attractions and learning materials that cannot be seen in the permanent exhibition. The permanent exhibition room is divided into rooms 1 and 2. In room 1, you can see at a glance the development process of ceramic culture on the Korean Peninsula, and in room 2, you can admire ceramic works that suggest the future development direction of Korean ceramics.

title: Gyeonggi Northern Children’s Museum
description: The Gyeonggi Northern Children’s Museum, located at the foot of Soyosan Mountain, has an exhibition hall under the theme of ‘Children dreaming in the forest.’ This contains the idea that children should develop their dreams by physically experiencing life with various living things in nature. Among the exhibition spaces with the forest theme of the forest of the past, forest of the present, and forest of the future, the ‘Forest of the Past’ on the first floor includes the Dinosaur Forest, Oreum Forest, and Sea Forest (children’s playground). The Dinosaur Forest is a space where you can explore the dinosaur forests of the past along with little Brachio while asking the question, “Did dinosaurs live in Dongducheon?” The Oreum Forest is a large physical development playground where you climb up and down the body of the giant herbivorous dinosaur Brachiosaurus, and the Sea Forest is an experiential exhibition room designed for infants under 36 months old with the theme of underwater marine life and adventure. When you go up to the second floor, the Natural Forest, the Five Senses Forest, the Imagination Forest, and the Learning Center are the ‘present day forest.’ It forms a ‘forest’ and a ‘forest of the future.’ The natural forest is a space where we, who have become as small as a blade of grass, meet and interact with the life in the forest up close and with our whole bodies, under the theme of ‘a world that can only be seen when it is small.’ The Five Senses Forest is an experiential exhibition hall that awakens the senses of the forest with museum characters based on the five senses. Imagination Forest periodically presents special exhibitions that colorfully explain the coexistence of various life forms for visitors of various generations to help children and all of them develop their dreams and imaginations. And at the learning center, we are creating a ‘forest of the future’ through education and practice that embodies the values ​​of nature, ecosystem, environment, and peace. In addition, the Gyeonggi Northern Children’s Museum is planning various exhibitions, education, publications, research, and exchange programs with children as the main characters to understand me and you and us and spread the value of respect for each other. In addition, school education programs in connection with education support offices in northern Gyeonggi Province, and collaboration with children's culture and arts education groups, local organizations, and activists are also underway. Based on this, we aim to establish ourselves as a representative cultural and artistic space in northern Gyeonggi Province where children and families can experience the ‘natural play forest’ and develop their dreams.

title: Gyeonggi Art Center
description: Gyeonggi Arts Center is a comprehensive performance hall located in Paldal-gu, Suwon-si, Gyeonggi-do. The establishment of a basic plan and a design competition began in 1984, and it opened as the Gyeonggi Arts Center in 1991. In 2020, the name was changed to Gyeonggi Arts Center and Gyeonggi Arts Troupe, and at the same time, it is transforming into a de-authorized open space. Gyeonggi Art Center was established to revitalize local culture and arts and provide various cultural benefits to residents of the province as a place where art is vibrant, interacts with society, and daily life becomes art. There are the Happy Grand Theater, Cozy Small Theater, Dreaming Convention Center, Exciting Outdoor Performance Hall, Shining Gallery, and Small Gallery. In addition to production performances, Gyeonggi Arts Center operates a variety of cultural and artistic contents such as cultural welfare, education, provincial projects, exhibitions, and rentals. It provides the best culture to the audience by leading the way in advanced and professional culture through continuous efforts to build cutting-edge facilities.

title: Gyeonggi Art Center Gallery
description: Gyeonggi Art Center Gallery is an exhibition space located inside Gyeonggi Art Center, a general performance hall located in Paldal-gu, Suwon-si, Gyeonggi-do, and operates short-term art and experiential exhibitions. Meanwhile, the Gyeonggi Art Center was built with the goal of becoming ‘a place where everyday life becomes art’, revitalizing local culture and arts, and allowing residents to enjoy culture. In addition to the gallery, it has facilities such as a large theater, a small theater, and an outdoor performance hall. Hyowon Park and Ingye Art Park are nearby, making it a good place to take a walk after viewing the exhibition.

title: King of Gyeonggi Rail Bike
description: "The largest artificial ecological wetland in the metropolitan area" 01. Wangsong Lake, where the metropolitan area's largest artificial ecological wetland rail park is located, is a reservoir with an embankment length of 640m and a total storage capacity of 2.07 million tons. It is a habitat for migratory birds in all seasons and a place where various fish species, wetland plants, and aquatic plants are distributed. In addition, there are facilities such as an avian ecology science museum, a nature learning park, and a clear water treatment plant in the vicinity, making it a natural and ecological learning education center. 02. Wangsong Lake, the best sunset view in the metropolitan area, is located in the center of the metropolitan area and is adjacent to six cities, including Anyang, Gunpo, Gwacheon, Suwon, and Seongnam. It can be accessed quickly and easily from Seoul and other nearby areas. In particular, the sunset view of Wangsong Lake is known as a spectacle rarely seen in the metropolitan area. It has world-class integrated railway facilities covering an area of 2,525,915㎡, including the Railway Museum and KORAIL Human Resources Development Center.

title: Gyeongbokgung Palace
description: Gyeongbokgung Palace is the first royal palace of the Joseon Dynasty, founded in 1395 (the 4th year of King Taejo's reign) after the founding of the Joseon Dynasty in 1392. Gyeongbokgung Palace was the center of Hanyang, with buildings placed on a wide terrain with Baekaksan Mountain (Bukaksan Mountain) as the main mountain, and a wide Yukjo Street spread out in front of Gwanghwamun, the main gate. The name of ‘Gyeongbok’ contains the meaning that ‘the new dynasty will enjoy great fortune and prosper,’ and it was here that Hunminjeongeum was created and promulgated during the reign of King Sejong. In addition, it was also called ‘Bukgul’ because it was located in the north compared to the eastern palace (Changdeokgung Palace) or the western palace (Gyeonghuigung Palace). If you look at the kings who held coronation ceremonies at Geunjeongjeon in Gyeongbokgung Palace, they include the 2nd King Jeongjong, the 4th King Sejong, the 6th King Danjong, the 7th King Sejo, the 9th King Seongjong, the 11th King Jungjong, and the 13th King Myeongjong. Gyeongbokgung Palace was destroyed by fire during the Japanese Invasion of Korea in 1592 (the 25th year of King Seonjo's reign), and was unable to be restored after that. It was rebuilt about 270 years later in 1867 (4th year of King Gojong's reign). During the reign of King Gojong, Geoncheong Palace, Taewonjeon, and Jipokjae were built, and in particular, Okhoru of Geoncheong Palace was also the tragic location where Empress Myeongseong was assassinated in the Eulmi Incident in 1895. After the Gyeongsul National Rule in 1910, Gyeongbokgung Palace began to be deliberately damaged, and most of the pavilions were demolished in 1915 under the pretext of holding the Joseon Industrial Exhibition, and in 1926, the Japanese Government-General of Korea was rebuilt. The scenery of Gyeongbokgung Palace was damaged by the construction of the government building. Afterwards, Gyeongbokgung Palace restoration work was carried out in earnest from the 1990s, and the Joseon Government-General building was demolished from 1995 to 1997, and the Heungnyemun Gate area, the Chimjeon area, Geoncheong Palace, Taewonjeon, and Gwanghwamun were restored to the present. In Gyeongbokgung Palace, the ponds of Gyeonghoeru and Hyangwonjeong, representative buildings of the Joseon Dynasty, remain in their original form, and the moonstone and statues of Geunjeongjeon are the same as those of the time. It represents sculpture art. Currently, the National Palace Museum is located on the west side outside Heungnyemun Gate, and the National Folk Museum is located on the east side of Hyangwonjeong in Gyeongbokgung Palace. The main cultural assets of Gyeongbokgung Palace include the historical site Gyeongbokgung Palace, national treasure Gyeongbokgung Palace Geunjeongjeon, national treasure Gyeonghoeru Gyeongbokgung Palace, treasure Gyeongbokgung Jagyeongjeon, treasure Gyeongbokgung Palace Jagyeongjeon Chimney of the Ten Jangsangsaeng, treasure Gyeongbokgung Palace Amisan Chimney, treasure Gyeongbokgung Geunjeongmun and Haenggak, treasure There is Gyeongbokgung Palace Punggidae, etc. ◎ Travel information to meet the charm of the Korean Wave The American national TV show ‘The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon’ held a special BTS broadcast for five days under the name ‘BTS Week’, and the place where BTS sang ‘Microcosm’ and ‘IDOL’ from the ‘Map of the Soul: Persona’ mini album became a hot topic. The place is Gyeonghoeru and Geunjeongjeon of ‘Gyeongbokgung Palace’, one of the palaces of the Joseon Dynasty. We recommend experiencing Korea’s past at Gyeongbokgung Palace, which shines beautifully in purple lights.

title: Gyeongan Market
description: Gwangju Gyeongan Market is a historic traditional market that has existed since the Joseon Dynasty and is located in the center of Gwangju City. Through the facility modernization project in 2010, environmental improvements such as arcade installation, water supply, gas, and electricity construction, and central passage maintenance were completed. In 2014, a parking lot was also created to improve user convenience. A regular market and a permanent market are operated in parallel, and the regular market sells a variety of products, including local agricultural products, miscellaneous goods, and clothing. In particular, there is a gallery window depicting Namhansanseong Fortress and ceramics, providing a unique attraction.

title: Daereungwon area, Gyeongju
description: Gyeongju Daereungwon refers to a group of ancient tombs from the Silla period located in Nodong-dong and Hwangnam-dong, Gyeongju-si. It consists of Nodong-dong tombs, Noseo-ri tombs, Hwangnam-dong tombs, Hwango-dong tombs, and Inwang-dong tombs. The Nodong-dong tombs are tombs from the Go Silla period and include Bonghwangdae, Sikri Tomb, and Geumnyeong Tomb. Bonghwangdae is the second largest tomb after Hwangnamdaechong with a base circumference of 230m, a diameter of 82m, and a height of 22m. It is a stone mound tomb with an overlay installed. The Noseo-ri tomb group consists of 14 large and small tombs on a large flat area. In addition to the Bonghwangdae Tomb in Nodong-ri, there is Tomb No. 130, which is large in size and forms a double wall, as well as Geumgwanchong Tomb, where a gold crown was excavated in 1921, and Seobongchong Tomb, where Sweden's crown prince and archaeologist Gustav VI Adolf stopped by during his visit to Japan in 1926 to investigate and observe excavations. In 1946, a bronze vessel engraved with the name of King Gwanggaeto of Goguryeo was discovered, and there are also Houchong, Eunpyeongchong, Ssangsangchong, and Machong that helped estimate the age of the Silla tomb. Pieces of pottery were excavated from Ssangsangchong, and fragments of horse bones and saddles were unearthed from Mamchong. The Hwangnam-dong Ancient Tombs are tombs from the early Silla Dynasty, some of which are located within the Daereungwon area. There are 30 tombs piled up in a circular shape. The large tomb is a stone mound tomb, and nearby there is a small tomb with no seal gate. Inside Daereungwon, there are the former tomb of King Michu, Cheonmachong Tomb, and Hwangnamdaechong Tomb. Cheonmachong Tomb was excavated from April 6 to December 4, 1973. Cheonmachong Tomb has a diameter of 47m and a height of 12.7m, and many relics, including a gold crown, were found there. Since a horse saddle draper with a drawing of Cheonmado was excavated at the time, it was named Cheonmachong and its interior is open to the public. The Hwango-dong Ancient Tombs are densely packed with large and small Silla period tombs. Although the burial mounds have been greatly damaged due to lack of maintenance over a long period of time, there are about 10 burial mounds that can be assumed to be ancient tombs. Judging from the structure of the tombs excavated in the adjacent area, these tombs are presumed to be stone mound tombs that mainly buried royalty or nobles from around the 4th to 5th centuries. The Inwang-dong tomb group is located in the easternmost part of the tomb group remaining in the central plain of Gyeongju. During the Japanese colonial period, 13 burial mounds were identified, and 10 new tombs were found to be in distribution. Some of the tombs were excavated, and the tomb styles of the Three Han and Three Kingdoms periods were confirmed. It can be seen that tombs began to be built from an early period. Most of the tombs from the Three Kingdoms period that still have fiefs are stone mound tombs, and judging from the excavated artifacts and the size of the remains, they are presumed to be the tombs of Silla nobles. ◎ Travel information to experience the charm of the Korean Wave - This is a park dense with ancient tombs where Bora spent her free time on a school trip in the drama <20th Century Girl>. About 20 large tombs create a dreamlike atmosphere as if they are drawing a ridge. The place where a magnolia tree stands between the burial mounds is a famous photo spot. It is recommended that you also tour Cheonmachong Tomb, the only one whose interior is open to the public.

title: Tomb of King Munmu, Gyeongju
description: This is the underwater royal tomb of King Munmu, the 30th king of Silla (reigned 661-681), and is a place where you can get a glimpse of the creative thinking of the Silla people. It is located 200m off the coast of Bonggil-ri in the East Sea, and is exposed 35m east-west, 36m north-south, and 5.3m above sea level. King Munmu inherited the achievements of his father, King Taejong Muyeol, and destroyed Goguryeo and prevented the Tang invasion, unifying the three kingdoms. In addition, it provided the basis for completing the national system by creating central government offices such as the Ministry of Military Affairs and the Ministry of Court, and laying the foundation for a military system of 5 small economic provinces, 9 Seodang, and 10 administrative districts for local governance. King Munmu, who achieved the unification of the three kingdoms, said that he would become a dragon to stop the invading Japanese pirates, and buried his body according to his will, which asked him to cremate his body in Buddhist style and bury his ashes in the East Sea. This rock is called Daewangam or Daewangbawi Rock, and the royal tombs under the sea are unprecedented in the world. Daewangam was made using natural rocks. A cross-shaped artificial waterway was created from east to west and north to south on a rocky island, and then dug out like a small pond in the middle to form a port. It is presumed that a wide turtle-shaped stone measuring 3.7m, 2.06m in width, and 0.9m in thickness was placed here at a depth of 2m under water to enshrine the remains. His son, King Sinmun, built Gameunsa Temple near the East Sea and built a drainage channel toward the East Sea under the shrine so that King Munmu, who became a dragon, could come and go.

title: Gyeongju Seokguram Grotto [UNESCO World Heritage]
description: It is said that Seokguram Grotto (National Treasure) was founded in the 10th year of King Gyeongdeok of Silla by Kim Dae-seong, the prime minister at the time. The structure of Seokguram Grotto, located 3 km away from Bulguksa Temple by climbing the ridge and 9 km away by the new road, is a harmony of squares and circles, straight lines and curves, and planes and spheres. In particular, none of the 38 figures carved around the wall are masterpieces, and their overall harmony shows a high degree of philosophy and scientific aspects. In the center, the original seated Buddha made of white granite overlooks the East Sea, and the gaze of the seated Buddha is towards Daewangam in front of Bonggil-ri, the tomb of the underwater king of King Munmu. The site of Gameunsa Temple, which protects the underwater king, and Igyeondae, where it is said that King Munmu was seen as a dragon, are located on the coast near Daewangam, and Bulguksa Temple and Seokguram Grotto were opened on December 6, 1995, along with the Tripitaka Koreana and Jongmyo Shrine of Haeinsa Temple. It is officially designated and protected as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The sky and sea, with the red sun over the horizon seen from Seokguram Grotto, are spectacular. After watching the sunrise at Seokguram Grotto, Seokjang-ro, which goes directly from Tohamsan Mountain to the east coast, was opened in 1998, allowing you to easily go to the sea off Gampo and Yangbuk. Enjoy raw fish that boasts the taste of the cleanest sea in the country, and tour Gameunsa Temple Site and King Munmu's Tomb to make an even more wonderful trip.
address: Seokguram Grotto, 238 Seokgu-ro, Gyeongju-si, Gyeongsangbuk-do, Gyeongsangbuk-do

title: Gyeongju Cheomseongdae
description: Cheomseongdae is believed to have been built during the reign of Queen Seondeok, the 27th queen of Silla, and is one of the landmarks that symbolize Gyeongju. It has a cylindrical part in the shape of a liquor bottle on top of the stylobate that serves as a pedestal, and the top part in the shape of the letter Jeong (井) is placed on top, and the height is about 9m. The cylindrical part is made of 27 layers of fan-shaped stones. The lower part, centered around the southeast-facing window, is filled with stone, and the upper part is open to the top and is hollow. The eastern half of the summit is blocked by Pandora, and the ends of long stones interlocked in the shape of the letter 井 protrude to the outside. This type of appearance is also found in the 19th~20th and 25th~26th levels, and it seems to have been suitable for hanging a ladder inside. According to an old record, “people are supposed to go up in the middle,” and it appears that they placed a ladder outside, went inside through the window, and then used the ladder to climb to the top and observe the sky. The stones that make up Cheomseongdae each have their own meaning. The shape of Cheomseongdae, which is round at the top and square at the bottom, symbolizes heaven and earth. The 365 stones that made Cheomseongdae symbolize the number of days in a year, the 27-tiered stone platform symbolizes the 27th Queen Seondeok, who built Cheomseongdae, and the 29-tiered and 30-tiered stones, including the pavilion stone at the top, represent the number of days in a lunar month. It is assumed that observers came and went, and the 12 upper and 12 lower tiers based on the window indicate the 12 months and 24 seasons of the year. This part suggests that Cheomseongdae was used to determine the timing of farming by calculating the movement of the sky and to predict good or bad fortune for the country. ◎ Travel information to experience the charm of the Korean Wave - Cheomseongdae, where Bogyeom and Jia passed each other in the drama <I Love You Today Too>, is a landmark representing Gyeongju and the oldest astronomical observatory in the world. Not only does it have great viewing value as a historic site, but it is also visited by many tourists who want to enjoy an outing as various flowers and plants bloom every season.

title: Gyeongju Hwangridan-gil
description: Hwangridan-gil is the youngest road in Gyeongju and is a combination of Hwangnam-dong and Itaewon’s Gyeongnidan-gil, meaning ‘Hwangnam-dong’s Gyeongnidan-gil.’ It refers to the area around Hwangnam-dong and Sajeong-dong on both sides of the road starting from Naenam Intersection to Hwangnam Elementary School Intersection. It is a street where you can fully feel the atmosphere of the past as old buildings from the 1960s and 1970s have been preserved as is. A few years ago, young people began to gather here, and cafes with a nice atmosphere, cute props, souvenir shops, and unique restaurants opened. In the beginning, shops were built mainly along the roadside, but as the outer edge of Hwangridan-gil expanded, unique shops began popping up in every alley. It has become an essential course when traveling to Gyeongju, and it is in the spotlight as a famous tourist attraction in Gyeongju as it allows you to visit the nearby tourist attractions of Cheomseongdae and Daereungwon.

description: Gyeongju Expo Grand Park is where the world's first culture and arts-themed cultural expo, 'Gyeongju World Expo', was held in 1998. Since then, it has hosted the Gyeongju World Expo 10 times over the past 20 years, raising Koreans' cultural pride and contributing to the development of human culture. Currently, it is a famous place in Gyeongju that lovers, friends, and families can visit and enjoy together based on various exhibitions, videos, performances, and experiential cultural contents. Major facilities include Gyeongju Tower, Gyeongju Solgeo Art Museum, Bium Meditation Trail, and Luminite. In addition, there are various facilities such as Timeless Media Art, Natural History Museum, and Gyeongju World Culture Expo Memorial Hall.

title: Gyeongpo Beach
description: Famous as the largest beach on the East Coast, it is located in Gangmun-dong and Anhyeon-dong, 6km north of the city and 1km from Gyeongpodae, and is filled with waves of waves from the East Sea. The combination of the waves crashing in as if trying to swallow everyone, the 1.8 km long, 1.44 km2 white sandy beach that embraces them, and the lush pine folding screens that quietly block out the noisy daily life creates a unique beauty of the beach. Gyeongpodae Beach is a 1.8km white sand beach with an average water depth of 1~2m. It is a place where many people visit every year due to its moderate depth and gentle slope. There is a thick pine forest around the beach, making it a perfect summer resort as you can enjoy sea and forest bathing at the same time. Every summer, the Summer Night Arts Festival is held at the permanent stage on Gyeongpo Beach, offering a variety of cultural attractions. Hiking by renting a bicycle around Gyeongpo Lake is also a specialty. In addition, there are Seoraksan Mountain and Odaesan National Park nearby, so you can explore mountains, the sea, and valleys.

title: ancient mountain
description: Godae Mountain is 832 meters above sea level and forms the border between Sinseo-myeon, Yeoncheon-gun and Cheorwon-eup, Cheorwon-gun, Gangwon-do. It is the closest mountain to North Korea among the mountains permitted for climbing. The origin of Godae Mountain appears to be related to the Shintan name, [Big Whale]. It refers to Bangorae (the furrow through which flame and smoke flows under the floor of an ondol room using firewood), and is called Godae Mountain because the valley is deep and high. Godasan Mountain has a total of three hiking trails that use Godasan Natural Recreation Forest as the starting and ending points. Course 1 is about 4.2km, and includes the Godasan parking lot - 1st hiking trail entrance - Keungol - Munbawi - Daegwangbong - Samgakbong - and climbs to the top of Godesan Mountain. Course 2 is about 4.3km, and goes from Godaesan Parking lot - 2nd hiking trail entrance - Maldeungbawi Rock - Kalbawi - Daegwangbong - Samgakbong - to the top of Godesan Mountain. Course 3 is about 4.0km long and goes from Godae Mountain parking lot to the 3rd hiking trail entrance to Leopard Falls to the summit of Godae Mountain. All three hiking trails take about 2 hours to 2 hours and 10 minutes. Course 3 is steeper than Courses 1 and 2, so hiking in a circle from Courses 1 and 2 to Course 3 is usually preferred. In particular, the secret scenery of Kalbawi Ridge, the highlight of course 2, and Leopard Falls, course 3, steal the hearts of many hikers. There is a pavilion and a large heliport near the top of the mountain, making it a great place to rest or enjoy the view. From the summit, you can see at a glance the Cheorwon Plain in the North, the Iron Triangle, the site of the greatest battle of the Korean War, the Taebongguk City Wall built around the new capital by Gungye, as well as Geumhaksan Mountain, Jijangbong Peak, Bukdaesan Mountain, and Hyangnobong Mountain, as well as Jongjasan Mountain on the banks of the Hantangang River. It is also a popular winter hiking destination, and people can hike to nearby Bogaesan Mountain and Geumhaksan Mountain. Nearby are Baekmagoji, Yeoncheon Station Icicle, Labor Party Headquarters, Key Observatory, Dongmakgol Recreation Area, Crane Theme Park, Herb Village, Jaein Falls (Hantangang River National Geopark), Hantangang and Imjin River columnar joints, Yeoncheon Jeongok-ri Ruins, Yeoncheon Horogoru, and Yeoncheon Gorangpogu Historical Park.

title: Godae Mountain Natural Recreation Forest
description: Godae Mountain Natural Recreation Forest, located in Daegwang-ri, Sinseo-myeon, Yeoncheon-gun, Gyeonggi-do, opened in 2017 and is close to National Road 3 and Shintan-ri Station on the Gyeongwon Line, so it is easily accessible and is a place where you can enjoy the clear and quiet natural environment unique to the border area. The main facilities include 14 forest houses, 1 forest recreation center, 6 rooms, 1 forest training center, 20 campsites, 1 public restroom and kitchen. It is a place where you can breathe with nature, wash away stress and tired mind and body, and add joy and comfort through various hiking and exploring trails leading to Godaesan Mountain (832m) and Bogaesan Mountain (877m). It takes about 2 minutes by car or 15 minutes on foot from Shintanri Station on the Gyeongwon Line. Nearby are Baekmagoji, Yeoncheon Station Icicle, Labor Party Headquarters, Key Observatory, Dongmakgol Recreation Area, Crane Theme Park, Herb Village, Jaein Falls (Hantangang River National Geopark), Hantangang River and Imjingang River Columnar Joints, Yeoncheon Jeongok-ri Ruins, Yeoncheon Horogoru, and Yeoncheon Gorangpo Historical Park. (Source: Godae Mountain Natural Recreation Forest website)

title: Gomo Reservoir
description: Gomori is a name given to a person who lived under the mountain with his old aunt. This grandmother passed away alone, and the village was opened in front of her grave. This place was called Gomoe-ap, Gomyo, or Gomo. For this reason, the name of the village became Gomori. Gomo Reservoir is a reservoir with a storage capacity of 1,300,000 tons and an area of ​​​​about 55,000 pyeong, located in the center of Jukyeop Mountain, 600m above sea level, east of Soheul-eup. It has a beautiful trail, fountain, and rest area, so it is convenient for nearby cafes, galleries, restaurants, walking trails, and hiking courses. It is also a pleasant place to explore or resort, and you can enjoy water leisure activities, making it a suitable day trip destination. The Gomo Reservoir fountain operates every 30 minutes from 12:00 to 17:30 from mid-April to mid-November. Every Saturday and Sunday, a flea market is held at the lake square, where Komori residents, artists, and skilled handmade sellers come out to show off their skills and sell them. Additionally, there are many restaurants and cafes that allow dogs, so there are many people outing with their dogs.

title: Gobongsan Mountain
description: Gobongsan Mountain is the highest mountain in Ilsan-gu, Goyang-si. The name of this mountain comes from the meaning of ‘high mountain peak’ or ‘raising a signal fire.’ When viewed from a distance, the north side is high and the south side is low. It is a famous mountain that appears in 'Samguk Sagi', a record of the Three Kingdoms period, and was a key military, transportation, and strategic point where Goguryeo, Baekje, and Silla fought fierce battles over the Han River basin. As proof of this, pottery pieces from the Three Kingdoms period are found here and there on this mountain. Gobongsan Mountain is home to pine trees, zelkova trees, oak trees, and chestnut trees, which always provide cool shade. At the foot of the mountain, there are small temples of Mangyeongsa Temple and Yeongcheonsa Temple, as well as cultural assets such as Jeong Ji-un's tomb and Hong I-sang's tomb. There are also many small rocks on the mountain, and the representative rocks include Madangbawi Rock, Jangsabawi Rock, Toad Rock, Cheukimbawi Rock, Imugi Rock, and Thunder Rock. Gobongsan Beacon Mound is located at the top. Old literature records that Gobongsanseong Fortress was located here and a beacon fire station was installed there. The current beacon mound remains as a rectangular stone mound centered on the peak of the mountain. The total circumference of the stone wall is approximately 120m, and the height is approximately 5m. Gobong Beacon Mound is a beacon mound made by piling up surrounding natural stones and is in a relatively good state of preservation with no special collapsed areas.

title: Gosam Lake
description: Gosam Lake, located in Anseong, Gyeonggi-do, is a 940,000 pyeong (940,000 pyeong) lake built in 1960 and is a place of natural beauty with a dreamy and lyrical sense of mystery. Gosam Lake, the main setting of director Kim Ki-duk's movie Island, is impressive with its blue water and pedestal floating on it. Gosam Lake is famous as a fishing spot, but after the movie was released, it also became known as a tourist destination. It is located relatively close to downtown Seoul, so it is possible as a day course. In the movie, the entire lake is set as an open set, so you can enjoy the tranquil atmosphere as it was in its original form. This place has clean water, shallow depth, and well-formed aquatic plants along the coast, so carp and carp are especially abundant. There are shops nearby that sell whole carp, native chicken, grilled eel, and spicy spicy stew restaurants. Nearby scenic spots include Mirinae, a sacred place for Korean Catholics who were so religious that they were reputed to be the only ones in the world who spontaneously accepted a new religion; there is also a temple of the 103rd Catholic saint who was sealed as a Catholic saint by the Vatican in 1984, the tomb and chapel of the first priest, Father Kim Dae-geon, a rectory, and a monastery. In addition, there are many fishing spots nearby, such as Misan Lake, so it is a place where Kang Tae-gong constantly visits.

title: Goseong Unification Observation Tower
description: If you stand at the Unification Observatory, located 70 meters above sea level where the Armistice Line and the Southern Limit Line meet, you can see Guseonbong Peak and Haegeumgang River in close proximity, and on clear days, you can see Oknyebong Peak, Chaehabong Peak, and Ilchulbong Peak. The front-line guard posts facing each other across the barbed wire fence of the ceasefire line below give a sense of the tension between North and South Korea. As a representative tourist attraction in Goseong, visited by more than 1.5 million tourists annually, there are religious facilities such as the Virgin Mary, Maitreya Buddha, and Jeonjeon Iron Tower for the displaced people who remember their descendants and families left behind in North Korea and those who wish for unification, as well as security education exhibits such as armored vehicles, tanks, and airplanes. Geumgangsan overland tourism can be seen taking place on the Donghae Line, a north-south connecting road that opened in December 2004.

title: Goseongsan Mountain
description: Goseongsan Mountain, which is 298m high, has a quite picturesque hiking course from Manse Pass to Unsuam. If you climb from Bangsin-ri, Yangseong-myeon, Anseong-si, you can first see Unsuam Hermitage. If you head northwest from the entrance to Bangsin-ri, you can see the atmosphere of Unsuam among the larch and pine forests. Unsuam Hermitage, where the clear sound of moktak greets you on the forest path, is designated as Gyeonggi-do Cultural Asset No. 25 and contains a Vairocana Buddha statue created during the Goryeo Dynasty. Unsuam Temple is a temple founded in the 26th year of King Yeongjo’s reign in the Joseon Dynasty. According to legend, a Bodhisattva decided to live with Buddha for the rest of his life and was initially laying a foundation under Musanseong Fortress. One day, in a dream, he received a revelation from the Buddha telling him to build a temple within the fortress. He entered the fortress, visited the place shown in his dream, discovered an old temple site, and built a temple there. Later, when this Bodhisattva died, Daewongun rebuilt this temple, which was overgrown with weeds, and put up a handwritten plaque praying for the peace of the nation and the name Unsuam. This temple became famous. However, because there was no one to take care of it, it was on the verge of collapse, so monk Hyeonam repaired it and rebuilt the main hall, which still stands today. If you have carefully looked around Unsuam, you can find a mineral spring by walking a short distance along the well-maintained hiking trail. If you cool off your sweat here for a moment and take a few steps, you will reach the summit of Goseongsan Mountain. When you climb to the top of Goseongsan Mountain, you can see the vast fields of Anseong Yangseong area and the plains extending to Pyeongtaek. After enjoying the surrounding scenery from the top, let’s walk towards Hill 216. When you come down from the summit, you will come across a small hiking trail that goes down towards Bibeopsa Temple. Instead of taking this route, you can also go over Hill 216 and descend behind the mountain lodge rest area. In particular, the March 1st Movement Memorial Hall has been newly built across from the mountain lodge rest area, so you can tour historical sites.

title: High Song Stop
description: This is the place where Kim Chung-ju, the grandson of Kim Mun-gi, who participated in the movement to restore King Danjong and suffered disaster, lived. It is said that Kim Chung-ju escaped from the capital during the night and moved around various places until he hid in Hwajeong-dong and made it his business to weave grass to build a house and bake and sell charcoal. He called himself Tanong (炭翁) and did not eat meat or alcohol all his life, and wore sackcloth and a hat. It is said that whenever his mind about King Danjong changed, he cried while looking at Yeongwol, where King Danjong's grave is located, and that the pine tree withered and died due to the tears he shed as he mourned the death of his grandfather and father. In the 27th year of King Sunjo's reign (1827), his 9th generation grandson, Jinsa Kim Cheo-il, built a pavilion called Gosongjeong (枯松亭) on the spot. Gosongjeong site is also called Tanong Goteo because he made a living by weaving grass to build houses, grilled and sold charcoal, and called himself an old man who burns charcoal. The pavilion measures 2 kan at the front and 2 kan at the sides, and has a gable roof that is shaped like an eight-pointed gable when viewed from the side. To the left of the pavilion, there is a rock with the inscription [Tanonggoji], and if you go up to the right of Gosongjeong, there is a rock called Mangwolam where he cried while drawing Danjong. The surrounding area has zelkova and juniper trees that are over 500 years old, creating an outstanding natural scenery.

title: Goyang Ilsan Lake Park Garosu-gil
venue: Goyang Goyang Ilsan Lake Park Garosu-gil
description: Ilsan Lake Park Garosu-gil is a street mall with 5 buildings from the 1st basement level to the 3rd floor above ground and is approximately 270m long. There are prop shops, cafes, and dessert stores on the first floor, and various food and beverage stores, including Korean food, Western food, and snacks, on the second floor. It is adjacent to the lake park, making it ideal for walking trails, and the dome-shaped building creates an exotic atmosphere reminiscent of Santorini. Terrace-type open-air cafes are popular as photo zones where you can enjoy European sensibility regardless of the season.

title: Goyang Flower Exhibition Hall
description: Goyang Flower Exhibition Hall is an exhibition hall built in Ilsan Lake Park by Goyang City with a budget of KRW 9.8 billion to commemorate the successful hosting of the 2000 Goyang World Flower Expo and to hold regular flower fairs and flower-related exhibitions. There are three exhibition halls indoors and two exhibition areas outdoors. The first floor of the exhibition hall includes a flower book cafe, flower shop, and main exhibition hall, and the second floor consists of a flower academy and cafeteria. There is also a seminar room and press center for academic conferences. It is affiliated with the Goyang Flower Culture and Arts Center, which offers various flower culture classes, and is located within Ilsan Lake Park in Goyang-si, so you can tour the lake park after viewing the exhibition hall event.
price: Free (6,000 won during the flower fair)

title: Goyang Cultural Center
description: Goyang Cultural Center opened in 1984 and has been leading the development of Goyang City's traditional culture through preservation, discovery, cultivation, and dissemination of Goyang's history and culture. Goyang Cultural Center plays the role of cultural guardian of Goyang City by conducting permanent traditional cultural performances and cultural arts forums (classes). Additionally, a digital library is in operation and traditional wedding ceremonies can also be held.
price: Gagok class: 150,000 won (3 months) Gayageum sanjo: 140,000 won (3 months) Gyeonggi folk song: 100,000 won (3 months), etc.

title: Goyang City Juyeop Children’s Library
venue: Goyang Goyang City Juyeop Children's Library
description: Jooyeop Children's Library has a total area of ​​2,049㎡, one underground floor and three above-ground floors, and consists of a children's book resource room (Book Love and Treasure Complex) filled with over 100,000 books, a multi-story room with computer access, and a social gathering place where performances and events can be held. As a library that emphasizes the concept of global culture, it presents a future vision to children through foreign fairy tales that express images of various lifestyles and cultures around the world, a story room where you can feel the old Korean emotions, a multi-story room, and a Bitgeum fairy tale room. It is inspired by the Mandaeru Pavilion of Byeongsan Seowon and has an architectural meaning that is similar to the structure of a hanok with a yard and bare feet. It is a pretty library that boasts wide windows, an interesting two-story structure, and a cute palace-like architecture. It is operated as a space that provides happiness to children, serving as a book playground.* Opening date: June 28, 2007

title: Goyang City Literary Center
description: Goyang City Arts Center is located in the same place as Goyang City Hall and Goyang City Council, and is a complex cultural space with a total of 334 seats that opened in 1989. It is equipped with improved convenience facilities and a stage system through remodeling in 2020, and is a cultural and artistic space where citizens take the lead by serving as a medium through which art can fill the daily lives of citizens. You can apply for rental at a time determined by the Goyang Cultural Foundation, and you must apply through the Goyang Cultural Foundation website (you can apply after registering as a member of the Goyang City Cultural Center). You must attach and submit a rental application form, performance plan, and a copy of your ID card, and approval notification will be individually notified in writing (via fax or email). The rental fee is relatively cheap. This place is not normally open and is only used when there are performances or events. It is mainly used for events such as various contests, training and education, and lectures.

title: Goyang Hangang Park
description: Goyang Hangang Park is a relaxation space with a walking path and a large lawn plaza with the Han River in the background. The walking trail connected to the DMZ Peace Road is good for a light walk while feeling the cool river breeze and fresh greenery, and the wide lawn along the Han River is good for enjoying a leisurely picnic with lovers, family, children, or alone. There are historical sites and tourist attractions nearby, such as Haengjusanseong Fortress, so exploring them together makes for a more enriching outing.

title: Goyanghyanggyo
description: Goyang Hyanggyo is a Hyanggyo that was founded during the reign of King Sukjong in the late Joseon Dynasty in Goyang-dong, Deogyang-gu, Goyang-si, Gyeonggi-do. Hyanggyo is a national educational institution during the Goryeo and Joseon Dynasties that was established for the education and enlightenment of local residents by holding memorial tablets of great Confucian scholars and holding ancestral rites. It is located on the eastern foot of Daejasan Mountain, and is a cultural heritage site that retains the traditional architectural beauty, starting with Hongsalmun Gate, Hanok buildings such as Myeongryundang, and walls, chimneys, and tiles. Although the detailed history after its founding is not told, it has been repaired several times, and the fence was repaired in 1970. The existing building is centered around the five-room Daeseongjeon Hall and includes the East House, Study Room, and Naesammun Gate, but there is no Myeongnyundang Hall. In Daeseongjeon, there are memorial tablets of five saints, and in Dongmu Seomu, memorial tablets of the 2 prefectures of the Song Dynasty and the 18 prefectures of Korea are enshrined. During the Joseon Dynasty, instructors were provided with fields, slaves, and Jeokjeok by the government to teach students, but now the educational function has disappeared. A memorial service is held in the spring and fall, and incense is burned on the first day and the first full moon. One Jeongyo (典校) and a funeral director are in charge of the operation. This Hyanggyo is designated as a Gyeonggi-do cultural property. Major experience programs include the Goyang Confucian Etiquette School, where you can learn proper manners and the spirit of a scholar through a scholar experience at a local school, and the Little Scholar Pungryu Playground, where you can have fun and enjoy a variety of traditional games.

title: Gonjiam Rental Shop I-One
description: This is I-One, a Gonjiam rental shop located near Gonjiam Ski Resort. We aim to rent good quality products at reasonable prices, not just blindly low prices.  You can rent not only skis/boards and clothing, but also gloves, helmets, protectors, and goggles. The space has been configured for maximum efficiency so that you can quickly rent equipment and clothing in a space of approximately 80 pyeong. The changing room has been expanded and remodeled to allow for neater use, and parking is available for more than 20 cars in front of the store.  We also have a variety of equipment including button step-on boards, inline skis, hammer decks, short skis, and advanced skis.

title: Gonjiam rental shop, good equipment house
venue: Gwangju Gonjiam rental shop, good equipment house
description: Konjiam Rental Shop Equipment Good House is located closest to the Konjiam Resort Ski Resort, making it convenient to use from rental to return. It is updated every year with the latest clothing and equipment, and is fully equipped with equipment suitable for all levels, from beginners to advanced. Thanks to the spacious and comfortable store environment, a big advantage is that even if you visit without a reservation, you can rent right away without waiting. In particular, we provide thorough assistance in setting up equipment so that beginners can enjoy skiing safely and happily.

title: Konjiam Resort Ski Resort
description: Konjiam Resort Ski Resort is the largest premium ski resort in the metropolitan area, located 40 minutes from Seoul. It is equipped with top-level facilities such as a total of 8 wide slopes, high-speed lifts, and cutting-edge snow removal systems, and provides differentiated ski services such as Korea's first 'part-time lift ticket', 'slope quota system', and 'ski mobile quick pass' to provide a more comfortable and premium ski life. In addition, there is a ‘panoramic slope’ that beginners and intermediate skiers can use from the top, so they can experience longer and more thrilling skiing. In addition, it brings joy by introducing content that allows people of all ages and genders to enjoy representative winter leisure sports in a more diverse way, such as premium ski lessons, the ‘fun slope’ loved by many skiers, the ‘large photo zone’ in the clock tower plaza, and the ‘snow sledding slope’.

title: Gongneungcheon
description: The place where Gongneungcheon begins is the boundary between Goyang-dong and Sindo-dong in Deokyang-gu and Jangheung-myeon in Yangju-si, and passes through Gwansan-dong, Sarihyeon-dong, and Jiyeong-dong before meeting the Han River at Gyoha-myeon in Paju-si. (Total length 30.5km). It is called Gongneungcheon, named after Gongneung, located in Samneung, Paju. The surrounding sedimentary plains are used as flower complexes and rice fields. It is a river that flows through Yangju-si, Goyang-si, and Paju-si, Gyeonggi-do and is the first tributary of the Han River. If you walk along the sound of the powerful running water of Gongneungcheon, you can easily encounter winter migratory birds such as egrets and flocks of geese, as well as natural monuments such as mandarin ducks and ducks.

title: Shared Brewing Venture Center Suljium
description: It is the first alcohol culture complex in the country to manufacture a variety of alcoholic beverages such as beer, rice wine, distilled liquor, and fruit wine using local agricultural products such as rice and grapes produced in Gapyeong, and to provide education, exhibition, and tasting spaces. We operate a variety of one-day experience programs such as makgeolli, distilled liquor, bangsho, mother liquor, and making alcohol bread, and when touring the brewery, you can sample alcoholic beverages produced directly at Suljium.

title: Gongju Gongsanseong Fortress [UNESCO World Heritage]
description: Gongsanseong Fortress is a representative castle of the Baekje period and is a fortress of Baekje that protected Gongju when the capital of Baekje was Gongju. It was the capital of Baekje until the capital was moved to Buyeo in the 16th year of King Seong's reign (538), and was the center of local administration until the Joseon Dynasty, making it an important relic of great historical value. It is a valley-shaped mountain fortress surrounding the valley of a hillside along the Geumgang River. It was originally an earthen fortress, but was remodeled into a stone fortress during the Joseon Dynasty. The date of its construction is not exact, and it was called Ungjinseong Fortress during the Baekje period, Gongjusanseong Fortress or Gongsanseong Fortress during the Goryeo Dynasty, and Ssangsusanseong Fortress after King Injo took refuge during the Yi Gwal Rebellion (1623) during the Joseon Dynasty. Immediately after the fall of Baekje, King Uija stayed here for a while, and it was also a base for the Baekje revival movement. During the Unified Silla period, Kim Heon-chang's Rebellion (822) occurred. It is rectangular in shape, about 800m from east to west and 400m from north to south. Gate sites can be found in four rooms, with Jinnamru, the south gate, and Gongbukru, the north gate, remaining. Only the ruins of the east and west gates remained, and in 993, Yeongdongru was restored on the east gate site, and Geumseoru was restored on the west gate site. Defense facilities such as Ammun, Chiseong, Godae, Jangdae, and Sugumun remain, and within the fortress are Ssangsujeong, Yeongeunsa, Yeonji, Imryugakji, and Manharuji. In addition, many relics, including lotus-patterned roof tiles, Baekje tiles, and pottery, as well as relics from the Goryeo and Joseon periods, were excavated. If you walk along the fortress wall, you can see the city of Gongju at a glance. During the Baekje Cultural Festival, you can cross the bridge from in front of Gongsanseong Fortress to Geumgang New Government Park. At Geumseoru, you can see the majesty of the Baekje Kingdom through the ‘Woongjinseong Guard Changing Ceremony’, and at Geumgang New Building Park, you can enjoy the beautiful night scenery of Gongsanseong Fortress.

title: Gongju King Muryeong’s Tomb and Royal Tombs [UNESCO World Heritage]
venue: Gongju King Muryeong’s Tomb and Royal Tombs [UNESCO World Heritage]
description: The Royal Tomb of King Muryeong and Wangneungwon, a historic site, are a collection of tombs of kings from the Ungjin period (475-538) of Baekje. There are a total of seven tombs in this area, including the tomb of King Muryeong, and they are located on the southern hillside of the Geumgang River. Across the valley, to the west are King Muryeong's tomb and tombs No. 5 and No. 6, and to the northeast are tombs No. 1 to 4. Tombs 1 to 6 were investigated during the Japanese colonial period, revealing the structure and form of the tombs, and King Muryeong's tomb was discovered during the repair work of tombs 5 and 6 in 1971. Tombs 1 to 5 are cave-type tombs made of stone, a representative tomb style of Baekje, while Tomb 6 and the tomb of King Muryeong are brick tombs, a tomb style that was widely popular in China at the time. The brick tomb is a new type of tomb that has never been seen before in Baekje, and is evidence of Baekje's active exchanges with the Southern Liang Dynasty of China. In particular, stone masonry and ceramics influenced by China, wooden coffins made of Japanese gold pine, and accessories symbolizing exchanges with Thailand and India were discovered in King Muryeong's tomb, providing a glimpse into Baekje's high-level international cultural exchange capabilities.

title: Gwacheon Cultural Center
description: The Gwacheon Cultural Center is a place that discovers, transmits, and preserves the local culture and traditional culture of the Gwacheon region, and conducts various cultural events and social education programs for Gwacheon residents. In addition, it manages cultural assets in the Gwacheon area, studies local history, opens a cultural school, a history and culture academy, and an experience sharing school to run various programs and hold cultural events. In the cultural school, there are gayageum classes, knot classes, literary painting classes, and samulnori classes, and in the experience schools, there are village miscellaneous activities, imaginative design activities, and walks. In addition, the Gwacheon Cultural Center hosts the Korean Chusa Calligraphy Exhibition and the Invitational Calligraphy Artist Exhibition. The cultural center has a reference room on the first basement floor, a part-time child care facility and an outdoor performance hall on the first floor, a local history center, a library, an open rest area, and a storage room on the second floor, and a garden and rooftop hall on the rooftop. Gwacheon Cultural Center's living culture center has an open space, a wind music hall, a soundproof practice room, a dance practice room, an audiovisual learning room, a meeting space, and a face-to-face space.

title: Gwacheon Citizen Center
description: Gwacheon Citizens' Center is a cultural and artistic performance hall located 135 meters away from Exit 10 of Gwacheon Government Complex Station on Seoul Metropolitan Subway Line 4. Befitting its reputation as the most livable city in the country, it boasts a beautiful and magnificent appearance in harmony with the natural scenery. It is a cultural, artistic, and sports complex cultural facility that opened on October 7, 1995. It is equipped with major facilities such as a large theater (929 seats), a small theater (380 seats), an outdoor performance hall, a gym, a bowling alley, a swimming pool, an ice rink, an indoor golf course, and a gymnasium, as well as auxiliary facilities such as a green shop, seminar room, conference room, and ice equipment store. In addition to cultural and artistic performances, there are various programs such as Taekwondo, yoga, aerobics, and ballet that help citizens enjoy leisure activities and improve the quality of life.

title: Gwanggyosan Mountain
description: Gwanggyosan Mountain is the main mountain of Suwon, protecting the city from the cold winds coming from the north of Suwon. Its original name was Gwangaksan Mountain, but it is said that it was renamed Gwanggyosan Mountain by King Taejo of the Goryeo Dynasty. Gwanggyosan Mountain is a mountain that stretches approximately 2km north to south between the Gyeongbu Expressway and the Seoul-Suwon road and is located in Sanggwanggyo-dong, Suwon-si. The ridge of the mountain is very quiet and gentle, and there are thick trees in between, making it a place where you can enjoy forest bathing or a day hike in peace. Since ancient times, Gwanggyosan Mountain has been called one of the eight scenic views of Suwon, and the beauty of the scenery of snow falling on Gwanggyosan Mountain and piled up on the trees, called Gwanggyojeokseol (光敎積雪), was selected as the first among the eight scenic spots. Until 1994, entry to the mountain was completely restricted in the fall (1 month) and spring (3 months) due to concerns about forest fires, but since the fall of 1995, it has been open year-round to provide residents with a rest area and expand opportunities for leisure use. In order to allow the forest environment to recover damaged hiking trails and natural scenery, the Gwanggyosan Mountain Rest Year System has been implemented in stages every three years since February 1, 2003.* Area 847ha, 582m above sea level (Sirubong)

title: Gwangmyeong Cave
description: Gwangmyeong Cave (formerly Siheung Mine), which the Japanese began developing in 1912 for the purpose of resource exploitation, was the site of conscription and exploitation during the Japanese colonial period and is an industrial heritage that retains traces of modernization and industrialization after liberation. Gwangmyeong Cave, which was used as a salted shrimp warehouse for 40 years after the mine was closed in 1972, was purchased by Gwangmyeong City in 2011 and transformed into a historical and cultural tourist attraction. Gwangmyeong Cave is evaluated as the best cave theme park in Korea that combines industrial heritage value and cultural value, and has achieved the miracle of an abandoned mine that surprised the world with more than 1 million tourists visiting each year. (Source: Gwangmyeong Cave website) ◎ Travel information to meet the charm of the Korean Wave - In the entertainment show <2 Days of Stone> and <Le Seraphim>, Le Seraphim members Chaewon, Yunjin, and Eunchae set out to complete a mission. This is the place I found. Gwangmyeong Cave, known as the best cave theme park in Korea, began development in 1912, and in 1972, Gwangmyeong City purchased the abandoned mine and transformed it into a tourist attraction.
