title: Gwangmyeong Cultural Center
description: Gwangmyeong Cultural Center was established in 1992 for the purpose of preserving traditional culture and developing local culture. We are contributing to cultivating citizens' cultural sensitivity and developing local culture by researching and disseminating local history, holding local cultural events, and researching and disseminating cultural and artistic programs. Children's culture school and adult culture school run programs such as violin, ballet class, pungmul class, calligraphy, Four Gentlemen, Gyeonggi folk songs, adult pansori, and Korean painting. The field trip program, conducted in connection with our hometown Gwangmyeong, is a cultural education program for young students who are starting to learn about the local community for the first time by directly visiting Gwangmyeong's local historical sites and cultural facilities to properly know and learn about the local history and culture, thereby fostering pride and local awareness as Gwangmyeong citizens. The Ori Cultural Festival has been held every year since 1992 to honor the local great man, Ori Lee Won-ik, and to foster pride in the hometown and local culture.

title: Gwangmyeong Upcycle Art Center
description: Gwangmyeong Upcycle Art Center is a complex art space where exhibitions, design education, and events are held under the theme of upcycling (adding artistic value to discarded items to create new works or products). Gwangmyeong Upcycle Art Center is the first upcycling hub in Korea, and is continuously conducting support projects, exhibitions, experiential education programs, contests, and performances to spread good art that does not end with one-time consumption but is practiced by creating other uses and values.

title: Gwangalli Beach
description: Gwangalli Beach is a beautiful beach located in Suyeong-gu, Busan. Featuring clear blue sea and fine sand, it is a popular attraction visited by many tourists during the summer. In particular, the scenery of Gwangan Bridge and the sea is beautiful, making it a famous night view spot. In addition to swimming in the sea, you can enjoy a variety of marine sports, and there are cafes and restaurants nearby, so you can spend a leisurely time enjoying delicious food. In addition, it is close to the city center and has excellent accessibility, making it a highly recommended place for travelers visiting Busan. Thanks to its variety of things to enjoy and convenient transportation, it is a tourist destination suitable for families, friends, and lovers alike.
priceDetail: Free

title: Gwangju Yangdong Market
description: Yangdong Market is a traditional market located in the western part of Gwangju and is the largest in Jeonnam. The origin of Yangdong Market is said to be a market held on the 2nd and 7th of every month on the white sandy beach under Gwangju Bridge in the 1910s. Yangdong Market is known as ‘the kitchen of Gwangju, the market with big hands’ to the citizens of Gwangju as it is filled with a wide variety of products and has an abundance of food, so much so that it is called ‘a symbol of generous people.’ People still say that you have to go to Yangdong Market to buy skates as it is the birthplace of holiday preparations, and Yangdong Market’s specialty, 『Yangdong Chicken』, which has often appeared in the media, can only be tasted here at Yangdong Market. It is a delicacy. In addition, during the May 18 Democratization Movement, Yangdong Market and Daein Market were places where Gwangju citizens demonstrated the spirit of unity and unity. At that time, merchants supported and encouraged the militia by providing them with rice balls, drinks, and medicine. As traditional markets began to decline due to the development of the distribution industry, Yangdong Market also began modernizing its facilities. We successfully carried out management modernization projects such as an integrated logo project, building an online shopping mall, and opening a merchant college, and it was clean and clear enough to win the grand prize for traditional market remodeling at the 『National Excellent Market Fair』, making it a space where you can shop without any problems wherever you go. In addition, Yangdong Traditional Market’s love for the region continues to this day. Yangdong Cheonwon Guksi, which provides lunch for the elderly at an affordable price, and Cafe ‘Moreless’ in River Market 276, which will be a dream creative center for disabled barista trainees, run experience programs such as cooking, crafts, and zero waste. The top 3 foods at Yangdong Market are Yangdong Chicken vs. Sunil Chicken, Yangdong Cheonwon Chicken, and lettuce fries. Nearby are the Yangnim History and Culture Village, the National Asia Culture Center, and the May 18 Memorial Park.

title: Gwanghalluwon
description: Gwanghalluwon is the garden of Gwanghallu Pavilion, which was created in the early Joseon Dynasty in Namwon-si, Jeollabuk-do. In the city near Namwon Station, there is Gwanghallu Pavilion, where Chunhyang and Lee Doryeong met, and the garden where Gwanghallu Pavilion is located is collectively called Gwanghalluwon. To the north of Nuwon, Gyoryongsan Mountain stands tall, to the south is Geumambong Peak, which is said to be as precious as a gold bar, and Jiri Mountain can be seen in the distance. Gwanghalluwon is the best pavilion in Korea that expresses a distant view of the universe, with Gwanghallu, symbolizing the Moon Palace, and Samsinsan Mountain, paradise on earth, on the edge of a pond symbolizing the Milky Way. It is one of the four major pavilions in Korea, along with Gyeonghoeru, Chokseokru, and Bubyeokru. Inside Gwanghalluwon, there are Gwanghallu, Ojakgyo, Wanwoljeong, Yeongjugak, Chunhyanggwan, Chunhyang Shrine, and Wolmae House. In addition, there are craft shops, There are auxiliary facilities such as a cafe. Lotus flowers, symbolizing paradise on earth, were planted in the lotus pond, and Ojakgyo Bridge, the bridge of love, where Gyeonwoo and Jiknyeo were unable to meet because they were blocked by the Milky Way, met once on July 7th, was installed over the pond. This stone bridge has four rainbow-shaped holes that allow water to flow on both sides, and is the most representative bridge in Korean gardens. At Chunhyang Shrine, a portrait of Chunhyang painted by artist Kim Eun-ho is enshrined. Every year, the Chunhyang Festival is held on Dano Day, May 5th of the lunar calendar.◎ Travel information to meet the charm of the Korean Wave This is a place where the palace where the Jade Emperor of Heaven lives in the legend is recreated on earth, and is a representative traditional pavilion in Korea. It is the filming location of various dramas such as <Woldam of Youth>, <Shurup>, and <The Joseon Lawyer>, and is the setting of <Chunhyangjeon>, a classic novel known to all Koreans, so Gwanghalluwon has long been the setting for a story that has dominated an era. I highly recommend taking a stroll around Gwanghallu Pavilion, one of the four major pavilions in Korea, and Ojakgyo Bridge of Love.

title: Gyodong-do Daeryong Market
description: Daeryong Market is an alley market that recreates the appearance of Yeonbaek Market in their hometown to make a living for residents who temporarily fled from Yeonbaek-gun, Hwanghae-do to Gyodong-do during the Korean War, to make a living as the Han River Estuary became a dividing line and they were unable to return to their hometown. Gyodong-do was the center of economic development for about 50 years, but now most of the displaced elders who created the market have passed away and the population has rapidly decreased, leading to a significant decrease in the size of the market. However, with the opening of Gyodong Bridge in July 2014, Daeryong Market, which looks like a 1960s movie set, has become a must-see for tourists to take pictures. Gyodong Giga Island (aka ‘Gyodong Bird’s Nest’) has been in operation since the end of March. Gyodong Bird’s Nest provides tourists with IT-based tourist information as well as bicycle and smartwatch rental services and various experience programs such as ‘VR video experience’ and ‘creating a Gyodong newspaper’.
address: 35 Gyodongnam-ro, Gyodong-myeon, Ganghwa-gun, Incheon Metropolitan City

title: Gurye Seomjin River Cherry Blossom Road
venue: Gurye Seomjin River Cherry Blossom Road
description: In early spring, when the yellow Cornus officinalis flowers are withering, white cherry blossoms, matching the clean riverside of the Seomjingang River, are in full bloom. This place, where the Seomjingang Riverside Cherry Blossom Festival is held, has been established since 1992, and white cherry blossoms are in full bloom along the riverside along National Highways 17 and 19, which connect Gokseong to Hadong. You can experience a wonderful drive while feeling the scent of spring, and it is also in the spotlight as an optimal marathon course. It is also a famous flower spot where the Gurye 300-ri Cherry Blossom Festival is held every March.
priceDetail: Free

title: Guryongsa Temple
description: This temple was founded by Master Uisang in the 8th year of King Munmu of Silla (668). The pond where nine dragons lived was filled in at the site of the main hall and the temple was founded and called Guryongsa Temple. However, it is said that it was renamed to its current name, Guryongsa Temple, in connection with the turtle rock legend in the mid-Joseon Dynasty. Also, according to the 'Chiaksan Guryongsa Historic Site', it is recorded that it was founded by Doseonguksa, a high monk of the late Silla Dynasty. Currently, a roof tile engraved with letters from the 45th year of Kangxi's reign has been excavated, showing that Guryongsa Temple was rebuilt in the 32nd year of King Sukjong's reign (1706). To the left and right in front of the main hall are Seosangwon, Bogwangnu, Jeokmukdang, and Simgeomdang's temples, as well as Wontongmun, Guksadan, Four Heavenly Kings' Gate, Beomjonggak, and Eungjinjeon. At the entrance to the temple, there is a stupa built during the Joseon Dynasty, and there is also a turtle rock that tells the legend of Guryongsa Temple and a Yongso under the waterfall. There is also a Hwangjanggeum sign made during the Joseon Dynasty, which prohibits unauthorized logging of pine forests around Chiaksan Mountain.
priceDetail: Free

title: Cloud Mountain Forest Bathing Area
venue: Gwangmyeong Cloud Mountain Forest Bathing Area
description: The forest bathing area located within Cloud Mountain is densely formed with a forest of trees about 20 meters high. The main facilities include a comprehensive play facility, a stream crossing, a flat bench, and benches, and it has the highest phytoncide concentration among the 13 forest bathing areas in Gyeonggi-do. With 356 fir trees planted and a 184m red clay trail created, it is gaining attention as a healing space that helps citizens and tourists relax, as they can experience the hiking trail barefoot. In particular, most of the forest paths connecting every corner of the forest bathing area are covered with wood chips, making it easy to walk.

title: Guri Wangsuk Sports Park
description: Guri Wangsuk Sports Park is a park created for citizens to rest and improve their physical strength. It is a complex sports and cultural space equipped with various exercise equipment and facilities such as soccer fields, tennis courts, and futsal courts. Originally a landfill, the site was stabilized for about 10 years. After 10 years of stabilization, 11.5 billion won was invested on a 57,479㎡ site to create sports park facilities and various auxiliary facilities to promote daily sports and utilize citizen leisure. In order to improve the basic physical strength of local residents, a sports park equipped with outdoor exercise equipment such as one artificial turf soccer field [6,262㎡], 17 tennis courts [11,027㎡], and one futsal field [800㎡], as well as convenience facilities such as walking trails, lighting fountains, sculptures, large green spaces, and concession stands, and rest areas have been created.

title: Guri Cultural Center
description: Established in 1991, Guri Cultural Center promotes local culture and arts and provides a space where local residents can enjoy cultural life. Main facilities include an exhibition room, multiple classrooms for culture school classes, a main auditorium, a library, and a rooftop sky garden. The cultural school operated by the Guri Cultural Center was opened in September 1995 and is composed of programs centered on pure culture and arts rather than entertainment-oriented courses with the purpose of realizing the cultural welfare of Guri citizens. Cultural school programs include traditional classes such as Korean dance, daegeum, pungmul, gayageum, and calligraphy, as well as general classes in acoustic guitar, saxophone, essay, and drum. You can apply for classes through the cultural center website. In addition, local cultural events such as the Donggureung Cultural Festival, Guri Beolmaldari Stepping, and Galmae-dong Dodang Gut are held, and Guri Cultural Magazine is published every month, and local history excavations, surveys, and research, and historical materials are collected and preserved.

title: Gubongdo
description: Gubongdo Island is an island connected by reclaimed land in Daebubuk-dong, Danwon-gu, Ansan-si, and was named so because it has nine beautiful peaks. As the name Daebudo Haesol-gil suggests, it is an island composed mostly of pine forests. If you walk about 1km northwest along the coastline of Gubong Island, you will come across two large rocks, which are called Gubong Seondol. The small rock looks like a grandmother and the large rock looks like a grandfather, so it is also called grandmother's rock or grandfather's rock, and although it is small, it is a photo point here. If you walk along the coastal road past the Gubonggi Seondol, you will arrive at the Ant Waist Arch Bridge. It is an arch bridge built on a narrow section like an ant's waist, and the sunset scenery here is so famous that it often appears in promotional photos of Daebu Haesol-gil, and Gubongdo is a representative sunset spot in the West Sea, as three of the nine scenic views of Ansan were selected as Gubongdo sunset spots.

title: Gwacheon National Science Museum
description: Gwacheon National Science Museum is an attractive science and culture experience facility where you can enjoy science and technology like play. It is the largest science museum in Korea and a landmark in the metropolitan area, making it easy to access as it is connected to a subway station near Seoul. Anyone can experience science in an easy and enjoyable way through various exhibitions ranging from basic science to cutting-edge technology in six permanent exhibition halls, special exhibition rooms, planetarium, and outdoor exhibition facilities. In addition, we are taking the lead in narrowing the gap between science and technology, which can be perceived as difficult and rigid, and the public, through science and culture events and experience programs that the whole family can enjoy.

title: Gwangju National Science Museum
description: The Gwangju National Science Museum is a central institution for the spread of science culture in the Honam region, located in Buk-gu, Gwangju. The main building's permanent exhibition hall, children's science hall, and artificial intelligence hall with the theme of light, sound, space, and the convergence of science and art are always in operation. In addition, special exhibitions on various science-related topics are held throughout the year, and scientific cultural events that allow people to enjoy science as a play in their daily lives are also held on a regular basis. The Gwangju National Science Museum also operates an educational program where students can naturally learn scientific principles through various experiments and experiential activities based on the scientific principles they learned at school. It is a place of learning and a place of relaxation for leisure where anyone, regardless of gender or age, can enjoy science through various programs for adults.

title: Buyeo National Museum
description: The Buyeo National Museum, located at the foot of Geumseongsan Mountain in the southeast of Buyeo city, was established in 1929 by the ‘Buyeo Historic Sites Preservation Society’ and is a cultural property of Baekje. The Buyeo National Museum began by collecting relics and displaying them in the guest quarters of the Joseon Dynasty government office located south of Busosan Mountain. From 1939, it was called the ‘Buyeo Branch of the Museum of the Government-General of Korea’ and finally received the name ‘Buyeo Museum.’ In 1970, a new museum was built at the southern foot of Busosan Mountain to display Baekje cultural relics scattered throughout the Baekje region, including the Buyeo region. On August 6, 1993, it moved to its current location and opened with a new look. Buyeo National Museum has four exhibition halls and an outdoor relic exhibition hall in an area of ​​61,429㎡ and displays about 1,000 relics. At the time of designing the building, the traditional Korean style was introduced and the permanent exhibition halls (prehistoric room, history room, Buddhist art room, and outdoor exhibition room) were placed with an octagonal courtyard at the center. In the prehistory room, relics from the Bronze Age and Iron Age excavated in the Chungcheongnam-do region, mainly in the Buyeo region, were displayed, and in the history room, relics from Baekje from the Sabi period and from the Three Kingdoms period were displayed. In the Buddhist art room, Buddhist artworks from Baekje during the Sabi period are displayed, and in the outdoor exhibition room, sculptures such as Buddha statues and stone pagodas are displayed.

title: National Institute of Biological Resources
description: The National Institute of Biological Resources, which opened in October 2007, is equipped with the largest facilities in Asia and is an institution that conducts basic research, including excavation and sampling of national biological resources. It oversees exhibitions and promotes the importance of preserving native organisms and biological resources on the Korean Peninsula. It is adjacent to the metropolitan area landfill in Gyeongseo-dong, Seo-gu, and has unique buildings that symbolize the institution, such as a water pipe modeled after the shape of a spine, a research building, an exhibition hall modeled after a leaf, and an education center. Korea's unique and native organisms are on display, and you can experience the real environment by reproducing forests, rivers, lakes, mud flats, and marine ecosystems. The outdoor green space is large and the walking trails are well-maintained.

title: National Institute of Ecology (Seocheon)
description: The Ecorium of the National Institute of Ecology displays over 1,600 species of plants and animals representing each climate, including the Tropical Hall, Desert Hall, Mediterranean Hall, Temperate Hall, and Polar Hall, which reproduce the world's five major climates, allowing visitors to vividly experience a living ecosystem. In addition, there are permanent thematic exhibition halls 1 and 2 where you can learn the basic concepts of the ecosystem, a special exhibition hall where ecosystem topics are held, an eco lab where ecological education is provided at each level, a children's ecology writing room, and a 4D video theater. The outdoor exhibition areas include the Geumguri Area, where you can observe the characteristics of the wetland ecosystem, the Hadaram Area, which reproduces forest vegetation for each climate zone in Korea, the Ancient Continent Area, which reproduces the habitat of Korea's representative deer, the Native Fish Area, where you can enjoy various types of egrets and ducks flying in the wild, the Eco Care Center, which is a quarantine facility to prevent highly pathogenic avian influenza and the protection of internationally endangered animals, and the CITES Animal Protection Facility to protect internationally endangered animals that are smuggled and trafficked. etc.

title: National Arboretum
description: The National Arboretum is Korea's leading forest species research institute, established independently from the Forestry Research Institute's Central Forestry Experiment Station on May 24, 1999, to successfully promote the Gwangneung Forest conservation plan established as a government measure in 1997. It is responsible for various roles in plants and ecosystems. The National Arboretum conducts research, collection, propagation, and preservation of forest plants, and collection, classification, production, and storage of forest biological specimens. It also conducts exchanges and cooperation between domestic and foreign arboretums, exploration and securing of useful plants, and information registration and import and export management of forest plant resources. In addition, its mission is to educate and promote the public about forests and preserve Gwangneung Forest. To this end, we are focusing on establishing a national plant resources management system, installing and operating a plant conservation center, supplementing and expanding the functions of specialized arboretums, exploring and securing useful plants at home and abroad, establishing a forest biological herbarium, expanding public education and promotion, installing a specialized arboretum library, and ecosystem conservation management of Gwangneung Forest.

title: National Arboretum Forest Museum
description: The Forest Museum, as part of the National Arboretum, was built over a period of 1 year and 6 months from October 25, 1985 to April 5, 1987 for the purpose of collecting data on forests and forestry, conducting national guidance and field trips, classifying and identifying specimens, storing, exhibiting, and researching. The building is 4,617㎡ (1,400 pyeong) made of reinforced concrete with one underground floor and two above-ground floors. The exterior was built using modern new materials such as granite, a domestic stone, based on the traditional ideas of Korean architecture that adapts to nature. The interior was constructed using domestic materials from Gwangneung, such as pine tree and larch, and the front wall of the museum is a stone mural engraved with a modern sense of the Baekje era mural Sansumunjeon, expressing nature such as mountains, trees, water, rocks, and clouds in a harmonious arrangement. Exhibition Room 1 (Living Forest) presented a beautiful forest by introducing a living forest video system using video art techniques using multiple monitors. Eight monitors are installed on the symbolic zelkova tree. Five monitors installed in the lower part show images of plants, insects, amphibians, and mammals living on the forest floor, and three monitors in the middle part show leaves, fruits, flowers, and birds and butterflies. For 8 minutes, visitors can enjoy the entire forest that changes depending on the season along with sweet music. The second exhibition room (Forest Culture Center) is an exhibition space with two themes: history and wood use. In the introduction, various seeds were displayed based on the concept of seeds being the source of forests and human life. The history section displays various contents related to forests from ancient times to modern times, and the wood use section displays information about our ancestors' wood processing and use. In the third exhibition hall (multi-faceted video theater), there are videos containing the importance of forests and the importance of biological conservation, and the structural features inside the video theater more effectively convey the content contained in the video. Exhibition Room 4 (Forest Life Hall) consists of the following corners: [Evolution of Animals and Plants], [Ecological Forest Diorama], [Humans and Plants], [Humans and Insects], [Humans and Mushrooms], [Earth Threatened], [Efforts to Prevent Various Threats through International Cooperation], and [Gwangneung Forest]. Exhibition Room 5 (Korea's Nature) is a laminated lumber made from larch and pine trees and using urethane resin adhesive parallel to the direction of the fibers, and presented a method of utilizing thinning small economy. It is a meeting place and a resting place, and anyone can play fun computer games, such as guessing the difference between pictures of beautiful plants, and more. The special exhibition room is used as a place for forest environment education for the public and youth education by planning and exhibiting environmental and ecological photography exhibitions, Korean bird and water species exhibitions, insect exhibitions, miniature painting exhibitions, and wooden furniture and woodcraft exhibitions.

title: National ASEAN Natural Recreation Forest
venue: Yangju National ASEAN Natural Recreation Forest
description: ASEAN Natural Recreation Forest, located near Jangheung Recreation Area, is less than an hour away from Seoul, Incheon, Ilsan, and Uijeongbu, making it the most accessible natural recreation forest in the metropolitan area. In addition, in order to promote friendship between Korea and ASEAN and to encourage social harmony among foreign workers and multicultural families, ASEAN traditional houses were built under the theme and used as lodging facilities, allowing people to experience various overseas cultural experiences and forest experiences at the same time. The area around the recreation forest is dominated by oak trees such as Quercus Quercus, Quercus Quercus, and Oak Tree. There are large and small strangely shaped rocks along the valleys and ridges, and the valley leading to Angoryeong Recreation Area is dotted with small waterfalls and cows, creating a beautiful natural scenery.

title: National Yangpyeong Healing Forest
description: National Yangpyeong Healing Forest is located at 262-10 Hwanggeo-gil, Yangdong-myeon, Yangpyeong-gun, Gyeonggi-do, at the southern foot of Samgaksan Mountain (538m), and has excellent accessibility within an hour from the metropolitan area. It offers a variety of healing facilities and specialized healing programs for each target, such as Sabak Road (1.1km barrier-free deck road), hammock zone, cypress pool, thermal healing room, meditation hut, and unmanned health management system.

title: National Women's Dictionary Exhibition Hall
venue: Goyang National Women's Dictionary Exhibition Hall
description: On December 9, 2002, Korea's first women's dictionary exhibition hall was installed at the Women's Plaza in Daebang-dong, Seoul. It was registered as a national museum in 2012, and was relocated and opened at the Goyang City Government Joint Building on September 1, 2014. It functions as a complex educational and cultural space to highlight the role of women in history and people who contributed to the development of history and to raise public awareness of gender equality. It consists of a special exhibition room on the first floor, a permanent exhibition room on the second floor, a storage room, and a research room. It illuminates the history of women from ancient times to modern times. Using digital media, physical materials, and media art, it reproduces the flow of Korean women's history from Queen Seondeok, the first queen of the Silla Dynasty in 632, to modern times. In primitive ancient society, women exerted political influence through their roles as goddesses, priestesses, ancestors, and queens. During the Goryeo Dynasty, women not only served as household managers and managers, but also accumulated wealth by engaging in commerce and trade activities. In addition to the lives of women who were active in artistic activities such as literature and painting despite Confucian control during the Joseon Dynasty, we can also get a glimpse of the efforts of women in modern and contemporary times to secure women's suffrage, education rights, and job rights. Starting with a special exhibition on the theme of women's power and creativity in commemoration of the first anniversary of its opening in 2003, special exhibitions are held every year, and gender equality education for children and youth and women's history lectures for adults are also held. Residents of local communities such as Goyang City are volunteering, and applications are accepted and operated through the volunteer portal.

title: National Science Museum
description: The National Science Museum is a center of science and technology culture built under the theme of ‘harmony between nature, humans, and science.’ It was established to promote the scientificization of people’s lives and to contribute to the development of young people’s interest in science and technology and their creativity. This is a space where you can easily and enjoyably access science in your daily life, and a comprehensive scientific and cultural space where you can accumulate, inherit, and utilize scientific knowledge of the past, present, and future. It also plays a role in fostering creativity and serving as the foundation for creating a rational society. We provide the public with opportunities to experience science, technology, and culture through exhibitions, education, and various science events. Excavation and preservation of science and technology cultural heritage, exhibition and educational research activities, and exchanges and cooperation with science museums across the country are also actively carried out.

title: National Museum of Korea
description: The National Museum of Korea has received a lot of attention and love from people since it moved to Yongsan and opened in 2005. You can fully enjoy and enjoy seven permanent exhibition halls presented by era and theme, special exhibition halls showing a variety of contents, an exhibition commentary program that helps visitors understand, a children's museum where you can enjoy and learn with all five senses, various educational programs, and realistic content using cutting-edge technology. The permanent exhibition hall displays and provides 9,884 artifacts, and exhibits are changed periodically to accommodate external exhibition schedules and the preservation status of artifacts. In addition, efforts are being made to improve completeness in various fields such as collection and preservation of collections, which are the basis of exhibitions, and academic research. The National Museum of Korea is also a healing space in the city where you can have a leisurely and enjoyable time while strolling through the garden where beautiful flowers bloom depending on the season. In modern society, where everything changes rapidly, museums are a place where you can take a break and look back. You can enjoy the value of culture and daily life while enjoying leisure time with family, friends, lovers, or by yourself.

title: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Gwacheon
venue: Gwacheon National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Gwacheon
description: The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art is the only national art museum in Korea that simultaneously accommodates the trends of Korean modern and contemporary art and the trends of world art. It opened in the Small Exhibition Hall at Gyeongbokgung Palace in 1969 and was moved to the Seokjojeon Hall at Deoksugung Palace in 1973. In 1986, it was newly built and relocated to Gwacheon, which has international-scale facilities and an outdoor sculpture hall. The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (Gwacheon) has a unique building exterior with traditional styles, including an old fortress wall and beacon tower that go well with the beautiful scenery of Cheonggyesan Mountain, and the walls and stairs of a traditional village. It fulfills its role as a national art institution both in name and reality, including collection and preservation of art works and materials, exhibitions, research and research, and related international exchanges and dissemination of art activities and improvement of art culture awareness through education. You can also appreciate the works of domestic masters such as Nam June Paik, Lee Jung-seop, and Chun Kyung-ja, and there are various educational programs. There is a shuttle bus from exit 4 of Grand Park Station on the metropolitan subway to the museum, and you can also take the elephant train to the museum, and Seoul Grand Park is nearby.

title: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Seoul
venue: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Seoul
description: The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (Seoul branch) is an art museum that focuses on contemporary contemporary art. Following the Gwacheon Pavilion, which opened in 1986, and the Deoksugung Pavilion, which opened in 1998, the Seoul Pavilion, which opened in 2013, is located on the site of Sogyeokseo, Jongchinbu, Gyujanggak, and Saganwon during the Joseon Dynasty. The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (Seoul Branch), which was built using the [Yard] concept, is designed as a space where anyone can enjoy and relax. The inside and outside of the building are organically connected and designed to harmonize with the surrounding attractions. The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (Seoul Branch) is a complex art and culture center equipped with various facilities, including an exhibition room, digital information room, multimedia hall, and movie theater, and hosts exhibitions of Korean contemporary art and new media convergence exhibitions.

title: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Cheongju
venue: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Cheongju
description: Since its opening at Gyeongbokgung Palace in 1969, the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art has been making efforts to foster it as a famous place for art and culture in the central region by opening the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Cheongju, which was a reconstruction of an old tobacco manufacturing plant in Cheongju, Chungcheongbuk-do, in 2018. In 2019, it held a commemorative ceremony to celebrate its 50th anniversary and is growing into an open art museum in the world that shares art culture. The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Cheongju unveils Korea's first open storage facility built on the collections of art museums, government agencies, and art banks. An open storage facility can be said to be an expanded concept of an art museum where collections, which are the basic components of an art museum, are stored and opened to the viewer, allowing not only the public to appreciate a vast amount of works, but also to learn about the invisible functions of the art museum. (Source: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art website)

title: chrysanthemum
description: Gukhwado Island is located 28km southwest of Ujeong-eup, Hwaseong-si, Gyeonggi-do. The eastern part of the island is Seongmun-myeon, Dangjin-gun, and the north is an inhabited island adjacent to Ippado Island. It is an island fishing village whose main business is collecting clams and oysters and other seafood. Because the flowers bloom late and fall late, it was called Manhwado Island using the character 'man (晩)' for late, but it was changed to Gukhwado Island because it was an island where many chrysanthemums bloomed during the Japanese colonial period. In fact, wild chrysanthemums are in full bloom all over the island. Gukhwado Island is located 10 minutes away from Janggo Port by boat and 1 hour away from Gungpyeong Port, and is a small island that can be explored on foot in 2 hours. Although it is about 10 minutes away by ferry from Janggo Port, it is a little-known island. Gukhwado Island seen from Janggo Port looks like an uninhabited island due to the pine forest that covers the island. Gukhwado Island, which boasts scenery that is worthy of an outing, is good for a day trip, but you can also stay on the island for a day or two and enjoy the atmosphere of a quiet and simple fishing village and spend some time relaxing. A place where you can safely enjoy water play at a beach with a gentle slope and clear water, go out with your child with a hoe and catch a variety of seafood such as conchs and clams, or enjoy fishing on a fishing boat is Gukhwado Island, an isolated island of wild chrysanthemums that are breathtakingly beautiful.

title: Gunsan Modern History Museum
description: Gunsan Modern History Museum, located in Gunsan, the central city of modern history, is a specialized museum and local museum with the theme of Gunsan's modern and maritime culture, and is a space where visitors can experience the history and culture of Gunsan. Gunsan Modern History Museum is a museum that exhibits the old Gunsan, which was the center of maritime logistics distribution as a trading port in the past under the motto that ‘history becomes the future,’ and the nation’s largest modern cultural resources, showing the thousand years of West Sea logistics distribution and Gunsan, an international trade port reaching out to the world. The first floor is home to the Marine Logistics History Museum, Children's Experience Center, and Donation Exhibition Room, the second floor is the Modern Data Center and Citizens' Open Gallery, and the third floor is the Modern Life Center and Special Exhibition Room.

title: Gunpo Cultural Center
description: The Gunpo Cultural Center is a research center that takes the lead in the collection, preservation, and dissemination of Gunpo's traditional culture and local history materials. We strive to preserve traditional culture and arts, promote the development and promotion of culture and arts through local love and local cultural activities that are factors of the local community, and strive to create an atmosphere of civic harmony by promoting the emotional life of citizens and their pride as citizens of traditional culture through the establishment of a sound culture.

title: Gungpyeong Tourist Site
description: Gungpyeong Tourist Site is a space where pine trees and the atmosphere of the West Coast come together, and is widely known as ‘Gungpyeong Recreation Area’. On the Gungpyeong Marine Pine Colony Trail, you can walk while feeling the scent of a pine forest full of phytoncide, and at Gungpyeong Beach, you can enjoy the beautiful sunset along with the open sea. The promenade and beach area are always bustling with visitors who spread out tents or mats and enjoy picnics. During the summer, a mudflat experience program is operated and is even more popular with families.

title: Gungpyeong-ri Beach
description: Gungpyeong-ri Beach is a small white sand beach in front of Gungpyeong Port with a length of 2km and a width of 50m. Located at the tip of the Namyang Peninsula, a dense bear pine forest that is over 100 years old is located right in front. At low tide, you can enjoy a variety of experiences, including tidal flat experience and sea fishing, on a 2km mudbed. At high tide, you can enjoy swimming in the sea for more than two hours a day. In addition to this, you can enjoy the walking path along the beach in both directions, including Gungpyeong Port and the sea pine colony. At Gungpyeong-ri Beach, you can set up shade tents and parasols on the beach, and car camping is also possible. Chabak and chaknik can be used at designated locations (private land) for a fee, and cooking is also possible.

title: Gwonseon General Market
description: Gwonseon General Market, located in Gwonseon-dong, Suwon, is a traditional market in the form of a commercial building consisting of about 110 stores. It has served as a daily marketplace for local residents, stocking a variety of items such as agricultural products, livestock products, marine products, and industrial products, and there are a variety of food stores such as sundae and pig's feet concentrated there. Well-equipped parking facilities make it convenient to visit by car, and arcades are installed throughout the market, allowing you to shop comfortably even in inclement weather such as rain or snow. Thanks to the shaded interior environment, it is relatively cool even in the summer, and user satisfaction is high.

title: Gwimokbong
description: Gwimokbong (height 1,036m), located in the middle of Cheonggyesan Mountain and Myeongjisan Mountain, is an unnamed hill. Climbers call it Gwimokbong because it is located on top of Gwimok Pass. It is adjacent to Myeongjisan Mountain to the east, Cheonggyesan Mountain to the west, and Gangsibong Peak to the north. Compared to the height of the mountain, the overall slope of Gwimokbong is gentle and not rugged, so you can enjoy easy hiking. There are large and small waterfalls and waterholes on the halfway side of the hiking trail, and the surrounding area is surrounded by strangely shaped rocks and dense forests. It takes at least 3 hours to reach the top of Myeongji Mountain. If you climb to the top of Gwimokbong Peak, you can view Hwaaksan Mountain and Myeongjisan Mountain, the highest peaks in Gyeonggi-do.

title: Grand Joseon Busan
description: Grand Chosun Busan, developed by a culmination of the capabilities and experiences that Chosun Hotel has shared with customers over the past 100 years, provides a hotel experience through exploration and innovation of the essence of the hospitality industry. In the magnificent atrium, a space that embodies the sea, nature, and colors of the city of Haeundae, you can feel optimal comfort and enjoyment during your stay even if you come without any preparation. The unique dining options of Aria, Palais de Sin, Lounge & Bar, and Chosun Deli add to the pleasure of gourmet cuisine, and the three banquet halls located on the 5th floor can be used for various purposes, such as invitation events and weddings. Premium bedding is provided in all rooms to ensure a good night's sleep, and guests can enjoy relaxation in various relaxation areas such as the swimming pool and sauna. Chosun Junior is Grand Chosun's kids-specialized brand that provides memories for children and parents a comfortable rest and relaxation during their trip throughout the entire hotel journey, from check-in to check-out and beyond. The Kids Room, which offers a differentiated sense of luxury in a design that takes children into consideration, is designed with the theme of the sea, forest, and sky to stimulate the imagination and curiosity of young customers.
address: Grand Joseon Busan, 292 Haeundae Beach-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan

title: glow safari
description: Glow Safari, located within Starfield Anseong, is an indoor theme park with the concept of an animal-free safari. The exhibition space was created under the setting of communicating with ‘Glow Animals’, mysterious animals that bring light to the human world. Although there are no actual animals, it provides a unique experience of interacting with animals by utilizing realistic media technologies such as holograms, interactive systems, and projection mapping. Depending on the theme that changes depending on the season, cute animal characters such as pandas, polar bears, and red pandas appear, and there are photo zones for taking pictures throughout the space.

title: Geumgwang Lake Park
description: Geumgwang Lake Park is a neighborhood park located near Geumgwang Bridge on the west side of Geumgwang Lake. Geumgwang Lake is a landmark in Anseong that boasts beautiful and tranquil scenery in all directions, north, south, east, west, and north. It is a V-shaped valley-shaped lake with good fishing conditions, making it a famous spot for smelt fishing in winter. In particular, the direction of Geumgwang Lake Park and Water Fog Park, located on the west side of Geumgwang Lake, has a well-developed waterside deck for taking a walk around the lake, and is close to nearby commercial areas such as restaurants and cafes, making it a good place to explore. By car, it is about 10 minutes from downtown Anseong and 30 minutes from Pyeongtaek, so you can visit without burden even on holidays.

title: Geumneung Beach
description: Geumneung Beach, located in Hallim-eup, Jeju City, is directly connected to Hyeopjae Beach, a popular attraction in the west. It has a similar scenery to neighboring beaches, from the blue-painted sea to the cute-looking Biyangdo Island and soft-touch sandy beaches, but its charm is that it is less crowded and more relaxed. The parking lot is directly connected to the beach, so there is no need to worry about moving your luggage. The newly built shower room is convenient as it offers hot water showers. When visiting this place, it is recommended to go during low tide when the water recedes. When the sea water recedes far away, a wide, fine sandy beach is revealed. There are natural pools here and there with shallow water that are great for children to play in. Seaweed and small seaweed left behind by the seawater naturally become toys for children. Thanks to this, you can enjoy it even without any preparation. However, at the entrance to the beach, small broken shells are mixed with the sand, so it is recommended to wear water shoes if possible.

title: Geumsan Boriam (Namhae)
description: In 683, Master Wonhyo built a chodang here and met Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva while practicing meditation. After that, the mountain was named Bogwangsan and the chodang was named Bogwangsa. Later, Lee Seong-gye is said to have prayed for 100 days here and founded the Joseon Dynasty. In gratitude, in 1660, King Hyeonjong made this temple the royal temple and changed the name of the mountain to Geumsan and the name of the temple to Boriam. Boriam, located at the top of Geumsan Mountain, is a beautiful temple where you can see all the strange rocks of Geumsan Mountain and the scenery of the blue South Sea at a glance. Within the precincts, the Jwasundae Rock, where Master Wonhyo is said to have meditated, attracts attention, and the nearby rock cave called Ssanghongmun is known to be the best among the 38 scenic views of Geumsan Mountain. It is one of the three major places of prayer in Korea, along with Hongyeonam Hermitage at Naksansa Temple in Yangyang-gun, Gangwon-do, and Bomunsa Temple in Ganghwa-do, Gyeonggi-do. Believers flock to it every day. Geumsan Mountain is called the Rock Zoo for its outstanding scenery, Geumgang River in the South Sea, and many animal-shaped rocks. It is a mountain overlooking the harmony of the indigo sea and green fields. At the top of Geumsan Mountain, where you can enjoy the beauty of Hallyeohaesang National Park, is Boriam Rock, the most famous of Korea's three major prayer sites, which is said to have been founded by Master Wonhyo. In addition, each rock in Geumsan Mountain preserves legends related to Buddhism, and Boriam Rock is surrounded by strangely shaped rocks such as Daejangbong Peak, Hyeongriam Rock, Hwaeombong Peak, Ilwolbong Peak, and Sambulam Rock. The course that goes up to Boriam from the entrance to Geumsan in Sangju Village is the best hiking course that harmonizes the dense forest and the South Sea. When you stay overnight and watch the sunrise in Geumsan, the view is so spectacular that you can't help but feel the harmony of heaven and earth. By car, there is a road that goes over Angang Pass, from Beoksigol in Idong-myeon, past Bokgok Reservoir, to the 8th ridge of Geumsan. (Source: Namhae Culture and Tourism)
operatingHours: - Winter season (November to April) 05:00~16:00 - Summer season (May to October) 04:00~17:00

title: Gisan Reservoir
description: A reservoir built in Gisan-ri, Baekseok-eup, Yangju-si, Gyeonggi-do. This reservoir is built on an area of ​​148,760㎡ and has a storage capacity of about 878 tons. It is a reservoir surrounded by high mountains, boasting beautiful scenery, and is famous as a fishing spot where carp are easily caught, making it a place visited by many anglers. Additionally, a walking trail has been built around the reservoir, making it great for taking a walk while enjoying the natural scenery.

title: Giheungseong Museum
description: The Giheungseong Museum, located near Gangha Art Park, is a museum that displays 1,000 model works created by its founder, Kiheungseong, over 50 years. It is the only museum specializing in models in Korea. Professor Ki Heung-seong is a master of architectural models and is an expert in the production of model buildings such as modern architecture and industrial models, as well as exhibition planning for museums and exhibition halls. A variety of models, including architecture, civil engineering, automobiles, factory facilities, aircraft, and ships, are on display on the first basement and second floors. In the first exhibition hall on the first basement floor, you can see model works of traditional Korean architecture from the Three Kingdoms period to the Joseon Dynasty. Teacher Ki Heung-seong collaborated with experts and conducted thorough historical research to reproduce the scale based on facts. The second exhibition hall on the second floor displays modern and contemporary architectural models from the 1960s to the present, including construction, architecture, and urban development, in which Ki Heung-seong personally participated, as well as famous overseas architectural models such as the White House and Bruj Khalifa. Admission is free, and you can have a drink at the cafe on the first floor. The outdoor waterside park behind the museum has walking trails, sculptures, and an observation deck so you can enjoy the beautiful scenery of the Namhan River.

title: Gimnyeong Seongsegi Beach (Gimnyeong Beach)
description: This beach is located in Gimnyeong village, and is called Gimnyeong because its appearance from the sky is shaped like the Chinese character for pyeong (平). It was built with sand piled on top of a huge rock rock, and Seongsegi means a small castle to prevent invasion by foreign powers. The waves crashing on the white sand make a cool sound, and the cobalt-colored seascape makes you feel the beauty of Jeju's nature. While walking along the beach, you can observe the Gimnyeong wind power generators that are powered by the wind of Jeju. Nearby, the seaside rock fishing spot where you can easily catch sea bream and sea bream is a popular spot for anglers, and various caves such as Yongcheon Cave, Dangcheomul Cave, and Manjanggul are located nearby, allowing you to enjoy a cool summer getaway. Due to the unique topography of Gimnyeong Beach, a geotrail has also been created, and the geotrail is a walking path that combines the geological resources of each region and the history and culture of the village by utilizing the UNESCO Global Geopark.

title: Gimpo Daemyeong Port
description: The salty air penetrating the tip of your nose, freshly caught fish jumping around, fishing boats returning from the sea in time for the tide, and people snooping around the fish market and raw fish restaurant. This is Daemyeong Port, Daegot-myeon, Gimpo-si, where the fresh vitality of life is alive and breathing. It is located 30 minutes away by car from Gimpo Airport, so it is close to Seoul, and ship owners and fishermen directly run raw fish restaurants, so the price of raw fish is about 20% cheaper than in other ports, according to people in the port. The raw fish restaurants that lead from the entrance to Daemyeong Port are filled with fresh raw fish just caught in each aquarium, and the sight of nets being spread out and cleaned in various places allows you to realistically feel the characteristics of the port. Daemyung Port is the only port facing the coast of Ganghwa Island, where you can enjoy the beautiful seascape. It is in the spotlight both at home and abroad due to the Daemyung Type 2 Fishing Port project and the holding of the Big Catch Festival. Daemyeong Port is a place where you can enjoy the beautiful seascape and the atmosphere of a traditional port, so much so that it was selected as one of the ‘7 best winter seas recommended by the Korea Tourism Organization’ in 2001. Daemyeong Port, which faces Ganghwa Island across the Ganghwa Strait, is not crowded with tourists like Sorae Port or Yeonan Pier, and boasts a friendly atmosphere where you can enjoy the quiet atmosphere of a fishing village. In particular, Deokpojin, the historical site of the fight against foreign powers in the late Joseon Dynasty, is located nearby.

title: Gimpo Independence Movement Memorial Hall
venue: Gimpo Gimpo Independence Movement Memorial Hall
description: Gimpo City Independence Movement Memorial Hall opened in Yangchon-eup in 2013. It was built to inherit the spirit of the independence movement that took place in the Gimpo area and to honor our ancestors. The place where the memorial hall was created is where the Orani Market Movement took place in 1919, and it is a space where you can see at a glance materials related to the anti-Japanese movement in the Gimpo area. The permanent exhibition hall on the first floor displays a video reproducing the independence movement that took place in the Gimpo area and the history of the independence movement across the country, including Gimpo. The last letter sent by Ahn Jung-geun's mother, Mrs. Jo Maria, to Dr. Ahn Jung-geun and items donated by Dr. Ahn Jung-geun to the National Security Foundation are on display. In the special exhibition room, special exhibitions on March 1st Independence Movement Day and August 15th Liberation Day, as well as exhibitions on various other topics are held. In particular, in 2023, the Metaverse Virtual Exhibition Hall was opened, which reproduces the interior of the permanent and special exhibition halls of the Gimpo City Independence Movement Memorial Hall in virtual space after 3D modeling, and you can learn about the history of the Gimpo Independence Movement in a fun way by solving various missions.

title: Gimpo Cultural Center
description: Gimpo Cultural Center, located in Unyang-dong, Gimpo, Gyeonggi-do, opened in 1964 and is actively promoting cultural projects such as preservation, transmission, and excavation of Gimpo's history and local culture, cultural events, and traditional culture education. Main facilities include classrooms for cultural school classes, a data room, and storage, and affiliated organizations include the Gimpo Studies Research Institute and the Gimpo City Folk Art Preservation Society, which conduct research and research on local history and local culture. As a cultural program, Gimpo Culture College runs cultural classes where you can learn about traditional culture and scholar culture.
address: Hanok Village (Art House), 170-1 Modamgongwon-ro, Gimpo-si, Gyeonggi-do

title: Gimpo Art Village
description: Gimpo Art Village is a cultural and tourism complex where traditional and modern beauty coexist. Located at the foot of Modam Mountain, you can enjoy the quiet charm of a Hanok village and beautiful natural scenery at the same time. It consists of 17 hanoks, 5 creative studios, an art center, an outdoor performance hall, and a traditional playground, and various cultural and artistic activities take place. For citizens, it is a friendly place where they can experience culture in their daily lives, and for tourists, it is a special travel destination that they want to visit again.

title: Gimpo Art Hall
description: Gimpo Art Hall is a public art center in Gimpo City built to improve the quality of life of Gimpo citizens and promote culture and arts. It consists of a 503-seat performance hall, gallery, and seminar room, and operates a variety of citizen participation contents such as high-quality planned performances and exhibitions, cultural arts education, and ‘Culture Day’ programs. The performance hall is designed to be suitable for plays, chamber music, recitals, etc., and the exhibition hall can display works of various genres such as paintings, calligraphy, and sculpture, serving as a center for local artistic activities.

title: Gimpo Ginseng Rice Beer Gallery
venue: Gimpo Gimpo Ginseng Rice Beer Gallery
description: It is a famous place where you can enjoy ginseng rice beer developed using Gimpo ginseng and golden rice, which are special products of Gimpo. It also has restaurant facilities where you can enjoy a variety of dishes along with ginseng rice beer. You can also tour the Ginseng Theme Hall, where you can see the growth, growth process, and efficacy of ginseng, and the Promotion Hall, where you can see the beer manufacturing process. Gimpo Ginseng Rice Beer Gallery is located at the entrance to Ganghwa Island, making it ideal for sightseeing in conjunction with nearby Daemyeong Port, Deokpojin, and Hamsang Park.

title: Tomb of King Gimhae Suro
description: It is the tomb of King Suro, the founder of Geumgwan Gaya, located in Seosang-dong, Gimhae-si, and has been designated as a historic site. It is a circular mound with a height of about 5m, and there are buildings such as Sungseonjeon, Anhyanggak, Jeonsacheong, and Jegigo, which enshrine a deity, as well as stone monuments such as shrines and public monuments. The major historic sites of King Suro's tomb include Sungseonjeon, which houses the shrine, Anhyanggak, where incense and axes for use in the Spring and Autumn rites are stored, Napleung Main Gate, the main gate of the royal tomb, and Gujibong Peak, which is shaped like a group of 10 turtles. King Suro ascended to the throne as the founder of the Garak Kingdom in 42 AD, took Heo Hwang-ok, princess of the Yayuta Kingdom of India, as queen in 48 AD, and is the progenitor of the Kim clan of Gimhae. It is said that in the 13th year of King Seonjo's reign (1580), Heo Yeop, the governor of Yeongnam, renovated the tomb into its current appearance. Inside the royal tomb, there is a memorial tablet for King Suro and Queen Suro, which is a place for the soul of the deceased and refers to a picture or fat of the deceased. The tombstone in front of the tomb was erected in the 25th year of King Injo's reign (1647) in the Joseon Dynasty, and Sungseonjeon is the name given by the king in the 21st year of King Gojong's reign (1884).

title: Nari Farm
description: Nari Farm, operated by Yangju City, is a nature-friendly healing space with the largest bay myrtle flower colony in the country. Every year around September, the ‘10 Million Flowers Festival’ is held and many tourists flock to the area. During the two months from September to October when the festival is held, entry times to the farm are set, but after the festival ends, you can walk and pass as usual. On the deepening cool fall days, you can enjoy happy times with your family and lover.
priceDetail: - Yangju city area 1,000 won - Adults 7,000 won - Youth 5,000 won

title: Nakgang Waterway Park
description: Nakgang Waterway Park, located to the left of the entrance to the Andong Dam Hydroelectric Power Plant, was created with the purpose of providing a comfortable resting and healing space for visitors by creating forest paths and gardens that match the surrounding water environment. Metasequoia and fir trees grow around a small pond, and the stone bridge and path over the pond create an exotic scenery, so it is called Korea's Giverny. There are benches here and there under the trees, so it is a resting place loved by Andong citizens as well as tourists. Taking pictures at the photo zones hidden here and there will make you feel like you are Monet. In addition, there is a walking path around Andong Dam and a waterside deck leading to Wolyeong Park, making it a perfect walking course for everyday use.
priceDetail: Free

title: Naksan Park
description: Naksan Park is connected to Daehakro and Dongdaemun and is a park where you can enjoy history and culture. Naksan was also called Camel Mountain because its terrain resembles a camel's back, and it was also called Taraksan Mountain because there was a royal ranch that supplied milk to the palace. After the 1960s, the original appearance of Naksan disappeared due to citizen apartments and crowded housing, and the Seoul Metropolitan Government established a plan to restore Naksan. As part of this plan, a park conversion project was carried out and it opened as Naksan Park in July 2002. Naksan Park's central plaza has the Naksan Exhibition Hall, a central stage, and a concession stand, so it's great for taking a break, and there's a parking lot right below the plaza, so it's easy to get to the central plaza. Naksan Exhibition Hall is a facility located at the entrance to Naksan Park. It displays the origins of Naksan, historical figures, photos and models of Hanyangdoseong, and provides various information to citizens visiting Naksan Park. Park use programs related to Naksan and Seoul Hanyangdoseong are operated on weekends, and anyone can use them for free. On one side of the square is Naksanjeong Pavilion. Naksanjeong is a pavilion created during the restoration of Naksan Mountain and is a place with a great view of Seoul. It has established itself as a resting place for citizens where they can feel the beautiful atmosphere of Seoul Hanyangdoseong and green forests, and is in the spotlight as a place where you can see the most beautiful night view in Seoul. There are various courses, including the Ihwa-dong Mural Village with houses and murals from the top of the hill, the Dongdaemun course to Heunginjimun and Hanyangdoseong-gil, and the Hansung University entrance course where you can walk while looking at the entire exterior wall. ◎ Travel information to experience the charm of the Korean Wave - Animation <K-Pop Demon Hunters> This is one of the places where Rumi and Jin-Woo walk while talking in the Netflix animation ‘K-Pop Demon Hunters’. The cityscape of Seoul unfolding beyond the castle walls is impressively captured, conveying the emotions in the animation more deeply. If you actually visit, you will be able to see the panoramic view of Seoul at a glance along with the quiet castle road, providing a special experience.
priceDetail: Free

title: Naksansa Temple
description: Naksansa Temple is a representative tourist attraction in Yangyang-gun, Gangwon-do and a scenic spot with great historical value. It is an ancient temple founded by Master Uisang in the 11th year of King Munmu of Silla (671) and is considered one of the three major Avalokitesvara shrines in Korea, along with Bomunsa Temple in Ganghwa and Boriam Temple in Namhae. The temple, with its natural beauty overlooking the East Sea, is one of the Eight Scenic Scenic Spots of Gwandong (eight scenic spots in Yeongdong, Gangwon-do), and its beauty has been passed down in numerous classics and poems since ancient times. Naksansa Temple is a historical temple that has been rebuilt and restored several times and possesses several cultural assets. Well-known examples include the 16m high Seawater Avalokitesvara Statue, Uisangdae, a pavilion built on a coastal cliff and a famous sunrise spot on the East Coast, Hongnyeonam Hermitage overlooking the sea, the Yangyang Naksansa Seven-story Stone Pagoda (treasure), which was built during the Joseon Dynasty but inherited the Goryeo Dynasty style, and the Yangyang Naksansa Temple Seawater Avalokitesvara Avalokitesvara, a monument and a collection of reliquaries (treasures), where Buddha's relics and other reliquaries were discovered. In 2005, a large forest fire occurred, destroying about 20 buildings, including the bronze bell, which had been designated as a treasure. You can apply for a temple stay through the Naksansa Temple website. ◎ Travel information to experience the charm of the Korean Wave - <Rino Log> We recommend walking along the ‘road where dreams come true’ that Rino walked, placing a small stone on top of the numerous stone pagodas and making a wish.

title: Nanjicheon Park
description: Nanjicheon Park is one of the five theme parks of World Cup Park. At Nanjicheon Park, you can enjoy a wonderful view of ponds and streams in harmony with the fields. A variety of aquatic plants and flowers are well preserved, so flora that is not easily seen in the city can often be seen. It is a perfect place for a family outing as children can have fun running around with the beautiful nature in the background. In spring, you can also see a variety of flowers, such as rape blossoms and colorful tulips, filled with the scent of spring. Double cherry blossoms, boasting lovely flower clusters, are also in bloom, adding to the fun of walking.
operatingHours: Open all the time ※ Please call for details
priceDetail: Free

title: Southern Water Resources Ecological Park
venue: Bucheon Southern Water Resources Ecological Park
description: Southern Water Resources Ecological Park is an ecological park created by eco-friendly purification of sewage flowing in from the Yeokgok drainage area and Oryu 3 drainage basin. The pyramid waterway, Silgaecheon, and garden are centered around a large lawn, making it a great place to take a walk. There are a variety of sports facilities such as futsal courts, basketball courts, and inline skating rinks, which are used as exercise spaces for residents. In the summer, there is a water park that children can enjoy, and in the fall, the leaves change color, making it perfect for families to enjoy a picnic.

title: Namsan Seoul Tower
description: Namsan Seoul Tower was built for the future of broadcasting culture and the tourism industry as Korea's first comprehensive radio tower that combines the functions of efficient transmission and reception of broadcast waves and a tourist observation facility that takes advantage of Korea's traditional beauty. Just as world-famous towers have become symbolic entities of a country or city, Namsan Seoul Tower has also served as a representative tourist destination in Korea and a symbol of Seoul for the past 40 years. Namsan Seoul Tower has become an object of interest and love among citizens due to its height, unique structure, and shape, which can be seen from all over downtown Seoul, and is solidifying its position as the number one tourist attraction enjoyed by domestic and foreign tourists. Recently, as the name has increased as a filming location for various entertainment shows and dramas that have driven the Korean Wave, it is a place where domestic and foreign tourists constantly visit.
priceDetail: [Observatory] - Adults (age 13 or older) 26,000 won - Children (age 3 to 12) 20,000 won - Seniors (age 65 or older) 20,000 won

title: Namsong Art Museum
description: Namsong Art Museum is located at the foot of the clean valley of Myeongji Mountain and Yeonin Mountain in Gapyeong and is a comprehensive cultural and art exhibition space where you can enjoy the beautiful scenery of the countryside and art using various cultural materials. Starting with the opening exhibition in 2006, this place has consistently held exhibitions of works of various art genres. In addition to the rich artistic activities of director Namgung-won, a master painter, the museum has planned and exhibited works of art with aesthetic value based on the domestic and foreign works of art it has collected and managed. It has the appearance of a traditional Korean hanok building and is a four-story building with a total land area of ​​2,210 m2 and a total floor area of ​​1,498 m2. It has exhibition spaces on the first and second floors, an experiential learning space on the third floor, and an open exhibition room on the fourth floor. There is also an outdoor parking lot for the convenience of visitors, and nearby auxiliary facilities are the Scarecrow Village, a cultural experiential learning and artist rest area. Scarecrow Village is located in the valley of Myeongjisan Mountain in Gapyeong. It is a resort area where busy city dwellers can breathe in nature, which is like a mother's arms. It is a beautiful village built on 10,000 m2 of land to allow people to enjoy the scent of culture and art in abundance.

title: Namyangju Cultural Center
description: * Namyangju Cultural Center, a place that preserves Korea's unique culture * Namyangju Cultural Center was opened in 1982 and has been active in promoting culture in the local community by conducting research and research on local materials and holding local cultural events in order to develop, preserve, and transmit the unique culture of the region. Namyangju City has been at the center of the history of the Korean Peninsula for a long time, so it preserves numerous cultural heritages. It is located in the northeastern part of the metropolitan area and the central part of Gyeonggi-do. It is surrounded by Cheonmasan Mountain, Chuknyeongsan Mountain, Bulamsan Mountain, and Ungilsan Mountain, and is a naturally blessed area along the beautiful Han River. * Namyangju Cultural Center’s Dasan Cultural Festival * Among the cultural projects conducted by Namyangju Cultural Center, the most important cultural project is the Dasan Cultural Festival. Dasan Cultural Festival is a local festival that commemorates the achievements and Silhak ideas of Dasan Jeong Yak-yong, a great Silhak scholar in the late Joseon Dynasty. The contents include holding art, writing, calligraphy, and photography contests for kindergarten, elementary, middle, and high school students in the district, and the general public, thereby contributing to discovering talent and turning the arts and culture around. It also honors the spirit of Dasan by selecting and awarding the Dasan Mokmin Award to civil servants from related organizations in the district for serving citizens. In addition, the Dasan Thought Lecture is held to disseminate Dasan's ideology to local residents and transform it into a civic festival, providing an opportunity to experience various genres of culture and arts such as traditional art performances and various exhibitions.

title: Namyangju City Museum
description: Namyangju City Museum, located in Wabu-eup, Namyangju, was established to preserve the history and culture of Namyangju and opened in April 2010. It is equipped with a permanent exhibition room, special exhibition room, and education room, and outside, you can see an outdoor performance hall and stone artifacts. The permanent exhibition room displays everything from Paleolithic relics excavated in Namyangju to various folk relics from the Joseon Dynasty and modern times, while the special exhibition room presents various exhibitions with new themes every year. (Source: Namyangju City Museum website)

title: Namyangju Hangang Park (Sampae District)
venue: Namyangju Namyangju Hangang Park Sampae District
description: Sampae Hangang Park, located around 630 Sampae-dong, Namyangju-si, is a beautiful waterside park that people from all walks of life can visit and enjoy throughout the four seasons by providing seasonal flower and flower complexes, a children's garden, a musical fountain, and a water park to citizens. A flea market is also held every Saturday from spring to fall where citizens can participate and sell or exchange recyclable items. Sampae Hangang Park also has a bicycle path, so you can not only enjoy bicycle riding while enjoying the atmosphere of the Han River and Bukhangang River, but it is also a great walking course. (Source: Namyangju City Culture and Tourism website)

title: Namyang Lake (Namyang Hwangra)
description: Namyang Hwangra is a place where 1,211ha of reclaimed farmland was created with the completion of the 2,065m Namyang Seawall on December 20, 1973. Namyangho, an artificial lake, is a tourist attraction created with an area of ​​967ha along with the construction of an embankment and is one of the eight scenic views of Hwaseong. Rice produced in the Namyang reclaimed land contains a lot of alkaline components and boasts the highest quality among Gyeonggi rice. The vast fields provide different richness depending on the season, but in particular, the golden fields of autumn combine with Namyang Lake to add abundance and fullness. In winter, it becomes a very good habitat for black geese, which search for plant-based food. On a fall day, a flock of white-fronted geese settle down in a golden field, and mallard ducks settle near Jangan Bridge. Just by parking your car on the side of the road and opening the window, you can observe migratory birds in winter without any special equipment. It is also famous as an ice fishing spot in winter. And to the left of the entrance to the Namyang Seawall is Namyang Lake, and to the right is the sea. It is a unique place where you can see the sea and the lake at the same time.

title: Nami Island
description: Nami Island is a small island located in the middle of the Bukhangang River. Its administrative district belongs to Chuncheon-si, but the docks to enter the island are mainly located in Gapyeong, Gyeonggi-do. The unique entry method using a boat or zip line is attractive. The entire island is decorated like an arboretum, showing off different charms each season, including the metasequoia road, birch road, and ginkgo tree road. Equipped with various sculptures, exhibitions, cafes, and restaurants, it is an international tourist attraction visited by millions of domestic and foreign tourists every year to enjoy walking and relaxation.

title: Namhansanseong Provincial Park [UNESCO World Heritage]
description: There is Namhansanseong Provincial Park, which houses Namhansanseong Fortress, one of the four fortresses that once protected Hanyang. These were Gaeseong in the north, Suwon in the south, Ganghwa in the west, and Gwangju in the east. In Gwangju to the east, there was Namhansanseong Fortress. It is located on Namhansan Mountain, 24km southeast of Seoul and 6km northeast of Seongnam City, with a total length of 12.4km (8.9km for the main castle, 3.2km for the outer castle, 0.2km for the Sinnam Fortress) and a height of 7.3m. There is a record that it was originally the royal castle of Onjo, the founder of Baekje, the son of King Dongmyeong of Goguryeo, about 2,000 years ago, and there is also a record that it was Jujangseong Fortress built in Hansanju in the 13th year of King Munmu of Silla (673) when the Silla-Tang War was in full swing. It is said that it was rebuilt several times in later generations using the old site, and was built in earnest during the reign of Gwanghaegun of the Joseon Dynasty (1621). Namhansanseong Fortress, built with stone walls, has a circumference of about 12km. Natural stones were used to stack the large stones on the bottom and the small stones on the top. There were 4 gates, a gate tower, and 16 secret gates in each of the east, west, south, and north, and there were poles in 4 places in the east, west, south, and north. Inside the castle, a fishery office was established, a government office, warehouse, and temporary palace were built. The temporary palace to accommodate in times of emergency consisted of 73 rooms for the upper palace, 154 rooms for the lower palace, and 26 rooms for the left palace, with a total of 252 rooms. 80 wells and 45 springs were built, and the administrative office of Gwangju-eup was also moved into the fortress. At this point, you can guess the importance of Namhansanseong Fortress and the population it can attract. The number of people who participated in the mobile training that was first conducted after the fortress was built (1639, 17th year of King Injo’s reign) was 12,700. However, only a few buildings remain in the castle now. The eastern and southern gates, Seojangdae, Hyeonjeolsa Temple, Yeonmugwan, Janggyeongsa Temple, Jisudang, Yeongwoljeong, Chimgwaejeong, Sungnyeoljeon General Iseo General Shrine, Bo, Ru, and Dondae remain. Among them, the four main gates, Sueojangdae, and some castle walls in the middle of the west gate are well preserved in their original form. Namhansanseong Fortress is designated as a historic site and provincial park.
