title: Mangwon Hangang Park
description: Among the Hangang River Parks, which are a resting place for Seoul citizens, Mangwon Hangang Park is located at the northern end of the river between Wonhyodaegyo Bridge and Seongsandaegyo Bridge, and is adjacent to Mapo-gu. The berm has a well-developed resting area, including a lawn and a walking path, and various exercise facilities and bicycle paths are also provided. You can visit with friends and loved ones and have some relaxation time. In addition, water leisure activities such as windsurfing, water skiing, and motor boating are conducted on the water, and there are cultural heritage sites such as Mangwonjeong Pavilion and Jeoldusan Shrine nearby, and it is connected to the World Cup Stadium and Incheon International Airport.
priceDetail: Free

title: Mangwolsa Temple (8 scenic spots in Uijeongbu)
venue: Uijeongbu Mangwolsa Temple 8 Scenic Spots in Uijeongbu
description: Mangwolsa Temple is located on Dobongsan Mountain, which has beautiful and outstanding rock peaks such as Jaunbong, Manjangbong, Seoninbong, and Jubong. There is a course that goes from the ticket office to Daewonsa Temple, Wonhyosa Temple, and Gwangbeopsa Temple in order, and a course that follows the Wondobong Valley. From Mangwolsa Temple, whichever of the two hiking trails you climb, you will reach Podae Ridge. Mangwolsa Temple was founded by Monk Haeho in the 8th year of Queen Seondeok's reign (639), the 27th queen of Silla, at the queen's order to commemorate the prosperity of the royal family. At that time, it was named Mangwolsa Temple to pray for Wolseong (月城) in Seorabeol. Many great masters of fortune have passed through this place since ancient times, and many famous monks such as Hyegeo and Yeongsodaesa from the Goryeo Dynasty and Cheonbong, Yeongwol, and Doam from the Joseon Dynasty stayed here, and it is a place where Zen scholars such as Mangong, Hanam, and Seongwol, who are called modern Taoists, stayed. If you go up the hill to the southwest from the main shrine of Mangwolsa Temple, you will find the Buddha statue of State Preceptor Hyegeo (Gyeonggi-do tangible cultural property). Even now, many monks are practicing meditation. If you go over the hill to the southwest from the large shrine of Mangwolsa Temple, you will find the stupa of State Preceptor Hyegeo. A stupa is a stone pagoda that enshrines the relics or remains of a famous monk, and is usually built near a temple. This stupa, which enshrines State Preceptor Hyegeo’s relics, is octagonal in shape. The overall height is 3.4m and the circumference of the tower is 3.1m. Looking at the overall shape of the pagoda, it consists of a spherical pagoda body placed at the stylobate, a roof stone, and an upper ring. The stylobate is composed of a foundation stone and a pedestal stone. The foundation stone is made of an octagonal three-tiered stone and is 80cm high. And then a false lease was placed on top of it. The body of the tower is shaped like a ball, and grooves are carved on the top of the roof stone and the bottom of the roof stone to ensure stability of the entire tower. The roof stone, including the bokbal and the orb, is made of a single stone, the falling surface represents the roof shape of a wooden building, and there are a total of eight ear flowers. The upper part has a roof stone and a single stone, and the characteristic feature is that the lotus flower pattern is engraved on the upper surface. State Preceptor Hyegeo, the main character of Budo, was of the Noh clan and served as a state preceptor during the Goryeo Dynasty as Hongso. However, Haengjang is not well known to the world.

title: Cicada Castle
description: Geoje Maemi Fortress is a wall built by Baek Soon-sam, who lost his home due to Typhoon Maemi in 2003, to protect his farmland from natural disasters. After farmland was washed away by a typhoon, he built a castle by himself over a long period of time by stacking square stones one by one near the beach and filling in the gaps with cement. The resulting Cicada Castle was not just a breakwater or fence, but had a unique appearance reminiscent of the European Middle Ages. Thanks to this unique scenery, which creates a rare exotic atmosphere, Maemisung Castle has now become one of Geoje's tourist attractions, and with photo zones everywhere, it is considered a good place for visitors to take pictures of their lives.
priceDetail: Free

title: Maetan Park
description: Maetan Park in Suwon City is a park created in 1989. It is located in a densely populated area of ​​apartments and is in the spotlight as a resting place for citizens. The park has sports facilities such as a multi-purpose playground, tennis court, badminton court, and basketball court. Multipurpose playgrounds are often used as event venues for companies, religious organizations, etc. In addition, there are convenient facilities such as a senior citizen center, mineral spring, and restrooms. The forest is thick, making it a suitable place for forest bathing.

title: Maehyang-ri Peace History Museum
description: It was used as a fighter jet shooting range by the U.S. Forces Korea for 54 years from 1951. The name ‘Kuni’ at Kuni Shooting Range originated from the U.S. military mispronouncing Goon-ri, the old name for Maehyang-ri. As it was a shooting range, various bomb remnants remain. It was reborn as a cultural and artistic space to publicize the pain of the Korean War. There are works made from shells and shell casings that are remnants of bombing training, such as the Statue of Peace.

title: Maehyang-ri Peace Memorial Hall
description: Maehyang-ri Peace Memorial Hall, a symbol of peace that overcame long pain, was established to remember the painful history of Maehyang-ri and to convey the value of peace to future generations. After the outbreak of the Korean War in 1950, Kuni Shooting Range was established in Maehyang-ri for shooting training by US military units. Until the closure of the Kuni Shooting Range in 2005, the roar of military aircraft and the sound of shells continued to be heard in Maehyang-ri Village, and residents had to live in pain due to casualties and environmental pollution caused by accidental explosions and unexploded bombs. After the Kuni Shooting Range was closed due to the active struggle of residents, the barbed wire surrounding the Kuni Shooting Range and some buildings were preserved to remember the pain of the past and the history of the closure movement, and in 2016, the Kuni Shooting Range was registered as Korea's first 'excellent architectural asset'. The famous Peace Memorial Hall, designed by world-renowned architect Mario Botta, is located on the right side of the site. Mario Botta, who values ​​‘connection with the past,’ designed a shape that embraces the entire Kuni Shooting Range site without encroaching on the existing Kuni Shooting Range buildings, and designed the current semicircular building. The memorial cenotaph located in front of the corridor of the memorial hall is a structure in which circular passages are vertically repeated. It is a cenotaph in memory of the victims, and functions as an observatory overlooking the Kuni Shooting Range, Nongseom Island, and the vicinity of Maehyang-ri. The Maehyang-ri Peace Memorial Hall consists of a permanent exhibition room that examines the process from the establishment of the Kuni Shooting Range to its closure, a special exhibition room that presents exhibitions planned by researching various topics related to the history and culture of Maehyang-ri, and a children's experience room. In addition, an exhibition room has been created in some of the existing buildings of Kuni Shooting Range, which is listed as Gyeonggi-do's No. 1 outstanding architectural asset, so you can view unique and lively exhibitions.

title: Meditherium
description: Meditherium is a medical-themed cultural space located near Paju Book City and is operated by Gunja Publishing, a publisher specializing in medical books. The purpose of this place is to acquire basic knowledge and relieve fears about medicine, which is inseparable from our lives. To this end, it is equipped with a cafe and bookstore where you can access medical books, a medical history museum, and a medical experience center where you can enjoy medical experiences such as playing a doctor, so you can read, learn, and experience medicine. In particular, the Medical History Museum displays medical tools and specimens used in the past, and at the Medical Experience Center, you can also learn CPR, which is essential in emergency situations. Nearby are tourist attractions such as Odusan Unification Observatory and Heyri Art Village, and Unjeong City and Jayu-ro are adjacent, making it easily accessible.

title: Myeongdali Valley
description: Myeongdali is the name of Dume Mountain Valley Village located in Seojong-myeon, Yangpyeong-gun, Gyeonggi-do. This village is considered a remote area of ​​Gyeonggi-do and is untouched by development. Even now, only a small number of people are guarding this place. This is why Myeongdali Valley at the foot of Samtaebong Peak preserves its pristine, ancient natural ecology. Because of the lack of foot traffic, this valley is still rich in a variety of wild flowers.

title: Myeongseongsan Mountain
description: This mountain is famous as a destination for silver grass hiking in the fall season. Myeongseongsan Mountain (922.6m), located 84km northeast of Seoul and about 7km from Uncheon, has Sanjeong Lake at the foot of the mountain, so you can enjoy hiking and the atmosphere of the lake. There is a legend that the joys and sorrows of Gungye, who founded Taebongguk, were hidden in the magnificent Myeongseong Mountain, which spreads out like a folding screen behind the lake. There is a theory that the mountain also cried as they cried over the sorrow of the fall of the country. There is also a legend that it is called Weeping Mountain because a servant and a horse who lost their owner to Wang Geon's servant cried so hard that the mountain cried. There is a legend that it is called Myeongseongsan Mountain by using the characters 'ul' and 'myeong'. Accordingly, starting in 1997, the Silver Grass Flower Festival at Sanjeong Lake and Myeongseongsan Mountain began to be held from late September to early October. With the development of a hiking trail in connection with the Sanjeong Lake tourist attraction, it is gaining attention as a hiking course preferred by professional mountaineers, beginners, and people of all ages. The view from the summit is Oseongsan Mountain to the north, Shanghai Peak, Daeseongsan Mountain, and Baekamsan Mountain to the northeast, Gwangdeoksan Mountain to the east, and Baekunsan Mountain and Gumgangbong Peak to the southeast.

title: Myeongji Valley
description: Gapyeong Myeongji Valley starts from the Myeongjisan County Park ticket office, passes Seungcheonsa Temple, and reaches Myeongji Falls. The water is clear and abundant, and many large and small reservoirs are distributed. This is where the water flowing down from Myeongji Mountain and Hwaak Mountain meet to form a 5km long valley. The water is so clear that you can see the bottom, and the water is cold enough to make you forget about summer. The water gets clearer as you go upstream, but it is too low for swimming, so most people enjoy swimming in the downstream. The depth of the water varies from shallow to deep, and the current is strong in some places, so you must wear a life jacket and play safely when playing in the water. It is easy to go down to the valley through the guesthouse at the entrance to Myeongjisan Mountain, and there is a path down to the valley next to the Dodae 1-ri Bridge. The parking lot at the entrance is also quite large, so you can park here or, when using public transportation, get off at the bus stop at the entrance to Myeongjisan Mountain and come to Myeongji Valley. Since there is little shade, it would be good to pitch a tent or shade cloth on a flat surface, and above all, it would be refreshing to take a dip in the valley water. The valley is wide, so you can enjoy it comfortably even if there are a lot of people. The water is clear, so it's good for snorkeling, and there are places for diving, so you can enjoy a variety of water activities. There is a tap at the top of the valley where you can wash your hands and feet, making it a convenient place to enjoy the summer with family and friends.

title: Myeongjisan County Park
description: Myeongjisan County Park is a designated county park on Myeongjisan Mountain, which straddles Buk-myeon and Jojong-myeon, Gapyeong-gun, Gyeonggi-do. There is an ecological exploration center at the entrance, where you can learn about medicinal herbs, rare plants, and wild flowers. There is a firefly cave, insect experience, plants, and fish on display, and various ecological experiences are possible. The hiking course starts at the end of Baekdun-ri, passes the 2nd peak of Myeongjisan Mountain, reaches the summit, and then descends to Ikgeun-ri via Seungcheonsa Temple. It takes about 6 hours. The second hiking trail starts from the Baekdun-ri bus terminal and passes through Ajaebi Hill and Myeongji 3 Peaks to the summit. It is about 6.5km long and takes about 4 hours and 20 minutes. Myeongjisan County Park carried out a Sky Cloud Bridge installation project inside the park in October 2019 and completed the first and second Sky Cloud Bridges. When you cross the skybridge, you will feel a different thrill from hiking. In spring, azaleas bloom here and there in abundance, and the 28km-long Myeongji Valley serves as a summer resort for travelers from the metropolitan area in the summer. The fall foliage is beautiful in the Ikgeun-ri Valley, Seungcheonsa Temple, and Myeongji Falls. This is because there are a lot of broad-leaved trees growing there. The course that goes from Sangpan-ri on the west side of Myeongjisan Mountain to the summit and down to Ikgeun-ri on the east side is an easy hiking course even for beginners.

title: Mona Yongpyeong Ski Resort
description: Mona Yongpyeong, located in the middle of Korea's Baekdudaegan Mountain Range, is located on a pristine plateau 700 to 1,500 meters above sea level that provides the most ideal biorhythm for the human body. It is called the Korean Alps and is about 200 km away from Seoul. Mona Yongpyeong, which started as Korea's first ski resort with modern facilities in 1975, is the ‘Mecca of Korean skiing’ and has played a leading role in the development and popularization of domestic skiing. Located at the foot of Balwangsan Mountain, 1,458 meters above sea level, it has an ideal location for skiing from mid-November to early April of the following year with an average annual snowfall of 250 cm. In addition, within the 5.2 million pyeong complex, various leisure sports facilities such as a 45-hole golf course, gondolas, swimming pools, and accommodations such as luxury hotels, condominiums, and hostels are in harmony with Mother Nature, making it a four-season comprehensive resort where you can enjoy a comfortable and pleasant vacation as well as leisure life away from daily business. The history of Korean skiing has developed along with Yongpyeong, and through the IOC Winter Olympics due diligence, It was evaluated as a world-class ski resort with complete hardware and software. Equipped with 28 diverse slopes including the Rainbow Slope, 14 lift facilities including a 3.7 km one-way gondola, and Korea's largest ski house (Dragon Plaza), Yongpyeong is used by the largest number of skiers in Korea. It is well-known internationally for successfully hosting the World Cup ski competition and the Asian Winter Games international competition for many years, and is also renowned among skiers and tourists from Japan and other Asian countries.
operatingHours: 09:00~23:00※ Please refer to the website for details

title: Moda Outlet Guri Namyangju Branch
venue: Guri Moda Outlet Guri Namyangju Branch
description: Moda Outlet Guri-Namyangju branch is an outlet that offers a variety of categories from fashion to food and beverage in one space. Located near Galmae Station, local residents visit it on a daily basis, and it is loved as a major shopping facility in the Guri and Namyangju areas. The brand composition was expanded through renewal in September 2025. Fashion, sports, living, and F&B brands are evenly distributed across four floors, so you can browse the products you need at once. The interior is neatly organized and provides a pleasant shopping environment, and it is relatively quiet, allowing for leisurely movement.

title: Moran Art Museum
description: The Moran Art Museum is a private art museum located in Maseok, Gyeonggi-do and opened in April 1990. The Moran Art Museum, which started out as a sculpture museum, has held various special exhibitions and currently introduces and exhibits not only sculpture but also various genres of art. The Moran Art Museum's outdoor sculpture exhibition hall is a space of approximately 8,600 pyeong, where works by famous domestic and foreign sculptors are displayed and various cultural events are held. The main building of the Moran Art Museum is a two-story building with six exhibition rooms where exhibitions are held. The storage and peony tower designed by architect Lee Young-beom are buildings that received a design award from the New York City branch of the American Institute of Architects, and can be said to be a place to store the museum's collections and materials as well as a sculpture. Inside the Peony Tower is the [Balzac] sculpture by Auguste Rodin (1840-1917), which was cast in plaster based on Rodin's original work at the Louvre's casting atelier. Moran Space (annex building) is a space that can be rented for cultural events and various exhibitions, and is where the Moran Museum's school and educational programs are held. At the Moran Art Museum, you can listen to exhibition explanations from professional commentators, and if you wish to apply, you can do so through the website. In addition, if you want to participate in exhibition-related programs, special education programs, and various cultural events, you can check detailed information and apply through the website. Not only indoor space but also outdoor space can be rented. The outdoor space (Area B) is rented out for wedding events, and other spaces are also rented out for performances, concerts, dramas and movie filming, etc.
price: * Individuals: Adults 7,000 won, Teenagers 5,000 won, Children 5,000 won *Culture Day (last Wednesday of every month), group viewing (10 or more people/advance reservation): 20% discount *Welfare card holders 5,000 won (65 or older, disabled, people of national merit, etc. / supporting documents required)

title: Mok-a Museum
description: Mok-a Museum is a private museum established to inherit and develop traditional Korean woodcraft and Buddhist art. It was founded by Park Chan-soo, Intangible Cultural Heritage No. 108 (Wood Carving). Construction began in February 1989, the exhibition hall was completed the following year, and it opened as a traditional crafts hall, followed by the construction of auxiliary buildings such as an arts and science laboratory, Sobanjeongsa, and an outdoor exhibition hall. It was officially opened in 1993 with the installation of the Maitreya Triad Buddha in the outdoor exhibition hall. The museum consists of an outdoor sculpture park and an exhibition hall on the first basement floor and three above-ground floors. The exhibition hall displays relics such as Buddhist statues, Buddhist paintings, and Buddhist woodwork, as well as Buddhist wood sculptures and woodwork works by Director Mok-a Park Chan-soo, and the outdoor sculpture park features the Maitreya Triad Buddha, Vairocana Buddha, White-robed Avalokitesvara, and a three-story stone pagoda in harmony.
price: Individual - Adults 5,000 won / Children, teenagers, seniors 3,000 won Group - Adults 3,000 won / Children, teenagers, seniors 2,000 won ※ National meritorious persons, disabled level 3 or higher - Free

title: Mokpo Coastal Ferry Terminal
description: Mokpo Coastal Ferry Terminal is a passenger terminal located in Hang-dong, Mokpo-si. It plays a role in connecting islands in the southwestern region of Jeollanam-do and Dadohaehaesang National Park. The waiting room can accommodate 1,738 people, and there are 7 shipping companies, including Namhae Express, Joyang Transportation, and Shinjin Shipping. Inside, it is well-equipped with convenient facilities such as a ticket office, information room, concession stand, snack corner, unmanned civil service issuance machine, nursing room, rest area, and restroom. In addition, the Mokpo Shinan Tourism Promotion Center is located in Building 2, where you can take a quick look around, and the 4th floor has a comprehensive culture and arts gallery and an outdoor garden, creating a space for resting.

title: Mokpo Marine Cable Car
description: Mokpo Marine Cable Car is a new central axis of marine tourism, leisure, and cultural tourism that provides a panoramic view of the beautiful scenery of Mokpo's original downtown, North Port, Mt. Yudal, as well as Gohado Island, the old center of Slow City Mokpo. Considering the topographical characteristics and excellent scenery of Yudalsan Mountain, it boasts the longest mountain in Korea at 3.23km and the highest height in Korea at 155m, offering a view of the original city center and the entire Dadohae Sea.

title: Monsterrium
description: Gimpo Monsterrium is a place where you can experience a zoo and aquarium in one place, and is located next to the Gimpo Fisheries Park cafe. It is also a famous filming location for the drama 'Weird Lawyer Woo Young-woo', and the exterior of the building, filled with the mysterious appearance of a swimming humpback whale, attracts visitors' attention. Here, you can see a variety of crustaceans, reptiles, rare animals, and even ancient fish. Although the scale is not comparable to large aquariums, the well-maintained transparent aquarium and clean indoor facilities give a pleasant feeling. You can take memorable photos at cute and fun photo zones located throughout the area. For children, the experience of feeding animals such as carp, turtles, rabbits, and alpacas is popular. At the reptile museum, you can also have the opportunity to touch the animals yourself. In addition, you can see the piraruq, the world's largest freshwater fish, which mainly lives in the Amazon River. If you go at the designated time, you can also enjoy the piraruq show. On the rooftop of the building, you can take the photo of your life at a place called the Stairway to Heaven, with the rooftop deck decorated with trick art as the background. The rooftop is also connected to the Fisheries Park cafe right next door, so it's a good idea to visit together.

title: Myojeoksa Valley
description: Baekbongsan Mountain is 589m above sea level, has a beautiful mountainous landscape, and is located along the Han River to the east, providing an excellent view. In the southern valley of Baekbongsan Mountain, there is Myojeoksa Temple, which is said to have been founded by Master Wonhyo during the reign of King Munmu of Silla. The long valley below is called Myojeoksa Valley. Myojeoksa Valley runs along a mountain path from Wolmun-ri, Wabu-eup, Namyangju-si, Gyeonggi-do to Myojeoksa Temple. After passing Myojeok Bridge, the valley begins in earnest. Many people visit the winding mountain road, which changes from narrow to wide depending on the section, and waterfalls with cool streams of water are formed here and there. Myojeoksa Valley is also undergoing changes due to the river gardening project that began in 2018. The water in Myojeoksa Valley is not deep, so anyone can enjoy swimming safely, and the depth of the water under the cool waterfall is about the knee level of an adult. It's great for family fun in the water.

title: Muju Deogyusan Resort
description: Muju-gun is an alpine region in Jeonbuk that contains Deogyusan National Park. Along with Jinan and Jangsu, Jeonbuk people also call these towns, the roof of Jeonbuk, collectively Mujinjang. The eastern part of Muju-gun forms a border with Gimcheon-si in Gyeongsangbuk-do and Geochang-gun in Gyeongsangnam-do. The Sobaek Mountain Range lies between them. During the Three Kingdoms period, the eastern part of Muju-gun was also the border between Silla and Baekje. Muju Deogyusan Resort, located at the foot of Deogyusan Mountain, boasts an area of ​​approximately 2.123 million pyeong. It is a four-season comprehensive resort for the whole family, and is equipped with an Austrian-style deluxe hotel called Tyrol, which suits the mountainous terrain, as well as family hotels and national hotels, providing comfortable accommodations for visitors and allowing them to enjoy a variety of leisure sports in the clean air.

title: Mujuchae Waterfall
description: Mujuchae Waterfall, located in Jeokmok-ri, Buk-myeon, Gapyeong-gun, Gyeonggi-do, is a waterfall formed by water flowing down the mountain range of the Gwangju Mountain Range, which starts from Domachibong Peak and continues to Gyeonchisan Mountain, Gangsibong Peak, and Cheonggyesan Mountain. It is located about 1km up past Yongso Waterfall. The waterfall flows down the rock wall, hits the rock, and falls like a spray of water. When viewed from a distance, it looks like unraveled white silk thread. It is located 34km away from Gapyeong-eup, and the area around the waterfall is well-organized with various forests, and it is famous for its fall foliage, which is as beautiful as the spectacular view of Seoraksan Mountain. There is a legend that in the past, military officers enjoyed drinking and dancing with vegetables as snacks, so it is called Mujuchae Falls, and the water is so cold that you feel cold even in the middle of summer. You can use the parking lot in front of Domachi Valley at Mujuchae Falls, and the path up there is well-maintained with deck paths and bridges, so you can walk while looking around comfortably and safely. As you climb the road, you can feel the fresh air with your whole body, and there is a bench installed in the middle of the road so you can rest if you are tired. Mujuchae Waterfall, which pours from the top of the rock, falls in two stages and is impressive with its grandeur and coolness. It would be nice to go here with the family and see the wonderful waterfall.

title: Muchangpo Beach
description: Muchangpo Beach is the first beach to open on the west coast in 1928. It is a beach with a 1.5km long white sand beach, 1~2m water depth, 50m white sand beach, water temperature of 22 degrees Celsius, and slope of 4 degrees. The surrounding area is dense with pine forests, making it a place where you can enjoy both sea bathing and forest bathing. Muchangpo Beach, which adds to the charm with its beautiful natural scenery of strangely shaped rocks and sea pine trees, is visited by many tourists every year due to the nearby sea fishing and abundant groundwater. In particular, here, a 1.5km sea road opens from the beach to Seokdaedo Island 2-3 times every month around the full moon and the last day of the lunar calendar. This is called the ‘Miracle of Moses.’ The opening of the Mysterious Sea Road in Muchangpo is a phenomenon in which the sea water is revealed during low tide due to the phenomenon of sea water splitting. When the sea road opens, it is very fun to catch crabs, clams, etc. along this road. If you climb up to the Muchangpo Observatory, located on a hill 50 meters away from the entrance to Muchangpo, you can enjoy a panoramic view of the mysterious sea road. With the phenomenon of water splitting as a motif, the Mysterious Sea Road Festival is also held every year in accordance with the sea road held on the first and last days of the lunar calendar. You can enjoy a variety of attractions such as celebratory performances by celebrities, a blow-blow fishing experience, and a mysterious sea road torch parade, as well as a variety of experiences such as bare-handed fishing experience, poisonous fishing ecology experience, clam catching experience, and crab meat catching experience.
priceDetail: Free

title: Mukho Port
description: Mukho Port in Donghae-si, Gangwon-do opened in 1937 and started as the first trading port on the east coast, but has now become a fishing base on the east coast. If you go to Mukho Port early in the morning when a fishing boat enters the port, you can buy freshly caught raw fish at the fish market, and it is also unique to watch the auction of the caught fish. Additionally, there are stores where you can shop for dried fish, etc. On Dongmunsan Mountain in Mukho Port, there is the Mukho Lighthouse, a manned lighthouse built in June 1963. The 12m high internal structure is made of two-story circular reinforced concrete, and the pure white lighthouse blends in with the blue sea to create a clear and clean image. A small park has been created around the lighthouse to provide a panoramic view of the sea, and as soon as you enter the entrance to the small park, a sculpture engraved with the words ‘From the Sun to the Boy’ is spread out widely.
priceDetail: Free

title: Mungyeongdansan Monorail
description: The longest monorail (3.6 km round trip) that allows you to tour the Baekdudaegan Mountain Range has been launched from Mungyeong, the best leisure sports experience tourist destination in the country. Dansan, which is said to have a flat mountain top that resembles a huge sky altar built by hermits in ancient times to offer sacrifices to the sky, is also famous for being a place where the sky meets, with good mountains, good water, and good air. Dansan, with its tourist and leisure spaces and beautiful natural scenery in all directions, is also in the spotlight as a filming location for various dramas such as the drama <Joseon Survival>. In addition to the monorail that can be enjoyed all year round, Dansan is growing into a true mecca of mountain tourism with a variety of experiences to enjoy, such as the starlight observatory around the summit of Dansan, a forest sledding slope, a forest camping site, a mountain bike road, Ojeongsan Mountain deck road, and a Doline wetland deck road.

title: Mungyeong Saejae Open Set
description: It is a filming set for the dramas <Kingdom>, <Red Sleeves>, and <The Moon Embracing the Sun>, and is connected to Mungyeong Provincial Park. The Gwanghwamun Set, which vividly embodies Gwanghwamun, is one of the most famous spots. Sets with various atmospheres, such as a hanok village, a low-income village, and a common people's village, are spread out over a large site, making it feel like time travel to the Joseon Dynasty. The motive for setting up the filming location in Mungyeong Saejae was, above all, because the mountainous terrain of Joryeongsan Mountain and Juheulsan Mountain is similar to Songaksan Mountain in Gaeseong, the capital of Goryeo, and the old roads are well preserved, making it a very suitable filming location for a historical drama. The current Mungyeong Saejae open set was completed on April 16, 2008, with production support from Mungyeong City, by demolishing a set set in the Goryeo Dynasty and creating a new Joseon Dynasty. The construction cost was 7.5 billion won, and 103 buildings, including Gwanghwamun, Gyeongbokgung Palace, Donggung Palace, Seoungwan, Palace Cabinet Temple, and noblemen's houses, were built on a 70,000㎡ site. There are 130 set buildings, including 22 existing thatched houses and 5 tile-roofed houses.◎ Travel information to meet the charm of the Korean Wave ‘Mungyeong Saejae Open Set’ is famous as a filming location for many historical dramas such as <Hwanhoon>, <Kingdom>, <Shuroop>, and <Moon Embracing the Sun>. The setting of this set is the Joseon Dynasty, and anyone who was curious about the Joseon Dynasty in the drama will be surprised by the vivid sense of reality as if they have stepped into the past. If you want to feel like you are in a historical drama, I recommend visiting the Mungyeong Saejae open set.

title: Mungyeong Saejae Provincial Park
description: This mountain, which crosses the ridge of Mt. Joryeong in the Baekdudaegan Mountain Range, has long been the highest and steepest hill on Yeongnam-daero, connecting the Han River and Nakdong River basin, and has been a key point for social, cultural, economic, and national defense. Saejae (鳥嶺) is also said to mean ‘a hill that is difficult for even a bird to fly over’ and ‘Sae (new jae)’ of a new hill. This place is famous for its beautiful natural scenery, historical ruins, folk tales, and folk songs. After the Japanese invasions of Korea, three gates (Juheulgwan, Jogokgwan, and Joryeonggwan) were installed in Mungyeong Saejae to serve as a fortress of national defense. The only remaining site, the winter site where travelers stayed, and the site of Gyogwijeong, where the new and old Gyeongsang provincial governors exchanged official seals, were rebuilt in 1999, and the Korean monument ‘Forest Fire’s Heart’, erected in the past to prevent forest fires, remains. It is a historical site steeped in various legends related to history, as well as the events of the Japanese Invasion of Korea, General Shin Rip, and Saddam left behind by Donghak and the Righteous Army. This area was designated and protected as a provincial park in 1981. Many cultural resources such as Hyeguksa Temple's Chungnyeol Monument, Joryeongwonji, and Donghwawonji, as well as natural scenery include Suok Falls, Yeogung Falls, Palwang Falls, and Yeongcheon Mineral Water. In particular, it is connected to Suanbo Hot Springs, Mungyeong Hot Springs, Mungyeong Island, Bongamsa Temple in Heeyangsan Mountain, and Seonyudong Valley, and is visited by many tourists. In addition, the plant resources observed in the Mungyeong Saejae area are classified by habitat and created under the theme of wet grass support, ecological wetland, ecological pond, dry grass support, and wild flower garden, and there is a natural ecological park and ecological maze park where visitors can engage in ecological learning and eco-tourism. There is a KBS filming site built by the Korea Broadcasting Corporation in Yongsagol behind the first gate of Mungyeong Saejae on February 23, 2000 to film a historical drama set in the Goryeo Dynasty. Mungyeong Saejae's Joryeongsan Mountain and Juheulsan Mountain are similar to Songaksan Mountain in Kaesong, the capital of Goryeo, and the old roads are well-preserved, making it a very suitable filming location for historical dramas. It has been the main filming location for KBS historical dramas such as Taejo Wang Geon, Morning of the Empire, The Age of the Unmanned, Dae Jo-yeong, and King Sejong the Great. It is also the location where films such as Scandal and Romantic Assassin were filmed, providing many tourists with things to see and enjoy.

title: Munsusan Mountain
description: Munsusan Mountain, located in the northwest of the Hannam Valley, is 376m above sea level and offers a cute mountaineering experience. It is also called the Geumgangsan Mountain of Gimpo due to its beautiful scenery in all four seasons. When you climb to the top, you can feel the pain of division as the waters of the Yeomha River and Han River flow leisurely below the mountain, and on a clear day, you can even see Songaksan Mountain in Kaesong, North Korea, across the Han River, almost within reach. At Munsusan Mountain, there is Munsusanseong Fortress, which was built in the 20th year of King Sukjong's reign (1694), the 19th king of the Joseon Dynasty, to defend Ganghwa Island against foreign enemies coming from the sea. You can feel the breath of our ancestors who resisted foreign invasions. There is a forest bathing area at the beginning of the hiking trail, which is perfect for a light rest and a walk while receiving phytoncide and negative ions.

title: Munsusan Forest Bathing Site
description: Munsusan Mountain is the highest and famous mountain in Gimpo. It is a scenic area with views of the Hangang Port and Seoul's Samgaksan Mountain to the east and the sea off Incheon in the distance to the west. The scenery is beautiful all year round and is called "Geumgang of Gimpo." It can be said to be a famous spot in Gimpo where you can enjoy forest bathing, a natural health method that involves walking in a lush forest and drinking the scent emitted from the forest, i.e., terpenes, essential oils, or putting it in contact with your skin. When you take a forest bath in Munsusan Mountain, your body and mind become clear and you feel stable. It is known to be effective in expectorating (removing phlegm), tonic, and constipation. It is also known to strengthen cardiopulmonary function. It acts on the circulatory system to increase blood pressure and stimulates the central nervous system to provide sedation. Munsusan Forest Bathing Ground, which provides various benefits such as emotional purification, mental and physical training, and fatigue recovery, consists of a hiking trail of approximately 4.6 km and a forest bathing trail of 1.4 km. Convenience facilities include an octagonal pavilion, benches, wooden huts, benches, outdoor tables, artificial trees, and lantern chairs, providing a comfortable space for citizens to relax. Equipped with sports facilities such as iron bars, parallel bars, forest bathing tables, crotch stretching, badminton courts, wrestling courts, volleyball, foot volleyball courts, and gateball courts, it can be said to be a resting area for citizens where they can engage in leisure activities. It is connected to Munsusanseong Fortress, which is about 4km long, and is a mountain education center with a history of resisting foreign invasions in the late Joseon Dynasty, making it the perfect place to feel the body odor.

title: Munan Mountain
description: * Munansan Mountain, a mountain suitable for family hiking * Munansan Mountain is a 533m mountain located in Hwado-eup, Namyangju City. There are two theories about the origin of the name Munansan Mountain. One theory is that it was named Munansan Mountain because there is a gate-shaped rock called Munbawi, and the other theory is that it was named so because the inside of the four main gates of Seoul can be seen from the ridge. Munansan Mountain is not steep, so you can hike it lightly. There is a course that starts from the 1st Geumnam Bridge, passes the summit, and comes down to Sambong-ri, Joan-myeon. You can also briefly go down to Baekwol-ri, Hwado-eup in the middle. The trail that passes through Munansan Mountain is the Munansan Trail, which is Course 5 of Dasan-gil in Namyangju-si. It starts from Ungilsan Station, goes around the village roads of Songchon-ri and Sambong-ri, passes Jaejaegi Pass, goes over the ridge of Munansan Mountain, and comes down to Piano Falls. There are many things to see along the route of Munansan Mountain, including the birthplace of Lee Deok-hyeong, a civil servant from the Joseon Dynasty, the Namyangju Studio Complex, the piano waterfall created at the Hwado Blue Water Center, a piano restroom, an environmental experience center, and an ecological park. Near the summit of Munansan Mountain and the ridge of the mountain, you can enjoy a view of the Bukhangang River and the outskirts of Seoul, including a rock called Munbawi. Although the mountain is low, it is located on the banks of the Bukhangang River, so the scenery is excellent and the hiking trail is not rough, making it a suitable hiking destination for families with young children. The biggest attraction of Munansan Mountain is Munbawi Rock. There is a first course that climbs to the top of Geumnam Bridge, passes through Musul in the north, and comes down to Sindangjae, and a second course that climbs to the top of Geumnam Bridge, then crosses 520 peaks and descends along the ridge to Sambong-ri in the south. The first course is about 9km and takes about 3 hours and 20 minutes, and the second course is 9.6km and takes about 3 hours and 45 minutes. There is also a short course that starts from Geumnam Bridge, climbs to the top, and then comes down to Baekwol-ri in the south. The hiking distance is 6 km and takes 2 hours and 30 minutes. There are park cemeteries and factories on the north side of the mountain, and there are few people.

title: Culture and Arts Center Maru Hall
venue: Pyeongtaek Culture and Arts Center Maru Hall
description: The Maru Hall of the Culture and Arts Center, located in Yongin Culture and Welfare Administration Town, opened in 2005 to promote the leisure and cultural life of Yongin citizens. It is operated by the Yongin Cultural Foundation, which was launched in 2011. The Culture and Arts Center is a building with 4 floors above ground and 1 floor underground, with a total area of ​​1,978 m². Yongin Cultural Foundation and several affiliated organizations are housed there, and it has a performance hall, exhibition hall, conference room, and Yongin Digital Information Library. In particular, it is equipped with facilities such as Maru Hall, a small theater that can accommodate 290 people (including 4 seats for the disabled), and an international conference room that can accommodate 180 people. In particular, Maru Hall has a stage area of ​​129.22 m² and was created to deliver the best sound by maximizing sound effects by reducing reflected sounds in the performance hall and maximizing reverberation. A variety of performances, focusing on children's plays and family plays, are held, and it is loved as a space where the whole family can enjoy cultural life comfortably. It takes about 4 minutes from Seoyongin IC and a 9-minute walk (462m) from Everline City Hall/Yongin University Station. Nearby are Everland, Korean Folk Village, Korea Job World, World Cultural Heritage Yunggeonreung Royal Tomb, Mulhyanggi Arboretum, Yongin Rural Theme Park, and Deokpyeong Dinosaur Arboretum.

title: Clear Water Arboretum
description: 'Mulmalgeum Arboretum' operated by Namyangju City. At the nature-friendly Arboretum in Sudong-myeon, you can enjoy a variety of plants in a beautiful scenery that changes with each season, and also enjoy the pleasure of directly observing various creatures living in the forest. In particular, the Mulmareum Arboretum, which was selected as a ‘Gyeonggi-do Wellness Tourist Destination’, operates in-depth and diverse programs. There are a variety of experiential activities tailored to different ages and interests, such as woodcraft experience, play forest (crafts made with natural materials), forest healing, forest interpretation in the children's forest, and firefly ecology learning center. Spend a special time relaxing to your heart’s content in the spacious and peaceful nature of Mulmareum Arboretum.

title: Mulmi Coastal Observatory
description: ‘Mulmi Coastal Observatory’, which serves as a place to rest, is another bunker for free travelers and is very popular. ‘Mulmi Coastal Observatory’, also nicknamed ‘Daejipo Observatory’ by local residents because it was built near Daejipo Village in Samdong-myeon, began construction in 2016 and opened in December 2019. Built with the concept of a lighthouse illuminating the South Sea, this place is cylindrical in shape with a 360-degree view, allowing you to enjoy the ‘feeling of floating in the sky.’ It consists of two floors. The first floor is a Namhae-gun specialty product store where you can buy a variety of items, and the second floor is decorated with a bakery cafe and a rooftop observatory.
operatingHours: 09:00~18:00 ※ Please call for inquiries as there is a possibility of seasonal change.

title: Water King Lake
description: Another name for Mulwang Lake, the largest in Siheung City, is Heungbu Reservoir. When the reservoir was installed in 1945, the administrative districts were Siheung-gun and Bucheon-gun, so the prosperity of Siheung and the wealth of Bucheon-gun were taken. It is the largest freshwater lake in Siheung City and a representative resting place. It is located near the metropolitan area, including Seoul, Anyang, and Ansan, and is surrounded by Mt. Gwanmusan (aka Seonginbong), Mt. Mahasan, and Mt. Unheung. A bicycle road was created between Podong Salt Farm and Mulwangho in 2003, and Suin Industrial Road is nearby, making transportation convenient and convenient facilities abundant. In 2023, the name was changed from Mulwang Reservoir to Mulwang Lake, and the rainbow that appears across Mulwang Lake after the rain is so beautiful that it is called a fresh scenery. The night view of the lake illuminated by colorful lights is beautiful, making you want to visit Mulwang Lake again. It is fun to visit hidden restaurants and colorful cafes in every nook and cranny, and the beautiful flowers and trees that bloom and fall each season are another attraction.

title: water garden
description: The Water Garden is a waterside park created as part of the Han River Restoration Project in 2012 and is a nature-friendly relaxation space where you can purify and heal your body and mind by communicating with nature. When you cross Baetnadeuri Bridge, the symbolic bridge of the Water Garden, a large flower complex has been created along the riverside promenade facing the beautiful Bukhangang River, where you can enjoy flowers in spring (poppy flowers) and autumn flowers (yellow cosmos). It's a great place to ride a bike, take a walk with your partner, or go on a family outing. (Source: Namyangju City Culture and Tourism website)
priceDetail: Free

title: Mulhyanggi Arboretum
description: Mulhyanggi Arboretum, located in front of Osan University Station on Line 1, is one of the representative arboretums in Gyeonggi-do, visited by more than 350,000 people annually. It was named Mulhyanggi Arboretum from the name of Sucheong-dong, which was said to be a place with clear water flowing since ancient times. The Gyeonggi Provincial Arboretum was built from 2000 to 2005 under the theme of 'Meeting of Water, Trees, and Humans' and opened in May 2006. Mulhyanggi Arboretum, built in downtown Osan City with an area of ​​34 ha, has a total of 1,930 species of plants in 24 theme gardens, including Mulhyanggi Forest Exhibition Hall, Water Drop Greenhouse, Warm Zone Botanical Garden, Bonsai Garden, and Rose of Sharon Garden, and is equipped with convenient facilities such as a visitor center, plant library, observatory, lawn, forest rest area, and nursing room. The arboretum is close to the subway station, has a gentle slope, has many rest areas such as shade and chairs, and has created a barrier-free sharing path, making it comfortable for people with transportation disabilities, children, and pregnant women to walk.

title: Museum Mountain
description: Museum SAN (Space, Art, Nature), hidden in the mountains, began construction with a design by Tadao Ando, ​​a master of minimalist architecture of exposed concrete, and opened in May 2013 with the final work of James Turrell, an artist of light and space. The museum begins with the Welcome Center and lawn parking lot along the trail and continues to the Flower Garden, Water Garden, Main Building, Meditation Hall, Stone Garden, and James Turrell Hall. The main building contains four wing structures connected into square, triangular, and circular spaces, embodying the architect's philosophy of connecting the land, sky, and people. In addition, the museum is running a variety of experiential and educational programs as well as permanent and temporary exhibitions. The Cafe Terrace, located on one side of the main building, is, as the name suggests, a good place to relax and enjoy the 360-degree view of the mountain. And at the meditation hall near the Stone Garden, you can relax your body and mind by concentrating on the aroma and the sound of the singing bowl, and enjoy a quiet time while appreciating the scenery through the curved window.
facilities: 웰컴센터 / 플라워 가든 / 워터 가든 / 뮤지엄 본관 / 스톤 가든 / 제임스 터렐관 / 청조갤러리 등

title: Mir Island
description: Mir Island, located in Gongju, is a beautiful island floating on the Geumgang River. It is a natural healing spot where various flowers brighten up the entire island every season. Starting with cosmos, a variety of plants such as pink muhly, dapsari, and sukrung harmonize together to create a spectacular sight. Especially in the fall, the pink muhly road along the island becomes popular, and the light pink waves blend in with the scenery of the Geumgang River, making it a popular photo spot. The trail across the flower field follows a gentle curve, and you can enjoy the harmonious scenery of the Gongju Railroad Bridge and the greenery of the mountain behind you while walking along the river. The road is well paved, so anyone of any age can take a walk comfortably. In particular, the deeper you go toward Gongju Bridge, the more beautiful the natural scenery becomes. It is a perfect space not only for families but also for people to enjoy a walk with their dogs.
priceDetail: Free

title: Mirinae Holy Site
description: Mirinae Shrine, located about 40 miles north of Anseong, Gyeonggi-do and called the beautiful Korean word for the Milky Way, is where the tombs of Korea's first priest, Father Kim Dae-geon, his mother Ursula, the third bishop of the Joseon Diocese who ordained Father Kim, Bishop Perreol, and Vincent Lee Min-sik, who buried Father Kim's body, are located side by side. This place came to be called Mirinae because Catholic believers hid here to escape the Shinyu and Gihae persecutions and formed a village of believers. At night, the lights coming from each house combined with the stream under the moonlight made it look like the Milky Way. Originally, Mirinae was one of the early Catholic missionary areas, including Gwangju, Siheung, Yongin, Yangpyeong, Hwaseong, and Anseong in Gyeonggi-do. When the parish was established in 1896, 50 years after Father Kim was buried in Mirinae, there were about 1,600 believers. Father Kim Dae-geon, who was martyred at the age of 26, was not even allowed to have a funeral by the government, so only 40 days after his execution, Vincenzo Lee Min-sik managed to remove the body and carry it on his back for a week, avoiding public attention, to bring it here to Mirinae and bury it. The full-fledged work to transform Mirinae into a sanctuary began in 1972, and the 103rd Saint Memorial Basilica was completed in 1989. When you enter the shrine, the first thing you see is the memorial cathedral standing in the middle of the shrine. This cathedral was built to commemorate the canonization of the 103rd person in the Catholic Church. On the Way of the Cross behind the memorial cathedral, there are 15 bronze sculptures depicting the process of Jesus being captured by Roman soldiers, hanging on a cross, suffering, dying, and being buried in a tomb. It takes 2 to 3 hours to tour the Mirinae Cathedral, where the tomb of Father Kim Dae-geon and the mandible (lower jawbone) are enshrined, the statue of Father Kim, the Cathedral of the Virgin Mary, and the Garden of Gethsemane (a garden made of natural rocks).

title: Mimesis Art Museum
description: Mimesis Art Museum has a land area of ​​1,400 pyeong, a total floor area of ​​1,100 pyeong, and consists of 3 floors above ground (1 floor underground). It is famous for its design that contains exhibition spaces of various sizes and numbers in one lump. The main feature of the white exhibition space, which is made up of various curved surfaces, is that it excludes artificial light as much as possible and brings in natural light, creating a soft and calm atmosphere, and allowing you to see the feast of light that changes from time to time. The Mimesis Art Museum does not lure visitors as a commercial exhibition space, but rather becomes a space that provides greater enjoyment than just the exhibition through the architecture itself. As Fernando Geha, a famous Portuguese architectural photographer, said that it will attract more visitors from all over the world than Brazil's Iberi Carmago Museum, designed by Alvaro Siza, the Mimesis Art Museum has been introduced to various foreign media even before its opening, and is having a great influence on domestic and foreign architects. Even now, there is a constant flow of visitors. Mimesis Art Museum plans to actively introduce ‘art that stimulates imagination’ in the future.

title: Misa Hangang Park No. 5
description: Misa Hangang Park No. 5 is a park along the Han River that is great for walking and exercising. It is equipped with a variety of facilities, including children's play facilities, a children's pool operated in the summer, a basketball court, and a grass plaza. The grass plaza also has a urethane track to help citizens engage in healthy activities. When you climb up to the observatory, you can see not only Hanam's Geomdansan Mountain, but also Namyangju and Yebongsan Mountain on the other side, and the open scenery in all directions is very beautiful.

title: Miho Museum
description: Miho Museum opened in July 2014 and contains the history of nature. Miho Museum is a place where you can learn about the past and present of the blue planet Earth, and it tells the story of the history of the Earth. It houses and exhibits a large number of animal and plant fossils from the Paleozoic and Mesozoic eras, including stromatolites, the first fossils of life on Earth. Additionally, a variety of mysterious minerals and insect specimens are on display. You can escape the gray city in the metropolitan area and feel the green nature, and in Dinosaur Village 1 and 2, where there are petrified wood and dinosaur exhibits, children welcome nature and dinosaurs as friends. You can engage in sensory and experiential activities with various exhibition specimens.
price: Adult: 11,000 won, Child: 10,000 won ※ Fees may vary, so please refer to the website or call for inquiries.

title: Mille Rock the Market
description: Mille Rock The Market, located in Suyeong-gu, Busan, is a complex cultural space operated by Borrier. There are escalators and elevators on both sides for convenient use. The graffiti on the wall you see as you enter creates an impressive photo zone. Aiming to be a differentiated open plaza-type experience space, this is a new lifestyle space that connects locals and culture. The space consists of Busking Square, a dream stage where anyone can be the protagonist, an ocean view stand where you can feel the Busan sea, and an F&B zone where you can experience high-quality domestic and foreign restaurant brands. Depending on the brand, some stores operate as pop-up stores for a set period of time, so if there is a brand you want to visit, it would be a good idea to check in advance before visiting.
priceDetail: Free

title: Sea Fragrance Arboretum
description: With the desire to preserve plant genetic resources and create a great forest recreation space on the west coast, Gyeonggi Province began the project in 2007 by establishing a basic plan to create an arboretum using provincial forests. Since then, steady efforts have been made to build various infrastructure facilities and a theme park, and it was officially opened in May 2019. Currently, about 300,000 plants of about 1,000 types are growing in the Sea Fragrance Arboretum, mainly plants from the coastal islands of central Korea. The total area is 300,000 pyeong (1,010,000 ㎡), and there are various unique theme gardens such as Sangsang Observatory, Sea Wave Garden, Rock Garden, and Rose Garden, which provide a view of the beautiful west coast scenery, as well as various recreational spaces such as a lily rest area and a small performance hall. Gyeonggi-do Sea Fragrance Arboretum will continue to strive to preserve plant genetic resources, which is the original purpose of the arboretum, and will continue to serve as a forest recreation space where one can experience the importance of the natural environment.

title: Baramsae Village Picnic Garden
description: Picnic Garden is a waterside park created in Gung-ri, Godeok-myeon, Pyeongtaek-si in 2013. Picnic Garden, which means ‘a garden where a smile (wind) stays,’ is a space where nature and people can come together to experience and relax in the nature of the Jinwi Stream. In 2018, the previously neglected island area was created into a themed island with four themes, including Ewha's Island and Garden of Light, so you can enjoy unique scenery and a unique night view through landscape lighting at night. You can enjoy seeing the sotdae and pinwheels installed here and there along the waterside deck and walking path, and experience and feel nature at the playground and various rest areas. (Source: Picnic Garden official website)

title: hill of wind
description: If you go down to the left on the way to Haegeumgang, you will come across Dojangpo Village, and to the north of that village is Windy Hill. The original name was ‘Ttibatneul’, but since 2002 it has been changed to ‘Windy Hill’. When you look at the sea from the hill, it is infinitely spacious and quiet, and the cool breeze gives you a refreshing feeling. Everything you see here has a leisurely, not boring feel to it. The island, the lighthouse, the cruise ship, and even the wind seem leisurely. It is the perfect place to throw the burden of your heart into the sea or let it blow away in the wind. A windmill was installed in November 2009 to provide tourists with something to see. (Source: Geoje Culture and Tourism website)
priceDetail: Free

title: Barunsaem Children’s Library
description: In Suwon City, in addition to general libraries, there are libraries exclusively for children: Wise Saem, Bareun Saem, and Wisdom Saem. Among these, Barunsaem Library is located in Maebong-ro, Yeongtong-gu, and is a knowledge information and cultural space established to help children, who can be said to be Suwon's future dreamers, grow into wise, wise, and upright children. We want to help growing sprouts have dreams, hopes, and curiosity, thereby improving their cultural experience and information mindset. This library also has a baby nest for toddlers, helping to create an atmosphere of reading books with parents from an early age.

title: Bounce Super Park Suwon Yeongtong Center
venue: Suwon Bounce Super Park Suwon Yeongtong Center
description: Bounce Super Park Suwon Yeongtong Center is located on the 3rd floor of the Fantasium building near Mangpo Station in Suwon, and unlike a typical kids cafe, it is a unique indoor playground that adults can also experience. It is divided into Zip Coaster, Giant Tower, Free Jump Zone, Net Play, Adventure Zone, Challenge Zone, Bounce Runner, Dunk Zone, Racing Zone, Multi-Court, Sports Arcade Zone, Super Trampoline Zone, and VR Zone, and is operated for 30 minutes each with facility inspection and charging. It is the first trampoline park in Korea, and it is mandatory to wear anti-slip socks for safety when using the trampoline. It is an indoor playground that adults can also enjoy, allowing them to understand childhood and increase intimacy with children. It is also popular as a date course for young people. It is a place where children can also enjoy special occasions such as birthdays, Christmas, and the end of the year.

title: half moon island
description: Bandalseom Island is named so because of its unique half-moon shaped topography. There is a long walking path along the waterway, so you can enjoy the ocean view while feeling the cool breeze. The scenery created by the open water and anchored ships provides a sense of openness that is difficult to feel in the city. There are restaurants and cafes scattered throughout, making it convenient to relax and eat. Bandal Island Cultural Park in the center of the island is a great rest area for taking a break while walking and is popular with families.

title: Firefly Village
description: Firefly Village is a typical mountain village located in Eomsori, Seorak-myeon, south of Gapyeong-gun, and boasts beautiful natural scenery. Eomsori, where the firefly village is located, was named 'Eomsori' because it is a neighborhood with many cows (puddles) that can be scary even during the day when you cross the many stone bridges and see large rocks and blue, deep water. It means to always live kindly and honestly with a solemn heart. A clear, clean and wide stream flows in the center of the village, and on both sides it is surrounded by pine pine forests, allowing you to breathe air rich in phytoncide. It is also a village that produces excellent agricultural products with fertile soil and abundant agricultural water. Most of the residents are engaged in agriculture rather than commerce, preserving the warm hospitality of our mountain village.

title: Banwol Lake
description: Banwol Lake is comfortably located in the innermost part of Daeyadong. It was completed in 1957, and the water from Jipye-gol, Saemgol, and Jijibawi-gol in the northwest flows in a southeast direction into Banwol Lake. While Baekun Lake in neighboring Uiwang is a clearly exposed terrain, Banwol Lake sits inward like a shy country girl and has a delicate beauty that seems to silently smile with its eyes. The small ridge across the lake creates a reliable water shadow all year round, and it is a quiet lake with a scarlet sunset at dusk.

title: Banwol Lake Park
description: Banwol Lake Park is a waterside park built on one side of Banwol Lake. As you walk along the trail, you can enjoy a relaxing time as the scenery of the open lake and surrounding greenery unfolds. Various sculptures, including large windmills and photo zones, are installed throughout the park, making them great for taking pictures, and you can take a break and enjoy some time on the bench. Sports equipment for simple exercises is also provided, making it popular with people of all ages.

title: Balang Reservoir
description: Balang Reservoir, located in Gwangtan-myeon near Jangheung Recreation Area, is an agricultural reservoir with an area of ​​165,289㎡ and a water depth of 4~5m, and is now a popular attraction as a reservoir fishing site. Balang Reservoir, also called Biam Reservoir, is especially beautiful at dawn when the fog rises. It is managed by the Korea Rural Community Corporation. It was created by blocking a valley at an altitude of 100m above sea level, so the surrounding scenery is beautiful and the water is clear and abundant in fish species such as crucian carp, carp, and persimmon, making it great for fishing. You can enjoy lure fishing by paying an entrance fee and stand fee at Balang Fishing Spot. Nearby are Jangheung Tourist Site, Gana Art Park, Duri Land, World Cultural Heritage Paju Samneung, Honey Land, Heyri Art Village, Paju Book City, Imjingak (Pyeonghwa Nuri Park), and First Garden.

title: Balan Manse Market
description: It used to be a place to sell special products and agricultural products from Hwaseong City, but is now used as a permanent market, and there are many foreign workers, so foreign food is easily available. As the birthplace of the March 1st Movement, the Balan Manse Mural Street has been created. Although it is a major transportation hub for all directions, the commercial district is gradually being modernized with the construction of new cities and industrial complexes.

title: Bangameori Beach
description: Bangameori Beach is located in Daebubuk-dong, Ansan-si, Gyeonggi-do, and is a good place to visit from the Seoul and Gyeonggi areas. The sandy beach is so wide that it doesn't get crowded even on weekends, and the sand is soft so it's good for walking barefoot. Even during high tide, the appropriate depth of the beach is good for swimming, and during low tide, it provides an opportunity to experience a vivid mudflat and walk along the moist mudflat. There is no additional cost for the mudflat experience, as long as you bring your own tools, and you can catch bamboo and crab. In addition, it is good to take a walk along the pine forest road next to the beach or enjoy the food culture street in Bangameori, where there are many restaurants and cafes with a nice atmosphere.

title: Banghwasuryujeong (Northeastern Pavilion)
description: Banghwasuryujeong (訪花隨柳亭), located on a high cliff adjacent to the east of Suwonseong Hwahongmun Gate, is one of the pavilions built during the construction of Suwonseong Wall in 1794 (the 18th year of King Jeongjo's reign). The official name is Dongbukgaknu, but the name Banghwasuryujeong was given because of its outstanding scenery, befitting the meaning of “looking for flowers and playing along the willows.” Once deteriorated due to a flood, it was rebuilt in 1848 and later extensively repaired as part of the Suwonseong Fortress restoration project. Banghwasuryujeong, which was designated a treasure in 2011, shows different appearances depending on the viewing position due to its unique plan and roof shape. For this reason, it is evaluated as the most original building in Hwaseong. The pavilion, where King Jeongjo rested during his journey to Hwaseong, offers a panoramic view of Yeonmudae and Dongbuk Gongsimdon to the east, and Janganmun Gate and Paldalsan Mountain to the west.
priceDetail: Free

title: Baedagol Theme Park
description: Baedagol has been called Baedagol since ancient times as a “village reached by ships.” Baedagol Theme Park began by cultivating lotus flowers to purify water to restore the natural ecosystem and raising carp to communicate with nature and people. The current theme park was created with the desire to make the present beautiful for future value. This is an experiential learning center where not only children but also adults can feel the importance of nature. There is a folk museum that operates all year round, a carp experience center, a futsal field, an alpaca farm, and a Nanta training center, as well as a swimming pool where you can cook in the summer. In the fall, we run Campnic, a night-free camping trip, and also run a chestnut and sweet potato experience center, and in the winter, you can even experience strawberry picking at a strawberry farm. In addition, there are places where children can play and experience activities in nature to their heart's content, such as sand play, archery, bunka and pedal carts, trampolines, 3D movie theater, sand art, big blocks, forest playground, bouncy ball zone, and sports zone, making it great for families to enjoy together.

title: Barron Holy Land
description: Baeron Shrine is a Catholic shrine from the late Joseon Dynasty located in Guhak-ri, Bongyang-eup, Jecheon-si, Chungcheongbuk-do. As the persecution of Catholics began in the late Joseon Dynasty, Catholics began to flock to Baeron in search of a place to hide, and a Catholic village for believers was naturally formed. During the Shinyu Persecution in 1801 (the first year of King Sunjo's reign), Hwang Sa-yeong wrote a white paper while hiding in a cave in Baeron, and was martyred that year. This is the area where Baeron Theological Seminary, Korea's first modern educational institution, was located from 1855 (the 6th year of King Cheoljong's reign) to 1866 (the 3rd year of King Gojong's reign). It is also the area where the tomb of Choi Yang-eop, who passed away in 1861 and became Korea's first overseas student and the second priest after Father Kim Dae-geon, is located, as well as the birthplace of Nam Jong-sam, a martyr in the Byeongin Persecution of 1866. Baeron Shrine belonged to the Gyeongseong Diocese in 1911 and then to the Wonju Diocese in 1968. It was developed in the 1970s and continues to this day. After liberation, Baeron became an important sacred site in Catholic history. Religious facilities within the Jecheon Barron Shrine include the Martyrs' House, St. Joseph's Cathedral, Hwang Sa-young's Martyrdom Tower, a priest's house and chapel, Father Choi Yang-eop's Memorial Cathedral, many annexed buildings, a cloistered convent, and the Salesian House, a social welfare facility. This is an important shrine in the process of establishing Catholicism in Korea, and pilgrims from all over the country are still constantly visiting the shrine.
priceDetail: Free (separate retreat program cost)

title: Baekgil Beach
description: If you stand on the vast sand of Baekgil Beach, you will see an exotic yet beautiful sea that makes you wonder if this is indeed our country. Baekgil Beach, located on the southwest coast of Jaeundo, 41.3km away from Mokpo Port, has endless fine sandy beaches along a vast coastline of over 3km, and the gentle slope and shallow water make it an endless sandy beach no matter how far you go. The white sand beach is 900m long and 70m wide (300m at low tide), and the sand texture is particularly fine, the pine forest is dense, and there are many coastal fishing spots nearby. The fish farm located in the abandoned salt pond near the beach cultivates high-quality fish such as sea bass, mullet, and prawn. In addition to Baekgil Beach, Jaeundo has nine beautiful sandy beaches, including Sawolpo, Bungye, Myeonjeon, Shinseong, Yangsan, Naechi, Daeseom, and Dunjang, making it an island with optimal conditions for a summer resort. In the past, people rarely visited the island because the sea route was long, but with the opening of Eunam Bridge between Amtaedo and Jaeundo and the opening of Aphae Bridge, passenger ships have been operating from Aphae Songgong Pier, and many vacationers are constantly visiting. The sunset seen from Yeondo Bridge is also spectacular.
priceDetail: Free

title: Nam June Paik Art Center
venue: Pyeongtaek Nam June Paik Art Center
description: In 2001, artist Nam June Paik and Gyeonggi Province began discussing the construction of an art center, and while Nam June Paik was still alive, he named this art center named after him as ‘Nam June Paik’s long-lived house.’ The Nam June Paik Art Center, which opened in October 2008, focuses on developing creative and critical research on Nam June Paik's thoughts and artistic activities and promoting his practice and activities in order to realize the ‘home where Nam June Paik lived for a long time’ as the artist hoped. Influenced by the tolerant, critical, and interdisciplinary work and life of Nam June Paik, the Nam June Paik Art Center conducts the following exhibitions, education, and research. Permanent exhibitions based on in-depth research into the world of Nam June Paik's works Regular special exhibitions based on controversial issues in contemporary art and academic research Educational programs such as workshops, seminars, talks, public lectures, and events that can serve as a focal point for research that provides the meaning of creativity, analysis of Nam June Paik's works, and various interpretations of the artist Nam June Paik Collections related to Nam June Paik encompassing various artistic fields such as music, innovative artistic practice, and media art Avant-garde art that pointed out the possibility of political and social meaning A publication and research program that analyzes the meaning of creativity and artistic practice as he interpreted Nam June Paik's spiritual legacy. With his nomadic temperament and inclusive spirit, Nam June Paik challenged not only the existing worldview but also avant-garde positions, opening up possibilities for art that were believed to have been exhausted. The Nam June Paik Art Center, which is creating ‘Nam June Paik’s long-lived home,’ hopes to evoke these characteristics of Nam June Paik and share his critical creativity. It takes about 5 minutes by car from Suwon Singal IC and about 4 minutes from Sanggal Station on the Suin Bundang Line, and there is a bus that goes from the station to the nearby area. Nearby are Gyeonggi Provincial Museum, Gyeonggi Provincial Children's Museum, Everland, Korean Folk Village, World Cultural Heritage Suwon Hwaseong Fortress and Yunggeonneung Royal Tomb, Giheung Lake Park, Deokpyeong Dinosaur Arboretum, Starlight Garden Space, and Hantaek Botanical Garden.* Opening date: October 8, 2008
price: Free (for special exhibitions, admission fees may vary)

title: Baekdamsa Temple
description: Baekdamsa Temple is a representative temple in Naeseorak. It is located on Baekdam Valley, where the clear waters of Gayadong Valley and Gugokdam merge. It was built by Master Jajang in the first year of Queen Jindeok of Silla (647) and was initially called Hangyesa Temple, but was later named Baekdamsa Temple because there were 100 pools from Daecheongbong Peak to the temple. It was destroyed by fire more than a dozen times, but was rebuilt in 1957 and is still standing today. Compared to the busy Oeseorak, Baekdamsa Temple is located at the entrance to the Naeseorak Mountain, which has a quiet and unexplored scenery close to a primeval forest, and is the representative temple of Naeseorak Mountain, which has isolated hermitages such as Bongjeongam Hermitage and Oseam Hermitage. Currently, Baekdamsa Temple has 24 buildings, including Iljumun Gate, Geumgangmun Gate, Bulmun Gate, Manbokjeon, Yosachae, Manhaedang, Nongamsil, and Jeokseondang, as well as the Manhae Memorial Hall and Manhae Education Center, which embody the literary ideas and Buddhist spirit of Zen master Manhae Han Yong-un, in addition to the existing buildings such as Geungnakbojeon, Nahanjeon, Sanryeonggak, Beophwasil, and Hwaeomsil, and are recognized as Korea's representative ancient temples. On one side of the valley in front of Baekdamsa Temple, there are stone pagodas built by people making wishes over the years at Baekdamsa Temple, providing something to see.

title: Baekseok Lifestyle Sports Park
description: It is a sports park equipped with a variety of sports facilities, including a soccer field, baseball field, little league baseball field, tennis court, basketball court, foot volleyball court, and badminton court. It is also equipped with daily sports facilities such as a running track and simple exercise equipment. This place, located in a place with a view of Bulgok Mountain in Yangju and fresh air, is not crowded, making it a good place to take a walk and exercise with children.

title: Baekunpo Sports Park
description: In accordance with the conditions for relocating the Sinseondae public water landfill, land owned by the Ministry of National Defense near Sinseondae Park was transferred free of charge from Nam-gu Office to create Baekunpo Sports Park. It is composed of 1 Masa Stadium, 2 artificial soccer fields, 1 baseball field, 4 futsal fields, and 8 tennis courts. Anyone can use the sports facilities by applying for rental on the Internet. In addition to sports facilities such as soccer fields, Baekunpo Sports Park also has the Nam-gu National Sports Center and Nam-gu Ice Rink, making it a park where you can experience a variety of daily sports. Oryukdo and Yeongdo are visible from the sports park, and it is also close to Igidae Park, making it a place where you can enjoy sports and sightseeing together.

title: Baekun Lake
description: It is an artificial lake built in 1953 near Lotte Premium Outlet Uiwang Branch. Located on a flat area where Cheonggyesan Mountain, Baekunsan Mountain, and Moraksan Mountain surround it like a folding screen, it boasts beautiful scenery and is full of restaurants and cafes, making it a popular attraction for tourists from the metropolitan area. This lake was originally created for the purpose of smoothly supplying agricultural water, but due to industrialization and urbanization of the region, farmland disappeared and is now a lake. At Baekun Lake, there is a 3km long Baekun Lake Deck Trail. It is quiet and secluded, so you can leisurely walk and splash around. Moomin Park, which opened in the lake in 2023, has a playground and an art ball with a diameter of 6m where various videos are shown every evening, making it a good place for families with children. There are a variety of things to enjoy, including a well-maintained large parking lot, a lake ring road that is great for driving, a dock where you can enjoy motorboats and duck boats, and a variety of restaurants and live cafes lined up on the lakeside, making it a great place for a family outing or a date for couples. Additionally, the Uiwang Baekun Lake Festival is held every September. It takes about 10 minutes by car from Pyeongchon IC and Indeokwon Station on Line 4, and there is a bus that leaves at once from the station.

title: Baekhyang Flower Nurmi Gallery
description: Baekhyang Kkot Nurmi Gallery is an exhibition hall run by a Kkot Nurmi master. Kkot Nurmi's work, which has been in the works for a long time, is on display. Flower press refers to an artistic activity that involves drying fresh flowers to remove moisture and air to maintain the color and beauty of the flowers, and utilizing these dried flowers. The process of drying real fresh flowers with nature as a motif creates a one-of-a-kind piece of work. In addition to picture frames, various types of works are created using brooches, bracelets, necklaces, earrings, furniture, etc.

title: Beomnyun Temple
description: Beomnyunsa Temple is the prayer site of the Avalokitesvara Shrine located at the foot of Munsusan Mountain in Yongin-si, Gyeonggi-do. Currently, Daeungjeon, Geungnakbojeon, Gwaneumjeon, Bhikkuni Seonwon, Samseonggak, Josajeon, Beomjonggak, and Yosachae are standing comfortably and proudly. The majestic main hall of 130 pyeong is built with red pine native to Mt. Baekdu, the sacred mountain of the nation, in the shape of the letter A in the Southern Buddhist style. It enshrines the 53-ton stone Sakyamuni Buddha, three times the size of the Buddha in Seokguram Grotto, as the main Buddha, and the 33-ton stone Bodhisattva Bodhisattva statues of Munju Bodhisattva as the left and right auxiliaries. On the left wall, there are 104 statues that promote Buddhism. The statues of Shinjungnim and Dongjinboan Bodhisattva are enshrined on the right, and the 1,250 Buddha Bodhisattva statues are enshrined to further inspire the faith of those who visit. Venerable Sangryun said, “I hope that Beomnyun Temple will establish itself as a Zen place for nuns and a sacred place for 20 million Buddhists.” He left a teaching saying, "A person who studies must shake off all attachments in the three worlds. If even the slightest attachment remains, it means that the studies have not yet been completed." Since the appointment of Chief Monk Hyeonam, continuous efforts have been made to make it a representative temple of Yongin City, and prayers have continued every day. Currently, it holds a three-story stone pagoda from the late Unified Silla Dynasty, which is a cultural asset of Gyeonggi Province.
address: 126, Rural Park-ro, Wonsam-myeon, Cheoin-gu, Yongin-si, Gyeonggi-do

title: Beophwasan Mountain
description: Beophwasan Mountain is a 385.2m mountain that spans all three districts: Jukjeon-dong, Suji-gu, Yongin-si, Mabuk-dong, Cheongdeok-dong, and Eonnam-dong, Giheung-gu, and Osan-ri, Mohyeon-myeon, Cheoin-gu. The name of Beophwasan Mountain comes from the Lotus Sutra, and the water that flows here becomes Tancheon, and many pine trees grow there. The time required to reach the summit is approximately 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours round trip, and the summit is a 3.2km climb from the entrance.

title: Beogi Art Museum
description: Opened in 2015, the Beoui Art Museum is an art museum that strives to make it easy for anyone to visit by promoting the convenience of the disabled and the elderly from its design. It is also a great place to visit with children as there are works of art, experience programs, and a small playground that even young children can enjoy comfortably. It is equipped with an exhibition building, artist's building, and auxiliary facilities, and operates various contemporary art exhibitions that the public can easily relate to.
