title: Bear Tree Park
description: Bear Tree Park, located in Sejong Special Self-Governing City, opened in May 2009. The plants and animals that founder Lee Jae-yeon has cultivated for over 50 years have grown into a forest and colony, forming the current Bear Tree Park. Bear Tree Park is a place where over 400,000 flowers and trees of over 1,000 species, as well as koi, black bears, and sika deer, come together on an area of ​​approximately 330,000 m2 (100,000 pyeong). Starting with the five-colored pond where over a hundred koi live, you can see hundreds of Asiatic Asiatic bears and brown bears performing tricks. Starting with the observatory where you can see Bear Tree Park at a glance, there is a Bear Tree Garden where flowers bloom all year round, and a pet zoo where you can see baby black bears, deer, peacocks, mandarin ducks, etc. Pine Garden created by collecting rare pine trees, Summer Garden where dead trees and juniper trees are in harmony, Rose Garden where you can admire thousands of roses, Wildflower Garden, a walking trail with domestic wild flowers, Bonsai Garden where you can see various types of bonsai, Tropical Greenhouse Garden where tropical plants that are difficult to find in Korea are gathered in one place, Mangyeongbiwon, which is full of various attractions such as cacti, fruit trees, and tree fossils, and between juniper trees that are over 100 years old. There is a juniper tree garden with a walking trail, and Songpawon, a European-style garden in the shape of a map of Korea with an 800-year-old zelkova tree. More than 1,000 koi fish, which were scattered across several outdoor ponds, gather in one place to survive the warm winter, creating an even more spectacular sight. When you sprinkle food, you can see schools of colored carp flocking together.

description: It is a valley that originates from Samtaegol on Tongbangsan Mountain (650m) and flows into the Bukhangang River through Nomun-ri and Susip-ri. Deep ponds and small waterfalls, including the kamaso, the folding screen, and the bat, form one of the eight scenic spots of Nomun. It is wide and shallow, and there are many natural swimming pools here and there, making it an ideal summer resort for families with children. If you follow the valley path, you will come across a stone pillar called Iljuam, and underneath it, there is a cow with deep water.

description: At the Byeongbangchi Observatory between Buksil-ri and Gyuam-ri in Jeongseon-eup, you can see the mysterious scenery of the Donggang River flowing at 180 degrees around Bamseom Island, which is shaped like the Korean peninsula. Byeongbangchi Skywalk is an observatory where you can feel as if you are walking in the sky, with tempered glass laid on the bottom of an 11m long U-shaped structure protruding from the edge of a cliff 583m above sea level. From here, you can see Bamseom Island, which is shaped like a map of the Korean Peninsula, and the beauty of the Donggang River, so it is popular with tourists.

It received its current name from ‘Boramae,’ the symbol of the Air Force Academy. It is located in Dongjak-gu, Seoul and is close to Gwanak-gu and Yeongdeungpo-gu, making it easily accessible. It is equipped with a variety of exercise facilities and relaxation areas, so it is used as a rest area in the daily lives of local residents. It is a representative park in the southwestern region of Seoul and continues to be loved by citizens as a space for leisure and cultural activities.

title: Boryeong Cheonbuk Oyster Complex
description: Cheonbuk Oyster Complex is a complex of oyster specialty stores located near the Hongseong seawall in the northernmost part of Boryeong. Cheonbuk oysters are one of Boryeong’s eight delicacies. In Cheonbuk Oyster Complex, oyster specialty restaurants are lined up along the sea of ​​Cheonsu Bay. Oysters are low in fat and rich in minerals, making them excellent in nutrition and taste. Oysters finish their spawning season until August and begin to gain weight in the fall, reaching their optimal condition in the winter. The best oysters caught from November to February are considered the best, and the 'Cheonbuk Oyster Festival' is held in the Janggeun-ri oyster complex every winter. At Cheonbuk Oyster Complex, you can taste a variety of dishes using oysters, such as grilled oysters, raw oysters, and oyster rice. title: Boreumsan Art Museum

In addition to works of art, you can enjoy collections such as wooden furniture, stone objects, and old roof tiles. You can drink tea, read a book, or even attend a small concert. We are striving to form a community that shares the museum's infrastructure with local residents, emphasizing the role of a family-oriented, lifestyle-friendly, and nature-friendly art museum.

Nearby, ‘Jewel Palace’, a fossil exhibition hall and precious metals exhibition and sales center, has opened, where you can see countless jewelery products. The museum building has one basement floor and two above-ground floors, and is equipped with storage, a machine room, a special exhibition room, a jewelry sales corner, and a permanent exhibition room. title: Boeun Beopjusa Temple [UNESCO World Heritage]
description: Beopjusa Temple, which means that the law of Buddha resides, is located at the foot of Songnisan Mountain. It was founded by Uisinjosa in the 14th year of King Jinheung of Silla (553 AD) and rebuilt by King Seongdeok and King Hyegong, from which time it began to acquire the scale of a temple. During the Red Turban invasion of Goryeo, King Gongmin took refuge in Andong and stopped by on his way back to the palace. King Taejo of Joseon prayed for 100 days before ascending to the throne, and King Sejo, who was ill, is said to have prayed for three days at Bokcheonam. By the mid-Joseon Dynasty, it had grown to be a magnificent temple with about 60 buildings and 70 hermitages, but due to the Japanese invasions of Korea, almost all of the temple's buildings were burned down. In 1624, the second year of King Injo's reign, it was rebuilt by Monk Byeok-am, and after several renovations, it remains as it is today. In the past, Beopjusa Temple's garam layout had the Hwaeom worship axis centered on Daeungbojeon and the Maitreya worship axis centered on Yonghwabojeon intersecting Palsangjeon at a right angle, but with the construction of the 33-meter-tall bronze Maitreya Buddha in 1990, the layout was scattered. In the precincts, there are about 10 yosachae (traditional quarters), including the main halls and religious offices, including Daeungbojeon, Yonghwajeon, Wontongbojeon, Myeongbujeon, Neunginjeon, Josagak, Jinyeonggak, and Samseonggak. More than half of Boeun's designated cultural assets are concentrated in the Songnisan area, including Beopjusa Temple, and among them, Beopjusa Temple has three national treasures. In addition, the Cheonwangmun Gate, the Seonhuigung Fabric that houses the memorial tablet of Crown Prince Sado's mother, Yeongbin Lee, the Neunginjeon Hall that enshrines the 16 Arhats, the Huegyeon Bodhisattva statue that burned his own body as an offering to Buddha, and the stone and iron pots that can easily hold 80 sacks of rice. Beopjusa Temple is a place where the belief in Maitreya has been passed down through a history of over a thousand years, and it offers temple stays so that people can experience basic Buddhist culture, such as prayer and Buddhist worship. Palsangjeon is a five-story wooden pagoda that is an important resource in the study of wooden pagodas in Korea. It was built by Uisin during the reign of King Jinheung of Silla, rebuilt by Byeongjin in 776, and rebuilt in 1605 after being destroyed by fire during the Jeongyu disaster in 1597. It continues to this day. It was named Palsangjeon because it depicts the eight scenes of Buddha's life divided into eight scenes. Palsangjeon is an important building that became the only example of a Korean wooden pagoda when the three-story wooden pagoda that was used as the main hall of Ssangbongsa Temple burned down in 1984. It has a total height of 22.7m to the top and is the tallest existing pagoda in Korea. In addition, the Seokyeonji is a masterpiece in which three tiers and a layer of bokryeondae were added to the octagonal stone lantern, and feldspar was placed on top of it in a cloud pattern to support a huge stone lotus pond, giving the appearance of a lotus flower floating on a cloud. It is considered to be a work of the Unified Silla period, made around the 8th century. The double lion stone lantern is one of the outstanding stone lanterns of Silla and was built in the 19th year of King Seongdeok (720). It is estimated. This stone lantern, in which the main stone of the stone lantern is replaced with a stone ruler, deviates from the typical style. The lower lotus stone and the double lion lotus cushion are all carved from a single stone on an octagonal base stone. It is characterized by the large stone and roof stone compared to other stone lanterns.

title: Ordinary reservoir
description: Botong Reservoir is a reservoir located in Botong-ri, Jeongnam-myeon, and has a trail around it, making it great for a light walk. At the entrance, there is a main photo zone and an observatory where you can enjoy the panoramic view of the reservoir, and the chairs in the rest area are great for staying for a while and enjoying the water. In the summer, the lotus flowers are in full bloom, making it a famous lotus spot, and it is also popular as a place to stay overnight. There are restaurants and cafes nearby, making it a suitable place for a family outing.

title: Ball Bear Park Bucheon Branch
venue: Bucheon Ball Bear Park Bucheon Branch
description: Ball Bear Park is a theme park located in Bucheon-si, Gyeonggi-do and is an indoor experience space suitable for children and families. The space is composed of a sports zone, challenger zone, digital zone, and infant zone, and can be used in a variety of ways depending on age and interest. The Sports Zone is a sports-themed space centered on family activities, and the Challenger Zone and Digital Zone feature a large ball pit, car racing, and AR/VR experiences. On weekends and public holidays, ''Ball Bear Park Tall & Fit'', a height measurement experience content, is operated. Because it is located close to Seoul, it is a popular place for family outings in the metropolitan area.

title: Bongdam 2 Ecological Sports Park
description: Bongdam 2 Ecological Sports Park is an urban park located in Bongdam District 2, and is characterized by the harmony of sports facilities and ecological space. A basketball court, a track, a badminton court, and a gateball court are built to serve as a daily exercise space for residents. There is a dense forest next to the park, and there is a wetland inside, allowing you to observe creatures and natural environments that are difficult to find in the city. In addition, there is a barefoot walking path, so it is great to enjoy walking and healing at the same time.

title: Bongeunsa Temple (Seoul)
description: Bongeunsa Temple is a thousand-year-old temple located in Samseong-dong, Gangnam-gu, the center of Seoul. It was founded in 794 by State Preceptor Yeonhwa and was initially called Gyeonseongsa Temple. Later, in 1498, Queen Jeonghyeon, the second wife of King Seongjong, greatly rebuilt this temple, located on the east side of Seolleung, King Seongjong's tomb, and changed the name of the temple to Bongeunsa Temple. During the Joseon Dynasty, it was a Zen Buddhist temple representing the Jogye Order, and in modern times, it was the site of Dongguk Station Gyeongwon, which carried out Buddhist studies and trained apprentices. Today, Bongeunsa Temple is creating a new history of Buddhism by operating a temple centered on practice. Through various programs such as temple stays, Buddhist universities, and sutra schools, we are not only promoting high-quality Korean Buddhist culture at home and abroad, but are also striving to maintain the status of an urban Daechal that realizes social welfare.

title: Busan Gamcheon Culture Village
description: Gamcheon Culture Village began as a home for refugees from the Korean War in the 1950s and is a place that preserves the history of Busan to the present. The uniqueness of Gamcheon Bay is demonstrated by the terraced group residences lined up in an orderly manner along the mountainside and the maze-like alleyways leading to all paths. It was an underdeveloped, underdeveloped neighborhood in Busan, but with the promotion of an urban regeneration project incorporating culture and arts, it has now become a representative tourist attraction visited by 1.85 million domestic and foreign tourists annually. With its beautiful pastel-colored houses and maze-like alleys cascading along the mountain slopes, it is called Santorini, the Machu Picchu of Korea. He also won the Presidential Award, the highest award at the 2016 Korea Space Culture Awards. At Gamcheon Culture Village, you can enjoy the picturesque village scenery in harmony with beautiful nature and admire various types of works installed in the alleys. You can also experience various crafts through the workshops of resident artists in Gamcheon Culture Village, so tourists are constantly visiting.

title: Busan Songdo Beach
description: Located 3km away from Jagalchi Market in Busan, it is the first beach to open in Busan in 1913. Beginning in 2000, a five-year maintenance project was carried out to expand the diminished white sand beach, install fountains, etc., and become a beach park. There is a fish market and Amnam Park nearby. Songdo, the first beach area developed in Busan in 1913, is connected to Amnam Park, an urban natural park opened from a military protection zone in April 1996, and Dudo Park, famous for sea fishing. Songdo is a place with a spectacular view of dense primeval forests, naturally preserved strangely shaped rocks, seagulls, the symbol of Busan, and a quiet seascape with Yeongdo in the distance in the background. It is equipped with a variety of accommodations and food facilities nearby, and has overpasses, walking trails, boat sites, It is well equipped with convenient facilities such as parking. Amnam Park on the Songdo coast is a coastal ecological park with an observatory that offers a panoramic view of the Songdo coast and Busan South Port, a 3.8km walking trail, roadside cafes, and raw fish restaurants. In Bumin-dong 3-ga, Seo-gu, Busan, there is the Provisional Capital Memorial Hall, which was used as the presidential residence for three years when Busan was the temporary capital during the Korean War. Songdo is located at the southern end of the Janggun Peninsula in Amnam-dong, Seo-gu, which has had a turbulent history.

The seascape seen through the pine forest on the coast and the boats floating leisurely on it provide a complete picture. It takes about an hour to walk around the park along the trail. The small island of Dudo and the white lighthouse standing tall there come into view like a painting.

There is a walking course around the Seongjigok Reservoir, which is lush with trees all year round, so the park is always full of citizens and offers a variety of things to see and enjoy. title: Buseoksa Temple [UNESCO World Heritage]
description: Buseoksa Temple is a temple of the Hwaeom Order founded by Master Uisang, the founder of the Haedong Hwaeom Order, at the royal order in 676, the 16th year of King Munmu of Silla. When the Great Master was studying in the Tang Dynasty, he heard the news of Tang Gojong's invasion of Silla and reported this to the king. He returned to Korea to unify national opinion with the doctrine of Hwaeom that he had cultivated and to overcome the trials at home and abroad. He founded this temple, and it became the birthplace of the Hwaeom ideology in Korea. The name Buseoksa Temple is said to have originated from the fact that there is a large rock to the west of the Buddhist temple, and this rock is said to be a floating rock, not attached to the rock below, but floating. During the Goryeo Dynasty, it was called Seondalsa Temple or Heunggyo Temple. According to the ink inscription discovered during dismantling and repair in 1916, Muryangsujeon was rebuilt in the early Goryeo Dynasty, but due to enemy fire in the 7th year of King Gongmin (1358), Muryangsujeon was rebuilt in 1376, the 2nd year of King U, and Josadang was rebuilt in 1377, the 3rd year of King U. The grounds include a stone lantern in front of Muryangsujeon, a seated stone statue of Buddha, a three-story stone pagoda, and relics from the Unified Silla period. There are pillars and stone foundations, as well as relics from the Goryeo period such as Muryangsujeon Hall, Josadang, a sculptured seated Tathagata statue, Josadang murals, Goryeo engravings, and Wonyung State Stele. In particular, Muryangsujeon is one of the oldest wooden buildings in Korea, and the Josadang mural is the oldest among the murals painted on a wooden building and is currently stored in the Relics Museum. The seated statue of Tathagata enshrined in Muryangsujeon is the best small statue handed down in Korea. It is said that the well to the west of Muryangsujeon is where Master Uisang's guardian dragon lived.

title: Busodamak (Chusojeong)
description: If you go to Busoheun Village, Gunbuk-myeon, Okcheon-gun, Chungcheongbuk-do, you can see a spectacular view called Busodamak. Busodamak is a strange rock cliff rising above the water, and is a whopping 700m long. It is a spectacular view that marks the end of the Eight Scenic Views of Chuso, which Song Si-yeol, a scholar of the Joseon Dynasty, praised as the Salt River. Busodamak was not a waterside cliff from the beginning. It was originally a mountain, but with the completion of Daecheong Dam, part of the mountain was submerged in water, creating a landscape that resembles a folding screen of rocks on the water. Chusojeong is a place where you can truly see the spectacular view of Busodamak. When you climb up the pavilion, you can clearly see the shape of a dragon gliding across the lake. The sharp rising rocks and the lake of unknown depth chill the heart, but the mystery of nature, which has been preserved for thousands of years, is even greater. You can also hike along the ridge of Busodamak. Below the narrow ridge road is a dizzying cliff where the blue water opens its mouth like a crocodile.

title: Bucheon Cultural Center
description: The Bucheon Cultural Center is a place for the development of local culture through the preservation and transmission of traditional folklore in the Bucheon region, local festivals, and cultural lectures. It records and preserves the customs of old lifestyles that are disappearing. Therefore, the Cultural Center holds the Seokcheon Nonggigodumari Festival, Coming of Age Reenactment, Meonmaru Dodang Well Festival, Witso Sasan Mountain God Festival, and Gogangdong Yujecheon Ceremony every year. In addition, we operate a Hanok lodging experience, where you can experience traditional culture and even hold a traditional wedding ceremony. The cultural classroom offers cultural lecture programs such as Boksagol Choir, Korean dance, Gayangju making, gayageum, haegeum, and pungmul performance.

title: Bucheon City Museum
description: Bucheon City Museum, a first-class specialized museum established with the theme of education, opened in 2003 and has an education exhibition hall where you can look at the history of Korean education from the Three Kingdoms period to the present day, an exhibition hall of European porcelain, which is the essence of European culture that has been loved for hundreds of years, a chief exhibition hall where nature created works over eons, and an earthenware exhibition hall where you can look back on the history of Jeommal pottery, and an exhibition hall where you can look back on the history of Jeommal pottery in the Bucheon area. It consists of the Bucheon Local History Museum, which contains excavated artifacts. As a comprehensive museum representing the cultural city of Bucheon, you can take a look at a variety of collections encompassing the past and present, East and West. It was established based on about 4,700 educational materials donated by current Director Min Kyeong-nam, and displays the history of education in Korea at a glance through educational materials by era, from Seodang education to national education during the Japanese colonial period to the 7th curriculum.

title: Bucheon Botanical Garden
description: Bucheon Botanical Garden is located in Bucheon Natural Ecological Park and is a plant paradise with two underground levels and two above ground levels where you can see all kinds of rare plants. Bucheon Botanical Garden was built as a glass greenhouse in the shape of a peach blossom, a symbol of Bucheon City, and consists of five theme halls, including an interesting plant hall, aquatic plant hall, subtropical plant hall, succulent plant hall, and native plant hall, and two plant experience halls. In harmony with the surrounding forest, it provides citizens with a variety of cultural and resting spaces as a place to learn about living, breathing nature. The Natural Ecological Park includes not only the Bucheon Botanical Garden, but also the Natural Ecological Museum, the Agricultural Relics Exhibition Hall, the Bucheon Mureungdowon Arboretum, and the Tuntun Infant Experience Center, so it is a good idea to tour them together and experience experiences appropriate for your age. It is conveniently located near Kkachiul Station on Seoul Metropolitan Subway Line 7.
closedDays: 1월 1일, 추석날, 설날, 매주 월요일 (단, 월요일이 공휴일인 경우에는 다음 날 휴원)

title: Bucheon Free Market
description: Bucheon Jayu Market is a traditional market located in Bucheon, famous for Boksagol. Jayu Market opened in Simgok-dong in 1947 after liberation and became the oldest traditional market in Bucheon. Until the late 1970s, it was the only market in the Bucheon area along with the nearby Bucheon Fruit and Vegetable Market. Specialties include peaches, and nearby attractions include Dangsan Cherry Blossoms and the Million Rose Park. In the 2000s, market modernization was promoted to restore the market, which had weakened noticeably. Through the second phase of the project from 2009 to 2012 and 2014 to 2015, a pleasant shopping environment was created by improving arcade facilities and signboards.
closedDays: 매월 첫째·셋째 일요일이 포함된 주의 화요일 휴무

title: Bucheon Bow Museum
description: It has been known to the world since ancient times that our people are good at making bows and shooting arrows well. The bow was an important weapon in many wars fought by our people from ancient times to modern times. The Bucheon Bow Museum was created to display the spirit and wisdom of our ancestors contained in our bows. Recognized for its value and importance as a cultural asset, it was protected as National Intangible Cultural Heritage No. 47 in 1971. It is the national arch that has been in existence for over 160 years for five generations centered in Simgokbon-dong, Sosa-gu, Bucheon-si to this day. The exhibition hall displays various supplies and relics related to national archery, including various bows, arrows, and fire trucks. It will be a good opportunity to recognize the spirit and wisdom of our ancestors contained in our bows.

title: Bupyeong Kkangtong Market
description: It is said that the Bupyeong Kkangtong Market in Busan was smuggled with all kinds of goods along with military supplies when the US military entered the market after the Korean War. In particular, a lot of canned goods such as fruits and fish were imported, so the name of the market became Kkangtong Market. It was also called 'Dottegi Market', and it is said that imported goods were supplied to major markets across the country at that time. Dottegi Market was called the international market because the market was so large and there were no foreign products or other items. Although the market has shrunk somewhat as the import of many and diverse products has been permitted, it is still a famous attraction where you can still feel its reputation and power. Currently, it also handles foreign-made electronic products such as liquor, clothing, decorations, accessories, fashion miscellaneous goods, and mini cassettes. The market street, which extends for about 110 meters, has 11 local food stalls, 6 multicultural food stalls including Japanese and Filipino food stalls, and 13 new clothing, accessories, and stalls. At the entrance to Bupyeong Kkangtong Market and at the intersection within the market, various attractions such as magic and other performances are provided twice a day, and colorful LED lights welcome you next to the market.◎ Travel information to meet the charm of the Korean Wave - Entertainment <New Genes Code IN Busan> ‘Bupyeong Kkang Tong Market’, where you can feel the culture of Busan, Korea, was introduced through New Genes’ reality entertainment program ‘New Genes Code IN Busan’. This is a multinational market where you can find food and goods from many countries. If you are planning a trip to Busan, we recommend stopping by ‘Bupyeong Kkangtong Market’ where you can experience old Korean culture, food, and traditions.

title: Bugak Sky Octagonal Pavilion
description: Bugak Sky Palgakjeong is a Hanok-style pavilion that preserves traditional Korean beauty on top of Bugaksan Mountain, 342 meters above sea level, and is a tourist attraction in downtown Seoul with a natural location. Bugak Skyway, which opened in September 1968, is a well-known attraction as a driving course leading to Bugak Octagonal Pavilion. The tourist road stretches to the northeast along the ridge of Bugaksan Mountain, the main mountain in Seoul, and is approximately 19km long. At Bukak Palgakjeong, the mountain range connecting Bukhansan Mountain's Bibong Peak and Munsubong Peak is spectacular, and on the other side, you can see the beautiful scenery of Seoul facing Namsan Mountain. Well-maintained street trees and approximately 100,000 ornamental trees bloom throughout the entire section, allowing you to enjoy a panoramic view of Seoul along with the Namsan Ring Road. There is also a rest area at the top of the ridge halfway along the road where you can stop for a moment and take a break while taking in the true scenery of Seoul. It serves as a tourist course that shows Seoul at a glance to domestic and foreign visitors who come from far away.
priceDetail: Free

title: Bundang Ice Arena
description: Bundang Ice Arena is an indoor ice rink located in Bundang, Seongnam-si, and is a sports facility specializing in ice hockey and skating. It has an indoor rink that is not affected by fine dust or weather, so you can exercise stably. Experienced instructors, including former national team coaches, provide customized lessons to provide systematic instruction tailored to your skill level. It operates a wide range of programs, from children's programs to hobby activities and basic physical fitness, and is visited by people of all ages, including office workers and students.

title: Mt. Bulgok
description: Bulgoksan Mountain, also known as Bulguksan Mountain, is not very high at 470m above sea level, but it is listed as a true mountain in Yangju on 'Daedongyeojido'. It rises on the border of Yuyang-dong and Sanbuk-dong in Yangju-si, and unlike other mountains near Seoul, it is not crowded even on weekends, which is good. Although the mountain is small, it boasts a dense landscape with strangely shaped rocks. Although it cannot see the light of day due to the nearby Dobong Mountain, it is a mountain with convenient transportation and azaleas in full bloom in the spring. In particular, Yuyang-dong is home to cultural relics, including the old Yangju-gun government office, making it a perfect place for an outing for children's education. Also, on the hillside is Baekhwaam Rock, which is said to have been founded by State Preceptor Doseon during the Silla Dynasty. It is said that the water in the mineral spring beneath Baekhwaam does not decrease even during droughts and does not freeze even during extreme cold. The road from Baekhwaam to the summit is rough. The rocky area at the top is a dangerous course when it snows in winter. When you reach the top, you can see Yangju City and Uijeongbu City at a glance with wide open spaces in all directions. In Yuyang-ri, there are cultural assets gathered, including Dongheon and Eosadaebi (Gyeonggi-do tangible cultural assets), where Pastor Yangju administered for over 400 years, Yangju Hyanggyo (Gyeonggi-do cultural assets), Yangju Byeolsandaenori (national intangible cultural asset) Training Center, Geumhwajeong Pavilion, where Pastor Yangju rested, and Yangjusanseong (Gyeonggi-do monument).

title: Bulgwangsa Temple (Gwangju)
description: It is a traditional temple located at the eastern foot of Namhansanseong Fortress in Mokhyeon-dong, Gwangju-si, Gyeonggi-do. It is believed to have been founded during the mid-Goryeo period. It was later destroyed by fire during the Korean War, but is currently being restored and operated by Monk Hyeonjin. It is a quiet temple that has completed the Intangible Cultural Heritage Yeongsanjae No. 50 course and is performing the 49th Jae Ritual in an orthodox manner. In addition, Bulgwangsa Temple boasts beautiful scenery along with natural scenery that changes in each of the four seasons, making it a popular tourist attraction visited by many people. Bulgwangsa Temple is a place where you can feel the deep history and tradition of Korean Buddhism.

title: Briggs Grape Papaya Tropical Fruit Experience Farm
venue: Ansan Brix Grape Papaya Tropical Fruit Experience Farm
description: Briggs Grape Papaya Tropical Fruit is an experience farm located near the Sea Fragrance Arboretum. A variety of grapes, such as Campbell and Shine Muscat, are grown using eco-friendly farming methods, and various crop harvest programs such as grapes, figs, corn, and potatoes are operated depending on the season to provide special time for children to communicate with nature. There are also several types of animals on the farm, including parrots, pigs, rabbits, ponies, and hamsters. The experience of searching for eggs laid by naturally free-range chickens is also popular with children.

title: Bigeum Valley
description: Bigeum Valley is a valley located within Sudong National Tourist Site in Sudong-myeon, Namyangju-si. Surrounded by Seorisan Mountain, Jugeumsan Mountain, and Cheonmasan Mountain on all sides like a folding screen, this valley is shaded by dense forests and has clear water, making it a popular summer resort. It is about 1.5km from Naebang-ri, and is an even better place because you can enjoy a light hike up Sirubong Peak, which is 540m high, along with a beautiful valley. The water in Sudong-myeon is so clear and plentiful that it is nicknamed Mulgol-an, and there are many scenic valleys around it, including Mulgol-an Recreation Area, Sudong Valley, and Geomdani Valley. The area from the entrance to Geomdani Valley to Bigeum Valley and the Neorae Rock area near Bigeum Bridge are known to have the best scenery.

title: secret forest
description: The Secret Forest in Gujwa-eup, Jeju City is a natural forest trail attraction that has become famous as a photo zone on social media. It has a different charm from Bijarim Forest and Saryeoni Forest Trail, which are famous forests in Jeju Island. There are photo spots with a variety of compositions and Jeju Island's unique sensibility, such as rare cypress forests, wide meadows, stone walls and cabins. In particular, you can see beautiful nature in all four seasons, including rape flowers and pink muhly. However, since it is private land, it is difficult to take pictures before entering, and in order to go to the paved road, you must refer to the address provided on the website. ◎ Travel information to meet the charm of the Korean Wave - <Burabocon CF> <Burabocon CF> In the first scene of the full version, Boo Seungkwan closes his eyes while feeling the green forest. The flower field where the band members jump up behind the sitting Seungkwan and the forest where they walk together are refreshing. Andol Oreum Secret Forest, as its name suggests, is a secretly hidden place. The natural forest doesn't even have a bathroom, but it's full of people who come to take snapshots. The dense forest leads to grassland and cypress forest, and there are photo zones here and there. In particular, it is recommended to take pictures in front of the mint-colored trailer as it is a must-take photo.

title: Bibongsan Mountain
description: Bibongsan Mountain in Anseong is a small and comfortable mountain with a height of 227.8m. At Bibongsan Mountain, there is an earthen wall built on the 9th ridge of the mountain as if it were wrapped around a belt, and at the top is Jangsu Rock, which is said to have left traces of an old general sitting there. In addition, Bibongsan Mountain has five temples including Yaksusa Temple, and has walking trails and exercise equipment (gym, badminton, etc.), making it an ideal place for people to enjoy hiking with their families. When you climb to the top of Bibongjeong, you can see the city of Anseong as well as nearby Bogae, Geumgwang, and Daedeok Gosam-myeon at a glance.

title: Vista Valley
description: Vista Valley, located in Hwado-eup, Namyangju-si, Gyeonggi-do, is a complex cultural space where you can enjoy culture and relaxation in nature. The horseback riding program, in which children and adults can participate, is provided with lessons tailored to the level of membership, and can be enjoyed in a variety of ways, from the first horseback riding experience to general lessons and mountain trekking horseback riding. After your lesson, you can enjoy a healthy meal at Conpapa, a restaurant in Vista Valley, or a leisurely cup of coffee at Ponytail Café, where you can hang out with horses. The scent of culture and art cannot be missed. The gallery holds a variety of exhibitions quarterly to provide a rich art experience, and at the Gagok Bookstore, you can find picture books and emotional books that can be enjoyed by both adults and children. You can enjoy a special time of reading in a space where books, scents, and thoughts come together. In addition, the Vista Valley Pickleball Club, newly opened in September 2025, is a lifestyle sports space that can be easily enjoyed by anyone of any age, from children to families, friends, and lovers. Vista Valley is a space where nature, sports, culture, and relaxation harmonize, providing a special experience at every moment of your stay.

title: Biseulsan Natural Recreation Forest
description: Biseulsan Natural Recreation Forest is a recreational spot located within Biseulsan Mountain, which has beautiful natural scenery and is rich in strangely shaped rocks. It is one of the top 100 famous mountains in the country announced by the Korea Forest Service. It is a recreational forest on Mt. Biseul with Hwahwabong Peak at the center and Gwangibong Peak of Cheonwangbong Peak on either side. The middle ridge of the mountain is mainly densely forested with coniferous trees, and the upper ridge has strangely shaped rocks and autumn foliage that create a spectacular view. The true flowers in spring, the fog and valley camping in summer, the maple leaves and silver grass in fall, and the ice garden in winter are also beautiful. As a result, Biseulsan Natural Recreation Forest is a place where you can relax with the gifts of nature all year round. In addition to a house in the forest, the forest has experiential facilities and things to enjoy, such as an auto camping site, a campsite, an outdoor performance hall, a pond, a youth training center, a physical training center, a lawn plaza, a photo spot, a water park, and a forest healing center. There is also Tamseok-ro, a walking trail lined with natural stones.

title: Pororo Theme Park Dasan With Travel
venue: Namyangju Pororo Theme Park Dasan With Travel
description: Pororo Theme Park Dasan With Travel is an edutainment space that creates educational effects while playing, and is a place for a play culture where children connect with each other and enjoy together with the friendly Pororo character. Pororo Park's important value and purpose is to create educational effects through play through a playful community for all children, and is a space where our children can have fun, experience, and study with mom and dad.

title: Root Park
description: Root Park is located in Chimsan-dong, Jung-gu, Daejeon, and is equipped with sculptures symbolizing surnames, the Korean Genealogy Museum, and various convenient facilities. It is a theme park that opened on November 1, 1997 with the theme of filial piety. It is an educational park that fosters loyalty and filial piety and the spirit of ownership, a family-friendly park with various events for families, and a natural park in the city with a natural scenery as a backdrop. It is equipped with a variety of facilities, including sculptures by surname where you can rediscover your roots, a deep-rooted spring water symbolizing the four gods and the 12 Jiji, a waterside stage where various events can be held, a grass plaza located in the center of the park, an observatory with a panoramic view of the park, an octagonal pavilion, as well as a forest bath, Hyo Cultural Garden, and a healing rest area.
address: Puri Park, 79 Puri Gongwon-ro, Jung-gu, Daejeon

title: Petite France
description: If you go about 10km along the lakeside road from Cheongpyeong Dam towards Nami Island, you can see a cluster of exotic buildings on the hill on the left. If you look at the buildings alone, it looks like a village on the Mediterranean coast, but if you look at it together with the beautiful surroundings of Homyeong Mountain, it looks like a country village at the foot of the Alps. This is the French cultural village of Petite France. Petite France’s concept is ‘flowers, stars, and the little prince.’ Petite France is a French cultural village that also serves as a youth training facility (Goseong Youth Training Center), and was created in the area of ​​Goseong-ri, Cheongpyeong-myeon, Gapyeong-gun. Petite France is made up of French-style buildings, and visitors can experience French food, clothing, and shelter culture while staying there. You can experience unique French culture at the Saint-Exupéry Memorial Hall, which explains Saint-Exupéry's life and the world of his works, including The Little Prince, the Music Box House, where you can hear sweet melodies coming from a 200-year-old music box, the French traditional house exhibition hall, which was built as an original French house, and the Antiques Exhibition Hall, where you can see sculptures and paintings of the French symbol 'chicken', porcelain, and other antiques collected in France and Europe. ◎ Travel information to discover the charm of the Korean Wave - Drama <The Tyrant's Chef> The room that appears in the modern-day flashback scene of Yeon Ji-young (Lim Yoon-ah), the main character of the drama 'The Tyrant's Chef', is Petite France's 'Marie's Room'. This place is also famous as a filming location for numerous Korean dramas, including 'The Tyrant's Chef', 'My Love from the Star', 'Secret Garden', 'Beethoven Virus', 'Vincenzo', 'House of Paper', and 'Iduna'. If you have experience watching these works, it will be an additional point of enjoyment during the viewing.

title: Saryeoni Forest Trail
description: Saryeoni Forest Trail is one of Jeju's 31 hidden scenic spots. It is a forest path filled with cedar trees that starts from Bijarim-ro and passes through Mulchat Oreum and Saryeoni Oreum. It is called Saryeoni Forest Road because it is a forest road that leads to Saryeoni Oreum. ‘Saryoni’ means a sacred forest or ‘to wrap threads in a circle so that they do not fall apart.’ When you walk through the forest, you can feel as if you are wrapped in the refreshing scent of cedar trees. In addition to the dense cedar trees, various tree species such as oak trees, hornbeam trees, bamboo trees, and cypress trees live here. Because various tree species inhabit it, it is also a home for mammals including badgers and Jeju weasels, birds including pittas and goshawks, and reptiles including pit vipers. Saryeoni Forest Trail is a popular destination for travelers who like trekking because the original appearance of the forest is not much damaged. It is also a Jeju Biosphere Reserve designated by UNESCO in 2002. In order to protect the forest, visitation to Mulchat Oreum was restricted due to the nature rest year, but the ‘Saryeoni Forest Eco-Healing’ event was held to temporarily open the area.

title: private bookstore
description: Private bookstores are independent bookstores known for their ‘book doctor’ concept, where the bookstore manager listens to a person’s tastes and concerns and recommends appropriate books. Beyond simply selling books, we help you look into your inner self through reading consultation. This is also the reason why customers continue to visit even remote alleys. The books on the shelves have underlines and notes from other visitors, so you can feel a strange sense of intimacy as you catch a glimpse of other people's reading traces.

title: Sacheon Sea Cable Car
description: As Korea's first cable car that operates both on the sea and in the mountains, it can solve all the shortcomings of existing cable cars that only operate on the sea or mountains, resulting in high passenger satisfaction. The total length is 2.43km, and you can get off at Gaksan Bus Stop and go up to the observatory to enjoy the beautiful scenery of the Sacheon Sea. While traveling by cable car, the boats floating in the sea for fishing can make you feel like you are looking at a watercolor painting, and sometimes you can even meet the native dolphin, ‘Sanghoe’. The cable car runs from Daebang Stop to Choyang Stop and Gaksan Stop and back to Daebang Stop on a round-trip basis, with a total of 42 cabins (28 regular cabins and 14 crystal cabins).

title: Sacheon Beach (Sacheon Beach)
description: Sacheon Beach is a very quiet and clean beach with a length of 300m and an area of ​​18,000㎡ located between Gyeongpodae Beach and Yeongok Beach. It opened on July 1, 1975, and is adjacent to Gyeongpo Provincial Park, so many vacationers visit it every year. It is a great place to enjoy a quiet summer vacation with a large pine forest, clean white sand beach, and shallow water. The fragrant smell and cool shade from the pine forest are even better for creating deep memories. Located near Anmok Beach, there are not many people here, so it is a secluded and quiet beach. The color of the sea here is a jewel emerald, giving the impression that you are on a foreign coast. If Gyeongpodae is a place visited by young couples, the nearby Sacheon Beach is a place visited by scuba divers, fishermen, and family tourists due to its clear water and calm waves. Because the sea changes its colors depending on the season, many people come to enjoy the seasons as they change. In addition, Sacheon Beach is considered a paradise for auto camping enthusiasts as it has a good environment for auto camping. Auto Camping Site is a comfortable camping site where you can smell the fragrant scent of pine trees.

title: Sangol Arboretum
description: Sangol Arboretum is an arboretum and large bakery cafe located in Siheung City. You can enjoy nature with your whole body in a space filled with the fresh scent of grass. On the second floor, you can get lost in thought while looking at the lush trees, and on the third floor terrace, you can spend a quiet time feeling the breeze. If you follow the walking path behind the cafe, a greenhouse garden appears, adding to the relaxation of a cup of coffee. The menu is diverse, from bakeries such as croissants, salt bread, and Mont Blanc to coffee and ade, so it is fun to choose according to your taste.

title: Sangumburi
description: Sangumburi is a natural monument and a crater with a circumference of over 2km. There are about 360 parasitic volcanoes distributed on Jeju Island, but except for Sangumburi, all volcanoes are in the form of craters that look like an overturned bowl, and Sangumburi Crater is the only volcano in Jeju Island that exploded without erupting lava or ash, blowing away the rocks there, leaving only a hole. This type of volcano is called Maar, and it is a very rare volcano in the world, with only one in Korea. In particular, there are many gaps at the bottom of Sangumburi, so all the water seeps through, so the plant ecosystem is uniquely distributed within this crater. Temperate and subtropical regions are formed depending on the height of the crater's interior, and are distributed in various ways depending on the amount of solar radiation and sunlight hours. In other words, the sunny northern cliff forms a subtropical zone, with a group of evergreen broad-leaved trees such as red thorn, red thorn, cypress, and sendal trees. The lower layer is home to rare plants such as eucalyptus orchids, as well as winter berries, etc. In addition, on the southern cliff, which does not receive much sunlight, there is a colony of temperate deciduous trees such as oaks, Japanese oaks, maples, and Korean pine trees, which have a distribution that is very different from that of the north. In addition, the Sangsan community, Jeju Korean lily community, Boksu community, and Byeonsan wind flower community, as well as the Sangsan community, Jeju Korean lily community, Boksu community, and Byeonsan wind flower community, as well as the Japanese oak community, which are difficult to find elsewhere, are very colorful and perfectly preserved, which is highly regarded as having a high academic research value. There is. It is also famous as a habitat for wild animals such as mammals such as roe deer and badgers, as well as birds and reptiles. In spring, the shape of clouds forming at the bottom of the crater and rising upward is almost mysterious, and along with colorful flowers such as sagebrush, gentian, and whirligig, Sangumburi shows mystery and beauty to tourists all year round.

title: Sanmagi old road
description: Sanmagi Old Road is an old road that connected Saorang Village, Oesa-ri, Chilseong-myeon, Goesan-gun, Chungcheongbuk-do, to Sanmangi Village, a mountain village. It is a trail that has been restored as if drawing on the old road that remains like a trace. Most of the old road section was made into a deck, minimizing environmental damage to show the living natural beauty, and the beauty of the mountains, water, and forests along the old mountain road is considered the highlight of Goesan. The Sanmagi Old Trail Trail consists of two courses and is full of things to see, with representative attractions such as the Dolmen Rest Area and the Pine Suspension Bridge. It was built along the Goesan Dam, showing the natural beauty that harmonizes with the Goesan Dam Lake. From Goesan Lake, you can tour the mountain village using a cruise ship or motorboat.

title: Sanjicheon
description: Sanjicheon Stream is a stream that runs from near Hallasan Mountain, through downtown Jeju City, next to Dongmun Market, the largest traditional market in Jeju City, and all the way to Jeju Port. In the 1960s, when industrialization was in full swing, environmental pollution problems arose when houses and commercial buildings were built over mountain streams, so a restoration project began in 1995. In 2002, Sanjicheon took on its current appearance with clear water flowing. Freshwater fish such as silverfish, mullet, yellowtail, and carp live there, so you can often see people enjoying fishing and children swimming in the summer. The shopping center Chilseongtong and Dongmun Traditional Market are located nearby, and it is also the starting point of the Jeju Olle Course 18, so the area is always crowded with people. The Sanjicheon Festival is held every year and various experience spaces, exhibitions, food markets, and exciting stages and performances are held along the path of Sanjicheon spring water. If you walk along Sanjicheon, you will find the Arario Museum, which has renovated old buildings into a unique modern art exhibition space, and other famous attractions include the Kim Man-deok Memorial Hall, which honors grandmother Kim Man-deok, who practiced sharing and service by giving everything she had to the people of Jeju in the past.
address: Geonip-dong, Jeju-si, Jeju Special Self-Governing Province

title: Sancheong Donguibogamchon
description: Donguibogamchon, located at the foot of Wangsan and Pilbongsan Mountain in Sancheong-gun, Gyeongsangnam-do, is the first oriental medicine-themed health experience tourist destination in the country. It is equipped with various facilities related to oriental medicine, such as the Expo Theme Hall, Oriental Medicine Museum, Oriental Medicine Experience Center, Oriental Medicine Theme Park, Donguibonga, Oriental Medicine Natural Recreation Forest, Bondiol Oriental Medicine Clinic, lodging facilities, and herbal medicine store, making it the mecca of Oriental medicine resort tourist destinations in name and reality. It is the number one healing trip. You can also use various oriental medicine-related experience programs such as oriental medicine heating experience, herbal scent bag making experience, wearing a medical doctor/medicine woman’s costume, and oriental medicine foot bath experience. ◎ Travel information to meet the charm of the Korean Wave - The place where Ban Ji-eum from the drama <Please Take Care of Me This Life Too’ took Seo-ha Seo-ha, showing her his past life, and enjoyed a tickling date is ‘Donguibogamchon’, an oriental medicine-themed space located in Sancheong-gun, the home of traditional oriental medicine. There are a variety of things to enjoy here, including a garden full of flowers and trees, an Oriental medicine museum, an Oriental medicine experience center, an observatory, and the Mureung Bridge that Banjieum and Documentoha crossed, so we recommend stopping by.

title: Sammaksa Valley
description: Sammaksa Valley is a valley formed by the gathering of clear and clean water streams flowing from Samseongsan Mountain. It is a popular summer attraction because you can enjoy water play in a dense forest. The current is not strong and the water is shallow, making it a popular destination for families. There are plenty of shaded areas, making it perfect for spreading out a mat and resting. Visitors with families with children are recommended to enjoy water play downstream, where various convenience facilities such as public parking lots, restrooms, and shops are nearby.

title: Sammi Market
description: It is a traditional market located in Sincheon-dong, Siheung-si, Gyeonggi-do, selling various foods and miscellaneous goods such as vegetables, fruits, meat, and fish. It is a representative traditional market in Siheung that is visited not only by locals but also by tourists due to its clean facilities and low prices. The food stall street located in the middle of Sammi Market is a great place to enjoy a variety of food and feel the warmth of a traditional market.

title: Samseonsan Arboretum
description: Samseonsan Arboretum is a nature experience learning center where over 1,160 species of plants grow. There are 10 facilities, including an outdoor garden where you can see various flowers and trees, as well as an exhibition greenhouse, Kids' Dream Forest, and the Korean Peninsula Small Park. There are also 23 exhibition gardens, including a hydrangea garden and an azalea garden. In addition, you can see diverse and beautiful scenery depending on the season, and it is well-equipped with convenient facilities such as a children's play area in the forest, a picnic area, a cafe, and water play facilities in the summer. Samseonsan Arboretum operates a variety of programs for children, teenagers, and the general public. We operate a forest interpretation program where you can experience nature while exploring the arboretum with a forest guide, a forest ecology experience for children, and a weekend experience program where you can experience hands-on activities such as playing and crafting.
priceDetail: Free

title: Samsung Palace
description: Located in Mukgye-ri, Cheongam-myeon, deep in the arms of Jirisan Mountain, the sacred mountain of the Korean people, if you walk about 1.5km around the mountain path in Cheonghak-dong, Cheongam-myeon, Samseong Palace is located at 850m above sea level. The exact name of Samseong Palace is Baedalseongjeon Samseong Palace. In 1983, Kang Min-ju (Hanpul Zen Master), a local native, restored Sodo from the Gojoseon Dynasty. It is a Baedal National Temple dedicated to the ancestors of the nation, Hwanin, Hwanwoong, and Dangun. It is establishing itself as a dojo for the people who protect Seondo, the orthodox domain of the nation, and practice Shinseondo. The 1,500 stone pagodas built by Master Hanpul, who inherited the practice of Seondo that has been passed down since ancient times, while practicing with monks, blend in with the surrounding forest and give off an exotic atmosphere. These stone towers are called Wonryeok Sotdae here. Sodo, a sacred place where ancestral rites were held to the heavenly gods during the Samhan Dynasty, was marked with a tall tree with a sculpture of a wild goose on it to prevent the common people from approaching. As if praying at Seonghwangdang, the old Sodo Island is being restored by building a sotdae with stones from the foot of Jiri Mountain to make a wish. It is the home of those who train martial arts, singing, dancing, and music to build a temple by building 3,333 sotdaes and regaining the unique spiritual culture of our people to create a Hongik Ingan world.

title: Samsung
description: ''Samseongsan Mountain'' is a mountain located across Sillim-dong, Gwanak-gu, Seoul, and Seoksu-dong, Anyang-si, Gyeonggi-do. It is the jinsan of Geumcheon-hyeon (the main mountain that protects each village), and Gwanaksan is the jinsan of Gwacheon-hyeon, located 5 ri west of the point where Ononsa Temple is located in Gwanmun-dong, Gwacheon-si, making it clear that the two mountains are separate mountains. There are also many theories about the origin of Samseongsan Mountain. It is widely known that the origin of Sammaksa Temple is the place where three great monks, Wonhyo, Uisang, and Yunpil, built a small hermitage and advanced to the capital in 677 (the 17th year of King Munmu's reign in Silla), and that the name of Samseongsan Mountain was purified by these three great monks and was called "Samseongsan Mountain." However, some in the Buddhist world believe that Sammaksa is the leader of the world of paradise as spoken of in Buddhism. Amitabha Buddha, Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva on the left, and Bodhisattva Mahasaeji on the right are called the Three Saints, and this is where the name of the mountain comes from. There are temples such as Sammaksa Temple, Yeombulam Temple, Mangwonam Temple, Anyangsa Temple, and Seongjuam Temple (Seoul), and the Baeksa Lee Hang-bok (1556-1618), who served as Byeongjopanseo five times during the Japanese Invasion of Korea (1592) and later as Uuijeong, climbed this mountain and recited it during his lifetime. The long poem “Chayuseongsamseongsanun (次游三聖山韻)” and the origin of Gogonokrok (高百祿) during the Japanese colonial period are said to have been passed down here. It is also a place with a deep history, where as early as 900, Wang Geon was passing through this place to conquer towns such as Geumju and Gwaju, where he met a monk named Neungjeong and built Anyangsa Temple, giving birth to the city name of Anyang today.

title: Samseongsan Forest Bathing Area
description: Samseong Mountain Forest Bathing Area, close to downtown Seoul and Anyang, is a forest resort that is great for light enjoyment. It is mainly used as a hiking trail for Sanseongsan Mountain and Gwanaksan Mountain. The forest bathing area is a 5km section that runs from the entrance to Anyang Art Park and passes Anyangsa Temple and the first and second observatories. It is part of a hiking trail that passes Anyangsa Temple and connects to the summit of Samseongsan Mountain and Gwanaksan Mountain. Convenience facilities such as exercise equipment and rest areas have been created between the dense forest paths, and you can see an open view as if you have reached the top after only 30 minutes of climbing. In particular, it is gentle for elementary and middle school grades, making it a great walking and trekking course for families with children. If you are a beginner or hiking with your family, we recommend climbing to the rest area in the middle, Anyangsa Temple, or Observatory 1. If you enjoy hiking, you can go up to Observatory 2 and try Sammaksa Temple or the summit of Samseongsan Mountain. From the forest bathing area, you can visit Anyangsa Temple. It is a fairly large temple that contains the origin of Anyang City's city name, and Anyangsa Temple's tombs and stupas, which are designated as tangible cultural assets of Gyeonggi Province, are well preserved. Nearby are Gwanaksan Mountain, Cheonggyesan Mountain, Gwanggyosan Mountain, and Pyeongchon Central Park. There are 44 convenience facilities of 9 types, including sports facilities such as iron bars, parallel bars, and waist twists, information signs, and hexagonal pavilions. The forest bathing course is about 5 km long, starting from the Anyang Amusement Park parking lot, passing Anyangsa Temple, Sammaksa Junction, a large pool, and ending with the Parkji Suspension Bridge.

title: Samyang Round Hill
description: A tourist ranch where you can commune with nature in the vast grasslands where you can feel nature itself, the scenery of wind power generators, and the peaceful pastures of sheep and cows spread out below. It is an affiliated farm of Samyang Foods, which operates the Samyang Ramen and Buldak brands. It was established in 1972 with the purpose of supplying good protein to the public and opened for tourism in 2007. In addition to the outstanding natural scenery, it is the only ranch in Gangwon-do where you can see a sheep herding performance and enjoy feeding sheep and ostriches. At the gift shop and cafe, you can find snacks and ice cream made from organic milk, boiled ramen, MD products, and local food products.

title: Samcheok Marine Cable Car
description: This is a cable car that offers a panoramic view of Yonghwa-Jangho Beach, which is famous for being beautiful on the east coast. When you get on the cable car, a beautiful sight unfolds where the emerald sea and strangely shaped rocks come together in harmony. The open East Sea seen through the car window borders the horizon, so when you look at the end, it is difficult to tell which is the sky and which is the sea. The view from the cable car varies depending on the weather. On a clear day, it feels like looking at a watercolor painting with pretty paints drawn by an artist, and on a rainy and cloudy day, it feels like looking at an elegant ink painting drawn by nature. Both Yonghwa and Jangho have walking trails leading to the coast, providing an opportunity to see the sea up close before your eyes.

title: Sangdaewon Market
description: Sangdaewon Market is a traditional market located in Sangdaewon-dong, Jungwon-gu, Seongnam-si. It is largely divided into sections A, B, and C, and each section has 20 to 30 stores. There are a variety of facilities, including side dish shops, rice cake shops, butcher shops, and restaurants, as well as repair shops and saunas. Thanks to the arcade, you can shop comfortably without being affected by the weather, such as rain, snow, sunlight, or wind. A comfortable and luxurious traditional market environment has been created, resulting in high satisfaction for both customers and merchants who come out to shop.

title: Sanglim Park
description: Hamyang Sanglim is a forest located on the Wicheon River to the west of Hamyang-eup. It is said to have been created by Choi Chi-won during the reign of Queen Jinseong of Unified Silla to prevent flood damage in Hamyang-eup. In the past, it was called Daegwallim, but as the middle part of this forest collapsed due to a flood, it was divided into Sanglim (upper forest) and Harim (lower forest). Currently, Harim has been damaged and only traces remain, and only Sanglim maintains its former appearance. It is mainly composed of oak trees and hornbeam trees, and the tangle of wild herbaceous trees and kudzu is reminiscent of the natural vegetation of a valley. With over 120 species of trees growing along the banks, it is also a great place for children to learn about nature.
priceDetail: Free

title: Sangju Eunsand Beach
description: Sangju Eunsand Beach, which uses the spectacular view of Geumsan Mountain as a long folding screen, is surrounded by a wide white sand beach with fine silver sand and a dense pine forest, making it one of the few beaches in the country with beautiful natural scenery. This place, located 21km south of Namhae-eup, is a place where the sand feels good under bare feet, and as many as 1 million travelers come here every summer. The 2km long half-moon white sand beach has a gentle slope and high water temperature, making it ideal as a summer resort for families. In addition, the Summer Festival is held in the summer and the Sunrise Festival in the winter, and there is a long tradition of vegetable hot dogs that can only be tasted here, emotional cafes that have become popular Instagram spots, and restaurants run by residents, so there is plenty to see and do.
operatingHours: Open all the time ※ If it is not an opening day, swimming is not possible as a safety manager is not present.

title: Sanghwawon
description: Sanghwawon, which is number 2 of Boryeong's 9 Scenic Views Plus, is a traditional Korean garden created by preserving the natural beauty of Jukdo Island as much as possible, cherishing every tree and piece of stone without damaging nature as much as possible, as its name suggests, which reveres harmony. As you walk along the ‘corridor’, a 2km-long roof-shaped promenade surrounding the entire island, you will see 33 seaside ponds with all kinds of aquatic life living in them, and the open West Sea beyond the stone walls made of five stones, a specialty of Jukdo Island. Inside, you can reach a forest path filled with pine trees soaring high into the sky, adding to the scent of pine trees, a sunset garden where you can enjoy the spectacular view of the West Sea sunset, and a Hanok village with eight traditional hanoks that were relocated and restored from all over the country in a place that was used as a rice field by the indigenous people of Jukdo Island. Additionally, on weekdays when it is not open for viewing, you can enjoy the Sanghwawon space privately and enjoy various programs such as family banquets, weddings, and workshops at the Hanok in the Hanok Village. Sanghwawon Korea Villa, an accommodation facility within Sanghwawon, is open only from Friday to Saturday, and individual reservations can be made through the website. If you want to enjoy the sunset in a quiet evening when there are no visitors and the beautiful natural garden at dawn, it is a good idea to stay here. Before visiting Sanghwawon, we recommend that you check the available visit schedule and time before visiting.
address: 408-52, Nampo Seawall, Nampo-myeon, Boryeong-si, Chungcheongnam-do, South Chungcheong Province

title: Saebyeol Oreum
description: Saebyeol Oreum is a representative mountain in the West, and was named so because it ‘stands alone like a morning star in the evening sky.’ Starting from the southern peak, there are ridges in the southwest, northwest, and northeast directions, and each ridge has its own peak. The west side is wide open in the shape of Samtaegi, and the north side is hollow. There are five peaks that are round like stars. Overall, it is a grassy field, but there are some scrub trees on the northern slope, and a cemetery has been created on the northwest slope.

title: Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market
description: Seogwipo Olle Market is the largest market in Seogwipo City. It is a traditional market that was created naturally in the early 1960s and has been a major foundation for Seogwipo's economy with over 60 years of tradition. Starting with 120m in 2001, arcade shopping malls currently totaling 620m have been installed, playing a pivotal role in Seogwipo's low-income economy. This parking lot provides maximum convenience to customers by introducing a one-hour free parking system, and for the convenience of customers who purchase goods at the market, it has a courier system that delivers them to the desired location free of charge. It also has an outdoor performance hall and a park with a fountain for youth, who are potential future customers.

title: Seodaemun Natural History Museum
description: Seodaemun Natural History Museum is a public natural history museum located at the foot of Ansan in downtown Seoul, and opened on July 10, 2003. This museum was established by a public institution to increase citizens' understanding of nature and provide opportunities for especially dreamy children and teenagers to directly see and experience information about various creatures, geology, and the environment. Museums provide both knowledge and interest in nature through not only exhibitions but also educational programs and experiential activities. It also serves as a cultural activity space for local residents. Seodaemun Natural History Museum provides an opportunity to experience the value of life and nature even in city life.

title: Seodaemun Prison History Museum
description: Seodaemun Prison was built under Japanese coercion at the end of the Korean Empire. For over 80 years, it was a site of suffering and history during a turbulent period in our modern and contemporary history, and was a representative institution of Japanese imperialism's oppression of our people's anti-Japanese independence movement. After opening under the name of Gyeongseong Prison on October 21, 1908, when our national sovereignty was taken away by the Japanese, a strong national independence movement protested against it, and the Japanese arrested and imprisoned many of our patriots. As the number of prisoners increased, they built another prison in Gongdeok-dong, Mapo, which was renamed Seodaemun Prison on September 3, 1912. It opened as the current ‘Seodaemun Independence Park’ on August 15, 1992, retaining as much history of national suffering as the name change. Seodaemun-gu began a project to turn the Seodaemun Independence Park historic site into a sanctuary in 1995. It was newly renovated and opened as the Seodaemun Prison History Museum to honor the souls of patriotic ancestors who fought against the Japanese invasion for the independence of the country and were imprisoned and died under severe torture and oppression, and to serve as a living educational center for history that awakens the spirit of independence of our ancestors to future generations.

title: Seodong Park and Gungnamji Pond
description: Gungnamji is a pond from the Baekje period. According to the Samguksagi (History of the Three Kingdoms), King Mu of Baekje built it to the south of the palace and is called Gungnamji. It is recorded in the Samguk Yusa that King Mu's mother gave birth to King Mu through a relationship with Yong and Jeong of Gungnamji. Currently, wells and foundation stones remain around the pond, which is the oldest artificial landscaping in Korea and provides a glimpse into the level of Baekje's landscaping technology. Gungnamji Pond, which created an island in the middle of a pond to express the idea of ​​immortals, is Korea's oldest artificial garden. It is said that Baekje's Lao Tzu-gong traveled to Japan and introduced Baekje's garden landscaping techniques to it. It can be seen that Baekje had outstanding garden decoration skills among the three kingdoms. It is a beautiful tourist destination in all four seasons. Currently, Gungnamji has developed into an ideal eco-friendly travel destination where nature and humans coexist, and active management is underway to preserve the natural environment. Thanks to this, tourists can experience history and nature at the same time, and more eco-friendly tourism is possible through bicycles and walking. Additionally, by touring historical sites, you can gain a deeper understanding of the historical value of tourist destinations. In July, the Seodong Lotus Festival, a beautiful feast of 10 million lotus flowers, is held, and in October and November, the Guttrerae Chrysanthemum Exhibition, decorated with various works, is held, adding to the beauty of Gungnamji.
priceDetail: Free

title: Seobongsan Forest Bathing Area
description: Seobongsan Mountain starts from Munhak-ri, Jeongnam-myeon and continues all the way to Bongdam-myeon. At 249m above sea level, it is a relatively high mountain in Hwaseong City. There are two theories: one is that the name was given because the summit resembles a phoenix when viewed from a distance, and the other is that it was named because it was said that a phoenix once lived here. Seobongsan Forest Bathing begins at the Hwaseong Food Integrated Support Center. Parking is free and you can purchase fresh local produce after completing the hike. Seobongsan Mountain has a forest bathing area centered around the Seobongsan Mountain Trail, where you can enjoy three different courses, so you can heal while looking at the greenery. There is an exercise facility 200m away on the way to the top, and at the beginning of the forest path, wild cherry trees, oak trees, pine trees, and maple trees form a tree tunnel in each section. After the second exercise facility, there is a long and steep uphill climb. The floor was covered with palm mats to prevent hikers from slipping, and ropes were tied between trees to ensure the safety of hikers. There are benches where you can rest along the way, and there is an octagonal pavilion at the top of Seobongsan Mountain, 2 km from the starting point, so you can enjoy the cool scenery of low mountains surrounding Deokwoo Reservoir like a folding screen. Seobongsan Mountain Forest Bathing Area is a place full of green and refreshing feeling, as the forest is so good that some people even turn back on the forest path even if they do not climb to the top of the mountain.

title: Seosuwon Library
description: After opening as the Seosuwon Knowledge Information Center, the name was changed to Seosuwon Library in August 2016. This is a small, quiet and cozy library that is constantly visited by Seosuwon citizens. Seosuwon Library has a variety of books, including philosophy and religion, and operates a variety of children's library programs to serve as a space for activities with citizens. The biggest feature of this place is that it collects works that have won famous domestic and foreign literary awards, provides book information services, operates various programs linked to award-winning books, and promotes specialized materials. In addition to various cultural activities, this place also provides [my first library service in my life], which allows pregnant women and infants who have difficulty visiting the library in person to borrow books from the local library via courier at home. In the 21st century era of knowledge and information, Suwon City has taken the lead as the nation's leading city for lifelong learning and culture, and has established 3 children's libraries in each region, the West Suwon and Buk Suwon libraries, and 2 general libraries in each region so that all citizens can use libraries nearby, resulting in 8 libraries along with the existing Seongyeong, Jungang, and Yeongtong libraries. In order to increase the number of libraries and stay ahead of the curve in service quality, excellent books are donated by citizens (groups) and new ones are purchased. We are making sure that citizens do not lack in acquiring specialized knowledge, and we are also building a user-centered one-stop electronic library, including books, member information, and unmanned automation, to ensure that there is no inconvenience in use.

title: Seounsan Mountain
description: Seounsan Mountain, located on the border between Gyeonggi-do and Chungcheongnam-do, is about 12km south of Anseong-si, Gyeonggi-do. At 547m above sea level, it is a small, gentle mountain with few rocks, making it ideal for a light hike with the family. In addition, there are many cultural historic sites such as Cheongnyongsa Temple and Seoknamsa Temple, so it is good for leisurely studying history, and there are even lakes around the mountain, so you can enjoy an elegant hike. If you climb from Cheongnyongsa Temple, follow the hiking trail on the left side of the temple for about 20 minutes, pass a private farm, and on the left, you will find Togulam Grotto, where Zen Master Naong prayed. After climbing through a dense forest for about 40 minutes, you will come to Jwaseongsa Temple, which overlooks the ridge of the Charyeong Mountain Range. Jwaseongsa Temple is a relatively recent prayer temple with a history of about 100 years. If you pass Yosachae above Jwaseongsa Temple and climb the path, you will come across Seounjeong Pavilion, which appears to be newly built. If you go up the trail again and climb the steep slope to the left at the fork in front of Toseong, you will come across Tanghyungdae, which is said to cleanse your heart. Tanghyungdae is considered one of the best observatories on Seounsan Mountain. From here, Anseong, Pyeongtaek, Seonghwan, and Cheonan can be seen. The feeling of turning back the way you came up and walking along the mountain path along the Saturn gives you a mysterious pleasure. After cooling off from the sweat at the summit, you can see the Eunjeokum and go down the dense forest path to meet the path you came up from Cheongnyongsa Temple again. Even if you look around and enjoy the mountain scenery here and there, two hours is a sufficient distance. If you turn off the path toward Cheongnyongsa Temple at the top and go down to the northeastern foot, you can go down to the front of the rock-carved Buddha statue of Seoknamsa Temple.

title: Seoul Myeongdong Cathedral
description: Myeongdong Cathedral, the cathedral of the Archdiocese of Seoul, is the place where the Korean Catholic Church community was first born and is the representative shrine of Korean Catholicism, housing the remains of martyred saints. It is located in Myeongdong 2-ga, Jung-gu, Seoul. It is the first large-scale Gothic Catholic cathedral built on the Korean Peninsula and the first parish church (cathedral where a priest resides and provides pastoral care) in Korea. It was designated as a historic site in Korea on November 22, 1977. It is a holy shrine where the remains of martyrs such as Bishop Imbert, Father Mimic, and Father Chastan are buried in the underground cathedral. On September 10, 1900, the remains of martyrs during the Byeongin Persecution, including Bishop Bernu, were placed in the cathedral's crypt from Yongsan Theological Seminary, but were later moved to their hometown. In 1926, the remains of the 79 martyrs from the Gihae Rebellion and Byeongo Rebellion were placed in the crypt, and then a beatified altar was installed in the left corridor of the cathedral and the 79th icon was placed there. During the war in 1950, the cathedral was occupied by the People's Army, and the remains of martyrs enshrined in the underground tomb were damaged. After the military regime era, it was recognized as the center of the struggle for democratization. In 1991, the decomposed remains were packaged, new corroded lead coffins were made, the remains were enshrined, sealed, placed in a sarcophagus, placed in a newly neatly renovated reality, and a stone tablet with an inscription written on it was completed. The entrance to the cemetery was remodeled with a glass door so that pilgrims could visit from time to time. Mass and confession times are held on weekdays and weekends. Even if you are not a believer, you can participate, and during Christmas, you can feel the reverent atmosphere among the colorful street decorations around you.
priceDetail: Free

title: Seoul Heonreung (Taejong and Queen Wongyeong) and Inlleung (Sunjo and Empress Sunwon) [UNESCO World Heritage Site]
venue: Seoul Heonreung (Taejong and Queen Wongyeong) and Inlleung (Sunjo and Empress Sunwon) [UNESCO World Heritage Site]
description: Heonreung is the tomb of King Taejong (reign 1400-1418), the 3rd king of Joseon, and Queen Wongyeong (1365-1420). It is a twin tomb with burial mounds arranged side by side within a single tomb. When looking at the tomb from the front, the tomb of King Taejong is on the left (west) and the tomb of Queen Wongyeong is on the right (east). In 1420 (the 2nd year of King Sejong's reign), Queen Wongyeong passed away and a tomb was built at the current location. When constructing Queen Wongyeong's tomb, King Taejong created his own tomb site in advance. Two years later, in 1422 (the 4th year of King Sejong's reign), when King Taejong passed away, a tomb was built on the west side of Queen Wongyeong's tomb, and it took on its current appearance. The tomb mounds were all surrounded by folding screen stones and railing stones, and the zodiac signs, Yeongjeo (Geumgangjeo), and Yeongtak (Geumgangryeong) were engraved on the folding screen stones. Around the burial mound, Munseokin, Museokin, Seokma, Jeongjeongseok, Jangmyeongdeung, stone statue (Honyuseok), Mangjuseok, setting sun, and lagoon were placed. In particular, Munseokin, Museokin, Seokma, Seokyang, and Seokho were placed twice as often as in other royal tombs, following the Hyeon·Jeongneung (玄·正陵) system of King Gongmin and Princess Noguk of Goryeo. There are two shrines in the shrine below the royal tomb, one erected after the death of King Taejong and the other stele erected again in 1695 (the 21st year of King Sukjong's reign) after the original stele was damaged. Inreung is the tomb of Sunjo, the 23rd king of the Joseon Dynasty (reigned 1800-1834), and Empress Sunwon of the Kim clan (1789-1857). Inreung is a joint tomb in which the king and queen are enshrined together in one mound. When viewed from the front, Sunjo is on the left and Empress Sunwon is on the right, following the principle of right-top-left-bottom. When King Sunjo passed away in 1834 (the 34th year of King Sunjo’s reign), it was built near Jangneung (Injo’s) tomb in Gyoha, Paju, the following year. However, it was said to be inauspicious according to feng shui, so it was moved to its current location in 1856 (the 6th year of King Cheoljong's reign). The site of the relocated Inreung was originally the site of King Sejong's old royal tomb. While constructing Inlleung, the stone monuments from King Sejong's old royal tomb and the old Heireung stone monuments of King Jungjong's second queen, Queen Janggyeong, which had been buried in the surrounding land, were taken out, polished, and used. The stone objects that were reused were the Munseokin, the Museokin, the Seokma, the Jangmyeongdeung, the stone statue (Honyuseok), the Mangjuseok, the sunset, and the Seokho, and some of the Seokyang, Mangjuseok, and Seokma were newly manufactured. This is recorded in 『Inreung Cheonbongsanneung Dogam Uigwe』, which was compiled after moving Inreung. After moving the tomb, when Empress Sunwon passed away the following year, she was buried in the tomb. There are two monuments inside the monument below the tomb. The first monument is a monument erected during the Joseon Dynasty (King Sunjo, Queen Sunwon), and the second monument is a monument erected during the Korean Empire (Emperor Sunjo Suk, Empress Sunwonsuk).
