title: Seoul Land
description: Seoul Land, which has the title of Korea's first amusement park, established itself as Korea's representative theme park as soon as it opened. It is located about 30 minutes away from Seoul Station and Myeongdong Station, so transportation is convenient, and nearby are the zoological and botanical gardens of Seoul Grand Park, a forest bathing area, and the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, making it a widely loved tourist destination representing Korea. Seoul Land not only operates over 50 types of rides decorated with Korean animation characters, but also seasonal facilities such as water play facilities (summer) and sledding slopes (winter), and introduces new performances, festivals, and events to provide fresh enjoyment for each season. In addition to various attractions, there are also spaces where visitors can enjoy a variety of experiences, such as Korea's largest all-in-one play park 'Seoulland Kraken Island', dinosaur exhibition and experience center 'Jurassic Land', and light festival 'Luna Park', making it an all-round theme park that the whole family can enjoy. 'Seoul Land Kraken Island', which opened in April 2024, is an experiential attraction that boasts an overwhelming scale with the main structure being similar to the height of a 6-story apartment. Children can run, roll, and climb as much as they like, and can have a new adventure with different experiences by directly hitting it with their bodies. In particular, Seoul Land's Kraken Island is gaining popularity among children with its new concept 'amphibious' type play gym that adds water play functions such as water bombs, water screens, and floor fountains. ‘Jurassic Land’, where you can see moving dinosaurs up to 18 meters long, is also popular. More than 100 different types of dinosaurs, fossils, and eggs are on display, and beyond simple viewing, you can expect an educational effect that stimulates children's five senses through experiences such as excavating dinosaur fossils and matching bones. In addition, Seoul Land's representative performances include the children's musical 'Animal Kingdom', 'The Legend of Luna Light' with a spectacular fireworks show, and the character fairy tale play 'Fairy Tale Forest'. It is full of attractions, things to see, and things to do, so we recommend visiting with the whole family.

title: Seoul Forest
description: Seoul Forest was the first water source in Seoul, established in 1908, and was newly opened in 2005 to turn the area around Ttukseom Sports Park into a large-scale urban forest. Currently, it consists of four unique spaces: Culture and Arts Park, Experiential Learning Center, Ecological Forest, and Wetland Ecological Garden, and provides a variety of cultural and leisure spaces adjacent to the Han River. In addition, Seoul Forest Park is the first park with citizen participation from creation to program operation.

title: Seohae and Jebudo Marine Cable Car
venue: Seohae and Jebudo Marine Cable Car
description: Jeongok Port, which matches the beautiful natural scenery of the west coast, and the location of Korea's longest maritime cable car, 2.12km above the sea on Jebudo Island, have been selected to create a new landmark where nature and people come together. Jebudo Island has a modern appearance and function that reflects the unique characteristics and beauty of the region, making it a tourist spot on the west coast and the metropolitan area. From the Seohaerang Cable Car, you can enjoy both the mud flat and the sea at the same time, and the best time to enjoy it is at sunset. Another special feature of the Seohaerang Cable Car is that you can view the mudflats from above. You can board the bus at either stop, and it is a west coast tourist destination where you can enjoy both Jebudo Island and Jeongok Port.

title: Seoho Art Museum
description: Seoho Art Museum, located on the Bukhangang River in Namyangju, was established by Gallery Seoho in Insa-dong for the balanced development of local culture and opened in May 2001. We sponsor local artists, plan exhibitions and projects, and carry out various cultural education and experience programs for local residents. The first floor of the building has a 70 pyeong exhibition room, art shop, and art room. In addition, various cultural events will be held in an outdoor lawn space of about 500 pyeong. The educational program being conducted at the museum is an exhibition-linked program for local elementary school students, and includes classes that involve viewing works on display at the museum and engaging in practical expression activities, as well as special experience programs held during vacation periods. In addition, we are also operating a visiting art museum program for people who have difficulty visiting art museums, such as married immigrant women and the elderly. Seoho Museum of Art provides opportunities for rich cultural experiences by holding not only exhibitions but also cultural events such as concerts, various performances, and seminars. On the second floor, there is a restaurant called [The Seoho] operated by the museum. It is a place where you can spend leisure time looking at the Bukhangang River seen through the full-length windows, and enjoy the pleasure of both sights and food.

title: Seohuri Forest
description: It is a 100,000 pyeong arboretum that opened in 2014. It is a beautiful space where the landscaping, which is based on the motto of a pristine forest but does not harm the natural feel, feels delicate. Depending on the species of trees, the inside of the forest consists of a pine forest, a secret forest, a maple forest, a metasequoia forest, a ginkgo forest, a dogwood forest, a birch forest, and an azalea forest. The forest bathing walking course is divided into Course A, which is 1 hour long, and Course B, which is 30 minutes long, depending on the length.

title: Seokryongsan Mountain
description: Seokryongsan Mountain, which came to be called Seokryongsan Mountain because there is a curved, dragon-shaped rock at the top, is a mountain that straddles Sanae-myeon, Hwacheon-gun, Gangwon-do and Buk-myeon, Gapyeong-gun, Gyeonggi-do. Seokryongsan Mountain, where waterfalls, walls, and cows are connected, has relatively gentle hiking trails compared to its majestic mountain scenery, but there are some steep points along the way. This forested area is a great place to walk while listening to the sound of clear water flowing in the Jomurak Valley. There are benches here and there where you can sit and rest, making it a great place to take a break in the forest. Also, there are a lot of wild flowers along the road, so it will be fun to hike up and see them. A total of 534 types of vascular plants growing in the Seokryongsan Mountain area are known to be distributed. Among them, a total of 16 types of Korean endemic plants were investigated, including sedge, cypress, cypress, and widower's windflower, and a total of 15 types of rare and endangered plants, including widower's windflower, Gaejokdori, and white peony, were observed. The hiking trail is gentle compared to the mountain terrain, making it good for hiking, but the temperature difference is relatively severe and more than 50% of precipitation is concentrated between July and September, so caution must be taken when hiking in the summer. Because there are a lot of rocks, it is better to take at least twice as much hiking time as walking on the mountain path. From the summit, you can see Baekun Mountain and Sachang-ri at a glance, as well as Hwaak Mountain, Myeongji Mountain, Gukmangbong Peak, Daeseong Mountain near the ceasefire line, and Baekam Mountain. The starting point of the hike is from Yongsumuk Jomurakgol.

title: Seoksan Valley
description: In Danwol-myeon, the border point between Yangpyeong and Hongcheon-gun, the Seoksan Valley, formed by the water stream that starts from Bongmisan Mountain and flows into Hongcheon River, swirls around Sorisan Mountain, continues next to the road. The valleys are deep and the forest is thick, so the sky is not visible, and the scenery is completely different from the tributaries of the Namhan River in Yangpyeong, so even in the middle of summer, a cool breeze flows through it. As you can see from the name Seoksan-ri due to its abundance of rocks, it is a clean area where fireflies can be found in abundance in the summer. As can be seen from the name Seoksan-ri, it boasts an unspoiled scenery and beauty along with Mt. Sorisan, and presents a superb view of strangely shaped cliffs and pine trees. The water is clear and smooth, and it is not deep, so it is safe to play in the water. The forest is thick and provides shade. The length of the valley is quite long, the amount of water is abundant, and there are many places to rest around the valley, making it a great place for a family resort or summer resort. Also, at the entrance of Yongmunsan Mountain, turn right at Deokchon Intersection and the road leading to Deoksu Intersection - Local Road 328 - Biseulgogae - Saneum Bridge - Yongsu Valley is a fantastic driving course. The evening water that comes out of the mud near the valley is famous for its delicious taste, and there are several pensions there. There is a paved road to the right of the three-way intersection in Saenggol Village from the closed Saneum Branch School. From the village where the paved road ends, take the road to the right and climb 300 meters, passing through a fir forest, you will reach a forest road. If you go about 150m along the forest road, there is a sign on the right informing you of the Bongmisan Mountain hiking trail.

title: Seoksu Sports Park
description: Seoksu Sports Park is a daily sports-centered park located in Manan-gu, Anyang-si, and was created so that residents can enjoy exercise and relaxation in their daily lives. There are various sports facilities, including soccer fields, baseball fields, basketball courts, and badminton courts, as well as walking trails and rest facilities, so the whole family can use them comfortably. Family visitors and local club gatherings are active, and it is especially crowded with citizens enjoying soccer and baseball on weekends.

title: Seonbawi Art Museum
description: Seonbawi Art Museum, located in the beautiful and pleasant environment of Gwacheon, connecting Seoul and Gyeonggi-do, is a genre art museum established in 2004 by genre painter Lee Seo-ji with the purpose of reviving, recording, and preserving disappearing traditional customs and disseminating them to future generations. On a site of about 780 pyeong and an exhibition area of ​​22 pyeong, it houses and displays about 1,000 genre paintings by the late Lee Seo-ji, who painted the lifestyles, customs, and natural scenery of our ancient ancestors throughout his life, as well as traditional dolls and miniature village models by Kim Si-on, a traditional doll artist who created humorous images of our ancient ancestors.

title: Seonamsa Temple [UNESCO World Heritage]
description: Seonamsa Temple, located on the east side of the foot of Jogyesan Mountain, built Biroam in the 7th year of King Seong of Baekje (529), and in the 1st year of King Gyeongmun of Silla, State Preceptor Doseon founded the current Seonamsa Temple with Seonpung at Dongri Sanmun, one of the 9 mountains of King Seonjong. On the other side, on the western side of the mountain, is the famous Seungbo Temple, Songgwangsa Temple. Around Seonamsa Temple, there are oak trees, camellias, maples, and chestnut trees that are hundreds of years old, and the fall foliage is especially famous. In addition, there is an arch-shaped Seungseong Bridge in front of the temple (treasure). The pedestal is made of natural rock, so it is sturdy, and the dragon head in the center is very mysterious. The three-story stone pagodas (treasures) standing on the left and right in front of the main hall also attract the attention of tourists. It is one of the temples where the most traditional temple culture remains. In addition to the 7 treasures, there are 12 local cultural assets, including the majestic and splendid Daeungjeon, Palsangjeon, Wontongjeon, gilt-bronze incense burner, and Iljumun. If you climb the hiking trail on the left side of the main temple of Seonamsa Temple, you can see the rock-carved Buddha carved on a huge rock that is 7m high and 2m wide. A native tea garden with 800 years of tradition, the Jogyesan Mountain hiking trail connecting Songgwangsa Temple to Seonamsa Temple, crystal-like valley water, lush trees, and fall foliage add to the beauty of this place. In addition, near Seonamsa Temple, like Jirisan Mountain and Baekunsan Mountain, Korean cypress trees grow naturally, so you can taste the mineral water around Gyeongchip every year. Seonamsa Chiljeon Seonwon is a Zen meditation place at Seonamsa Temple, a temple located on the eastern foot of Jogyesan Mountain, Songju-eup, Suncheon-si, Jeollanam-do. As Taegochonglim, the only general forest of the Taego Order, it is a general monastery where numerous monks are practicing in Gangwon and Seonwon. ‘Chiljeon’ is a group of seven buildings located at the top of Seonamsa Temple. In the wild tea field behind Seonamsa Temple, there is a colony of native tea that is over 800 years old. When it comes to wild tea produced from tea farms, Hwagae tea is considered the best, but when it comes to purely natural wild tea, Seonamsa tea is considered the best. The characteristics of Seonamsa wild tea are described as ‘savory and deep taste.’ This is because the tea trees grow in shaded areas thick with cedar and oak trees, so the tea leaves are soft, and the fog and humid climate create a deep taste. However, it is not easy to taste Seonamsa tea. The Seonamsa tea field is not large, so the yield is small and it is treated as a precious treat.
priceDetail: Free

title: Seonyudam Valley
description: It is located in the Baekun-dong Valley in Dopyeong-ri, Idong-myeon, and is one of the 8 scenic spots in Pocheon. As the name suggests, it is said to be a place where immortals used to play, so it is called Seonyudam. The upper stream of Yeongpyeong Stream, which circles the foot of Baekun Mountain, is blue and very beautiful. The shadow of the steep rock wall submerged in water is nice, and the light reflecting off the rock wall is also beautiful. Three letters called Seonyudam are engraved on the rock wall, which are said to have been written by Yang Sa-eon during the Japanese invasions of Korea. Seonyudam Valley is over 10km long, and the water in the valley is clear and fresh in spring and fall. In particular, the valley that descends from west to east is backed by cliffs and dense forests, so the sun does not shine on the valley water throughout the day, making it even cooler. There are about 10 households residing in the upper valley, and there are both bed and breakfasts and restaurants, so eating is not a big inconvenience. Also, if you go briefly to Baekun Valley, you will find the famous Idong Galbi. Cooking is prohibited in Seonyudam Valley, and although there is a free parking lot opposite the Riverside Pension, it is full even on weekdays and you have to be very early to park on weekends. There are free tents and tables set up by Pocheon City, so you can grab an empty shaded spot. The water depth is shallow and the current is not fast, so it's perfect for playing in the water by bringing a tube and goggles.

title: Seonyudo
description: It was originally called Gunsando, but it came to be called Seonyudo because the shape of the peak, which is about 100 meters above sea level at the northern end of the island, looks like two immortals sitting face to face and playing baduk. Seonyudo, which has an area of ​​2.13km and a population of over 500, forms the Gogunsan Archipelago along with Sinsido, Munyeodo, Bangchukdo, and Maldo, and is the central island of the archipelago. Seonyudo is the center of the Gogunsan Archipelago and is an important strategic point in the West Sea. Seonyudo, which served as the headquarters of the naval forces during the Joseon Dynasty and served as a base, was also controlled by a naval commander. During the Goryeo Dynasty, it was not only a port of call on the Yeo-Song trade route, but it was also a maritime hub as an anchorage base for ships during the Japanese invasions of Korea, with Admiral Yi Sun-sin staying at Seonyudo for 11 days to reorganize his battle lines after his victory in the Battle of Myeongnyang. There is a famous spot called the Eight Scenic Views of the Gogunsan Archipelago, and the center of the eight scenic spots of Gogunsan Mountain is Jinmal of Seonyudo. The Lee and Kim clans dominate Seonyudo, with the Park, Lim, and Go clans also living there. As a folk religion, there were the Oryongmyoje, Jangsaengje, Susuje, and Burakje, but the traditions have been cut off, and relics include a shell mound and a group of monuments depicting a naval ancestor. It is connected to Jangjado Island in the southwest by Jangja Bridge, so it can be easily accessed. (Source: Gunsan City Culture and Tourism)

title: Seolmaejae Natural Recreation Forest
description: Seolmaejae Natural Recreation Forest is a recreation forest in the metropolitan area that can be reached within one hour from Seoul. This natural recreation forest opened on June 1, 1999 and has a total area of ​​70ha. Seolmaejae refers to the hill at the entrance to the main gate of the recreation forest. It is said that it was called Seolmaejae because plum blossoms bloomed in the snow on a winter day when there was a lot of snow in the past. The pine and larch forested areas, gorosoe, maple colonies, azalea, and pine hiking trails lead to Yumyeongsan Mountain and Yongmunsan Mountain, and the Yongcheon Valley and Yumyeongsan Valley are adjacent, making the scenery very impressive. The recreation forest has lodging facilities, a campsite, a playground, a badminton court, a foot volleyball court, and a sky water table, as well as auxiliary facilities such as a large auditorium, an event hall, and a lounge. Experience programs include valley trekking and woodworking experiences. It is suitable for group picnics, outdoor training, etc., and is adjacent to a survival game center, a paragliding slope at Yumyeongsan Mountain, and a paragliding practice range for beginners, making it great for enjoying outdoor leisure sports. In addition, Yongcheon Valley and Yumyeongsan Valley are close by, making it a suitable resort area. When using public transportation, get off at Yangpyeong Station on the Gyeongui-Jungan Line and take a city bus to Yongcheon-ri. It is a 20-minute ride.

title: Seolmijae Art Museum
description: Seolmijae Art Museum is a cultural and artistic space filled with the scent of nature. It is responsible for one axis of Korean contemporary art by planning cultural education and artist invitation exhibitions and exchange exhibitions for the Gapyeong community. In order to develop Gapyeong region culture, it holds special exhibitions by inviting artists from Gapyeong through an annual contest. It all started when Director Chugyeong opened a studio in Seorak-myeon, Gapyeong-gun after living in Seoul in 2007. It was established to not only cultivate the cultural knowledge of Gapyeong-gun residents, but also to nurture young artists and provide creative art education to students in Gapyeong area. The exhibition room on the first floor of the Seolmijae Museum of Art is 35 pyeong, and special exhibitions are mainly held there. Seminars are mainly held at the Art Institute, and through three creative studios, new artists are fostered and a community is formed and revitalized. In addition, it is equipped with an outdoor experiential learning room to provide experiential education programs to students in Gapyeong. In addition, we are making efforts to develop art through exhibitions, projects, and art education.

title: Seolbongsan Mountain
description: Seolbongsan Mountain is about 394m high and is a mountain that protects Icheon City. Seolbongsan Mountain, which surrounds the city of Icheon from the west, is also called Buaksan Mountain, Muhaksan Mountain, and Buhaksan Mountain. Seolbongsan Mountain has a total of five hiking trails, with both Deulmeori and Nalmeori being the parking lot of Seolbong Park. Course 3 is a course that goes through park entrance → Hoam Mineral Water → Seolbongsanseong Fortress → Summit → Hwadujae → Haksojeong. It is considered a representative hiking course that allows you to see cultural relics such as Seolbongsanseong Fortress, a castle from the Silla Dynasty, Yeongwolam Hermitage and Seolbong Seowon built during the Goryeo Dynasty, and various rock peaks including Kalbawi on the way to the summit, Three Brothers Rock, Hoam Valley, and Hoam Mineral Springs. The course is 6.85km in total and takes about 120 minutes. Although it is a bit long, it is an easy course that even beginners and children can climb. In particular, Seolbongsan Mountain is widely known for its azalea colonies that bloom in abundance in spring, and many tourists flock there. After hiking, you can tour the museums and art galleries in Seolbong Park, Seolbong Sculpture Park, etc., or relieve fatigue by taking a hot spring bath at the nearby Anheung Recreation Area in the city. There is a Icheon Tourist Information Center near the first parking lot near Seolbong Reservoir, where you can get tourist information if necessary. In addition to Seolbong Park Parking Lot 1, which is the main parking lot, there are separate parking lots at all museums, art galleries, and other facilities in the park, so you can use the parking lot located nearby for each course. It takes about 8 minutes by car from Sindun IC, and about 10 minutes by car from Icheon Station on the Gyeonggang Line and Icheon General Terminal. Nearby are Sagimaggol Ceramic Village, Yes Park, Icheon Seolbong Hot Springs Land, Miranda Hotel Spa Plus, Seongho Lake Lotus Complex, Hantaek Botanical Garden, Jisan Forest Resort Ski Resort, Icheon Termeden, and Deokpyeong Dinosaur Arboretum.

title: Seoraksan Cable Car
description: The best way to comfortably enjoy the secret scenery of Seorak Mountain is to use the Seorak Cable Car. The cable car station is located in Seoraksan National Park, and it takes about 10 minutes to reach Gwongeumseong Fortress, which is 700 meters above sea level. Since one-way tickets are not available, you must purchase a round-trip ticket. Even while traveling by cable car, you can admire famous attractions such as Ulsan Rock and Manmulsang through the glass window. When you reach Gwongeumseong Fortress, the majestic scenery of Seoraksan Mountain unfolds like a panorama. There is a legend that Gwongeumseong Fortress, built during the Goryeo Dynasty to prevent enemy invasions, was built by two generals from the Gwon and Kim clans in one day. Now only the foundation remains, reminding us of past history. Seoraksan Mountain, seen from the top of Gwongeumseong Fortress, is majestic and mysterious with various strangely shaped rocks. If you stand at the top, you can capture the entire scenery of Oeseorak. Just below Gwongeumseong Fortress, Anakam Rock, built during the Silla Dynasty, and the Muhak Pine Tree, which has survived for hundreds of years, cannot help but excite one's admiration. There are many tourists on weekends, public holidays, and fall foliage season, so it is best to plan your trip taking the waiting time into account.
operatingHours: Detailed times will be announced on the website 1 day prior to operation.

title: Seorak Beach
description: Yangyang Seorak Beach is a place where you can enjoy water play and surfing, making it a great place to spend your summer vacation. Seorak Beach, located 8km north of Yangyang-eup, has shallow, quiet waters and is located on a road where you can tour Mt. Seorak, Naksansa Temple, and Osaek Mineral Water, making it an optimal travel destination for families. The white sand beach is 1km long and 80m wide and has a gentle slope, making it suitable for children to play. There are many tourist resources nearby, including Naksansa Temple, a thousand-year-old temple, Uisangdae Pavilion, Hongnyeonam Hermitage, and the Seawater Avalokitesvara Statue, making it a place where you can enjoy both summer vacation and sightseeing. The waves are high, making it great for swimming and surfing, and there is also a space where you can relax with an umbrella and a mat. It is a small beach that is not widely known among the beaches on the East Sea, so it is popular with tourists looking for a quiet and secluded beach. Naksan Beach is located to the south, and Mulchi Port and Hujin Port are located to the north, making it a good place to enjoy fresh seafood.
address: Habok-ri, Ganghyeon-myeon, Yangyang-gun, Gangwon Special Self-Governing Province

title: Seolhaewon
description: It is a luxury integrated resort located behind Yangyang International Airport. It is a resort that presents a vision of relaxation and healing in the Seorak region, and you can enjoy a golf course, luxury accommodations, hot spring sauna, and auxiliary facilities. Seolhaewon means ‘a garden of rest embracing Seorak Mountain and the East Sea.’ As befits its name, Yangyang Dongho Beach is located to the east of the accommodation, and the foot of Seoraksan Mountain is located to the west. The resort is centered around Seolhaewon, which was selected as one of the top 10 golf courses in Korea, and has various types of rooms, including mountain stays, Seol Hot Springs, and golftels. All rooms have a view of the golf course, and depending on the room location, you can see the natural scenery of Seoraksan Mountain and the East Sea. Mountain Stay, a two-story luxury villa, consists of seven types, including a pool suite with a pool and a spa suite with a cypress sauna. Seol Hot Springs, a condominium with hot spring water supplied to all rooms, stands out with its 10 different room designs, including a pool suite with a family pool. There are several auxiliary facilities within the resort. You can use the clubhouse restaurant that serves unique seasonal food, the Seolhae trail where you can take a walk while smelling the scent of pine trees, and the hot spring sauna where you can wash away fatigue with hot spring water.

title: Seopjikoji
description: As can be seen from the name of Seopjikoji (Jeju dialect meaning Koji Cape), Seopjikoji is a landform with a protruding tip shaped like a nose tree. Location-wise, it protrudes from the coast of Shinyang-ri, Seongsan-eup, Seogwipo-si. It is not that easy to get to for outsiders, but in most cases, you can reach the end of Koji by entering the village from the Shinyang-ri coastal national highway, looking at the sign, and following the concrete road. Or, if you are coming from Seogwipo, go about 7km past downtown Pyoseon, and when you see a coastal road sign on the right, turn right here and run along the sea all the way while looking at the panoramic view of Seopjikoji. Soon you will see the white sand beach of Shinyang Beach, and when you reach the village, turn right and follow the concrete road. In particular, the rape blossoms here have a more vivid and beautiful color than anywhere else in harmony with the bright sunlight and blue sea. On top of Koji Hill, which is wide and flat, there is a stone beacon station called Hyeopjeondae, where beacon fires were lit in the old days. It is about 4m high and 9m wide, and is relatively preserved in its original form. The peak rising northeast of Yeondong is called Red Oreum, an oreum made of red volcanic ash called song in Jeju. The sight of the white lighthouse at the top evokes another exotic atmosphere, contrasting with the yellow rape flower field, the red earth of the Oreum, and the blue sky and sea. There are iron stairs up to the lighthouse, so you can easily climb up. If you climb up on the railing of the lighthouse, the amazing coastal scenery of Seopjikoji unfolds right in front of you.

In addition, we are helping to provide high-quality cultural life by operating a cultural school. Cultural classes include folk songs, Chinese calligraphy, Korean dance, pansori, gayageum, and pungmul.

It is built with 4 floors underground and 2 floors above ground, and has a large theater with 645 seats and a small theater with about 200 seats. The grand theater provides a comfortable performance environment with high-end speakers and an acoustic design that minimizes the inflow of external sounds. In addition, office space for local art groups such as the Seongnam Arts Council and the Seongnam Women's Choir are located together, serving as a center for civic art activities.

description: Seongnam Arts Center, which opened on October 14, 2005, embodies cutting-edge trends in performing and exhibition arts and aims to be a local cultural space. Since its opening in three performance halls (Opera House, Concert Hall, and Ensemble Theater) and exhibition spaces (Cube Art Museum, Gallery 808, Bandal Gallery, and Permanent Exhibition Hall), Seongnam Arts Center, operated by Seongnam Cultural Foundation, has established itself as the center of Seongnam culture and arts by presenting original cultural contents such as domestic premieres, Seongnam exclusives, self-produced projects, and local programs. In addition, it operates various facilities such as the World Musical Instrument Exhibition Hall, Seongnam Media Center, Central Park Outdoor Performance Hall, and Book Theme Park, providing citizens with a friendly cultural rest area and bringing joy to their daily lives. Various culture and arts support policy projects, including the Sarangbang Culture Club, which has attracted attention as a cultural brand symbolizing Seongnam, and the creative education programs of the Seongnam Media Center and Academy in cooperation with the local community, including citizens, schools, and companies, are laying the foundation for all citizens to enjoy culture and arts and communicate through culture and arts.

title: Seongsan Ilchulbong [UNESCO World Natural Heritage]
description: Seongsan Ilchulbong, which is 180 meters above sea level, is a volcanic body that exploded underwater about 5,000 years ago, which is rare among Jeju Island's numerous craters. The explosion that occurs when lava mixes with water breaks the lava into fine volcanic ash, which is piled up in a cone around the crater. It was originally a volcanic island, but sand and gravel piled up between the island and the land near Shinyang Beach, connecting it to the mainland. At the top of Ilchulbong Peak, there is a crater with a diameter of 600 m, a floor height of 90 m above sea level, and an area of ​​214,400 m2. Since ancient times, the sunrise view seen from the top of Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak has been said to be the best among the 10 scenic spots in Yeongju (Jeju's scenic spots). The sunrise rising from the horizon beyond the flowing blue sea colors the entire sea, captures the hearts of those who see it, and makes them admire it.

title: Seongseong Lake Park
description: Eopseong Reservoir, which was created by combining the 'seong' of Eopseong-dong and the 'seong' of Seongseong-dong, was transformed. The water quality of Eopseong Reservoir deteriorated to grade 6 and it lost its function as an agricultural reservoir. As a result of Cheonan City's water quality improvement and natural ecosystem restoration project, it was transformed into 'Seongseong Lake Park'. Visitor center (promotion center/experience center), grass yard and forest playground, ecological trail, and Seongseong Mulbit, a nature observation bridge. It is an eco-friendly ecological park in the midst of urban life where nature and people coexist, including Nuri Bridge, artificial plant islands, and water circulation facilities. In this park, you can see various amphibians such as endangered golden frogs and mallards, as well as mandarin ducks, mallards, and white-cheeked ducks.

If you go up the trail while looking at plants such as hydrangea, sycamore, and maekmundong, there are stairs made of stone and wood here and there, so you can trek without getting bored. At the top of the park, there is a fitness center with exercise equipment and a tap with cool mineral water. There is a high-pressure duster at the exit, and there is also a cool mineral spring that is the pride of this park. ※ Pets are allowed (bring leash and waste bag)

In addition, it is a garden of water and flowers that was created as a space for culture and art and a breath of our history through the creation of various facilities and experiential events, including the Lotus Museum, Water Lily Greenhouse, Seokchangwon, and Sangchunwon.

description: Sejong Gugakdang is a municipal performance hall in Yeoju City and was built in 1990. The Korean traditional music hall, built by Yeoju City to support and promote the cultural and artistic activities of Yeoju citizens, was built with one floor underground and one floor above ground. The Korean traditional music hall, which has a performance hall with 388 seats and a practice room, is a base for various cultural and artistic activities, where various cultural and artistic performances are held. It is well-equipped with auxiliary facilities necessary for performances, such as special lighting facilities, stage curtains, projection screens, pianos, and stage sound equipment, and supports Yeoju citizens to enjoy high-quality cultural and artistic performances such as concerts, performances, plays, exhibitions, and lectures. To apply for rental, you can apply in person or by email after checking the facility. Nearby, there are tourist attractions such as Yeojuhyanggyo Confucian School, Joseon Hyojong Yeongneung Relic, and Yeoju Ceramics Complex, and you can also enjoy the Icheon Rice Culture Festival.

It is a place where the white sand and black basalt that are revealed when the water goes out are in beautiful harmony with the emerald sea. Among Jeju's many beaches, the small Sehwa Beach is widely known thanks to Bellongjang and Sehwa Folk Oil Market. This five-day market, the largest in the eastern region and held right next to the beach, provides a glimpse into the lives of the islanders every five days.

title: Sonobell Vivaldi Park Ocean World
description: Hongcheon Sonobell Vivaldi Park is a four-season leisure complex located in Hongcheon-gun, Gangwon-do. It has a variety of leisure sports facilities such as golf, skiing, and water play, as well as a variety of accommodations such as hotels, condos, and pensions. Ocean World, located within Sonobell Vivaldi Park, opened on July 5, 2006 and provides people with fun and enjoyment with a variety of water play facilities. Ocean World is an eco-friendly water park that minimizes damage to the natural environment, and all ages can enjoy comfortable relaxation and thrilling fun at the same time. The total size is 126,645㎡, including 43,291㎡ indoor zone, 25,787㎡ extreme zone, 19,284㎡ wave pool zone, 31,242㎡ dynamic zone, and 7,041㎡ mega slide zone. This is 14 times the size of a soccer field and can accommodate 23,000 people at the same time. Gangwon area Ocean World, which was built to create the illusion of being transported to an unimaginable sea amidst a clean forest with curving ridges, closely resembles Egypt. It is an even more attractive place as it is equipped with various sculptures that convey the breath of Egypt, such as pyramids, sphinxes, and pharaohs. This place is largely divided into indoor zone, extreme zone, dynamic zone, and mega slide zone. The indoor zone can be used by various age groups, including a wave pool, lazy river, tube/body slide, bathe pool, waterplex for infants/children, sauna, and outdoor open-air bath. True to its name, the Extreme Zone is in the spotlight among young people, including Surfing Mount, which boasts Korea's only 8-foot V wave, and Extreme River, where you can experience the thrill of continuous waves. The Dynamic Zone is a space that provides thrilling fun with thrilling themed water play facilities such as the world's longest Monster Blaster at 300m, the 6-seater Super Boomerango, and the ultra-large Giant Waterplex. The Mega Slide Zone, newly created in 2011, allows you to enjoy a variety of thrills, including the world's first Super S Ride, Korea's first and largest 8-seater Cairo Racing, the ultimate thrill Double Tornado Slide, and the maximum centrifugal force Double Spin Slide.

title: Sorae Mountain
description: The name ''Sorae'' is said to have originated for the following reasons: firstly, the terrain is shaped like a conch; secondly, there are many forests near the stream, i.e., it originated from Solnae (松川); and thirdly, the terrain is narrow, i.e., Solda → Narrow. According to the story, in the 7th year of King Muyeol of Silla (660), So Jeongbang of the Tang Dynasty personally led the military as a member of the Silla-Tang allied army to attack Baekje, departing from Laeju in Shandong Province, China, passing through Deokjeokdo Island and staying on this mountain. From then on, it is said that it began to be called ''Soraesan'' by combining the ''So(蘇)'' of Sojeongbang and the ''Rae'' of Raeju. Sorae Mountain, which has such a beautiful natural scenery that even citizens of nearby Incheon and Bucheon come to enjoy it on holidays, is a place that is loved by citizens as a resting place where they can comfortably relieve accumulated fatigue and tension if they take a little time out of their busy daily lives. On a clear day, Sorae Mountain Forest Bathing Park, which clearly overlooks downtown Seoul and the West Sea with the naked eye, was established in 1992 by the city of Siheung to improve the health and emotional life of citizens. It was created with an investment of 50 million won. The existing 5km long trail from the entrance to Naewonsa Temple to the summit has been maintained with various sports facilities, a reading forest, and a forest for strength training using wooden ropes. In addition, Soamcheon Mineral Spring and Cheongryong Mineral Spring quench the thirst of all those who visit Soraesan Forest Bathing Area by providing high-quality water. At the foot of the mountain is the tomb of Hayeon, who served as Yeonguijeong during the reign of King Sejong of the Joseon Dynasty, and on the eastern side of the mountain, Korea's largest rock-carved Bodhisattva statue, known to be from the early Goryeo Dynasty, is engraved on a folding screen rock, making it an excellent nature study center and the birthplace of history for children. If you walk for about 1 hour and 30 minutes through a lush forest of pine trees and pine trees, you can find peace of mind and body thanks to the aromatic substance called phytoncide emitted from the trees. There is no place like this as a resort using natural health therapy. In addition, hang glider demonstrations that sometimes decorate the skies of Sorae Mountain on weekends provide a new world for enthusiasts and a variety of attractions for the general public.

title: Mt. Sorisan
description: Although the height is not that high at 479m, the mountain slope is rather steep, and the scenery is so beautiful that locals call it Salt River. There is a story that it was called Surisan Mountain because vultures lived on the rocky cliffs of the mountain, but it was later changed to Sorisan Mountain. Because the forest is dense and the valley is beautiful, many families visit here for vacation in the summer. The summit and main ridge are made of rocks, and the side of Saneumcheon Stream is a rocky cliff. Yongso Valley, located between Saneum-ri and Seoksan-ri, is a popular resting place due to its strangely shaped cliffs, abundant, clear water, and pebbly spaces here and there. The Sorisan Gorosoe Festival is held every March.

title: Soyosan National Tourist Site
description: Soyosan Mountain (587.5 m) is made up of exquisitely shaped natural rocks and strangely shaped peaks, reminiscent of a panoramic view. The mysterious atmosphere of the abyssal valley on a summer day and the deep beauty of fall foliage make it the most famous mountain north of Hansu, and is called Sogeumgang (Mt. Geumgangsan) of Gyeonggi. Starting with the Freedom Protection Peace Museum located at the entrance to the Soyosan tourist attraction, there are tourist attractions such as the Healthy Five Elements Road, which prays for the happiness and health of tourists, the site of Princess Yoseok's villa filled with the affectionate story of Great Master Wonhyo and Princess Yoseok, Wonhyodae, where Great Master Wonhyo prayed, Jajae Rock, a thousand-year-old temple, Cheongnyang Falls, and Wonhyo Falls.

title: Soyo Living Sports Park
description: Soyo Life Sports Park is a sports-centered park and multi-purpose sports space that supports local residents’ health promotion and leisure activities. It is equipped with a variety of sports facilities, including an artificial turf soccer field, badminton court, basketball court, and futsal court, so anyone can enjoy exercising without burden. Sincheon flows in front of the park, making it pleasant to take a walk or walk along the waterway. Ssamzie Park in Sangbongam-dong is located nearby, so you can take a break after exercising.

title: Sojourn Art Museum
description: ‘Sojeon Art Museum’ is based on a ceramic collection donated by the late Kim Yong-san, who was the chairman of the Sojeon Foundation. It was exhibited in Yeonji-dong, Jongno-gu, Seoul in 1994, and then moved to Daeya-dong, Siheung-si, Gyeonggi-do in 1996 and opened. Designated as a ceramics-centered theme art museum by Gyeonggi Province in 1997, it preserves and exhibits masterpieces of ceramics, Buddhist art, paintings, crafts, and sculptures that express a variety of Korean aesthetics. The Sojeon Museum of Art, located in a beautiful natural environment, consists of a permanent exhibition hall where you can see luxury ceramics from the Goryeo and Joseon Dynasties and an outdoor garden where sculptures by masters such as César and Bourdelle are displayed.

title: Sokcho Oeongchi Sea Scent
description: Sea Fragrance is a unique coastal walking course that stretches 1.74km from Sokcho Beach to Oeongchi Port. It is largely divided into the Sokcho Beach section (850m) and the Oeongchi section (890m), and each section has a different atmosphere. If you want to take a leisurely walk along the beach, the Sokcho Beach section is suitable, and if you want to capture dynamic scenery, the Oeongchi section is recommended. The Oeongchi section has been off-limits to civilians for decades, and contains a natural beauty that has remained untouched for a long time. It is also famous as a filming location for the drama ‘Boyfriend’. Along the wooden deck trail and the dirt road, the blue sea continues endlessly, and the sound of crashing waves adds to the refreshing feeling. The sea water is so clear and clean that the bottom is clearly visible. The Oeongchi section is comprised of four themed courses: Bamboo Meditation Path, Sky Deck Path, Security Experience Path, and Rock Observation Path. The coastal border fence surrounding the security experience road is a partial remnant of what was installed after the armed communist infiltration incident in 1970. It is also very fun to see the strange rocks formed on the coast, such as Oyster Rock and Centipede Rock.

title: Sokcho Tourist & Fishery Market
description: Sokcho Tourist & Fishery Market, considered a must-visit for a trip to Sokcho, is a place overflowing with fresh seafood and specialties from the East Coast. Also, it is full of all kinds of food, including squid sundae, abai sundae, and fried chicken. The combination of large commercial buildings with one floor underground and two floors above ground and specialized alley markets adds to the attractions. The first floor of the commercial building houses dry goods, vegetables, and food, and the second floor houses clothing, daily necessities, general stores, and Nonghyup Hanaro Mart, where you can purchase a variety of products. There is also a raw fish center in the basement, where you can taste fresh live fish and seafood at low prices. The alley market is divided into five alleys, including Fruit and Vegetable Alley, Sundae Alley, and Salted Fish Market Alley, depending on the product. The fresh produce, fish, and dried fish spread out on the stalls make me slow down. Dakgangjeon Alley, a popular destination for tourists, has many crispy and spicy chicken gangjeong stores. Each store captivates the taste buds of tourists with different know-how. All alley markets are equipped with rain protection facilities, so you can visit comfortably even when it rains. They have a clean and comfortable environment and a spacious parking lot.

title: Sokcho City Museum·Sokcho Displaced Persons Cultural Village
venue: Sokcho City Museum·Sokcho Displaced Persons Cultural Village
description: Sokcho City Museum is a cultural experience tourist attraction where you can experience and learn about the history, culture, and natural environment of Sokcho from prehistoric times to modern times. In addition to the old traditional culture, the mountain culture formed around Mt. Seorak, the fishing village culture with the East Sea as its base of life, and the culture of displaced people who fled during the Korean War are explained step by step in an easy-to-understand manner. The museum’s permanent exhibition is divided into four exhibition rooms. The first exhibition room introduces the natural environment and cultural characteristics of Sokcho, and the second exhibition room displays the fishing village formed on the beach and the lives of the displaced people. The third exhibition room is a space tailored to the eye level of children and provides a variety of traditional cultural experiences. Inside the Sokcho City Museum, the Displaced People’s Culture Village and Balhae History Museum are located together. In the outdoor Cultural Village for Displaced Persons, North Korean houses such as Gaeseong House, Pyeongyang House, and Hwanghae-do House are on display, and lodging experiences are also available. The Cheongho-dong alley, where refugees from the North lived together after the Korean War, and the old Sokcho Station, which was demolished in 1978, are also recreated. The Balhae History Museum is a space that examines the history of Balhae, which ruled Manchuria and the northern region of the Korean Peninsula. Photos, videos, and relics of historical sites are on display, and you can also experience Balhae's tomb culture.

title: Sokcho Beach
description: Sokcho Beach, which first opened in 1976, is one of Korea's representative beaches. The advantage is that it is close to downtown Sokcho and the express bus terminal is within walking distance, so transportation is convenient. Sokcho Beach has clear and clean sea water, shallow depth, and gentle slope, so it is crowded with vacationers from all over the country every summer. Especially during the peak season of July and August, the wide beach is filled with people without space to step on them. The area around the beach is well-equipped with restaurants and convenience facilities. There is a pine forest behind the beach, and there is also a small park and walking path. Even after the holiday season, tourists continue to visit the beach. This is because the sculptures installed all over the sandy beach offer a variety of things to see regardless of the season. The initials ‘ㅅㅊ’ symbolizing Sokcho, a large compass showing the directions of countries around the world, and vibrant dolphin sculptures all catch the eye. The large picture frame with the blue sea in the background and the Stairway to Heaven stretching toward the sky are the most popular photo zones here. Every year, tourists can enjoy busking, summer beach festivals, and Sokcho Craft Beer Festivals here to create more enjoyable memories. If you visit at the right time, you can enjoy performance events such as band performances and concerts.

title: Sokcho Beach Ferris Wheel (Sokcho i)
venue: Sokcho Beach Ferris Wheel Sokcho Eye
description: It is the only place in Korea located on a beach, so you can enjoy a panoramic view of the blue sea of ​​Sokcho and the beautiful scenery of Seoraksan Mountain. Sokcho i is a 22-story apartment building with 36 Ferris wheels with a capacity of 6, allowing up to 216 people to use them at the same time. The travel time is approximately 15 minutes and air conditioning is provided during the summer. Bringing in food other than bottled water is prohibited. You can feel the sparkling clear sea and Sokcho during the day, and a romantic atmosphere with bright lights at night.
operatingHours: - Weekdays 10:00~20:00 (Ticket sales close at 19:30) - Weekends and public holidays 10:00~21:00 (Ticket sales close at 20:30)

title: Songdo Central Park
description: Songdo Central Park, a park filled with nature between a forest of high-rise buildings in Songdo, was created with New York's Central Park as a motif. It is Korea's first seawater park using seawater and an urban park that takes advantage of Korea's topographical characteristics. The artificial waterway is equipped with water leisure facilities such as water taxis and canoes, and it is a landmark and relaxation space in Songdo where you can enjoy various cultures and arts throughout the park. There are five themed gardens within Central Park. The Sunset Garden, located at the western end of Central Park, is a space with attractions such as the West Boat House, waterside stage, children's garden, and cube sculpture, while the Emotional Garden is a landscape observation space consisting of facilities such as an observation deck and tidal support, as well as the Face of the Global Village, a work of art made with masks symbolizing 120 countries around the world. Grass Garden is a complex art space where you can enjoy various sculptures and public art works, such as the Manneken Pis statue, observation deck, wetland garden, and firefly house. The Walking Garden is a traditional theme space where you can see deer grazing leisurely. Songhwajeong, located high in the east, offers a picturesque night view with the moonlight. The Terrace Garden, where the UN Square, East Boat House, and Folk Playground are located, is a cultural and artistic space where various events are held throughout the year.
operatingHours: Open all the time ※ Please call for details

title: Songsansaji Neighborhood Park
description: Songsansaji Neighborhood Park is a green space where you can enjoy nature and historical sites. In the middle of the park is the ruins of Songsansa Temple, a Gyeonggi-do monument that houses the memorial tablets of six loyal subjects of the late Goryeo Dynasty, and around the shrine is a dense pine forest and a wide lawn plaza. The garden, which reflects traditional elements such as a pond and a crepe myrtle garden, gives you a sense of the tranquil elegance of a Korean garden. It is also suitable for families as it is well-equipped with convenient facilities such as a folk yard where you can experience traditional swings and neolttwigi, walking trails, a children's playground, and exercise equipment.

title: Songjeong Station (old)
description: Songjeong Station is a train station in Songjeong-dong, Haeundae-gu, Busan. It belongs to the Donghae Nambu Line built for the purpose of transporting seafood and resources on the East Coast. The Donghae Nambu Line opened to Gyeongju and Pohang in 1918, and to Busan, Ulsan, and Gyeongju in 1935, serving people for a long time. In particular, the scenery outside the window along the sea was considered beautiful. Songjeong Station began operations as a simple station staffed by station staff in 1934 and was promoted to a regular station in 1941. It appears that the station was rebuilt at this time, and it retains the architectural characteristics of train stations from the 1940s, similar to Unsan Station and Danchon Station. Although cargo operations were discontinued in 1976, its railroad historical value was recognized and it was designated as a registered cultural property. It has recently been renovated as the starting and ending station of the Haeundae Beach Train, which utilizes the old railroad tracks of the Donghae Nambu Line, and is attracting many tourists.
operatingHours: 09:30~22:00 ※ Operating hours may vary depending on the situation.

title: Songchu Valley
description: Songchu Valley is a valley located in Uldae-ri, Jangheung-myeon, Yangju-si, Gyeonggi-do. It is located at the Songchu Obong branch of Bukhansan National Park and is easily accessible from anywhere in the metropolitan area. The name was given because it is a valley with many pine trees and sycamore trees. Around the valley, there are dense forests such as pine trees, cottonwood trees, and maple trees, and strangely shaped rocks that harmonize with the valley water, creating a beautiful scenery.

title: Sudeoksa Temple (Yesan)
description: Sudeoksa Temple is a temple located at the southern foot of Deoksungsan Mountain (495m) in the Charyeong Mountain Range near Deoksan Hot Springs. It is so large that it is the headquarters of the 7th Diocese of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, which oversees the Jogye Order temples in the Naepo region of South Chungcheong Province. It is an ancient temple that was founded around the 6th century during the Baekje Dynasty and boasts a history of nearly 1,500 years. It boasts a scenery so beautiful that it was selected as the No. 1 scenic spot in Yesan-gun. The founding story is that a young man fell in love with a young woman, and her condition for marriage was that he build a temple. After building the temple, he held Nangja's hand and she disappeared, and it turned out that she was the incarnation of Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva. Sudeoksa Temple, which was founded with these tales, went through several renovations during the Goryeo, Joseon, and Japanese colonial periods and is still standing today. Here, cultural assets from the Baekje period to the Joseon Dynasty remain. In addition to the Daeungjeon Hall designated as a national treasure, the Nosanabulgwaebultaeng and Myobop Lotus Sutra designated as treasures, as well as the three-story stone pagoda and seven-story stone pagoda, many cultural assets designated by Chungcheongnam-do are also preserved. In addition, various Buddhist cultural assets are stored in the Geunyeokseong Archives, and the thatched house where artist Lee Eung-no (1904-1989) practiced his art, the historical site of Lee Eung-no (Sudeok Inn), and the Seon Art Museum, which displays works by Lee Eung-no and modern and contemporary artists as well as Buddhist artworks, are also located within the precincts. Temple Stay operates a variety of programs to suit needs and tastes.
priceDetail: Free

title: Sudeok Mountain
description: Sudeoksan Mountain is a mountain formed by a mountain range that extends straight down to the south from the summit of Hwaaksan Mountain, the highest peak in Gyeonggi-do, and rises again. Near the top of this place are Sinseonbawi Rock and Daewonsa Temple. It is said that it was called Sudeoksan Mountain or Suseopsan Mountain because a high monk helped him and accumulated virtue at Daewonsa Temple. Sudeoksan Mountain is not well-known as a hiking destination because it is overshadowed by the fame of nearby Myeongjisan Mountain and Hwaaksan Mountain, but it is not visited often by people, so it maintains its natural appearance. The height of the summit of Sudeoksan Mountain is 795m, and when you reach the top, you can see Mongdeoksan Mountain and Bukbaesan Mountain to the east and Myeongjisan Mountain to the west, offering a panoramic view of Gyeonggi-do's famous mountains. Since it is relatively natural, beginners should carefully read the hiking guide before visiting. In spring, trees begin to bud and you can see azaleas and various wildflowers.

title: Arboretum Road Night Market
description: It is a night market created as a tourist attraction in the form of a complex theme park in the oldest and largest pine tree colony in Jeju Island. It is the first night market in Korea with an area of ​​approximately 4,000 pyeong and a pristine night market created in a pine forest. Currently, there are a total of 18 food trucks in operation, including 2 trucks operated by multicultural families, 9 trucks operated by young entrepreneurs, and 7 trucks in the Jeju region, and about 30 teams of sellers comprised of small business owners in the Jeju region are operating.

title: Suwon Yeongtong Library
description: In the 21st century era of knowledge and information, Suwon City has taken the lead as the nation's leading city of lifelong learning and culture, and has established 3 children's libraries in each region, the West Suwon and Buksuwon libraries, and 2 general libraries so that all citizens can use libraries nearby, resulting in 8 libraries along with the existing Seongyeong, Jungang, and Yeongtong libraries. In order to increase the number of libraries and stay ahead of the curve in service quality, we receive donations of excellent books from citizens (groups) and purchase new ones so that citizens can acquire specialized knowledge. We are also building a user-centered one-stop electronic library with books, member information, and unmanned automation to ensure convenient use.

title: Suwon Hwaseong [UNESCO World Heritage]
description: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress was completed in September 1796 after King Jeongjo, the 22nd king of the Joseon Dynasty, moved his father's acupuncture point to Suwon Hwaseong out of filial piety toward Crown Prince Jangheon. Suwon Hwaseong Fortress was built by King Jeongjo, the 22nd king of the Joseon Dynasty, who was installed as crown prince, but was embroiled in a factional dispute and could not ascend to the throne. He enshrined the wish of his father, Crown Prince Sado, who died in a dungeon from Baebongsan Mountain in Yangju to Suwon Hwasan, the most famous site of Joseon, and moved the town office near Hwasan to its current location under Paldalsan Mountain in Suwon. Not only did King Jeongjo's filial piety become the basis for the fortress, but it was also built as the center of a political plan containing grand political aspirations to eradicate factional politics caused by party strife and realize strong royal politics, and was intended to be used as a defense fortress south of the capital. Suwon Hwaseong Fortress is a type of fortress that cannot be found in China or Japan, and has both military defense and commercial functions. It can be said to be the best of Oriental castles with the most scientific, rational, and practical facility functions. (Source: Suwon Cultural Foundation website)

title: Suwon KT Wiz Park
description: Suwon KT Wiz Park is a baseball stadium in Suwon that opened in 1989 and provides an optimal playing environment for both players and visitors by introducing a ubiquitous sensor network system that automatically controls temperature, humidity, and lighting. ICT infrastructure such as wireless Internet has been established within the stadium, allowing various services such as admission registration, parking information, seat search, and food ordering to be conveniently used through mobile devices. Considering the tastes and convenience of visitors, various types of seats are provided, including exciting seats, friendly seats, couple seats, and disabled seats.

title: Suwon Gwanggyo Museum
description: Suwon Gwanggyo Museum is composed of the ''Gwanggyo History and Culture Room'', where you can see the history of Gwanggyo at a glance, focusing on relics excavated during the construction of Gwanggyo New Town, the ''Sogang Civil Service Room'', which displays donated materials covering various aspects of Korea's modern history, including politics, society, and culture, and the ''Saun Jonghak Room'', which consists of various donated relics related to the territory including Admiral Yi Sun-sin and Dokdo, and the history of the Japanese invasion. Suwon Gwanggyo Museum is located within Gwanggyo Historical Park, along with historical sites such as Sim On's tomb and Hyeryeong-gun's tomb, and is a cultural space for 1.2 million Suwon citizens where they can learn and relax at the same time. In addition, artifacts from prehistoric times to modern times excavated in the Gwanggyo New Town development area are on display, allowing visitors to explore a variety of history and culture, and experience history and culture through donated artifacts. It is also attracting attention as a place for weekend family outings by providing opportunities for children to encounter and understand the artifacts on display in various ways through the Children's Experience Room.

title: Suwon Messe
description: Suwon Messe, an exhibition and convention center, was built by a consortium between Messe Awards, Korea's No. 1 exhibition organizer, and KCC, the land owner. It is the largest exhibition hall in southern Gyeonggi Province and is Korea’s first private convention center operated by the private sector. As this is the first project attempted in Korea, it was built with reference to many overseas operation cases, such as visiting and consulting on the Sands Expo and Convention Center, the first private convention center in the United States at the time of construction. Suwon Messe is located at the top industrial center in Korea, with over 90 industrial complexes within a 30km radius, and is located adjacent to the Suwon Station transfer center, making it easily accessible by public transportation. Suwon Messe has established itself as an exhibition and convention center that turns everything you imagine into reality. Admission fees for exhibitions displayed at Suwon Messe are selected and set by each exhibition host company.
price: 3,000 won for the first hour / maximum daily rate 30,000 won

title: Suwon Cultural Center
description: Suwon Cultural Center is a non-profit cultural organization established in 1957 for the purpose of promoting local culture and was established to provide various cultural benefits to citizens. There is a cultural school for the lifelong education of citizens, which opens various courses and runs them all year round, and plays a pivotal role in the cultural development of Suwon by planning and holding cultural events. Major projects include the Daeboreum Folk Game Festival, King Jeongjo's Tomb Road Experience Pilgrimage, Humanities History Tour, Let's Play at Suwon Hwaseong Fortress with Straw Shoes, Suwon Hwaseong Fortress Construction Experience, Special Performances, and New Year's Bell Ringing on New Year's Eve. We are making great efforts to discover local history and preserve and transmit local culture, and we also run cultural and artistic events. By playing a leading role in the restoration of Suwon Fortress, the root of Suwon, it is contributing greatly to the formation of Suwon's modern cultural scene, including contributing to the development of Suwon as a cultural and tourism city by laying a stepping stone to be registered as a World Cultural Heritage.

title: Suwon Museum of Art
description: Suwon Museum of Art, Suwon's first municipal art museum, is a cultural and artistic space located in Suwon Hwaseong Temporary Palace Square and aims to provide art for the public, creative art education, and a shared art space. The art museum operates four spaces, including ‘Suwon City Art Museum’, ‘Suwon City Manseok Exhibition Hall (formerly Suwon Art Exhibition Hall)’ located in Manseok Park, ‘Suwon Children’s Art Experience Center (formerly Children’s Ecological Art Experience Center)’ in Pajang-dong, and ‘Suwon City Art Space Gwanggyo’. Based on this, the Suwon Museum of Art is developing into an art museum that cultivates citizens' emotions and represents the metropolitan area through diverse and high-quality exhibitions that take advantage of the characteristics of each museum, exhibitions that can be enjoyed and appreciated, and unique exhibitions based on the region. (Source: Suwon Museum of Art)

title: Suwon Olympic Park
description: Suwon Olympic Park is a park created in front of Suwon City Hall in 1987 to commemorate the hosting of the 88 Seoul Olympics. It is loved as a resting place for citizens as it has sports facilities such as a badminton court, foot volleyball court, tennis court, and basketball court, as well as a pavilion, a grass plaza, and a pine forest path. In the summer, a water park with water slides, showers, and changing rooms is open, making it great for use with children. Additionally, the dog shelter has separate areas for large dogs and small and medium-sized dogs, so dogs can run around safely.

title: Suwon Sports Complex
description: Suwon Sports Complex is a sports complex that opened in 1971. A variety of sports facilities, including the main stadium, baseball field, indoor gymnasium, and artificial turf field, are gathered in one place and are used as a venue for citizens' health promotion, sports activities, and local community exchange. The main stadium is the home stadium of K-League Suwon FC and is operated as a type 2 stadium certified by the Korea Association of Athletics Federations, and is open to the public for free on days when there are no games. Volleyball games are mainly held at Suwon Gymnasium, and you can enjoy daily sports such as badminton and table tennis at the National Sports Center.

title: Suwon Convention Center
description: Suwon Convention Center is a modern convention facility that opened in 2019 and is located within the MICE complex, providing convenient facilities for international conferences, exhibitions, and various business events. It is operated as a space where various MICE events such as international conferences, exhibitions, and forums are held, and efforts are also being made to create a green MICE environment for sustainable operation. Since it is adjacent to Gwanggyo Lake Park, it also serves as a comfortable resting place for citizens.

title: Suwon Tapdong Citizen’s Farm
description: Suwon Tapdong Citizen's Farm is a space where citizens can enjoy walking and relaxation by creating seasonal flower gardens in a large field. Every year, various themed flower fields such as cosmos and lotus are operated, and especially in the fall season, the dapsari and reeds are spectacular, attracting many visitors. The four areas of vegetable garden on one side are sold only to Suwon citizens. After receiving an application, only those who are finally selected through a lottery and training can use it, and it must be grown using ecological farming methods that do not use chemical fertilizers and pesticides.

title: Suwon Hwaseong Museum
description: Suwon Hwaseong Museum is a specialized museum that can comprehensively show the history and culture of Hwaseong, and provides effective and systematic guidance to visitors to Hwaseong, the cultural prosperity of the King Jeongjo era, and the excellence of Hwaseong. Suwon City established Suwon Hwaseong Museum, a UNESCO World Heritage site that is the pride of our nation's cultural heritage, and the Suwon Hwaseong Museum to publicize the excellence of our culture in the late Joseon Dynasty and to create a space where local culture and art can breathe. Hwaseong Fortress is considered a model of military architecture around the world in the 18th century and the flower of the castle culture of the Joseon Dynasty. It is not just a castle, but an entire city. The Hwaseong Museum displays various cultural events through models and relics, including the thoughts and spirit of King Jeongjo, who built Suwon New Town and built Hwaseong, as well as the people who participated in the construction of Hwaseong, Jang Yong-yeong, a soldier stationed in Hwaseong, and King Jeongjo's eight-day journey to Hwaseong.

title: Sujongsa Temple
description: Sujongsa Temple is a subsidiary temple of Bongseonsa Temple, located near the summit of Ungilsan Mountain in Songchon-ri, Joan-myeon, Namyangju. This temple was once praised by Seo Geo-jeong as having the best view among Eastern temples. It offers a view of Yangsu-ri, where the Bukhan River and Namhan River meet, and even the nearby mountains. It is said that Sujongsa Temple was first built during the Silla Dynasty, but the detailed history is unknown, and there is an anecdote related to King Sejo of the Joseon Dynasty. It is said that while King Sejo was spending a night in Yangsu-ri on his way to Gangwon-do for treatment of a chronic illness, he went to a place where he could hear the soft sound of a bell, and found that there were 18 statues of Arhats in the crypt, and water drops falling from a crevice in the rock made the sound of the bell. Accordingly, there is a legend that King Sejo built a temple to enshrine 18 Arhats and named it Sujongsa Temple. However, the remains of King Sejo's aunt, Princess Jeonggi, in the temple indicate that it was already a sizeable temple before that. Existing temples include Daeungbojeon, Eungjinjeon, Yaksajeon, Sansingak, Jonggak, Gyeonghakwon, and Yosa. Important cultural heritages include the relics in Sujongsa Temple and the Sujongsa Five-story Stone Pagoda, which are designated as treasures. Inside the temple, there is a 500-year-old ginkgo tree that is said to have been given by King Sejo. Although the scenery in all four seasons is beautiful, the scenery in the fall when the leaves change color is known to be especially spectacular. It takes about 15 minutes to walk 400m from the Sujongsa Temple parking lot to the temple.

title: Sutasa Temple
description: Gongjaksan Mountain is 887m above sea level, and when viewed from the top of the mountain, the entire Hongcheon-gun area can be seen at a glance. The mountain was named so because its shape resembles a peacock with its wings spread. Also, when viewed from Hongcheon-eup, it looks like a giant lying down toward the sky. The azaleas in the spring and the autumn leaves in the fall are very beautiful, and the strangely shaped cliffs, bonsai-shaped cypress colonies, and snow-covered winter mountains are also spectacular. Sutasa Valley, which stretches for about 12km from Sutasa Temple to Nocheon-ri, Dongmyeon, has wide rock formations and large ponds forming a mysterious scenery. On both sides of the valley, strangely shaped cliffs and dense forests protect it, so if you take a break here, you can often fall into a state of samadhi. In addition, Sutasa Temple, a thousand-year-old temple located at the end of Gongjaksan Mountain, one of Korea's 100 famous mountains, is the 33rd generation of Silla. It is said to have been founded by Master Wonhyo in the 7th year of King Seongdeok's reign (AD 708). It is the best ancient temple in the inland region of Yeongseo, preserving the hipped roof of Daejeokgwangjeon, bronze bell made in 1364, and three-story stone pagoda, and housing numerous cultural assets, including Wolinseokbo, Daejeokgwangjeon, temple bells, a posthumous Buddhist painting, and Hongwudangbudo.
priceDetail: Free

title: Suncheon Bay Wetland
description: Suncheon Bay is a bay located in the midwestern part of the southern coast of Korea, surrounded by Suncheon City, Goheung County, and Yeosu City in South Jeolla Province. The large bay surrounded by the long stretches of Goheung Peninsula and Yeosu Peninsula is sometimes called Suncheon Bay, and the northern sea-level bay surrounded by Inan-dong and Daedae-dong of Suncheon-si and Seonhak-ri and Sangnae-ri of Haeryong-myeon is also called Suncheon Bay. Even if we consider only the seawater area of ​​Suncheon Bay in the administrative district, it is a very large area of ​​over 75㎢. The total area of ​​the tidal flats exposed during low tide reaches 12㎢, and the total area of ​​the tidal flats is 22.6㎢. In addition, from the confluence of Dongcheon and Isacheon in Suncheon to the front of the tidal flat of Suncheon Bay, a huge reed colony with a total area of ​​5.4㎢ is spread out.

title: Starfield Goyang
description: Starfield Goyang is located at a gateway connecting Seoul and northwestern Gyeonggi Province. The beautiful natural environment of Bukhansan Mountain and traditional Korean architectural motifs, such as castles, towering gates, and watchtowers, were reinterpreted in a modern way and incorporated into architectural design. From trendy fashion and beauty specialty stores to reasonably priced warehouse hypermarkets and upgraded markets, you can enjoy a variety of shopping and leisure cultures comfortably and comfortably in one space. The whole family can make precious memories together, with an Aqua Field where you can enjoy hot spring water all year round, a cinema with the latest facilities, a complex play area for children, and various specialized service facilities. title: Starfield Suwon
description: Starfield Suwon, the fifth Starfield to open, is an 8-story complex shopping mall center consisting of a flagship store, the open cultural space Byulmadang Library, and about 80 various stores. Starfield Suwon is a place that many people visit because they can enjoy food, beverages, and cultural activities all in one place. Stores of various categories such as large supermarkets, restaurants and cafes, beauty, fashion clothing, and lifestyle are lined up. By introducing a complex space that combines carefully selected flagship stores and pop-up stores with entertainment, it provides an extraordinary experience of feeling the brand identity by directly seeing, hearing, and touching.

title: Starfield City Wirye
description: Starfield City Wirye is a new type of urban lifestyle mall where everything you need for life, including shopping, culture, and relaxation, can be found in one place. We propose happiness that can be enjoyed in everyday life through accessibility close to the city and comfortable space aesthetics on a human scale. From movie theaters, bookstores, trendy restaurants, E-Mart Traders, fashion, beauty, and lifestyle, it is a one-stop shopping paradise that satisfies both cost-effectiveness and convenience. At Starfield City, performances for children are held every week, and there is a pet park on the 10th floor rooftop garden where dogs can play without a leash. ※ Information on traveling with dogs - Only vaccinated pets (dogs, cats) are allowed on leashes or accompanied by cages - However, fierce dogs are not allowed (Tosa dog, American pit bull terrier, American Staffordshire terrier, Staffordshire bull terrier, Rottweiler, Dogs such as Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasilei, English Bull Terrier and their mixed breeds, and other dogs with a high risk of attacking and injuring people) - The leash is adjusted and fixed within 1.5m for safety - Entry standards vary by store.

title: Starfield Anseong
description: Starfield Anseong is a complex shopping theme park in the southern part of Gyeonggi Province that combines shopping, leisure, and entertainment. Equipped with Traders, Megabox, and Aquafield, you can enjoy shopping and leisure in one place, and with a family zone-centered structure, it is actively used by families. There are experiential spaces such as Byul Madang Kids and Pet Park, and the food zone featuring major restaurants across the country is also popular. From the 63m observatory, you can view the entire Anseong area, increasing the satisfaction of your visit.

title: Starfield Market Ilsan
description: Starfield Market Ilsan Branch is a shopping mall complex introduced by renewing the existing ‘The Town Mall’. Rest and cultural spaces such as the Book Ground and Kids Ground were expanded to enhance experience elements for family visitors. Traders and Electro Mart are located on the first basement level, and retail and F&B stores are located on the first and second ground floors. In addition, various brands such as Daiso, Olive Young, and Musinsa Standard are located here, making it ideal for enjoying shopping and leisure in one place.

title: Starfield City Bucheon
description: Starfield City Bucheon is a regional shopping complex that serves as a lifestyle-friendly shopping infrastructure necessary for daily life. A shopping environment where people stay is created by adding experiential content such as F&B, a book cafe-type space, and a kids zone to the sales-oriented structure. Convenience facilities such as a hospital, dental clinic, beauty salon, fitness club, daycare center, and playground are all located in one place, making it convenient to use. In addition, various pop-up stores are periodically operated to expand the range of experiences for visitors.

title: Story Miniature Museum
description: Story Miniature Museum is a museum located in Heyri Art Village, Paju City, and was established within Aji-dong Theme Park. Ajidong Theme Park is a company that develops customized content under the Korean theme park brand Ajidong and conducts business such as theme parks, characters, entertainment, trade, and venture business support and fostering. The Story Miniature Museum is comprised of artists from Heyri Village with a 20-year history and artists from Switzerland, Germany, Taiwan, France, and Korea who love art, giving messages of love and hope through music boxes, artists' dolls, fairy tale dioramas, and miniatures. The exhibition room is comprised of a music box zone that reminds us of the importance of human life and nature, a fairy tale zone that takes you to the world of the deepest, a Nutcracker zone that represents the dolls that come to mind in winter, a miniature village Dream Village zone, a ball-jointed doll zone with free joint movement, and a world doll zone that depicts traditional costumes of each country with Madame Alexander's dolls on a world map. It is enough space to create unforgettable memories with your children.

title: Spadium 24
description: Spadium 24, located in Dasan-dong, Namyangju-si, Gyeonggi-do, is a 24-hour jjimjil spa facility where you can enjoy not only a jjimjilbang but also cultural facilities. The sauna has a variety of facilities, including a book cafe, lounge, and active zone, so you can experience everything in one place. It is designed to provide a variety of ways to relax for those who want a quiet and comfortable vacation. It is a good place to visit if you want to escape from the daily life of the city and enjoy relaxation and healing in nature.

title: splice resom
description: Splace Resom is a complex relaxation space where you can enjoy a water park, spa, and resort all at once with Deoksan hot spring water with a gushing temperature of 49.6 degrees, with a long history of about 600 years. Hot spring water from the government-designated recreational hot spring is supplied to all 406 rooms as well as all water play facilities in the water park, including 15 outdoor baths, water slides, and bade pools, so you can enjoy hot spring water all year round at Splace. In particular, the hot spring water here contains a large amount of silica along with various minerals such as silicon, calcium, and magnesium, which are helpful for skin care, anti-aging, strengthening blood vessels, increasing immunity, and relieving arthritis pain. In addition, there are a variety of things to enjoy, including Lara Golf Club, My Little Place, and Mini Car Land. The resort rooms are composed of six types of rooms, allowing various customer groups such as friends, couples, and families to comfortably stay in a suitable space.
