title: Yeoju Yanghwanaru
description: Yanghwa Ferry is a ferry from the Joseon Dynasty that connects Yanghwa-dong, Naeyang-ri, Neungseo-myeon, Yeoju-si, and Chohyeon-ri, Daesin-myeon. There are well-established bike paths and walking paths along the riverside, making it a great place to walk while looking at the beautiful view of the Namhan River. Yanghwa, meaning willow flower, was given the name because there were many pussy willows along the riverside. It was also called Naeyang Naru after the local name of Naeyang-ri, which owned a ferry. Yeoju, located along the Namhan River, has long been a key point for water transportation between Hanyang and the central inland areas of Gangwon-do and Chungcheong-do, with about 12 ferry ports, enabling active exchange of goods and people. In the past, the Namhan River was crowded with boats such as rafts used by sailors who made rafts in Yeongwol and Jeongseon in Gangwon-do and went to Seoul, transfer boats and sailboats that carried salt and exchanged it for beans or tobacco, and Hwangpo sailboats, which were passenger ships that transported people. In particular, Yanghwanaru was used as a major route to the cattle market in Icheon's Goksujang. From nearby parts of Neungseo-myeon and Heungcheon-myeon in Yeoju, Baeksa-myeon and Bubal-eup in Icheon-si, cattle were mainly loaded onto ferry boats at Yanghwa Ferry and traveled to and from the grain harvesting area, but now it is difficult to find traces. Course 6 of Yeoju Yeogang-gil, a river-themed trail in Yeoju, includes Yanghwanaru. It is not easy to find the ferry port as there are no traces left. However, since Yanghwa Ferry is included in the Yeoganggil course and a stamp has been installed nearby, it is recommended to follow the GPS guidance using the Yeoganggil application. If you follow the bike path along the river, you will see two monuments on the side of the road and a marker that says Yanghwa Ferry. There are no convenient facilities such as parking or restrooms, and since it is entirely a rice field, access directly from the village road to the riverside is limited.

title: Yeoju Cultural Center
description: It is a local culture and arts promotion organization located in Yeoheung-ro, Yeoju-si, Gyeonggi-do. It is a non-profit culture and arts organization. Yeoju Cultural Center is a place to inherit and develop Yeoju's local cultural history and local culture. It discovers and preserves local historical materials and carries out local cultural events, cultural education activities, and projects to revitalize lifestyle culture and arts. Yeoju Cultural Center, established and opened in 1970 under the Local Cultural Center Promotion Act, moved to its current location in 2012. The cultural center is equipped with facilities such as local exhibition halls, classrooms, conference rooms, data rooms, and theaters, and operates educational projects such as youth cultural schools and liberal arts classes, and holds festivals and various commemorative events. In addition, it was established to improve the quality of cultural life of local residents, disseminate high-quality culture and arts, and contribute to the development of local culture through the development of local culture, research, surveys, holding local cultural events, and active domestic and international exchanges. It takes about 9 minutes by car from Yeoju Station on the Gyeonggang Line. It is adjacent to Silleuksa Temple, and nearby are King Sejong's Yeongneung Royal Tomb, King Hyojong's Yeongneung Royal Tomb, Yeoju Premium Outlet, Pasaseong Fortress, Mok-a Museum, Yeoju Insect Museum, and Hwangpo Sailboat.

title: Yeoju Museum
description: Yeoju Museum, which opened in 1997 as the ‘Yeoju County Local History Museum’, researches, collects, exhibits, and educates Yeoju’s history and folk materials, discovers new academic materials, and plays a role in establishing Yeoju’s identity. 2016년 7월 14일 새롭게 개관한 여마관(신관)의 건립으로 각지에 흩어졌던 여주지역 발굴출토 국가귀속유물을 한자리에 모았다. The Yeoju Museum’s ‘Hwangma Hall’ includes a special exhibition room, Ryu Ju-hyeon’s literature exhibition room, the Namhan River Chief Exhibition Room, and the Joseon Royal Tomb Room, and the new building, ‘Yeoju Museum’, has a Yeoju History Room, a cafeteria, a research room, and a classroom. It has established itself as a space for various cultural experiences encompassing Yeoju's past and present, including holding special exhibitions every year, operating traditional culture education, and operating a museum university. It is also striving to excavate, preserve, and pass down Yeoju's cultural assets through academic research and excavations.

title: reverse icicle
description: When you cross the small bridge across Chatancheon Stream ahead of the border sign announcing National Highway 3, Cheorwon-gun, on the border of Yeoncheon-gun and Cheorwon-gun, Gangwon-do, a sign informing you of station icicles appears. Station Icicle, which is the end of Course 12 of Pyeonghwa Nuri-gil and is also connected to Course 7 of Pyeonghwa Nuri-gil Bicycle Road, is located in the 28.2km section from Gunnam Flood Control Area to Yeokicicle. Reverse icicles (sung ice) open in abandoned tunnels at the foot of Godae Mountain, and are formed when falling water falls on ice on the ground and grows, or when groundwater rises due to thermal molecular pressure and grows into the ice on the ground. It grows from mid-December and can only be seen until March. Due to safety concerns, it is best to visit outside.

title: Yonkang Gallery
description: Just thinking about Yeoncheon, the northernmost area facing the DMZ, makes you feel tense, but when you actually face it, you melt into the peaceful and natural scenery. Yeongang Gallery is a place where you can enjoy the quiet rural scenery and the beautiful scenery of the Imjin River and Hantangang River and sublimate them into art. The former Security Exhibition Hall, located inside the Civilian Control Line in Jung-myeon, Yeoncheon-gun, has been reborn as <Yonkang Gallery>, a culture and art exhibition space. <Yonkang Gallery> is the first art space built within the Civilian Control Line after the armistice, and is a meeting place between the ecology of Yeoncheon, which has been fully preserved under the geopolitical conditions of a border area, and contemporary culture and art. It is a complex space. This gallery made a new architectural attempt with a large façade work containing the scenery of Yeoncheon and the “Gate of Peace” containing messages of peace sent from all over the world.

title: Yeonboram Ranch
description: In Seoam-ri, Gimpo-si, there is a ranch where you can experience Nakdong, which operates on a reservation basis. If you follow the country road overlooking the rice fields, you will first see the play zone. If you park here and go further in, you will see Yeonboram Ranch. Yeonboram Ranch, which believes in happy cows and healthy milk, is popular with families for its cleanly maintained ranch and various entertainment activities. Although it is not a large ranch, it has a well-maintained experience center, cafe, and play facilities, so children will never be bored. The experiential class, which is held twice a day, consists of giving milk directly to a young calf, feeding the animals in the ranch, and making cheese and pizza with parents. While the pizza is baking, you can go outside and ride a tractor or even experience milking a cow yourself. It is truly packed with a tasting of homemade pizza at the end, providing satisfaction to both children and parents. The play zone is a play area for young visitors and can be used for free without time restrictions. Yeonboram Ranch is a space that presents precious memories to growing children through the experience of directly touching and feeding animals with pure eyes.

title: Yeoncheon Horogoru
description: Horogoru is located on an important road connecting Kaesong and Seoul, and was built on a basalt cliff formed by a tributary flowing from Wondang-ri into the Imjin River. Regarding the etymology of Horogoru, “The terrain around here looks like a gourd or gourd.” There is a theory that it was called Horogoru, and another theory is that ‘Hol’, meaning town, and ‘Guru’, meaning castle, were combined to become ‘Horogoru’. Among the Goguryeo government ruins investigated in the Gyeonggi-do region, it is one of the three major flat fortresses along with Dangpo Fortress and Eundaeri Fortress. The eastern wall of Horogoru was built by blocking the eastern part of the basalt plateau, and the highest part is 10 meters, and from the top of the wall, you can see a spectacular view of the surrounding area as well as the Imjin River. The first excavation of Horogoru was conducted from November 2000 to May 2002 to confirm the construction method and structure of the wall. The entire perimeter of the Horogoru Castle Wall is 401m, with the south wall being 161.9m, the north wall being 146m, and the east wall being 93.1m. The interior area is 606m2 and is located on a basalt cliff about 28m high. The eastern wall shows a fortress construction technique that appropriately combines the advantages of stone and earth by building the wall high with stones on top of several layers of compacted earth.
priceDetail: Free

title: Yeoncheon Cultural Center
description: Yeoncheon Cultural Center is a place to inherit and develop Yeoncheon's local cultural history and local culture. It is a space where local cultural festivals, cultural education, and life culture and arts revitalization projects are carried out while discovering and preserving local historical materials. Yeoncheon Cultural Center, established and opened in 1987 in accordance with the Local Cultural Center Promotion Act, was rebuilt and moved to its current location in 1999. The Cultural Center is equipped with facilities such as a local exhibition hall, classrooms, conference rooms, a library/data room, an auditorium/theater, and an exhibition room, and operates a variety of cultural events and educational programs. It takes about 3 minutes by car from Yeoncheon Station on Line 1, about 1 minute from Yeoncheon Public Terminal, and 9 minutes on foot (595m). Nearby are Godae Mountain Natural Recreation Forest, Hantangang River Recreation Area, Hantangang River Tourist Site Auto Camping Site, Yeoncheon Jeongok-ri Ruins, Jeongok Prehistory Museum, Jaein Falls, Pocheon Shinbuk Resort Springfall Hot Springs, and Pocheon Herb Island.

title: Yeoncheon Surewul Art Hall
description: Yeoncheon Sureul Art Hall, located within Yeoncheon Public Stadium, was opened to promote the leisure and cultural life of Yeoncheon citizens. Surewul is a pure Korean word for Chatan [車灘], and it was named Surewul because King Taejong's family fell while crossing the rapids on his way to Yeoncheon to meet Lee Yang-so, a Goryeo Jinsa who was living in seclusion in Dodanggol. Yeoncheon Surewul Art Hall uses the old place name to reflect its historical origin and meaning. Yeoncheon Sureul Art Hall is equipped with a large performance hall that can accommodate 550 people (including 5 wheelchair seats) and a small performance hall that can accommodate 166 people (including 3 wheelchair seats). Yeoncheon Surewul Art Hall is a three-story building, with convenience facilities and auxiliary facilities such as an information desk, office, continuing education room, workshop room, customer service room, nursing room, dressing room, and large practice room on the first floor. It is equipped with performance facilities such as a ticket office and sound control room on the second floor, first-floor auditorium for large performances, small performance hall, and performance facilities such as second-floor large performance auditorium, dressing room, and stage machine room on the third floor. There is. Various cultural events, movie screenings, performances, and concerts are held frequently in the large and small performance halls. Even if there are no performances, an art exhibition is held in the lobby on the first floor. Outdoors, there is a sculpture park with works that were exhibited in the 2013 Hantangang Contemporary Outdoor Sculpture Exhibition and a fountain with a map of Korea embossed on it, making it worth a stroll. It takes about 17 minutes by car from Eunhyeon IC and about 3 minutes from Yeoncheon Station on the Gyeongwon Line, and there are buses that go from the station to nearby locations. Nearby are Godaesan Natural Recreation Forest, Baekmagoji, Yeoncheon Station Icicle, Labor Party Headquarters, Key Observatory, Dongmakgol Recreation Area, Crane Theme Park, Jaein Falls (Hantangang National Geopark), Hantangang and Imjin River columnar joints, Yeoncheon Jeongok-ri ruins, Yeoncheon Horogoru, and Yeoncheon Gorangpo Historical Park.

title: twelve streams
description: Twelve Streams is a valley in Yeoncheon that boasts picturesque scenery. The water is clear and clean, and there is a shallow stream, so it is crowded with vacationers in the summer. Twelve Streams is Sudongcheon Stream, a local second-class river, and refers to twelve streams that run from Choseong-ri, Cheongsan-myeon, Yeoncheon-gun to Deokdun-ri, Sikbuk-myeon, Pocheon-gun. It originated from the fact that there were twelve Silgaecheon Streams that had to be crossed in the old days when there were no bridges. A landscape created by rocks such as Seonnyeobawi Rock, Manjangbawi Rock, Pyeonbawi Rock, and Bongbawi Rock, and cows of Mujangso, Boanso, Doraso, Dolmukso, Ssangmuso, and Yongsugolso unfolds along the road of about 10 miles. Twelve stream amusement parks are formed around a small bridge called Beopsu Bridge. The amusement park is home to Twelve Stream Mushroom Village, Rural Experience Village, large restaurants and cafes, and eateries, and you can find a suitable spot to soak your feet. As it is a local stream, there is no separate public parking lot or restroom, so you must use facilities such as nearby restaurants and cafes. It takes about 11 minutes by car from Eunhyeon IC. Nearby are Soyosan Mountain, Hantangang Resort, Hantangang Tourist Site Auto Camping Site, Yeoncheon Jeongok-ri Ruins, Jeongok Prehistory Museum, Jaein Falls, Pocheon Shinbuk Resort Springfall Hot Springs, and Pocheon Herb Island.

title: Yeolhwadang Book Museum
description: In the new headquarters of Yeolhwadang in Paju Book City, a book museum has been created with over 40,000 old books that were created in the past and nourished the souls of many people, as well as contemporary good books from around the world that are beautifully made and shine in our times. ‘Gallery Lotus’ opened in 2004 at the same time as Yeolhwadang opened its headquarters in Paju Book City. A total of 14 exhibitions were held until June 2008, focusing on art collections and photo collections published by Yeolhwadang. Afterwards, in 2009, a new building was expanded and ‘Library + Bookstore’, which combines the characteristics of a library and a bookstore, was opened, and five exhibitions were held here. ‘Library + Bookstore’, the predecessor of Yeolhwadang Book Museum, is a collection of old books from the East and the West, including Chinese classics collected by Yeolhwadang’s publisher for over 40 years, art books that Yeolhwadang’s editorial department has kept for a long time, and beautiful books from around the world hand-selected by the editor. Taking advantage of the characteristics of an art publishing company, it has relatively organized books on culture and arts, including art, photography, design, architecture, and traditional culture, as well as other humanities books. In addition, with the steady influx of donated books, it has acquired the appearance of a book museum. Newly opened as the ‘Yeolhwadang Book Museum’ in July 2012, it is a place where you can not only gain knowledge and information, feel the beauty of the book itself, but also retrace the steps of our publishing industry and feel the true book culture through various books from around the world through excellent books that have become history in themselves in this era when the crisis of paper books is being talked about, and various unique books made at the same time.
price: Individuals 10,000 won Elementary, middle and high school students 7,000 won Groups (10 or more people) 7,000 won

title: Yeonggeumjeong
description: Yeonggeumjeong is a place with large and wide rocks on the beach below Sokcho Lighthouse in Dongmyeong-dong, Sokcho-si. The origin of the place name is that when waves hit the rocks, a mysterious Yulgok is heard, and this sound is similar to the sound of a spiritual ‘geomungo’, so it is called Yeonggeumjeong. It is located a short distance from the city, and the scenery is beautiful, so it is a place where Sokcho citizens enjoy summer vacation and fishing all year round. Currently, Sokcho City has developed the Yeonggeumjeong area as a tourist destination and has built an actual pavilion near the southern breakwater. This pavilion is a maritime pavilion built on the rock of Yeonggeumjeong and can be entered by crossing a 50m bridge. The feeling of looking at the sea from the sea pavilion gives a different and refreshing feeling from the breakwater, but the pavilion itself is a concrete pavilion, so it is disappointing. It is usually called Sunrise Pavilion, and the words Yeonggeumjeong (靈琴亭) are written on the pavilion plaque.
priceDetail: Free

title: Yeongnam Alps Ice Valley Cable Car
venue: Yeongnam Alps Ice Valley Cable Car
description: It is a cable car that allows you to tour the mountainous area called the Yeongnam Alps. You can ride a large 50-seat cable car from the lower platform to the upper platform at 1,020m above sea level, and climb about 1.8km in about 10 minutes. The cable car runs every 20 minutes. When you get off at the upper platform, walk up the 250m gentle deck road called Sky Love Road for about 10 minutes and you will reach an observatory called Noksandae. From here, you can view the Yeongnam Alps' Gajisan Mountain, Baekunsan Mountain, and Eoreumgol Valley toward downtown Miryang. It takes 1 hour one way from the upper platform to Sajabong Peak of Jaeyaksan Mountain, 1 hour 40 minutes one way to Sumibong Peak of Jaeyaksan Mountain, 1 hour one way to Mt. Neungdong, and 2 hours one way to Sajapyeong Silver Grass, so many people who like trekking use it, and there are also hikers who use the Fern Bungyo-Pyochungsa course through Sajapyeong Silver Grass Field.

title: Yeongwol Jangneung (Done) [UNESCO World Heritage]
description: Jangneung is the tomb of Danjong, the 6th king of the Joseon Dynasty (reigned 1452-1455). When Danjong passed away in 1457 (the 3rd year of King Sejo's reign) as Prince Nosan, Yeongwolho Commander Eom Heung-do secretly took Danjong's body and temporarily buried it in the current location. Afterwards, in 1516 (the 11th year of King Jungjong's reign), the tomb was located and a burial mound was built, and in 1580 (the 13th year of King Seonjo's reign), a stone monument was erected and ancestral rites were held. In 1698 (the 24th year of King Sukjong's reign), the king's status was restored and the tomb was renamed Jangneung, and it was rebuilt in its current form. Unlike other royal tombs of the Joseon Dynasty, Jangneung contains buildings for King Danjong's loyal subjects. At the entrance to Jangneung, there is the Nakchon Monument, which commemorates the wishes of Yeongwol-gun Governor Park Chung-won, who visited the tomb of Nosangun and held a ancestral rite. Next to the burial chamber, the Jeongryeo-gak of Eomheungdo, who built a tomb for King Danjong's body, is a memorial to the relatives, loyalists, eunuchs, court ladies, and slaves who sacrificed their lives for King Danjong. There is a jangpanok (藏版屋) that holds the memorial tablets of 268 people and a food altar (配食壇) where ancestral rites are held for them.

title: Yeongwol Cheongnyeongpo
description: Cheongnyeongpo is located in the upper reaches of the Namhan River in Gwangcheon-ri, Nam-myeon, Yeongwol-gun. This is where King Danjong, who was dethroned and exiled to Yeongwol, stayed. Danjong, the 6th king of the Joseon Dynasty, ascended the throne to his uncle, Grand Prince Suyang, and served as King Sang. The following year, in 1456, King Sang was dethroned to Prince Nosan due to the movement of the six ministers, including Seong Sam-mun, to restore King Sang. Afterwards, he was exiled to Cheongnyeongpo after passing through Wonju and Jucheon, escorted by 50 soldiers led by Cheomji Jungbuwonsa Eodeukhae. Cheongnyeongpo is surrounded by water on three sides: east, south, and north, and to the west is a rugged rock wall called Yukyukbong, making it impossible to enter or leave without using a ferry. King Danjong lived in exile in this quiet place, cut off from the outside world. At the time, there was a house where he could live, so it is said that the commander, Eom Heung-do, secretly came here at night to pay his respects. (Source: Yeongwol-gun Culture and Tourism website)

title: Youngeun Museum of Art
description: Youngeun Museum of Art, located in a natural forest in Gwangju-si, Gyeonggi-do, opened in November 2000 and is a complex cultural facility that combines the Museum of Contemporary Art, which researches, possesses, and exhibits contemporary contemporary art works, and a creative studio. The spacious site houses an art gallery building, studios for artists in residence, and a research building. The residency program, which started in 2000, is a creative support project hosted by the Youngeun Museum of Art and supports the creative activities of domestic and foreign artists. The art museum building, which has one floor underground and three floors above ground, is equipped with three exhibition halls, a seminar room, a data room, a lecture room, and a flat studio. The Youngeun Museum of Art introduces the works of major domestic and international contemporary artists through special exhibitions and individual exhibitions, and provides opportunities for a more familiar and close encounter with contemporary art through exhibition planning that not only art professionals but also the general public can sympathize with and understand. In addition, experience programs such as the Youngeun Creative Studio tour program and art museum picnic are prepared for various age groups, from teenagers to adults.
price: [Museum exhibition admission fee] General 10,000 won / Students (elementary, middle, and high school) 7,000 won / Children 5,000 won

title: Yeongildae Beach
description: Yeongildae Beach is the largest beach on the east coast, located in Buk-gu, Pohang-si, Gyeongsangbuk-do. It is widely known as Pohang's representative beach along with nearby Songdo Beach. From here, you can see the POSCO steel mill and an open view of Yeongil Bay, and the fine white sand beach is suitable as a summer resort for families. The depth of the water is gentle and the waves are calm, creating an environment where children can safely enjoy water play. The beach is equipped with a variety of convenient facilities, including showers, changing rooms, restrooms, and parking lots. Another major advantage is that it is located in the city center and is easily accessible by public transportation or car. During the summer, various marine leisure activities and cultural events are held, creating a lively atmosphere. Nearby, there are abundant tourist resources such as Yeongildae Marine Cable Car, Pohang Canal, and POSCO History Museum, making it a suitable tourist destination. Yeongildae Beach is the best resort where you can feel the relaxation of the sea in the middle of the city.
priceDetail: Free

title: Yeongjip Palace Museum
description: Yeongjip Archery Museum is Korea's first museum specializing in bows and arrows, established on December 30, 2000. The name of the museum is a combination of the pen name Yeongjip (楹集) of Yoo Yeong-gi, a national intangible cultural heritage holder, and Gungsi (弓矢), meaning bow and arrow. The position of director is taken over by Yoo Se-hyeon, the son of Yoo Young-gi, who holds the National Intangible Heritage Archery Market. The museum is located in Paju, Gyeonggi-do. Inside the exhibition room, restored and collected bows and arrows are displayed by type, and it is a space where various types of bows and arrows from home and abroad are constantly on display. It is also a place where visitors can experience traditional archery through a simple archery range. It is a place where you can have a variety of experiences with bows and arrows, as a crafting experience using the principles of the Bangtaegi bow and crossbow is also provided.

title: Yeongheung-myeon Energy Park
description: Yeongheung Energy Park is a field trip where you can gain a proper understanding of electricity and energy and directly experience information about the domestic power industry. It is a power promotion center that introduces the importance of energy and nature and the advanced system of a cutting-edge eco-friendly thermal power plant through various contents. In addition, it is equipped with a 300-seat Harmony Hall, a cultural classroom, a gallery, and an outdoor performance hall that hosts various cultural and artistic performances and local events in order to strengthen solidarity with the local community and revitalize local cultural benefits. It is attracting attention as a cultural relaxation space not only for local residents but also for students from the metropolitan area and many visitors.

title: Yeongheung Arboretum
description: Yeongheung Arboretum is a botanical garden created to take advantage of the mountainous terrain surrounding Yeongheung Forest Park. When you enter the arboretum, you can see green lawns, forests and parks with various themes, and in the landmark greenhouse, you can see unique plants that give an exotic feel. Additionally, at the visitor center where citizens can take a rest, they can view the arboretum, use the cafe, or see various exhibitions and educational programs. In addition, it is open at night for a certain period of time, so you can feel another charm of the arboretum combined with lighting at sunset.

title: Yeongheung Forest Park
description: Yeongheung Forest Park is an urban neighborhood park created by taking advantage of the topography of the hill. There is a youth experience forest where you can walk slowly along a dense forest path, and a forest playground where children can run around and play in the dirt and trees. In addition, facilities with various functions, such as a citizen participation center, a walking trail, an in-line skating rink, a floor fountain, and a foot volleyball court, are located throughout the park and are suitable for anyone to use. Yeongheung Arboretum is located near the park, making it a great place to take a walk or relax by linking the two spaces.

title: Yedangho Monorail
description: The Yedangho Monorail is a tourist monorail located within the Yedang Tourist Site in Husari, Eungbong-myeon, Yesan-gun. It is a mountain train-type monorail that allows you to safely view the Yedangho Suspension Bridge, Sculpture Park, and the scenery of Yedangho Lake. The rider capacity is 24 people, and it runs along the 1,320m waterfront of Yedangho Lake for about 22 minutes. In particular, as Korea's first themed night landscape lighting monorail, it expresses the four seasons of Yedang Lake and media art such as moon sculptures, sculpture park lighting, media facades, and holograms, providing viewing content to monorail passengers not only during the day but also at night. Nearby tourist attractions include Yedang Lake Central Ecological Park, Good Brothers Park, Bongsusan Natural Recreation Forest, and Yesan Permanent Market in addition to Yedang Tourist Site.

title: Yeari Museum
description: Yeari Museum consists of a world culture hall, a Korean culture hall, a cultural product hall, a special exhibition hall, and an outdoor exhibition hall, and displays about 300 artifacts related to funeral rites from the East and the West. Exhibits are replaced periodically to ensure the preservation of artifacts. The World Cultural Center realistically reproduces the funeral culture of Asia and Europe, such as the funeral rites and catacombs, and the Korean Cultural Center realistically reproduces in miniature the state funeral of King Jeongdo the Great, the 22nd king of the Joseon Dynasty, recreated through thorough historical research, allowing visitors to enjoy the majestic state funeral procession of the king during the Joseon Dynasty. The special exhibition hall displays artifacts related to rituals of each tribe, including various shapes from Ghana, Africa.

title: Odusan Unification Observatory
description: Odusan Unification Observatory opened on September 8, 1992 to soothe the sorrow of separated families over their lost homes and to use it as an experiential center for unification education. Odusan Mountain, where Goguryeo and Baekje fought, climb to the observatory at the top, and you can see the spectacular view of the Han River from the south and the Imjingang River from the north joining and flowing into the West Sea, as well as the mountains and streams of Hwanghae-do, North Korea, which are visible right in front of you but cannot be accessed at will, and the appearance of North Korean residents at a glance. Inside the observatory, various exhibition halls are operated using various techniques to easily learn about the government's unification policy, the footsteps of past governments' unification efforts, and the reality of North Korea. Since its opening, Odusan Unification Observatory has received more than 20 million visitors, and has now become an international unification education center frequented by Koreans as well as foreigners.

title: Ordinary Dogs
description: Ordinary Dogs is a pet photography studio run by a photographer with many years of experience. We carry out various concept photography, including ‘puppy photo’ that clearly captures the dog’s face. Works that utilize ideas such as an LP design frame, ‘Music Dog’, which includes a theme song for dogs, and a ‘Plastic Model’ concept created by combining dogs’ favorite items, stand out. The photographer, who personally raises a dog, carefully adjusts the filming environment to ensure that the animal is not stressed.

title: Oryukdo Skywalk
description: The old name for Oryukdo Skywalk was ‘Seungdumal’. The Seungdu horse was called ‘Seungduma’ because it looked like a horse saddle, and the female divers and local residents called it ‘Jalroggae.’ It is said that after the sea-loving Seungdumal sailed safely across the six islands of Oryukdo Island one after another, the bulging part of the Seungdumal was narrowed down to create a wharf and a hill at the estuary. Construction began on September 12, 2012, and opened on October 18, 2013 in Seungdumal, which is also the border point between the East Sea and the South Sea, and was named Oryukdo Skywalk, meaning walking on the sky. The Skywalk is a 15m glass bridge with a steel beam installed on a 35m coastal cliff and 24 glass panels connected in a horseshoe shape on top. The floor glass is safely designed with high load bulletproof glass with a thickness of 55.49mm, specially manufactured by attaching bulletproof film to four 12mm glass plates. The sight of waves hitting the cliff through the transparent glass beneath your feet is dizzying enough to make you feel dizzy. The sea that spreads out in front of the skywalk is beautiful and colorful at any time, making it a famous place for photography, and on days when the weather is nice, it is the closest place to see Tsushima Island.

title: Osan Bird Park
description: Osan Bird Park, a four-season ecological experience learning center where you can see, touch and feel birds and trees, opened in May 21 and is a space that makes citizens happier as a four-season ecological experience learning center where you can see, touch and feel birds and trees. By further developing the know-how accumulated in the operation of Gyeongju Bird Park, we are creating a healing space that children and families, citizens and tourists, and all animals and plants can enjoy in their daily lives. Osan Bird Park is a space where citizens can enjoy. We want to provide a happier space, so it is a good idea to plan your movement as it is a large space on the 1st to 4th floors that children, families, citizens, and tourists can all find and enjoy in their daily lives.”

title: Osan Culture and Arts Center
description: The Osan Culture and Arts Center opened in April 2004 to promote the leisure and cultural life of Osan citizens. It is operated by the Osan Cultural Foundation, which was launched in 2012. Osan Culture and Arts Center consists of a large performance hall and a small performance hall. In particular, the main performance hall has a total of 3 floors, 1 underground floor and 2 above ground floors, and is equipped with a three-dimensional stage such as the main stage (sunken stage) and side stage (elevated stage), as well as cutting-edge lighting and sound facilities, allowing you to vividly feel the performance. Various cultural events, movie screenings, performances, concerts, etc. are held frequently in the large and small performance halls.

title: Osan Museum of Art
description: The Osan Museum of Art opened in 2012, and at the time of its opening, it was a cultural exhibition space under the name ‘Culture Factory Osan.’ After receiving official approval from Gyeonggi Province in 2017, it was changed to ‘Osan Museum of Art’. The building consists of four floors above ground and one underground, and since being registered as an official art museum, it has been performing various roles as a public art museum as well as high-quality exhibitions. We operate a children's experience program.

title: oasis
description: Oasis is a cultural complex created by remodeling the retired patrol ship ‘Haeuri 12’. It began operating as the ‘Hamsang Observatory’ in 2012, and was completely reorganized in 2022 before opening in its current form. The sealed substructure of the existing warship was removed and replaced with an open deck, increasing the sense of openness, and the West Sea scenery can be enjoyed from various angles from various places. Another feature is that a completely different seascape unfolds depending on the tide. Exhibitions, cultural programs, and small-scale performances are held here and there from time to time, making it a complex cultural space for the region.

title: Ojeong Art Hall
description: Ojeong Art Hall, operated by the Bucheon Cultural Foundation, opened in 2003 and is a valuable cultural space in Bucheon City. Ojeong Art Hall has 404 seats and a stage area of ​​226 square meters. It is a cultural space for Ojeong-gu and Bucheon citizens and is operated as a multi-purpose performance hall that satisfies local residents' desire to enjoy culture and provides various cultural events. Free movie screenings, musical performances, music concerts, and art exhibitions for children are always held in the art hall. It is a 20-minute walk from Exit 5 of Sports Complex Station on Line 7 of the metropolitan subway station and the northern exit of Sosa Station or Yeokgok Station on Line 1, and close to Bucheon IC.

title: Okyeonji Songhae Park
description: Okyeonji Songhae Park is a representative tourist attraction in Dalseong-gun and is named after broadcaster Song Hae, an honorary resident of Dalseong-gun. This place, where you can see a variety of flowers every season, is made up of various attractions such as a trail deck, a 100-year underwater bridge, a pinwheel rest area, an observatory, a gold cave, and an ice wall, as well as a variety of flowers and plants. Especially if you visit in spring, it is famous for its cherry blossom trees in full bloom and you can enjoy the unique scenery of lakes, windmills, and tulips. The Songhae Memorial Hall is located nearby, making it a good place to tour.
priceDetail: Free

title: Onyang Hot Springs Land
description: Onyang Hot Springs Land is a comprehensive hot spring water park located in downtown Asan (Onyang). Onyang Hot Springs is the oldest hot spring in Korea and has a history of approximately 1,300 years, dating back to the Baekje and Unified Silla periods. During the Joseon Dynasty, it was a place where not only King Sejong the Great but also other kings such as Sejo, Sukjong, Yeongjo, and Jeongjo stayed for rest or treatment of illness. Onyang Hot Springs Land is equipped with a hot spring bath (sauna), a jjimjilbang, a children's hot spring (kids water park), and a gym, so anyone of any age can enjoy Onyang hot spring water. Here, natural alkaline hot spring water (PH 8.42) is supplied to all businesses within the facility without any processing. Onyang Hot Springs is a traditional hot springs spot that boasts the best water quality in the country. It is also a great place for relaxation and healing as it has various auxiliary facilities. Onyang Hot Springs Land can be visited via Oncheon-daero, Chungmuro, and Munhwa-ro on National Routes 21 and 45, and the Asan Hyeonchungsa IC on the Asan-Cheonan Expressway is close to the highway. For public transportation, you can use the Janghang Line and Onyang Oncheon Station on Metropolitan Subway Line 1.
operatingHours: [Monday] - Hot spring bath 00:00~23:00 - Jjimjilbang 00:00~22:00 [Tuesday] - Hot spring bath 05:00~24:00 - Jjimjilbang 10:00~24:00 [Wednesday~Sunday] - Always open

title: Wadong Sports Park
description: Wadong Sports Park, located in Danwon-gu, Ansan-si, Gyeonggi-do, is a good resting place for Ansan citizens and industrial complex workers around the park. Many flower trees are planted, so the scenery in spring is especially beautiful. The 56,895.9㎡ site has a plaza, multi-purpose playground, children's playground, basketball court, and walking trails, and you can enjoy roller skating and inline skating. On one side of the park, there is a public monument to Hong Sun-chil, a March 1 independence activist. There is a Wadong Insect Experience Center in the park where children can experience insects, and there is a Wadong Gymnasium nearby.

title: Waon Beach
description: Waon Beach is a beach located in Waon Village, Sangnae-ri, Haeryong-myeon, Suncheon-si, Jeollanam-do. A monk saw a rock at the nearby Sangbong Uri and said that it had the shape of a cow lying down and that warm water flowed down the mountain. From then on, it was called Waon. It is a quiet beach adjacent to Goheung Peninsula and Suncheon Bay to the southwest and Gajeong-ri, Yulchon-myeon, Yeosu-si, Jeollanam-do to the east. It is about 3km long. It is a place with beautiful sunset views, and the sight of the sun setting over Sol Island in front of Waon Beach creates a spectacular sight. Due to low tide, a wide mud flat is revealed, and a narrow and winding waterway is created in an S-shaped line. You can also see winter migratory birds, including black cranes.

title: Wawoojeongsa Temple (Yongin)
description: Wawoojeongsa (臥牛精舍) is a temple located in a place where the 48 peaks of Yeonhwasan Mountain in Haegok-dong, Yongin-si, Gyeonggi-do are surrounded like a folding screen. It is a patriotic temple built in 1970 by Buddhist monk Haewolsamjang (genus name: Kim Hae-geun), a displaced citizen, to achieve national harmony by invoking the merits of Buddha. It is the head temple of the Nirvana sect of Korean Buddhism and has over 3,000 Buddhist statues enshrined there. There is. Among the many Buddhist statues, the Buddhist head erected at the entrance of the temple and the reclining Buddha on the mountainside are famous. The 8m high Buddha head is very large, and the Reclining Buddha is 3m high and 12m long and is carved from juniper wood imported from Indonesia. There is a huge Buddhist head within the precincts, the Jangyuk Ozon Buddha, which was made with 100,000 pounds of brass over 10 years, the Bell of Unification weighing 12 tons (the bell was rung during the 1988 Seoul Olympics), the largest bronze Maitreya Buddha statue in Korea, and the stone Yaksha Tathagata Buddha. The world's largest and only Buddha statue of Buddha is also a point of pride at Waujeongsa Temple. The main body of this Buddha statue is made of white jade, and the pedestal is made of sapphire. The Stone Pagoda of Unification next to the stairs leading to Nirvana is built by gathering stones from sacred sites around the world. At Waujeongsa Temple, about 3,000 Buddhist statues from India, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, China, Thailand, etc. are on display, allowing you to see Buddhist culture from around the world at a glance. This World Ten Thousand Buddha Hall contains prayers for world peace. Waujeongsa Temple enshrines all the Three Jewels. The Buddha's True Body Relics, the Pari Tripitaka Koreana, and the Sanskrit Tripitaka Koreana, imported from India, Sri Lanka, and Myanmar, are enshrined here.
priceDetail: Free

title: Wangbang Valley
description: It refers to the valley around Wangbang Village, located 8km east of downtown Dongducheon, and is famous as a clean valley with clear water flowing from Wangbang Waterfall on Mt. Wangbangsan Mountain. It's quiet because there aren't many people, and the water is clean. Cooking is not possible, but you can eat the food you prepared, and there are parking lots and portable restrooms along the way, so you can use them. The water level is appropriate and the stones on the bottom are not sharp, so you can enjoy family water play with your children. Nearby are Nangbawi Rock, Sonbawi Rock, Cheungdae Rock, Julbawi Rock, and Wangbang Waterfall, and the natural appearance without any commercial features such as flat rental adds to the sense of friendliness.

title: Wangbangsan Mountain
description: Wangbangsan Mountain (737m), which has been called the true mountain of Pocheon City, is a mountain towering west of Pocheon-eup. Around the 3rd year of the reign of King Heongang of Silla (872), when State Preceptor Dosan was staying here, the king himself visited and encouraged it, so it was called Wangbangsan Mountain, and it is said that the temple where State Preceptor Doseon lived was called Wangbangsa Temple. The current Wangsansa Temple was restored at the temple site. Wangbangsan Mountain is a mountain located at the northern end of the Cheonbo Mountain Range, a branch of the western Gwangju Mountain Range. The clear waters of Wangbangsan Mountain gathered together to form Hobyeonggol Valley. The hiking course is an 11.36 km course that goes from Muleok Pass (Mureok Pass) to the Wangsansa Fork, climbs to the top of Wangbangsan Mountain, then returns to the Wangsansa Fork and returns to the starting point of Muleok Pass. It takes about 4 hours and 20 minutes. When you climb to the top of Wangbangsan Mountain, you can see Dongducheon City and Soyosan Mountain to the northwest, and Pocheon-dong and Seondan-dong to the east, as well as Gukmangbong Peak and Unaksan Mountain behind them, as if forming a folding screen. Another hiking course allows you to reach the summit by passing the stone top peak in an east direction from Ojijae Pass, and from the summit, you can descend in a northwest direction to reach Suwibong Pass. The total hiking time takes 4 to 5 hours. There are tourist attractions nearby, such as Soyosan Mountain, Sinbuk Hot Springs, and Simgok Valley. Course 1: Hobyeonggol > Wangsansa Temple (Bodeoksa Temple) > Forest Road > Summit Course 2: Catholic Church > Gateball court > Sports facilities > Stone pagoda > Fork (left) > Main ridge > Summit Course 3: Muleo Pass > Seonamneung > Fork (go straight) > Main ridge > Summit Course 4: Simgok Reservoir > Parking lot > Valley (path) > Fork (Wangbangsan Mountain, Guksabong) > Front left Ridge (South Ridge) > Summit Course 5: Ojijae Pass > Main Ridge (North Ridge) > Summit

title: Waemok Village
description: Waemok Village is a village on the west coast located in the northernmost part of Dangjin City. It is famous as the only place in the country where you can see the sunrise, sunset, and moonrise all in one place. Located at the northernmost tip of the Taean Peninsula, it has a unique topography that extends long and thin, bisecting the West Sea. Because the nearby Namyang Bay and Asan Bay are located deep inland, the village was given the name Waemok Village due to its protruding appearance like a heron's neck. Between Nojeokbong Peak and Janggohang Hill, which rise about 3km southeast of Waemok Village, a rock that stands like Munpilbong Peak, as if a brush was stuck upside down, attracts attention. This rock, visible across the sea from Waemok Village, is a place that attracts the attention of people looking for unexplored natural scenery. This village has several lodging facilities, camping sites, restaurants, a Yachting Around the World promotional exhibition hall, and a beach. Waemok Village can be accessed via national highways No. 38, local roads 633, 647, and 615, and the West Coast Expressway Songak IC and Seosan IC are close by. Nearby are Janggo Port and Seokmun Sports Park.

title: Oeam Folk Village
description: This village has been designated as a national folk cultural heritage. The village was formed about 500 years ago, and because of its good site, it was selected as one of Korea's top 10 villages to live in. The village residents have been engaged in farming for generations and have maintained their traditional culture, providing a variety of things to see and experience to visitors. The village holds the Jangseung Festival every year in New Year, the straw culture festival in October, and the winter solstice event in November. In front of the village, Jeojatgeori, a market from the Joseon Dynasty, has been created, where you can enjoy food and performances. As you enjoy traditional culture at Oeam Folk Village, which cultivates our beautiful traditional culture, traditional cultures that once seemed difficult will soon feel familiar. ◎ Travel information to experience the charm of the Korean Wave - Drama <Missing 2>The main filming location of the drama ‘Missing 2’ is Oeam Folk Village. In this drama, where the story of chasing the truth of an incident unfolds against the backdrop of a village of souls visible only to the main characters, Oeam Folk Village creates a mysterious and quiet atmosphere, adding to the immersion of the drama.

title: UseArboretum
description: Yongdo Arboretum, located in Maehwa-dong, Siheung-si, Gyeonggi-do, is an experiential learning center in nature. There is a garden with over 100 kinds of wild flowers, a botanical garden with various plants growing, an herb village with the fragrant scent of grass, a water park suitable for children's level, animals that children like, and a sledding slope that can be enjoyed all year round.

title: Yongduam Rock
description: Yongduam Rock, located on the northern beach near Jeju Airport, is called Yongduam Rock because its shape resembles a dragon's head after being washed by waves and wind over a long period of time. According to legend, when a dragon stole the jade beads of the Hallasan Mountain spirit and ran away, the angry Hallasan spirit shot an arrow and dropped the dragon onto the beach, causing its body to submerge in the sea water and its head to the sky, where it hardened. Another legend is that a white horse, whose wish was to become a dragon and ascend to the sky, was caught by a general and hardened into a rock on the spot. There are various cafes and restaurants on the Yongdam-Dodu coastal road that runs from Yongduam to Dodu Port, so you can enjoy a drive that is both enjoyable for the eyes and the mouth. Have a cup of tea at Cafe Village, which has emerged as a specialty of Jeju, and follow the sea road to Iho Beach, Hagwi Beach, and Aewol-eup. North Jeju's coastal road from Aewol-eup to Yongduam is the most popular dating course for Jeju people.
priceDetail: Free

title: Yongmeori Coast
description: Yongmeori Beach is a beach located in front of Sanbangsan Mountain. If you walk down from Sanbangsan Mountain Rest Area, you will come across Yongmeori Beach with its beautiful coastal scenery. You can admire the sandstone layers that have been accumulated over tens of millions of years and the coastal cliffs created by waves. The caves, which are cave-like like small rooms, and the vast erosion zone of the rock wall spread out to create a spectacular view. The name Yongmeori was given because the shape of the hill resembles a dragon entering the sea with its head raised. According to legend, Qin Shi Huang, who knew that the dragon's head was in great shape to become a king, sent a messenger to cut off the dragon's tail and back with a sword. At this time, blood flowed and Sanbangsan Mountain continued to cry in pain for several days. There is a road right next to the beach where the waves break white, and the cliffs are curved like waves. A narrow but flat wave pad has been developed in front of the sea cliff, which serves as a trail for circumnavigating Yongmeori Beach. During bad weather or high tide, entry is prohibited due to high risk, so it is best to check the viewing times in advance before visiting. As you walk along the sandstone layer, you will find women divers setting up stalls and selling seafood at the coastal area, and at the entrance to Yongmeori, there is the Hamel Monument. ◎ Travel information to meet the charm of the Korean Wave - Drama <Hwanmoon> In episode 2 of the drama 'Hwanmoon', this is the place where Jang-wook (Lee Jae-wook) arrives in search of Mu-deok (Jung So-min) who fell into the Gyeongcheon Lake. The unique and beautiful scenery created by the rock layers carved by the waves is awe-inspiring to those who see it.
operatingHours: 09:00~17:00 ※ Visiting hours change depending on low tide and high tide, so please call before visiting.

title: Yongmunsa Temple (Yongmunsan Mountain)
description: Yongmunsa Temple, located in the Yongmunsan Tourist Complex, is a temple belonging to the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism and is located at the foot of Yongmunsan Mountain in Yongmun-myeon, Yangpyeong-gun. Yongmunsa Temple is said to have been founded by Master Daegyeong in the second year of King Shindeok of Silla (913), and according to one theory, King Gyeongsun (reigned 927-935) personally visited and founded it. In the 4th year of King U of the Goryeo Dynasty (1378), Master Jicheon moved and enshrined the Tripitaka Koreana from Gaepung Gyeongcheonsa Temple, and in the 4th year of King Taejo of the Joseon Dynasty (1395), it was rebuilt by Monk Joan. Yongmunsa Temple includes Daeungjeon, Sannyeonggak, Chilseonggak, Yosachae, Iljumun, Temple Stay Training Center, and Tea Garden. At Yongmunsa Temple, the largest ginkgo tree in Asia, estimated to be about 1,100 years old, with a height of 42m and a root circumference of 15.2m, is designated and protected as a natural monument. There is a legend that this tree was planted by Prince Maui, the son of King Gyeongsun of Unified Silla (reigned 927-935), while going to Mt. Geumgang with sorrow over losing his country, and another legend says that the cane carried by Master Uisang was planted and grew into a tree. If you go 2km up the valley from Yongmunsa Temple, you will come across Yonggakbawi Rock, which resembles a dragon's horn, on the mountainside. If you go 1km further up from here, you will find Madangbawi Rock, a large rock that can accommodate about 100 people. Temple stay is also operated, and you can choose between a relaxation program and an experiential program.

title: Yongmunsan Mountain
description: It is a mountain located on the border of Yongmun-myeon and Okcheon-myeon in Yangpyeong-gun, Gyeonggi-do, reaching a height of 1,157m. It is located 8km northeast of Yangpyeong and 42km east of Seoul. Although it belongs to the Gwangju mountain range, it is an independent mountain massif with a magnificent mountain body that extends 8km east to west and 5km north to south. With Yongmunsan Mountain as the main peak, Doil Peak (864m) 5.5km east-northeast, Jungwonsan Mountain (800m) 4.5km to the east, Baekunbong Peak (940m), 3.5km to the southwest, and other peaks are rising to form a mountain range. The summit is flat and the ridge has a developed plateau. In particular, in the middle of Jungwonsan Mountain, there are Yonggye and Jogye. There is a grand canyon, and the land in between is on a 100m high rocky cliff, reminiscent of Mt. Geumgangsan. The north has a gentle slope and the south has a steep slope, piled rock formations appear, and deep valleys and waterfalls can be seen. In the northwest area of ​​Yongmunsan Mountain, a high-level flat surface of about 4㎢ at an altitude of 700 to 1,100 m appears. In the valley at the foot of the southern mountain, there are ancient temples such as Yongmunsa Temple, Sangwonsa Temple, Yunpilsa Temple, and Sanasa Temple. The ginkgo tree within the grounds of Yongmunsa Temple is designated as a natural monument, and the tree occupies an area of ​​260㎡. In addition, there are two treasures, a stupa and monument of State Preceptor Jeong Ji, which are treasures.

title: Yongmun Millennium Market (5th, 10th)
description: Yongmun Millennium Market is one of the three major traditional markets in Yangpyeong-gun and is a 5-day traditional market with over 200 stalls right when you get off at Yongmun Station on the Gyeongui-Jungang Line. It is famous as a tourist market due to the presence of the Yongmunsan Mountain Tourist Complex and the Freshwater Fish Ecology Museum. It is operated as a market filled with culture and art, with plenty of food, things to see, and things to enjoy, rather than simply a place to enjoy shopping. (Source: Yangpyeong-gun Culture and Tourism website)

title: Yongso Waterfall
description: Yongso Waterfall, located in Jeokmok-ri, Buk-myeon, Gapyeong-gun, Gyeonggi-do, is a waterfall that flows into Yongso, 3km upstream of Domachi Valley from Sampalgyo Bridge leading to Jomurakgol. The water stream of the waterfall is the source of the Domachen Stream, which flows down the rugged mountains around 1,000m above sea level, including Seokryongsan Mountain, Domachiryeong, Sinro, and Gukmangbong Peak. As the name of the waterfall suggests, it does not fall with a roar from a high place, but the water that flows down between rocks gathers in a place surrounded by rock walls to form a pond, and small and large waterfalls run along the valley. The name Yongso originated from the legend that a dragon was seen by a pregnant woman while ascending to heaven, fell and became a cow instead of being able to ascend. This waterfall and pond are called Jeokmokyongso (赤木龍沼) and are considered the 5th scenic spot among the eight scenic spots of Gapyeong. It is famous as a place to take many pictures due to the beautiful scenery of the surrounding autumn leaves. It is located 3 km away from Jeokmok-ri 3.8 Bridge, a 40-minute walk, and the surrounding oak and maple trees are in good harmony, and azaleas are in full bloom in May. The area near Yongso Falls is an area of ​​concern for safety accidents while playing in the water. It is said that the depth of the water is as high as 4m after heavy rain, and safety guards are deployed during the summer. Swimming is not always prohibited, but it is prohibited when the current is strong or after rain, so you must wear safety equipment when playing in the water and be careful not to be swept away by the current.

title: Yongin Poeun Art Hall
description: Poeun Art Hall, located on the site of Yongin Arpia Sports Complex, opened in April 2004 to promote the leisure and cultural life of Yongin citizens and is operated by the Yongin Cultural Foundation. The name of Poeun Art Hall comes from Poeun Jeong Mong-ju's pen name, and is a world-class performance hall equipped with cutting-edge facilities. It has a total area of ​​13,826 m², a stage area of ​​1,109 m², and 1,258 auditorium seats. It is a cultural experience center where citizens can enjoy high-quality performances as well as an environment that can perfectly support performance activities, auditorium seats where they can enjoy the performance comfortably, and a rest area in the lives of citizens who can enjoy relaxation. It takes about 17 minutes by car from Pangyo IC and about 5 minutes (345m) on foot from Jukjeon Station (Dankook University) on the Suin Bundang Line. Nearby are Everland, Korean Folk Village, Korea Job World, World Cultural Heritage Yunggeonreung Royal Tomb, Mulhyanggi Arboretum, Yongin Rural Theme Park, and Deokpyeong Dinosaur Arboretum.

title: Yongin Cultural Center
description: Yongin Cultural Center, located in Yongin City Cultural Welfare Administration Town, is a place to inherit and develop Yongin's local cultural history and local culture. It discovers local historical materials and carries out projects for cultural education, local cultural festivals, and the development of culture and arts. Yongin Cultural Center is a non-profit, special corporation, and cultural institution representing the region. It is a corporate organization under the Ministry of Culture and Tourism whose purpose is to contribute to the balanced promotion of local culture and development of local culture by soundly nurturing and developing local cultural projects and local cultural centers with certain facilities and scale. Yongin Cultural Center, established and opened in 1957 under the Local Cultural Center Promotion Act, moved to its current location in 2017. The cultural center is equipped with facilities such as a local data room, classroom, auditorium/theater, conference room, data room, and exhibition hall, and operates various cultural events and educational programs. 용인문화원은 향토문화의 전승, 발굴 창달선양사업, 향토사 발간사업, 지역의 특색을 개발한 향토축제의 토착화, 평생학습의 사회교육프로그램인 문화학교 운영, 향토문화고취사업, 문화예술창달사업등 다양한 문화사업으로 지역민의 문화적 향수와 욕구를 충족하고자 노력하고 있으며, 지역문화의 발판에서 구심점 역할을 수행하는 중요한 기관으로 이바지하고 있다.

title: Yongin City Museum
description: It is a museum where you can see the history of Yongin City at a glance through about 400 pieces of materials, videos, and photos, and is Yongin's representative historical and cultural experience space. Located in Giheung-gu, Yongin-si, this place opened in November 2009 as the 'Yongin Cultural Heritage Exhibition Hall' to preserve the Paleolithic cultural layer discovered during the development of the Dongbaek District in Yongin, and was changed to its current name in March 2018. It consists of an exhibition room that introduces historical materials of Yongin from prehistoric times to the present, including Paleolithic era artifacts excavated from Dongbaek-dong and Middle East ruins, and an outdoor exhibition room that displays restored models of remains in the Yongin area. In addition, children and teenagers can see and experience the history of Yongin firsthand in the history experience room and video experience room, which are equipped with various experiential materials and new media systems.
price: Free museum admission / experience fee separate

title: Yongin Natural Recreation Forest
description: Yongin Natural Recreation Forest is located at the southern foot of Jeonggwang Mountain, 562 meters above sea level. It is a residential rest area with beautiful natural scenery, accommodations, walking trails, and a children's playground. 숲속체험관 내의 8개의 객실, 숲속의집 14동, 목조체험주택 3동, 카라반 4동 등 다양한 규모의 숙박시설이 조성되어 있다. The standard number of people staying at the accommodation is 4 to 13, so not only family vacationers but also various group gatherings are possible. Within the recreational forest, there are facilities such as a large lawn plaza where users can freely engage in activities such as picnicking and resting, a multi-purpose playground where various sports activities can be performed, an eco-adventure that can stimulate children's sense of adventure, and a zipline that provides a thrilling aerial experience. In addition, there are hiking trails and trails where you can enjoy contemplation and relaxation while walking through the forest. Eco Adventure has created an eco-friendly wooden play facility in the forest, taking advantage of the natural terrain, to stimulate children's sense of adventure and curiosity. Play facilities for various age groups, from infants to teenagers, are installed, including zip lines, net play platforms, and rocking toys. In addition, a performance hall and learning space have been created for various learning activities such as performances and outdoor learning in the forest. By utilizing the surrounding areas of the forest and adjacent rice fields and wetlands, a biotope was created where various species can inhabit and where food can be supplied to various wild animals. By installing a wooden path around the wetland using on-site felled trees, an experiential and learning space was created where biological observation was possible. In order to protect and efficiently utilize various water resources within the forest, there is also a waterway (145m) that passes through the entire recreational forest.

title: Yonghwasa Temple
description: Yonghwasa Temple is a quiet temple located at the foot of Chilbosan Mountain, a resting place for Suwon citizens. If you climb the stairs from the temple entrance, you will see a small precinct. Daeungjeon and Daejabijeon are located side by side, and Sansingak is behind them. Inside the main hall is the Maitreya Stone Buddha, which is characterized by being slightly tilted to the right. There is a legend that this stone Buddha was originally discovered buried in Chilbosan Mountain, and Yonghwasa Temple was built in its place. Even now, many people pray here.

title: Woo Seok-heon Natural History Museum
venue: Namyangju Woo Seok-heon Natural History Museum
description: Based on the Namsan Seoul Tower Stone and Mineral Exhibition Hall, established in 1988, it was established in December 2003 in Naegak-ri, Jinjeop-eup, Namyangju-si, Gyeonggi-do as the only geology and natural history museum in the Seoul-Gyeonggi region. In 2005, it was registered as a career recognition institution by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism and the National Museum of Korea, and it serves as a vibrant educational site that satisfies children's inquisitiveness through various special exhibitions and useful learning programs. * House of Beautiful Stones, Woo Seok-heon * Woo Seok-heon (愚石軒), meaning 'House of Beautiful Stones', serves as a natural history museum specializing in geology centered on minerals, rocks, and fossils, and at the same time contains the infinite potential for scientific development contained in these stones. It directly visits fossils, minerals, and rock production areas scattered around the world, collects various specimens with the highest value and academic significance, and exchanges them with domestic and foreign universities and research institutes. There is. It operates a life history museum, an earth science museum, an animal ecology museum, and a special exhibition hall, and each exhibition hall displays rare natural history materials such as authentic fossils, minerals, rocks, meteorites, and marine-related specimens.

title: Ueumdo
description: Ueumdo Island, which was named because the island resembles a cow or because the sound of a cow can be heard coming from the land, became a land rather than an island due to the development of reclaimed land in Sihwa Lake. Proof of this is the dinosaur egg fossil discovered near Ueumdo Island. The dinosaurs discovered here are believed to be from a group habitat dating back to the Cretaceous period of the Mesozoic Era about 100 million years ago. About 30 dinosaur egg nest fossils and 200 egg fossils were discovered in 12 locations. The dinosaur egg fossil site, which has such rare value, is a popular tourist attraction made famous by people who enjoy visiting Ueumdo Island to take pictures.

title: Ungye Falls
description: Ungye Falls, a representative attraction of Gamaksan Mountain in Jeokseong-myeon, Paju-si, Gyeonggi-do, is a charming 20m long valley along Silmaceon Stream. It boasts an abundant amount of water and is also called Biryong Falls. The scenery of blue water pouring from the cliff is spectacular. Because the water falls almost vertically, it is also a popular ice training spot in the winter. Due to its proximity to the cease-fire line, Mt. Gamak has been a no-go zone for a long time, so Ungye Falls is also not well-known, retaining its natural appearance untouched by people. If you go 3-4 minutes from Seolmagyo Bridge, there is a ticket office and Turtle Rock Rest Area, and if you climb the path that curves around the ridge on the left, you can see Ungye Falls. Recently, as Gamaksan Mountain Suspension Bridge has become famous, Ungye Falls is also becoming famous as many tourists visit it. However, access to Ungye Falls is prohibited and only viewing is allowed. I recommend taking a tour of Gamaksan Mountain and Beomryunsa Temple via the famous Gamaksan Suspension Bridge. Entry to the mountain is restricted from February 1 to May 15 and from November 1 to December 15 due to the forest fire prevention period.

title: Ungil Mountain
description: * If you want a light weekend hike, Ungilsan Mountain * Ungilsan Mountain (610m) is a mountain that rises 40km east of Seoul and 4km northwest of Yangsu-ri, where the Bukhan River and Namhangang River meet. In 《Sujongsa Jungsugi》 written in 1890 (the 27th year of King Gojong's reign), it appears as Ungil, and in the older 《Donggukyeoji Seungnam》, it is written as Jogoksan Mountain. Sujongsa Temple, located halfway up the mountain, has an octagonal five-story stone pagoda, a local cultural asset, and a ginkgo tree that is over 500 years old. Above all, the old people said that it was the best temple in Haedong, with an outstanding view of the Namhan River and Bukhangang River. Several poems are written about the place where Seo Geo-jeong, Zen Master Choui, Jeong Yak-yong, Song In, and Lee I stayed. The water tastes good and it is a place with a deep connection to tea. * The beauty of hiking Mt. Ungil * Transportation is convenient as a city bus connects to the bottom of the mountain, and the hiking trail is smooth, making it a suitable place for family hiking or light weekend hiking. The pleasure of hiking on Ungilsan Mountain can be experienced from climbing the northwest ridge. After leaving Sujongsa Temple, take the northwest ridge and walk leisurely for about 20 minutes to reach the summit. There are three ways to come down from the summit: go back down the way you came up, or take a left after Sujongsa Temple and go down to Songchon-ri. Alternatively, if you take the long ridge extending from the summit to the northwest, you will take the 463m highland - Saejae Pass - Ancient Farm, and then take a traversing course that leads to Deokso.

title: Unjeong Lake Park
description: Unjeong Lake Park is a 724,937㎡ park located in the center of Unjeong Town in Wadong-dong, Paju-si. In addition to various convenience facilities and event facilities, it is equipped with a future plaza with green grass and play areas, a dreamy garden with a view of a reservoir, a pinwheel hill with colorful flowers blooming every season and a large pinwheel installed, and a sky fountain that spews water up to 50 meters high.

title: Ulsan Industrial Square
description: Up Square, located on Samsan-dong Design Street, one of Ulsan's two major downtowns, is a shopping mall complex where you can see global sensibilities and the latest trends in lifestyle, culture, commercial fashion, etc. at a glance. On the first basement floor, there are things to see such as a large bookstore, digital record store, stationery store, coffee shop, and clothing. There is also a kids park, making it great to visit with children. The 2nd to 5th floors are convenient for shopping as you can see various fashion brands in one place, including women's suits, men's suits, casual clothes, sports clothing, and a shoe multi-shop. On the 5th floor, there is a restaurant area with delicious Jjamppong, pork cutlet, rice noodles, ramen, and conveyor belt sushi restaurants. A flea market is often held at an event hall next to the restaurant area, and there is also a movie theater, making it a popular place for dates in Ulsan.

title: Wondang Market
description: Wondang Market, which was the main axis of Goyang City's original downtown 30 years ago, is a small but meaningful market that also serves as a resting place where people gather and chat. It is an area about 30 minutes away from Seoul and quite a lot of people live here, providing convenience for grocery shopping to residents. It is located in front of Lee's Shopping Mall, which was built in 1984 near Wondang Station. In addition, there is a small but fragrant flower market as befits Goyang City, a city of flowers.

title: Wondae-ri Birch Forest (Whispering Birch Forest)
venue: Wondaeri Birch Forest Whispering Birch Forest
description: Wondaeri Birch Forest, also called Whispering Birch Forest, is a natural eco-tourism site. This place, which was formed by planting 690,000 birch trees on 138 ha from 1974 to 1995, has 7 trails in the forest, a classroom in the forest, an observatory, an ecological pond, an Indian house, a wooden bridge, and wooden stairs, so you can enjoy forest bathing and healing. You can reach the birch forest by walking along the forest path that starts from the birch forest information center, which is the entrance. There are two forest paths: the Wongwon Forest Road, which takes about 80 minutes on foot, and the Wondae Forest Road, which takes about an hour. As you climb the hiking trail, you will see a dense forest filled with birch trees over 20 years old. The white trunks and leaves of the birch forest shine as if snow has fallen, and the birch forest stretching towards the sky gives an exotic atmosphere. Within the forest, you can choose from trails of various difficulty levels and distances. The most popular course is Course 1 (Birch Course), which allows you to see a concentrated growing area of ​​pure white birch trees. It is about 0.9km away and takes about 50 minutes. In winter, the forest covered in white snow and the pure white birch trees come together, making it a popular photo location. Visitors with families with children can enjoy a variety of nature-themed activities such as a forest classroom and an Indian house at the Children's Forest Experience Center.
address: 760 Birch Forest Road, Inje-eup, Inje-gun, Gangwon-do, Information Center ~ Birch Forest

title: One Mount Snow Park
description: One Mount, located within the support site of Hallyu World and KINTEX in Ilsanseo-gu, is the largest complex cultural space in the northwest area of ​​the metropolitan area, consisting of three buildings with a total floor area of ​​161,602㎡, 2 floors underground and 9 floors above ground. With the motto of being the best playground on earth, One Mount provides cultural spaces such as shopping malls, snow parks, water parks, and membership-only luxury sports clubs, as well as various entertainment activities throughout the year, such as various performances, events, and parties. * Snow Park One Mount Snow Park is Korea's first winter-themed indoor theme park and is a space where you can enjoy a variety of entertainment on snow and ice at once. It consists of the Ice Lake, where you can enjoy 101 fun items such as reliefs, unique sleighs, and animal sleighs designed with the concept of Santa's village in Northern Europe; the Ice Road, where you can enjoy unique experiences that are sometimes dizzying and sometimes dreamy as you pass through 7 themed caves; and Snow Hill, where you can go sledding while being met with white falling snow in sub-zero temperatures all year round. It is the world's first themed space where you can see the aurora show and ice show in a fairytale village made of ice, and is expected to become an attractive tourist destination for not only Koreans but also foreigners.

title: World Cup Park
description: World Cup Park is located on 800,000 pyeong of the beautiful island of Nanjido. Two huge mountains and a large flat landfill site were created with Seoul City waste over 15 years from 1978 to 1993. To celebrate the hosting of the 2002 World Cup and the new millennium, the Nanjido landfill was stabilized and turned into a park. By creating an area of ​​2.7 million m2 into a large-scale environmental and ecological park, it was reborn as a World Cup park loved by Seoul citizens. It was created as five theme parks, including the representative park, Peace Park, Haneul Park, Noeul Park, Nanjicheon Park, and Nanji Hangang Park. Peace Park, built on 135,000 pyeong in front of the World Cup Stadium, commemorates the first World Cup match of the 21st century and is a modern, high-quality open plaza that can enhance the image of Korea and Seoul. It was created to serve as the front yard of the World Cup Stadium and as a central park in the northwest region of Seoul. As a park that represents the entire World Cup Park, it is a space that pursues coexistence and symbiosis between nature and humans and prays for ‘peace.’ Currently, World Cup Park is filled with 733,000 trees of 92 species, and Nanji Pond and Nanjicheon Stream are added to create a beautiful natural landscape. The World Cup Park Exhibition Hall, where you can see the overall history and changes of Nanjido, and Nanji Pond, where you can see various species of plants, animals, and birds, are the park's famous attractions. Now, even on days when there are no soccer games, citizens naturally continue to walk lightly, and it also serves as an educational ecological park by planning various learning programs and events. It has developed into an environmental, ecological and energy theme park coveted by people around the world.
operatingHours: Hours of use vary by month, so please refer to the website.

title: Wolmido
description: Since the establishment of the Cultural Street in July 1989, Wolmido has become known as a place for culture and arts, a place for meetings and exchanges, and a performance venue. It is a famous place that comes to mind when you think of Incheon. This place is lined with cafes and a raw fish center, so you can choose and enjoy food that suits your taste while looking out at the cool sea. On holidays, hundreds of thousands of people flock from all over, making it a resting place for Incheon citizens and surrounding citizens. Wolmido Culture Street has created a characteristic section for tourists and established a place for meeting and exchange, a place for culture and arts, and a place for various performances to promote convenience for users, contributing to the promotion of citizens' cultural awareness and the development of local art culture.
priceDetail: Free

title: Woljeonggyo Bridge
description: Woljeong Bridge, a bridge from the Unified Silla Dynasty, was lost during the Joseon Dynasty. After 10 years of investigation, historical research, and restoration, all restoration was completed in April 2018. According to <History of the Three Kingdoms>, it is recorded as having been built in the 19th year of King Gyeongdeok (760) during the Unified Silla Dynasty, and at the time, it served as a connection between Wolseong and Namsan in Gyeongju. From November 26, 1984 to September 8, 1986, it was confirmed for the first time that there was a wooden bridge during two excavations and collection of data for restoration design. Afterwards, a bridge measuring 66.15 m in length, 13 m in width, and 6 m in height was restored through construction from 2008 to 2013. From April 2016, construction to build two gate towers at both ends of the bridge was carried out, and was finally completed in April 2018. On the second floor of the gate tower, there is an exhibition hall where you can see videos of the restoration process of the bridge and excavated relics. It is good to be able to see Woljeong Bridge during the day, and Woljeong Bridge at night has another attraction and is a popular place for the night view of Gyeongju. If you look at Woljeong Bridge from the stepping stones installed in front of Woljeong Bridge, you can see the scenery of Woljeong Bridge shining softly above the river.
priceDetail: Free

title: Woljeongsa Temple/Woljeongsa Fir Forest
description: Woljeongsa Temple is a temple founded by Master Jajang in the 12th year of Queen Seondeok of Silla (643) on Odaesan Mountain, a Buddhist holy site. It is the headquarters of the 4th diocese of the Jogye Order and has about 60 temples and 8 hermitages. It also possesses numerous cultural assets, including the national treasure octagonal 9-story stone pagoda, the treasured stone seated Bodhisattva statue of Woljeongsa Temple, and the wooden seated seated monk statue. A fir forest with over 1,700 fir trees spreads out for about 1km from Woljeongsa Iljumun to Geumgang Bridge. The fir forest is a representative tourist attraction of Woljeongsa Temple, a thousand-year-old temple loved by visitors in all four seasons, and it is a must-visit place if you visit Woljeongsa Temple. Woljeongsa Temple operates temple stays divided into relaxation and experience types, where you can escape from the secular world and recharge your tired body and mind in the mountains. In addition to the temple stay, there is a Woljeongsa monastic school for the general public to experience the life of a monk. In addition, Odaesan Meditation Village (OMV) is approximately 99,170㎡ in size, which is 14 times the size of a soccer field, and is equipped with accommodations, cultural experience facilities, restaurants, gardens, and forest trails, providing people who are tired from work and competition with the opportunity to recover their mind and body through meditation in a natural resting place. In addition, there is also a 9km walking experience on Seonjae-gil from Woljeongsa Temple to Sangwonsa Temple and a Zen meditation yoga school with Monk Jeongnyeom, head priest of Woljeongsa Temple, and Sohan, an Indian yoga master.

title: Wiyangji (Wiyangji poplar tree)
description: Wiyangji (位良池) has the meaning of ‘a name given for being built for good people’, but this name was recently changed and the original name was Yangyangji. Yangyangji, which is said to have been built during the Silla Dynasty, was a water reservoir that irrigated rice fields, but lost its original function due to the construction of the huge Gasan Reservoir nearby. However, instead of irrigating the rice fields, it attracts many tourists with its picturesque scenery. In addition, it is a popular travel destination so much so that it is selected as one of the eight scenic spots of Miryang. The colony of pop trees boasting magnificent pillars along the circumference of the reservoir boasts a beautiful scenery all year round. Spring days are the peak of Wiyangji when the poplar trees bloom in abundance as if white snow has fallen. On a clear day, the flowers of the poplar tree reflected in the pond are as beautiful as a watercolor painting. Since ancient times, the Ipop tree has been known as a tree that predicts a good harvest in the coming year, because the flowers in full bloom look like white rice. It is surrounded by a dense forest of beautiful willows and pine trees, so you can enjoy beautiful scenery all year round, and Wanjaejeong, a pavilion owned by the Andong Kwon family, built in 1900 on an island floating in the pond, adds to the oriental beauty.
