title: Wind 1947 Kart Theme Park
description: Wind 1947 Kart Theme Park is an experiential theme park located in Topyeong-dong, Seogwipo-si, Jeju-do. Wind 1947 Kart is located against the backdrop of Jeju’s beautiful southern landscape. There are various experience centers here, including ‘Wind 1947 Kart’, an activity the whole family can enjoy, and Jeju’s only indoor BB ‘Survival Experience Center’. You can also visit ‘J Factory’, a brunch cafe with an industrial feel, and ‘Attic’, an unmanned cafe, a Jeju emotional space that creates perfect relaxation. Children and adults can create fun and happy memories through education, experience, relaxation, fun, and activities. The course is designed safely so you can enjoy it without any worries, and it is an even more meaningful and thrilling experience as you can ride the cart while looking at the panoramic view of Hallasan Mountain.

title: Glass Island Museum
description: Daebudo Glass Island Museum is a cultural experience space where the artistic spirit of the best glass artists melts and breathes in a wide space, fantastic glass sculptures, beautiful sunsets, and the West Sea mudflats come together spectacularly. Daebudo Island is a representative outing destination filled with glass island art museums and MacArt museums where you can admire various sculptures, a fairytale-like themed exhibition hall with lighting added to the natural objects of the universe made of glass, a glass sculpture park where the nature of the sea and reed forests harmonizes well, and an experiential learning space where you can make your own glass craft works. The theme exhibition hall that reproduces nature with glass and special exhibitions by modern glass artists are held, and in the glass craft demonstration hall, you can watch glass craftsmanship demonstrations by glass sculpture artists three times a day. McArt Glass, comprised of active artists, develops and produces its own design products and strives to incorporate original and artistic glass sculpture products into architecture, urban cultural spaces, and various art genres. In particular, there is a large lawn garden where children can run around, and it is fun to see sculptures with various themes placed along the outdoor walking path, and it is also a perfect photo zone. The MacArt Museum displays works of various genres, including paintings, three-dimensional works, installations, and video, and holds exhibition events at least four times a year, allowing visitors to enjoy new works each time. At the art shop on the first floor of the MacArt Museum, you can purchase crafts and design products made by domestic glass artists.

title: Yumyeongsan Mountain
description: Located in Gail-ri, Seorak-myeon, this mountain is 864 meters above sea level and is loved by hikers due to the water that flows continuously in the valley of strangely shaped rocks. The ridge is gentle and gentle, making it a great place for hiking with the family. The forest is dense, and the valley here is connected to glass-like clear cows such as Batso, Yongso, and Madangso, creating a spectacular sight. From the top of the mountain, you can see the Bukhangang River to the north, Cheongpyeong Lake, and the Namhan River to the south, as well as the surrounding mountains such as Yongmunsan Mountain, Hwaaksan Mountain, and Myeongjisan Mountain. The nearby Yumyeong Mountain Natural Recreation Forest, directly managed by the Korea Forest Service, is equipped with log cabins, campsites, and walking trails, and is suitable for hiking in all seasons. A cultural village has been created nearby. There are two hiking courses: Course 1 and Course 2. Course 1 is 2.0km (1 hour and 30 minutes) but requires climbing a steep ridge, Course 2 is 12.7km (1 hour and 10 minutes) into a valley, and the remaining 1.6km (50 minutes) allows you to enjoy forest bathing while hiking along the valley. Yumyeongsan Mountain is also known as a driving course due to its beautiful scenery. Car and motorcycle enthusiasts should take this course at least once. It has many slopes and sharp curves, so it is a very popular touring destination for those who like driving, so caution is required as it is known to be a mountain road with many traffic accidents.

title: United Nations Memorial Park
description: The UN Memorial Park is the world's only UN military cemetery, where fallen UN soldiers who sacrificed their lives for the cause of world peace and freedom are buried. This cemetery was created by the United Nations Command in January 1951, the year after the Korean War broke out, to bury the fallen. As the cemetery was completed in April of the same year, the remains of fallen UN soldiers temporarily buried in Kaesong, Incheon, Daejeon, Daegu, Miryang, and Masan began to be buried. In November 1955, the National Assembly of the Republic of Korea permanently donated the land here to the United Nations to repay the sacrifices of the UN forces. It was resolved to designate the cemetery as a sacred site, and on December 15, 1955, the United Nations, upon receiving the National Assembly's resolution from the Korean government, adopted a resolution at the United Nations General Assembly to permanently manage the cemetery. It is a sanctuary where the souls of fallen UN soldiers are buried among the warriors from 16 countries that dispatched troops and 5 countries that sent medical support groups to protect the freedom and peace of the Republic of Korea during the Korean War. At first, about 11,000 fallen soldiers were buried in this memorial cemetery, but it was later relocated at the request of bereaved families or the home government, and currently has 2,300 remains. The UN Forces Memorial Tower, built by the Korean government in 1978, has the combat equipment dispatched to the Korean War, the number of personnel, and the status of fallen soldiers engraved on a copper plate in Korean and English. The Commonwealth Memorial Tower, built by the British government, commemorates the noble sacrifice of those who died in battle in the Commonwealth countries, whose bodies were never found.
address: UN Memorial Park, 93 UN Pyeonghwa-ro, Nam-gu, Busan

title: Yulgok Arboretum
description: Yulgok Arboretum is a place created for the conservation, propagation, and exhibition of plant genetic resources. It is a place where a well-maintained city forest with dense forests was transformed through a reforestation project in the 1960s. Officially opened in June 2021. Currently, there are 21 thematic plant gardens within Yulgok Arboretum, and along with 70 trees of 15 species donated by citizens, a total of 300,000 plants of 1,300 species, including 80,000 trees of 700 species and 220,000 plants of 500 species, are planted. Yulgok Arboretum operates forest experience programs such as a children's forest experience program for infants and a forest healing program that can be participated by people in their 80s, such as Healing Forest, Family Forest, Mother's Vitality Forest, Silver Forest, and Nordic Walking. In addition, the 5km-long arboretum trail surrounding the arboretum includes an observatory overlooking the Imjingang River, Solhyanggi-gil, and Munbawi Rock, providing a rich and diverse charm. In addition, the Imjingang River to the north and Mt. Papyeong and Mt. Gamak to the east provide a panoramic view of the Imjingang River area and famous mountains where people live and die. It is also close to the surrounding historical sites of Yulgok Yi and Hwang Hui, making it possible to engage in tourism in the area.

title: Yuldong Park
description: Seongnam Yuldong Park is a natural lake park created to maximize nature, with beautiful scenery including lawns, hills, and lakes. Since the Baekje period, it has been called Yuldong Park because there are many chestnut trees. The park contains the Cheongju Han Clan Munjeonggong Burial Ground Monument (Gyeonggi-do Cultural Heritage Material), the March 1st Movement Memorial Tower, and is famous for its bungee jumping site. In addition, it provides various rest areas and tourist elements, such as a large lawn plaza open to citizens, a 1.8km waterside trail where you can take a walk around the lake while feeling the beauty of nature, a book theme park that encourages voluntary book reading and a family space where curiosity and imagination come together, a children's playground, and a dog park.※ Bicycles are not allowed in the park.

title: Yulbom Botanical Garden
description: Yulbom Botanical Garden and Agricultural Arts Center are ''rural art theme farms''. It is an agricultural tourism service space that provides attractions and rest by not only cultivating and producing agriculture, but also beautifying and turning it into a work of art from a visual perspective. Let’s enjoy a seasonal rural experience using fresh, honestly grown agricultural products along with a comfortable rest in clean nature! [Usage information and viewing precautions] - It is composed of a 10,000 pyeong outdoor botanical garden and a 10,000 pyeong agricultural product cultivation complex, and is a walking course that takes about 30 minutes to 1 hour. - As a botanical garden with a resting concept, there are many benches and benches provided here and there. - You can bring a mat. (Shade and tents cannot be installed) - Lunch boxes can be brought in. (Cooking is prohibited and all trash brought in must be cleaned up and returned.) - Pets are not permitted to enter. - Sports equipment (balls, kickboards, bicycles, badminton, etc.) cannot be brought in. - Strollers are available (however, it is inconvenient to use because there are unpaved roads in places.)

title: Yulam Hot Springs Charcoal Kiln Theme Park
venue: Yulam Hot Springs Charcoal Kiln Theme Park
description: Since ancient times, natural spring water has flowed from a small pond behind Yulam Hot Springs all year round and does not freeze even in the middle of winter, so it has been known as a place for nearby residents to wash their clothes. It is said to be a place to bathe and receive treatment as it is said to be effective in treating eye diseases, skin diseases, and arthritis. In particular, Yulam Hot Spring Water is a natural hot spring water that gushes out from bedrock 700 meters underground due to the regional characteristics of the geologically extensive hot spring water vein, where red clay and granite strata can store a large amount of hot spring water. The size of the bath is so large that it is supported by nine thick pillars. Based on the women's bath, there is a hot bath, a boiling bath, an event bath (rooibos bath), a cold bath, a sauna (dry, wet), and a bed sauna. The charcoal kiln is divided into a high temperature room, a medium greenhouse, and a low temperature room, and is also equipped with a lounge and foot bath. Yulam Hot Springs, where the best hot spring facilities and nature come together, is located less than an hour away from the metropolitan area, making it highly accessible. Provence Yulam Aqua Spa is located just above, making it a great place to enjoy water play with children.

title: Eunsan Eoulim Ecological Museum
description: This is a museum with amphibians, reptiles, birds, and arthropods. A 1 hour and 30 minute commentary program will be held focusing on amphibians and reptiles. You will learn about amphibians and reptiles such as lizards, snakes, turtles, and frogs by directly experiencing them. After the explanation, you can experience things such as observing living things through a microscope, experiencing red and blue glasses, and brain development puzzles.
price: Infants (48 months to 13 years old) 15,000 won, adults 10,000 won, disabled people and people of national merit 9,000 won ※ Fees may vary, so please refer to the website or call for inquiries.

title: Eunpyeong Hanok Village
description: Eunpyeong Hanok Village is a modern Hanok village located in Jingwan-dong, Eunpyeong-gu. It was newly created following Bukchon and Seochon. It is a historical and cultural village in harmony with the national park, Bukhansan Mountain, and Jingwansa Temple. Eunpyeong Hanok Village sells land to individuals so that they can build only hanoks, so each hanok has a different shape and wood color depending on the owner's taste, making it a pleasure to see. In addition, it is equipped with convenient facilities such as walking trails and cafes, making it suitable for outings. Since this is a residential area where residents live, most places except commercial facilities are occupied by Hanok Village residents or are private property, so viewing the inside of the Hanok is not possible. However, in some houses, the interior can be viewed with permission from the owner.
priceDetail: Free

title: banking market
description: Bank Market is a traditional market with over 40 years of tradition, and half of the merchants have been doing business together for over 30 years, maintaining a brother-sister-like relationship with the merchants and local residents. Although the number of stores is small, it is a traditional market that is essential to the local community. Since Namhansanseong Fortress was registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, many tourists visit Gyeonghan Market. After climbing Namhansanseong Fortress, you can go to a side dish shop that offers the taste of fresh ingredients, and even feel the pleasure of eating dishes made with ingredients such as fresh vegetables and meat. The walls of Namhansanseong Fortress can be walked 300 meters, and when you look down from the walls of Namhansanseong Fortress, you can see downtown Seoul and Seongnam City at a glance. Nearby tourist attractions include Namhansanseong Fortress, Pangyo Museum, Singudae Botanical Garden, Moran Market, and Bank Botanical Garden. A characteristic of the banking market is the introduction of a joint coupon system. As part of traditional market marketing to compete against large discount stores, it is a system in which coupons are issued by merchant associations and sold to merchants in the market. Merchants gave coupons to customers who made purchases over a certain amount, and customers collected coupons and exchanged them for gift certificates at the merchant association, which could be used like cash at coupon affiliated stores. In addition, we are working to create a market that can be more helpful to customers by holding various events through coupons.

title: Uiwang Moomin Park
description: Uiwang Moomin Park is a park with the theme of ‘Moomin and Friends’ by Finnish painter Tove Jansson, and was created with the concept of a treasure hunting trip in nature. It features a variety of experience spaces, including a character photo zone that recreates the journey of the Moomin friends, a natural grass plaza where children can play, and an art ball where you can enjoy the Moomin travel story at sunset. Another attractive point is the panoramic view of Baekun Lake, one of the eight scenic spots of Uiwang.

title: Uiwang Cultural Center
description: The Uiwang Cultural Center is a special public interest corporation cultural organization with national financial support established under the Local Cultural Center Promotion Act. It carries out projects such as the inheritance and development of local unique culture, preservation of local history, fostering of traditional culture, and cultural festivals. In addition, in order to establish Uiwang's history and tradition and promote culture and arts to satisfy citizens' cultural needs and improve their quality of life, we are actively promoting citizens' social education activities by operating cultural schools, lifelong education programs, and support for youth cultural and artistic activities. Uiwang Cultural Center is a special public interest corporation (government-funded institution) that was approved by the Governor of Gyeonggi Province on August 6, 1999 and opened on September 29, 1999, among 211 local cultural centers nationwide established by the Local Cultural Center Promotion Act. In addition, it was approved as a quasi-cultural school by the Governor of Gyeonggi Province on December 2, 2000, and was designated as a lifelong learning center in the Gyeonggi Province area by the Gyeonggi Provincial Office of Education on April 6, 2001.

title: Uijeongbu Science Library
description: The Government Science Library, the first astronomy and space specialized library in northern Gyeonggi Province, started in 2007 as a science-specialized library equipped with an observatory and space experience room. In 2020, the entire space was reorganized through a complete remodeling and the Children's Science Experience Room's 4D experience room was completely renovated and is currently in operation. In particular, the Uijeongbu Astronomical Observatory (in the Songsan Reservoir sports facility) was created separately in November 2019 to contribute to fostering creative scientific talent. Uijeongbu Science Library will serve as a comfortable resting place for citizens and a place of learning to develop potential capabilities. There are classrooms, a data storage room, a restaurant, and an art hall on the first basement floor, and on the first floor there is a reading room exclusively for children, a reading room exclusively for infants and toddlers, a digital information room, a reading room exclusively for the disabled and the elderly, and a relaxation area. The second floor has a humanities room, a periodicals room, a multimedia education room, and a seminar room, and the third floor has facilities such as an astronomy and space experience room, a natural science room, and an office.

title: Uijeongbu Art Library (8 Scenic Views of Uijeongbu)
venue: Uijeongbu Uijeongbu Art Library Eight Scenic Views of Uijeongbu
description: Opened in December 2019, it is Korea's first specialized library that combines an art museum and a library. On the first floor, there is an Art Ground exhibition room (a small-scale special exhibition exhibition space), and the second floor is the main reading space and contains children's and infant materials, general materials, etc. The third floor is an open studio and multipurpose hall: An open studio and multipurpose hall are operated as a creative space for prospective artists and a space for operating cultural programs.

title: Uijeongbu Music Library (8 scenic spots in Uijeongbu)
venue: Uijeongbu Uijeongbu Music Library Eight Scenic Views of Uijeongbu
description: Uijeongbu Music Library is a public library specializing in music that combines books and music to deliver music to a synesthetic space beyond the auditory realm. The space was designed with the theme of black music (jazz, blues, hip-hop, R&B, etc.) that reflects the regional characteristics of Uijeongbu City, and the collection was composed of books and non-book materials such as CDs, LPs, sheet music, and DVDs. We aim to improve the quality of life of citizens and implement the role of a local music platform created together with citizens.

title: Uijeongbu Memory Repository
description: Uijeongbu Memory Repository is a complex cultural space created by collecting citizens’ memories. It features a blue exterior that was remodeled from an old Veterans Hall building, and the narrow staircase and low ceiling create a nostalgic atmosphere of the past. In the Memory Hall, a permanent exhibition space, you can see Uijeongbu in the 1960s, including a U.S. military base, a coffee shop, and a theater, and in the storage room, you can see historical materials and maps of Uijeongbu. You can also experience school uniforms in the ‘Uijeongbu as a School’ corner, which recreates the scenery of an old classroom, including wooden chairs, blackboards, and silver lunch boxes.

title: Uijeongbu Cultural Center
description: Uijeongbu Cultural Center is a place to inherit and develop the local cultural history and local culture of Uijeongbu. It is carrying out projects to discover and preserve local historical materials, creative local cultural festivals and cultural content exchange projects between regions, cultural education projects, and living culture and arts revitalization projects. Uijeongbu Cultural Center, established in accordance with the Local Cultural Center Promotion Act on December 23, 1989, opened in the Citizens' Center in 1990 and moved to its current location in 2003. The cultural center is equipped with facilities such as a local exhibition hall, classrooms, conference rooms and data rooms, a literary theater that can accommodate 140 people, and an outdoor performance hall, and operates a variety of cultural events and educational programs.

title: Uijeongbu Arts Center (8 scenic spots in Uijeongbu)
venue: Uijeongbu Uijeongbu Arts Center Uijeongbu 8 Scenic Spots
description: The Uijeongbu Arts Center, located near Uijeongbu City Hall, was created to promote the leisure and cultural life of Uijeongbu citizens. It opened in April 2001, and reopened in January 2024 after remodeling work. The Uijeongbu Cultural Foundation is in charge of operation. Built with one floor underground and two floors above ground, the Uijeongbu Arts Center is equipped with a large theater (accommodating 1,025 people), a small theater (accommodating 237 people), an international conference hall (accommodating 177 people), and an exhibition hall. Additionally, convenience facilities such as barrier-free facilities and a nursing room are provided. Since its opening, it has been fulfilling its role as a cultural source for not only the Uijeongbu region but also the northern Gyeonggi and northeastern Seoul regions through excellent performances and exhibitions. In particular, by attracting high-quality performances and setting admission prices at mid-to-low prices, it opened the way for a ‘reverse viewing’ process of Seoul audiences visiting local performance halls. In addition, by continuously hosting brand festivals unique to Uijeongbu Arts Center, such as the ‘International Music Theater Festival’ and the literary festival ‘Cheon Sang-byeong Arts Festival’, it provides citizens with the opportunity to experience various genres and excellent domestic and international performances.  It takes about 3 minutes by car from Howon IC and about 10 minutes [652m] on foot from Uijeongbu City Hall Station on the Uijeongbu Light Rail. Nearby are Uijeongbu Eastern Plaza, Uijeongbu Budae Stew Street, Uijeongbu Rodero Street, Gonje Neighborhood Park, Nogang Seowon, Hoeryongsa Temple, Dobongsan Mountain, Suraksan Mountain, and Jangheung Recreation Area.

title: Yi Sun-sin Park
description: Yi Sun-sin Park is a park that commemorates the spirit of Admiral Yi Sun-sin. It is located near the Dongho Port breakwater in Tongyeong-si and is a representative tourist attraction in Tongyeong-si, visited by 490,000 tourists a year. On August 14, 1592, in a battle between the Joseon navy and the Japanese navy, the Joseon navy led by Admiral Yi Sun-sin defeated the Japanese navy, securing a food supply route and causing the Japanese navy to lose its fighting spirit. It is a park created to commemorate the greatest victory site of the Japanese invasions of Korea. There is a pavilion in the center of the park, and the bronze statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin, 17.3m tall, faces the sea off Hansan Island, and there are facilities such as the Tongyeong Maritime Soldiers' Memorial Tower, coastal waterside deck path, hydrangea trail, barrier-free sharing path, lawn plaza, and children's playground. To the north is Mangilbong Peak, to the south is Tongyeong Port, which is like a lake, and to the south. The scenery of the sea where the crane wing formation of the Battle of Hansan unfolded is beautiful. A new Children's Forest Experience Center was established in 2023 and has been operating children's forest education and forest interpretation programs since July.
priceDetail: Free

title: Yi Sun-sin Square
description: Yi Sun-sin Square, located in Jungang-dong, Yeosu, is a place where you can see and feel the historical scene, including information on Admiral Yi Sun-sin, who led the Japanese invasions of Korea to victory and an introduction to the volunteer army at the time. The square is the starting point of a historical, cultural and tourism belt linked to surrounding historic sites such as Jinnamgwan, where Admiral Yi Sun-sin developed his military plans and issued military orders. The Turtle Ship Festival, the oldest patriotic cultural festival in Korea, is held every May. The most eye-catching structure here is the Turtle Ship, which is a replica of its original form. It was designed not only for its exterior appearance but also for viewing from the inside. If you go inside the turtle ship, you can feel the dynamic appearance of the naval forces and vivid scenes from the Japanese invasions of Korea during the Japanese invasions of Korea. You can also try simple experiences. There were three turtle ships that were active during the Japanese invasions, one each built at the Jeolla Jwasuyeong, Bangdapjin, and Suncheonbu shipyards. The location of the turtle ship is exactly where the Jeolla Jwasuyeong shipyard was located. On one side of Yi Sun-sin Square, there is a mural depicting the life of Admiral Yi Sun-sin and the process of the Japanese invasions of Korea.
priceDetail: Free

title: Jaehyo Lee Gallery
description: Lee Jae-hyo Gallery is the studio and exhibition hall of world-renowned sculptor and installation artist Lee Jae-hyo. It is a space with a personally designed exhibition hall, gallery, and cafe. Although it is a cultural space in a remote place, there are many places to look around, such as fallen leaves on the ceiling and stones hanging in the air, and it is well-equipped with convenient facilities. You can view works and drawings made from materials such as stone, wood, nails, and fallen leaves, and it consists of a total of five exhibition rooms and a cafe. The admission fee includes the exhibition fee and drinks. It is a recommended date spot near Seoul and is open until 6 p.m., and admission closes at 5 p.m., one hour earlier. You can visit without a reservation, but it is best to leave plenty of time as there is a lot to see.
price: Adults 15,000 won Middle and high school students 13,000 won Elementary school students 11,000 won

title: Icheon Cultural Center
description: The Icheon Cultural Center, located in the Jungni-dong Administrative Welfare Center, is a place to inherit and develop Icheon's local cultural history and local culture. It is carrying out projects to discover and preserve local historical materials, host creative local cultural festivals, exchange projects for cultural contents between regions, cultural education projects, and revitalize lifestyle culture and arts. Icheon Cultural Center, established and opened in 1963 in accordance with the Local Cultural Center Promotion Act, moved to its current location with the completion of the new Jungni-dong Administrative Welfare Center building in 2019. The cultural center is equipped with facilities such as classrooms, conference rooms, exhibition rooms, and auditoriums, and operates various cultural events and educational programs.

title: Icheon Seolbong Hot Springs Land
description: Icheon Seolbong Hot Spring Land, located in the Icheon hot spring district, is a hot spring resort famous for its mineral water hot springs with a 600-year-old tradition, visited by King Sejong of the Joseon Dynasty and even King Sejo. The hot spring water, which is famous for its good water, is a hot spring attraction visited not only by local residents but also by tourists from other places. Icheon Seolbong Hot Springs Land is largely divided into a sauna & jjimjilbang where you can enjoy hot springs and a family bath where you can enjoy private baths. It is a four-story building with a women's bath on the first floor, a sauna and restaurant on the second floor, a men's bath on the third floor, and a mini swimming pool with a family bath and slide on the fourth floor. The swimming pool is an outdoor facility and is operated only during the summer season. In particular, the family baths are available for two or four people and are so popular that reservation competition is fierce on weekends. The jjimjilbang has a snack bar and a restaurant where you can grab a meal, as well as entertainment facilities such as an arcade and karaoke room, as well as convenient facilities such as a massage room. Aeryeonjeong and Anheungji are within walking distance, making it a good place to visit for a walk when the lotus flowers are in bloom. It takes about 4 minutes by car from Icheon Station on the Gyeonggang Line and about 10 minutes (658m) on foot from Icheon General Terminal. Nearby are Seolbong Park (Gyeonggi Ceramic Art Museum, Icheon City Museum, Icheon City Woljeon Art Museum, Seolbong International Sculpture Park, etc.), Sagimaggol Ceramic Village, Yes Park, Seongho Lake Lotus Complex, Hantaek Botanical Garden, Jisan Forest Resort Ski Resort, Icheon Termeden, and Deokpyeong Dinosaur Arboretum.

title: Icheon City Museum
description: Icheon City Museum is a city museum located in Seolbong Park. Starting in 1997, a plan to build the Icheon Agricultural Museum was established to collect local farming tools and various household tools. The name was changed to Icheon Folk Museum in November 2000, and the building was completed in December 2001. Afterwards, it was reopened as the Icheon City Museum on May 24, 2002, remodeled and reopened in 2013, and reopened in 2021 with a new building and the ceramic culture history room in the old building. Icheon City Museum is divided into a new building and an old building. The exterior of the old building, which flows naturally through the new building, is modeled after the exterior of Changgyeonggung Palace, giving you the feeling of being in an old palace. Among the permanent exhibition rooms, the History and Culture Room and the Modern and Contemporary Culture Room in the new building contain a variety of materials related to Icheon, from prehistoric times to modern and contemporary artifacts, allowing you to view the history and culture of Anyang at a glance. The Ceramic Culture History Room in the old building displays the history of pottery from each era, starting with an explanation of the raw materials and production methods of pottery, as well as the works of Icheon pottery masters. In particular, it houses a celadon embossed plate from the Goryeo Dynasty, which has been designated as a treasure. There is also an experience and learning corner for children. The Sansuyu Playground on the 3rd floor of the new building offers various activities such as painting rubbings, bricklaying Seolbongsanseong Fortress, matching pottery, and reading, as well as free programs for groups and individual visitors in the education room. In the ceramic culture history room of the old building, you can experience exhibitions such as pottery decoration (pattern stamping) and kiln lighting games. It is located within about 10 minutes by car from Icheon Station on the Gyeonggang Line and Icheon General Terminal. Icheon City Museum is located in Seolbong Park, so you can visit Icheon City Woljeon Art Museum, Seolbong Seowon, Seolbong International Sculpture Park, Literature Hill, and Seolbong Reservoir within the park. Nearby are Icheon Ceramic Village, Seongho Lake Lotus Complex, Hantaek Botanical Garden, Jisan Forest Resort Ski Resort, Icheon Termeden, and Deokpyeong Dinosaur Arboretum.

title: Icheon Art Hall
description: Icheon Art Hall, located on the site of Icheon City Hall, opened in June 2009 to promote the leisure and cultural life of Icheon citizens. It is operated by the Icheon Cultural Foundation, which was launched in 2021. Icheon Art Hall has two floors underground and three floors above ground and has a large performance hall (accommodating 1,200 people), a small performance hall (accommodating 451 people), and an art gallery that can display various works such as art, ceramics, and photography. The large performance hall can perform various genres such as musicals, opera, ballet, and plays, while the small performance hall is suitable for performances such as plays, chamber music, and recitals. There are also practice rooms for dance, choir, theater, ballet, and orchestra that can be used freely by citizens as well as professional artists. On the first floor, there is a children's playroom that can be used by preschool children aged 36 months to 7 years during performances, and a cafeteria where they can wait and relax before and after the performance. It takes about 13 minutes by car from Sindun IC. It takes about 5 minutes by car from Icheon Station on the Gyeonggang Line and Icheon General Terminal, and there are buses that go from the station to nearby locations. Nearby are Seolbong Park (Gyeonggi Ceramic Art Museum, Icheon City Museum, Icheon City Woljeon Art Museum, Seolbong International Sculpture Park, etc.), Sagimaggol Ceramic Village, Yes Park, Seongho Lake Lotus Complex, Hantaek Botanical Garden, Jisan Forest Resort Ski Resort, Icheon Termeden, and Deokpyeong Dinosaur Arboretum.

title: Icheon Hot Springs Park
description: It is a neighborhood park in the city center located in Anheung-dong, Icheon-si, Gyeonggi-do. In a space of approximately 84,000 m2, there is a multi-purpose playground, There is an open-air foot bath installed in December 2017 using hot spring water from the adjacent Anheung Recreation Area. There are sculptures here and there in the park, so you can take a light walk to look around. Seohee Youth Cultural Center is right next to it.

title: Ichon Hangang Park
description: Ichon Hangang Park is located at the northern end of the riverside between Jungnangcheon Bridge in Geumho-dong and Wonhyodaegyo Bridge in Ichon-dong. In fall, reeds, silver grass, and cosmos bloom along the lakeshore, making it a frequent walking and jogging course for citizens. Youth plazas for teenagers, In addition, the Han River Crossing Experience Center has been created and is being used as a teamwork training center for individuals, workplaces, schools, and other groups. ◎ Travel information to meet the charm of the Korean Wave - Drama <Sisyphus> In the drama <Sisyphus>, Seohae (played by Park Shin-hye) is a park where she is saddened while recalling memories with her father. The site is large, so you can enjoy a variety of leisure activities such as walking, picnicking, and cultural activities.
priceDetail: Free

title: Ichung Leisure Sports Park
description: Ichung Leisure Sports Park is a large-scale leisure sports park located in Pyeongtaek City. It is equipped with sports facilities for a variety of sports, including soccer fields, tennis courts, badminton courts, basketball courts, futsal courts, foot volleyball courts, softball courts, ground golf courses, inline skating rinks, weightlifting courts, wrestling halls, swimming pools, and wrestling courts, allowing citizens to engage in active daily sports activities. The park has well-developed walking trails, a children's playground, and convenient facilities, making it a suitable picnic spot for families. There is also a public rest area where you can use your dog, so dog owners also enjoy visiting.

title: Iho Tewoo Beach
description: Iho Tewoo Beach (Iho Beach) is a great place to take pictures of Jeju Island with its pony lighthouse. The red and white ponies provide an exotic scenery with their starkly contrasting colors. In addition, it is closest to downtown Jeju, making transportation convenient and well-equipped with convenient facilities. The gentle slope of the white sand beach attracts many vacationers, and it has a pine forest that is perfect for camping. At low tide, when the sea level is lowest, you can see Wondam along with the endlessly wide white sand beach. Wondam is one of Jeju's traditional fishing methods that uses the difference between high and low tides to catch fish. At Iho Tewoo Beach (Iho Beach), there is a restored Iho Mosalwon.
address: Doriro, Jeju-si, Jeju Special Self-Governing Province (Ihoil-dong)

title: Incheon Chinatown
description: Incheon Chinatown was formed when Incheon Port opened in 1883 and the Jemulpo area was designated as an extraterritoriality area of ​​the Qing Dynasty in 1884. It is a place that has preserved the unique culture and customs of the Chinese people for over 120 years of history, and every time I look around every corner of the alley decorated in red, I feel as if I have traveled to China. In the past, there were mostly stores selling goods imported from China, but now there are many Chinese restaurants. The Chinese living in Korea who are currently guarding this street are run by the second or third generation of the early settlers, so they are not able to maintain much of the traditional culture that the first generation maintained, but they are sticking to the taste of China. It is also the place where Jjajangmyeon, which is loved by people of all ages, was created, and there are many various foods such as white Jjajang, lamb skewers, fried pork buns, and oven-baked dumplings.

title: Ilsan Market
description: Ilsan Traditional Market is Goyang City’s representative traditional market with a 100-year history. Through the modernization project, a ceiling arcade was installed, allowing people to shop comfortably regardless of the weather. Customer satisfaction is high as we sell fresh fruits, vegetables, dried fish, and seafood at low prices. There are also various street foods such as fried chicken and hotteok, making it perfect for a food tour. In addition, it has a variety of items ranging from daily necessities to interior accessories.

title: Ilsan Lake Park
description: Ilsan Lake Park is a neighborhood park created in connection with the Ilsan New Town housing site development project. By creating the largest artificial lake in Korea, we are reproducing a natural ecosystem that city dwellers cannot access and providing a variety of surrounding scenery and recreational spaces using the lake. 특히 호수를 중심으로 한 4.7㎞의 자전거도로와 메타세쿼이아길 등 9.1㎞의 산책로는 시민들이 특별히 좋아하는 장소이다. In addition, various ecological cultural facilities such as an ecological nature learning center, plastic arts, and a cactus exhibition hall have been created. In addition, the park is becoming a famous place not only domestically but also internationally, with the Goyang International Flower Expo, Fall Flower Festival, and Lake Art Festival held every year. ◎ Travel information to meet the charm of the Korean Wave - Drama <Agency> It is a park that artificially created nature that is difficult for city dwellers to access. It is home to the largest artificial lake in Asia, an artificial island, and a grass plaza, as well as over 100 species of wild flowers and over 200,000 trees, making it a great place to relax. This is the place where Goain took a walk to calm his complicated mind and met Jeong Jae-hoon to cheer him up.

title: Ilwol Arboretum
description: Ilwol Arboretum is a flat plant culture-centered arboretum (area: 101,500㎡), completed in December 2022 and opened in May 2023. Under the goal of 'bringing more living nature into the daily lives of citizens', we are operating 16 thematic gardens, including an ornamental garden, dry garden, forest garden, fertility garden, ecological observation garden, grass garden, grass garden, winter garden, wetland garden, rainwater garden, and vegetable garden, as well as an exhibition greenhouse displaying plants from the Mediterranean dry climate zone.

title: Ippado Hongam
description: Ippado Hongam is a cliff on the southern coast of Ippado and is one of the Eight Scenic Views of Hwaseong. Ippado is an island located to the north of Gukhwado Island in the West Sea, west of Ujeong-eup. The name of the island comes from the meaning of “standing and catching the waves.” It is a small island with a total area of ​​0.44㎢, 70km from Seoul, 40km from Incheon, and 50km from Suwon in a straight line, and is a cute linear island connected by hills with most elevations less than 50m. Excluding the gentle ridges to the east and west of the center and the sand and pebble fields on the coast, the entire island consists of a steep slope of more than 30%, and the north and south coasts form cliffs. Hongam, a red rock formation towering over the island's southern coast with ancient mysteries, is considered one of the Eight Scenic Views of Hwaseong, creating a spectacular landscape-like landscape in harmony with sea birds such as sea pine and seagulls that grow wild here and there between the rock walls. To get to Hongam, you can follow the hiking trail from the lighthouse, but if you check the tide, you can also take the coastal path. Ippado Island has clean seawater, and along with nearby Gukhwado Island to the south, it is crowded with vacationers and anglers during the summer. There is a Seohaedo ferry that operates from Gungpyeong Port to Ippado Island, and it operates on a reservation system on weekends. For further inquiries, you can contact the Gungpyeong Port Seohaedo ferry office.

title: Jaraseom Island
description: Jaraseom Island is an island located in Gapyeong-eup, Gapyeong-gun, Gyeonggi-do. Jaraseom Island, which was created in the Bukhangang River with the construction of Cheongpyeong Dam in 1943, is located about 800m away from Nami Island in a straight line. It was given the name ‘Jara Island’ because it is an island overlooking a ‘hill that looks like a jar’. Jaraseom Island, which is made up of four islands including Dongdo, Seodo, Jungdo, and Namdo, is also building leisure and ecological park facilities. In the Seodo area, there is an auto camping site and an ecological and cultural park with a grass plaza over 100m in diameter in the middle, and a natural ecological theme park, ‘Ewhawon [二和園]’, has been created at the western end of the Jara Island camping site. It is also known as the place where the Jaraseom International Jazz Festival is held.
priceDetail: Free※ However, there is an entrance fee when visiting during the festival period.

title: Jayu Park
description: The answer to how to enjoy Jayu Park can be found in its name. The joy of the environment provided by nature and the sense of space provided by the park. When these two come together, there is a point where you feel infinitely better about the leisure you are enjoying. That is why so many people gather in Central Park in New York and the Luxembourg Palace in Paris. Jayu Park is a place that offers the same kind of enjoyment. I think it would be good to say that it is a park for everyone’s sense of freedom. There is also a children's traffic park here where various traffic signs and traffic lights can be installed to provide traffic safety education for children. This is a great place for children growing up in Anyang to learn the joys of parks for the first time, but it also provides great enjoyment to adults. People who are interested in history can imagine the Bronze Age by looking at the five dolmens that look like large blocks of stone, and if you miss classical music performances, you can visit Pyeongchon Art Hall. It is also perfect to go with foreigners who are visiting Korea for the first time. Of course, you can just rest on a bench or pavilion in Jayu Park. The biggest advantage of Jayu Park is that all of this is in one place. (Source: Anyang City Hall website)

title: Giant Jet
description: Giant Jet, Korea's largest extreme family theme park with an area of ​​1,500 pyeong, is a place where you can have fun without getting bored with over 30 different attractions. It is about three stories tall and has high ceilings and large windows, making it look much larger. Attractions vary depending on height. Those over 130cm can use the Kartmaster, which allows them to drive their own car, the Sky Challenge where they walk in the air while relying on a single rope, those over 120cm can use the zipline, bungee jumping, and climbing that crosses the giant jet diagonally, and those over 110cm can use the parabolic slide and angel's stairs. In addition, there is a children's carousel, a train village, a jungle gym, Bangbangi, a ball pit with a slide and a jungle gym, and fun things to do are hidden in every corner of the rest area.

title: Jail Forest Bathing Area
description: 'Jail Forest Bathing Park', a natural resort in the city that opens the green forest preserved in a development restricted area as a resting place for citizens, is the first forest recreation facility in Uijeongbu City, officially opened in March 2024. It provides a pleasant forest environment by combining a 3ha pine tree forest and a dense forest preserved in its original form as a development restricted area. Walking trails, picnic areas, forest rest areas, wooden benches, wind baths, sawdust barefoot paths, and hydrangea gardens have been created so anyone can relax in nature without burden. In particular, a picnic area is operated in the pine tree rest area within the forest bathing area so that families, friends, and lovers can enjoy a comfortable rest together. Several rest areas have been prepared so that people can relax comfortably while breathing in the clean air and phytoncide emitted from the 17ha forest bathing area. The reason why Jail Forest Bathing Site is even more special is because residents directly participated in brand design, production of branding sculptures, and planning participation programs from the construction stage, which added to the symbolism of ‘Jail Forest Bathing Site loved by citizens and owned by citizens.’

title: Jajakdo Beach
description: Jajakdo Beach is made up of white, fine sand and white sand developed along a crescent-shaped coastline. The swimming width is long and the water depth is low, so it is a beach that families with children can enjoy. The scenery of the strangely shaped rocks on the left and right sides of the beach is very beautiful. Compared to other places, the white sand beach is longer and the pine forest grows thicker, boasting a unique scenery. It has been loved by many tourists since it opened in July 1991. The sight of rocks with smooth surfaces scattered in various shapes by strong waves is very impressive, and there is a snorkeling point.
priceDetail: Free

title: Jamsil Baseball Stadium
description: Jamsil Baseball Stadium, which opened in 1982, has a capacity of 50,000 people and is Korea's representative baseball stadium with an average of 20,000 visitors per day during the season when baseball games are held. It is currently the home stadium of the LG Twins and Doosan Bears. Games 5, 6, and 7 of the Korean Series are also held. During the professional baseball season, Jamsil Baseball Stadium's night lights brighten the Han Riverside and Olympic Boulevard, providing unique enjoyment to visitors watching the night games. It is located at exits 5 and 6 of Sports Complex Station on Line 2.

description: Jangsuam Temple, located in Masanhappo-gu, Changwon-si, Gyeongsangnam-do, is a temple that is introduced as a restaurant with a view through SNS. There are many visitors, not only religious people, but also for outings. There are 108 stairs on the way up to the temple grounds after passing Jangsuam Iljumun Gate, which is great for enjoying the scenery. (Source: Changwon City Official Blog)

title: Jangtaesan Natural Recreation Forest
description: Jangtaesan Natural Recreation Forest is the only place in Korea with a dense metasequoia forest, making it a suitable place for families to enjoy forest bathing along with exotic scenery. This place, which blends well with the natural scenery, not only has a well-established walking path, but also a health acupressure path, a nostalgic play, a suspension bridge, a textbook botanical garden, an ecological pond, and a classroom in the forest, so you can enjoy nature learning and relaxation at the same time. In addition, there is a small (380㎡) exercise space where you can enjoy group entertainment, mini-soccer, and basketball games, and a space where you can specially experience the metasequoia forest through a skyway, observatory, and slope play facility. You can also view the sunset from the observatory on Hyeongjebawi Rock at the top of Jangtaesan Mountain and see strangely shaped rocks such as Janggunbong Peak and Peddle Rock.

venue: Janghang Skywalk Gibeolpo Naval Battle Observatory
description: It is a 15m high and 250m long skywalk located in Janghang Pine Forest Bathing Area, which boasts a beautiful pine forest and mudflats. It can be viewed in conjunction with the Marine Biological Resources Museum, and you can feel the cool and dizzying fun of walking across the sea and the open sky above a sea pine forest. There is an observation deck at the end of the skywalk, where you can enjoy a beautiful view.

title: Jaein Falls (Hantangang UNESCO Global Geopark)
venue: Jaein Falls Hantangang UNESCO Global Geopark
description: Jaein Falls has been widely known as a scenic spot for a long time. Jaein Falls is truly spectacular as a small stream flowing down from Jijangbong Peak in the north pours into a basalt columnar joint cliff that is about 18 meters high. In addition, the area around Jaein Falls is known as a habitat for the natural monument Eoreumchi and the endangered pink janguchae, and there is also a beautiful love story related to the name of the waterfall. At Jaein Falls, you can observe various characteristics of basalt, including columnar joints, sink caves, portholes, and gas tubes. The waterfall, which is about 18 meters high, continued to erode beneath the waterfall, creating a pothole as deep as 5 meters. A pothole refers to a deep hole created by a vortex (a phenomenon in which water swirls) in a depression or crack in a rock in a river. <Source: Hantangang River Geopark>

title: Jeongok Prehistory Museum
description: Jeongok Prehistory Museum is a relics museum built at the Jeongok-ri Paleolithic site, a historical site that rewrote the history of global Paleolithic research with the discovery of East Asia's first Acheulean-type hand axe. The exhibition space was organized with relics on various topics to systematically understand human evolution and Paleolithic culture, focusing on Paleolithic relics such as Acheulean-type hand axes excavated from the Jeongok-ri Paleolithic site.

title: Current Lipogu
description: Jeonri Port, located in Haseong-myeon, Gimpo-si, is the only port in the Han River Estuary. It is the only port in the Han River Estuary. It is the northernmost fishing ground of the Han River Estuary, and is a brackish water area where fresh water and sea water meet, making it a treasure trove of ecology. In the past, you had to row to catch fish, but now up to 60 horsepower is allowed. The fishermen here make a living by catching fish along a 14km section from under the Gimpo Bridge to the current fishing limit. Many whooper swans and white-faced ducks visit here, and even civilians can go there in the winter to taste the famous shrimp, mullet, and croaker of Jeonyuri Port. In particular, the crabs here are said to be of the highest quality, so much so that they are even featured on the Surat table. Because it is adjacent to the Military Demarcation Line, if you want to go out to catch fish, you have to report departure to the military unit sentry every time, and on days when soldiers are training or when there is fog, the water area is not open, making it difficult to launch a boat. However, in 2007, the 200m military barbed wire fence around the port was relocated, creating an environment where tourists could enter and purchase marine products, as well as view the Han River from a short distance away. title: Jeonju Hanok Village, Jeollabuk-do [Slow City]
description: Jeonju Hanok Village is the largest traditional Hanok village in Korea with over 700 Hanok houses in the Pungnam-dong area of ​​Jeonju, and is the only urban Hanok village in the country. It is an important space in the development of Korea's modern residential culture that began in 1910. It is home to important cultural assets such as Gyeonggijeon, Omokdae, and Hyanggyo, as well as about 20 cultural facilities. If you walk along Hyanggyo-gil, Choi Myeong-hee-gil, and Gyeonggijeon-gil, you can see the beautiful alleys of Hanok Village and feel the atmosphere of Hanok. When night comes to Jeonju Hanok Village, you can enjoy a sweet night view with angel lanterns lighting up Taejo-ro and lights that make the Hanok walls stand out even more. You can also find unique travel spaces such as Jeonju Nanjang, Jaman Mural Village, night market, and youth mall. The beauty of Hanok lies in the roof line, and the hem of the roof slightly points towards the sky, which is the characteristic and style of Hanok. The structure of Hanok is largely divided into the main building and the sarangchae. Another characteristic of Hanok is the ondol room. In Korea, people mostly sit down, so they put ondol on the floor. The structure of Ondol is to create a furnace outside the room, and when a fire is lit under the furnace (inside the furnace), the Ondol becomes warm. The biggest characteristic of Ondol is that it is cool in the summer and warm in the winter. If you go to Hanok Village, there is a separate Hanok Living Experience Center. You can also experience an ondol room yourself in the Seonbi Room and Gyusu Room within the Hanok Living Experience Center. During the Hanok living experience, the traditional Korean food served here is served in Napcheong Yugi [納淸鍮器], adding flavor and style. This is a place where you can experience two things: living in Jeonju Hanok Village and tasting the famously delicious Jeonju Bibimbap.

title: Jeonju Nanjang
description: Jeonju Nanjang is a theme park-type museum where you can take pictures, experience things, and enjoy the famous Jeonju Hanok Village, which was created after 3 years and 6 months of construction by collecting 25 years of data. Jeonju Nanjang, a modern history museum where each vivid prop holds historical value, is divided into about 70 theme zones and offers a variety of attractions. From a 110-year-old well where you can draw water yourself, to actual exhibits with a retro feel, you can experience Korean modern history firsthand. In addition to its high learning effect, its very existence has sufficient historical value. It is a compilation of modern props collected over 25 years, creating a nostalgic scene in each street. It presents a unique experience that brings memories and nostalgia to past generations and freshness to the generations to come.

title: Jeongdong-Simgok Badabuchae-gil
description: ‘Jeongdong’ in Jeongdong-Simgok Badabuchae-gil comes from the meaning of being directly east of Hanyang, where the king resides, and ‘Simgok’ comes from the meaning of a village in a deep valley. The topography of Jeongdongjin’s ‘Fan Tip’ and the shape of the terrain where the trail is located resemble a fan spread out toward the sea, so the name ‘Jeongdongsimgok Sea Fan Road’ was selected. It is a designated natural monument, and is the only coastal terrace in Korea where you can observe tectonic changes from 2 to 2.5 million years ago, which holds the secret of the creation of the East Sea. An approximately 3.01km trail has been created from Jeongdong Port (Jeongdong Ticket Office) to Simgok Port (Simgok Ticket Office), allowing you to enjoy the beauty of the unexplored scenery from the blue waves of the East Sea and magnificent strangely shaped rocks. This place has been used only as a military border patrol reconnaissance route for coastal security, and presents a natural unexplored scenery.

title: Jeongdongjin Beach
description: There are three places where you can swim in Jeongdongjin: the sea in front of Jeongdongjin Station, the sea in front of Hourglass Park, and the sea at the Jeongdongjin breakwater. Wide and easy to use places are the beach in front of Jeongdongjin Station and the sea in front of Hourglass Park. Hourglass Park illuminates the day and night, and is a tourist attraction with Sculpture (Sunrise) Park and Heonhwa-ro to the south. In particular, in front of Jeongdongjin Station, there are many rocks where you can pick and eat clams, mussels, seaweed, and sea urchins, so many people visit. In addition, as it is the closest port to the sea in the world, many tourists see the sun rising majestically from the blue waves of the East Sea. With the launch of the Jeongdongjin Sunrise Tourist Train in 1997, it has grown rapidly and is crowded with tourists all year round.
priceDetail: Free

title: Jeongseon 5-day Market / Jeongseon Arirang Market (2nd, 7th)
description: Jeongseon 5-day market is Korea’s representative traditional market. It is held on days ending on the 2nd and 7th, and is filled with local residents as well as travelers from all over the country. But it started out as a busy rural oil market. Local residents mainly traded wild vegetables, agricultural products, and daily necessities. Jeongseon's coal industry was flourishing and busy, but with the decline of the coal industry, it went through a period of stagnation. Then, in 1999, it was revived with the Jeongseon Five-day Market Tourist Train (currently the Jeongseon Arirang Train A-Train). A train trip to a friendly rural market stimulated the travelers' emotions. The fact that it is the home of Jeongseon Arirang also played a role. Various performances and events also added to the excitement of the market. In particular, the local food in Jeongseon Bay was fascinating. There is no end to the list of gondre rice with its bitter scent that whets the appetite, millet kkumi with a chewy texture, and slurping, which is delicious when you eat it while slurping the bridge of your nose. Thanks to this, you can truly experience the essence of gourmet wellness. It is full of seasonal specialties, such as bear and sesame seeds in the spring, waxy corn in the summer, and wild grapes in the fall, making it perfect for shopping for agricultural products. If you visit during the five-day market or weekend market (Saturday), you can experience a more intense market scene. However, there is a permanent Jeongseon Arirang Market, so you can feel the warmth of the Jeongseon traditional market whenever you visit. CheongArang Mall, a youth market near the east gate, is also worth a visit.

title: Jeongwang Market
description: ''Jeongwang Market'', located in Jeongwang-dong, Siheung-si, Gyeonggi-do, is right behind the Jeongwang Children's Library. It is easily accessible as you can walk from Jeongwang Station or take a bus. Jeongwang Market was recognized as a traditional market in July 2016, 15 years after its formation. You can purchase various foods and miscellaneous goods such as vegetables, fruits, meat, and fish, and taste street food. Recently, in line with the Corona era, we are also operating a short-distance delivery service.

title: Jeongjohyo Park
description: Jeongjohyo Park is a park adjacent to Hwaseong Yungneung and Geolleung, National Historic Site No. 206. King Jeongjo's first burial site and the excavation site of the former Suwonbu government office are located here, providing a place for historical education for local residents. Rest areas and convenience facilities are well-established, and the ‘Jeongjohyo Cultural Festival’, a historical and cultural festival, is held every year and presents various entertainment such as performances and experience programs for family visitors.

title: Jebudo
description: 서신면 앞바다에 있는 작은 섬, 일명 ‘모세의 기적’을 볼 수 있는 신비의 섬 제부도는 썰물 때면 하루에 두 번씩 바닷물이 양쪽으로 갈라져 섬을 드나들 수 있는 길이 열린다. It is not far from the metropolitan area and has convenient transportation, making it a suitable destination for a two-day, one-night vacation for families. The sunset reflected on the water is considered one of the most beautiful places on the West Coast. At the ‘2017 Red Dot Design Award’, one of the world’s top three design awards, the ‘Art Park’ and the ‘Landscape Bench’ of the coastal promenade each won the main prize in the communication design category. Jebudo Island, which has been reborn as an ‘island of culture and art’ where design, architecture, and art come together, was selected as one of the top 10 promising tourist attractions in Gyeonggi Province in 2017, and was selected as one of the top 10 promising tourist attractions in Gyeonggi Province in 2017, and selected every two years by the Korea Tourism Organization for 2019-2020. It was also selected as one of the top 100 tourist destinations in Korea. It is a representative tourist destination on the west coast of Gyeonggi Province, visited by over 2 million tourists annually. (Source: Hwaseong City Hall Culture and Tourism website)
priceDetail: Free

title: Jebudo Beach
description: Jebudo Beach, located on Jebudo Island, a small island in the West Sea that opens twice a day, is a 1.8km long white sand beach located in Jeburi, Seosin-myeon, Hwaseong-si, Gyeonggi-do. It is a beautiful beach with an oddly shaped cliff on the right and Maebawi Rock on the left. The water temperature at Jebudo Beach is moderate, the slope is gentle, and the water does not suddenly become deep, so even children and the elderly can enjoy swimming relatively safely. At low tide, the mudflats spread out widely, allowing for natural experiences such as catching clams or observing sea creatures. Mud flat experiences are possible all year round, and to protect fishing grounds, collection is limited to less than 1 kg per person. In addition to the mudflat experience, a variety of experiences are available depending on the season, such as sea fishing, fishing for fish, pier fishing, and goby fishing. You can also enjoy various water sports such as surfing, kayaking, and jet skiing, as well as the walking trail between the beach and the port.

title: Jade Garden
description: This is an exotic arboretum with the theme of ‘Little Europe in the Forest’, and 24 themed gardens were created on a site of approximately 163,500 m2 while maintaining the natural topography as much as possible. A European sensibility can be felt everywhere, including the Italian-Tuscan-style visitor center at the entrance to the arboretum, the English-style border garden decorated with English-style flower beds, and the Italian wedding garden with Italian-style garden style and waterways. The walking trails around the arboretum are largely divided into the Tree Smell Path and the Forest Wind Path. The tree-scented path in the center has wood chips on the floor and provides easy access to all parts of the theme garden. The wind path in the forest is good for walking in the summer because the trees are lush and cool. Each course takes about 40 to 60 minutes one way and is interconnected along the way. All courses start at the ticket office and end at Gardener's Cottage or Sky Garden at the top. It is equipped with convenient facilities such as Honeybee Cottage, a cafe that can be found while walking, and Studio Jade (Gift shop). It is open at night depending on the season, and a shuttle bus runs between Gulbongsan Station on the Gyeongchun Line and the arboretum.

title: Jeju Rainbow Coastal Road
description: Dodu-dong Rainbow Coastal Road is a unique road located a 10-minute drive from the airport. The protective walls installed along the coastal road to prevent vehicle crashes were painted rainbow colors to reflect residents' opinions about coloring them, and it became a popular tourist attraction as it was called the Dodu-dong Rainbow Coastal Road. There are various statues around, including the Haenyeo statue, which are fun to look at, and Dodubong Peak is within walking distance, and is one of the hidden scenic spots on the Olle Trail course. The slope is gentle so it is not difficult to climb.

title: Jeju Sanbangsan Mountain Carbonated Hot Springs
venue: Jeju Sanbangsan Mountain Carbonated Hot Springs
description: Jeju Sanbangsan Carbonated Hot Springs is a public hot spring in Seogwipo and a carbonated hot spring that is rare to find in Korea. The hot springs here are also called Gumyeongsu, which means the sound of pigeons crowing and water that saves people. Since ancient times, it has been said that drinking the water from this place cures diseases and is good for high blood pressure and the heart. This is because carbon dioxide gas absorbed into the skin stimulates and expands capillaries, which ultimately has the effect of lowering blood pressure and relieving the burden on the heart. Carbonated hot springs are also known to be good for skin care and fatigue relief. The ceiling and walls of Sanbangsan Carbonated Hot Springs are all made of glass, so it feels like you are enjoying a hot spring in nature, and it is great to enjoy bathing while looking at the refreshing view of Jeju.

title: Sanbangsan Mountain in Seogwipo, Jeju
description: Sanbangsan Mountain is an oval-shaped dome-shaped volcano that towers over the flat terrain of the southwestern part of Jeju. It is called one of the three major mountains of Jeju along with Hallasan Mountain and Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak. It is a sacred mountain with a mysterious atmosphere, where rain falls when clouds surround it. There is a legend that the Jade Emperor created it by pulling out the peak of Hallasan Mountain and throwing it. In particular, there is Sanbanggul Cave, which is dug deep into the rock wall on the southwestern slope of Sanbangsan Mountain, and the view of the Yongmeori Coast and sunset from this cave is outstanding. In order to protect natural heritage scenic spots, it is designated and managed as a public restricted area, so if you wish to enter for management or academic purposes, you can enter with permission from the Director of the National Heritage Administration. (Source: National Heritage Administration)

title: Jeju Camellia Arboretum
description: Jeju Camellia Arboretum is an arboretum with hundreds of round-shaped baby camellia trees that have been carefully cultivated from cuttings since 1977 by the great-grandson of the grandmother who cultivated the camellia colony in Wimi-ri. You can see hundreds of large baby camellia trees in harmony, and there are various things to see, including hundreds of types of camellia trees, wild flowers, palm trees, an observatory, a pond, a radiation pagoda, and sculptures. There is also a fountain and walking path, so you can walk while looking at the scenery of camellia flowers every winter. It is also a good place to visit with family, friends, or lovers and take pictures with the camellia tree in the background.

title: Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest
description: Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest is a healing spot dominated by cedar trees. The name Jeolmul was derived from the fact that there was water with good medicinal properties nearby, and the water supply was so abundant that residents used it for drinking because the water did not dry up even during previous droughts. It is said to be particularly effective in treating neuralgia and gastrointestinal diseases, and water quality tests are conducted regularly in Jeju Island and Jeju City. The cedar trees that form the main tree species in the recreation forest were planted after removing the undergrowth in the mid-1960s. The superior cedar plantation area has been developed into a natural recreation forest, providing a famous forest rest area that is visited by the most people in the country. The recreational forest is equipped with a variety of facilities, including walking trails, mineral springs, waterfalls, ponds, lawn plazas, woodcraft experience centers, exercise facilities, children's play facilities, and lodging facilities, so you can have a comfortable time. The trails are relatively gentle, have low slopes, and do not have stairs, so the elderly, children, and the disabled can use them comfortably. Additionally, a variety of animals and plants live within the recreational forest. Near the recreation forest is Jeolmul Oreum, a parasitic volcano, and there is an observatory at the top where you can see a horseshoe-shaped crater. If the weather is good, you can see Seongsan Ilchulbong to the east, Musucheon, the largest river in Jeju, to the west, and Jeju City to the north.

title: Lighting Museum
description: The Lighting Museum, established in 2004 and registered in 2005 (No. 05-Park-05), is the only museum specializing in lighting in Korea and has the following goals. * Restore and regenerate the lost unique lighting culture. * Rediscover human lighting culture by presenting the past, present, and future of light. * Create a future-oriented convergence lighting culture. * Establish a culture of healthy light where nature and humans coexist and develop.

title: Jomurak Valley
description: Jomurak Valley is a rugged valley located at the uppermost stream of Gapyeong Stream, which flows at the foot of Seokryongsan Mountain (1,120m), and is 6km long with waterfalls, dams, and streams. It is said that the name Jomurak came about because the birds danced and enjoyed the beautiful landscape, and it is also said that the name was given because of the chirping of mountain birds. As the wide stream narrows, the waterfall continues through the flowing waterfalls such as Golbaengi, Jungbang, Scallop, and Kudzu. When it reaches Bokhodeung Falls, the water spreads out like a fan as it hits the rocks, making you feel the pinnacle of beauty. Each cow is surrounded by rocks and trees, and from the cracks in the rocks comes a cold wind that makes you feel chilly even in the middle of summer. Gapyeong is known as a good valley for swimming and is a place where many vacationers stay in the summer. There are stairs right below Sampalgyo Bridge that can go down to the valley. The water flows a lot and is clear enough to see clearly, and the depth of the water varies slightly, with the deepest part being about 3 to 4 meters, making it good for adults to play in the water as well. The trails are well-maintained, so you can enjoy a quiet walk while feeling nature. There is a lot of shade from the trees at the bottom of the valley, so it is cool and you can also feel refreshed by the large and small waterfalls. Life jackets are available for free in front of the valley, and you must pay attention to safe water play. The only downside is that there is no parking lot, so you have to park on the side of the road.

title: Jo Byeong-hwa Literature Museum
description: The Jo Byeong-hwa Literary Museum is a literary memorial hall that permanently displays the poet Byeong-hwa Cho's relics, creative writings, and paintings. It is located like a pretty country house in Pyeonun Hill, Nansil-ri. It contains the poetic spirit of dreams and love that poet Cho pursued throughout his entire life's creative activities, and is a place where a trace of modern Korean literature has been preserved. The Jo Byeong-hwa Literary Museum is a two-story building with a total floor space of 85 pyeong that was built as a cultural room in 1993 with the land provided by poet Cho and support from the national treasury. It has an 8-pyeong attached building. It has two exhibition rooms on the first floor and a seminar room on the second floor. The literature museum contains special exhibitions, over 160 books including 53 original poetry collections, essay collections, and art collections left behind by poet Cho Byeong-Hwa, and the poet's relics. In Pyeonun Hill, in addition to the Literature Museum, there is Pyeonunjae, a tomb built by the poet next to his mother's grave in 1963, centered on a large lawn, Cheongwaheon, a country house where the poet used to write or rest after retiring from teaching, and the grave of poet Cho Byeong-hwa. In line with the poet's poem, which is easy to read but also conveys deep emotion, you can feel the gentle and profound scenery in this Pyeonun Garden. In addition, the Dream and Love Poetry Festival is held at the Literature Center every May, providing a great opportunity to convey the resonance of literature to many people.

title: Jo So-ang Memorial Hall
description: A place where you can trace the footsteps of the representative independence activist Jo So-ang. It is a space where you can see the noble life of the independence activist Jo So-ang, and it is a special space where you can reflect on the independence spirit and national spirit of the teacher who sacrificed himself for the independence and democratic development of his country. Inside the memorial hall, there are various materials and exhibits that explain Jo So-ang's life, thoughts, and the historical background of the independence movement to which he contributed. Additionally, a beautiful garden has been created around the memorial hall, allowing visitors to spend a comfortable time in nature. Inside the memorial hall, there is Jo So-ang's original home, an ecological pond, a memorial space, a lawn plaza, and a Yangju yellow zelkova tree designated as a natural monument.

title: Paper Art Museum
description: The Paper Art Museum is Korea's first paper sculpture art museum and is a happy and beautiful art museum that shares with neighbors through culture and art expressed in various ways using paper and art. It is equipped with a children's art museum, a traditional play experience center, a Hanok experience center, and a craft making experience center. It is a healing space where you can play in the outdoor lawn park and even stay in a Hanok.
price: - Adults (free coffee/drinks provided): KRW 9,000 - Children (over 30 months ~ under 18 years old): KRW 5,000 - Infants (up to 30 months): Free

title: Jugeumsan Mountain
description: Jugeumsan Mountain (813m), also known as Bidansan Mountain, is a mountain that straddles the border of Gapyeong, Pocheon, and Namyangju in Gyeonggi-do, and is surrounded by famous mountains such as Seori, Cheonma, Cheolma, and Chuknyeongsan Mountain. The strangely shaped rocks near the summit and the beautiful Bigeum Valley combine to create a silky mountain landscape. 이 산의 서북쪽 산 자락에는 베어스타운 스키장이 자리 잡고 있으며, 정상에서 남쪽으로 흘러내리는 비금계곡은 오염되지 않은 모습을 간직하고 있다. It is called Bigeum Valley because in the past, scholars came to the mountain to play and hid their geomungo there. There are two hiking trails: one from Naechon and one from Bigeum Valley. To climb from Naechon, start the hike from Pyeongsa Bridge at the entrance to Sagimak. Cross the stream at Hapsugok, go up the valley, pass the steep stone path and waterfall, take the left ridge path to the hill, then pass the silver grass field and climb the southern ridge to the summit. The descent goes from the summit (triangle point) along the west side of Amreung, past Shinseondang at the south of Ambong and down to Neunggol, or along the southeastern ridge road to Bigeum-ri. To hike in Bigeum Valley, start from the Bigeum Valley parking lot. There is a way to climb the southeastern ridge past Bawibong and reach the summit, then go through Bawibong and the southern ridge to go down from Sirubong to the parking lot, and from the summit, past Anbu Falls, and down to Sagimak Pyeongsa Bridge. At the top, there are two summit stones erected by Pocheon and Namyangju, respectively. If you go to the heliport behind the Jugeumsan pavilion, you can see the Dokbawi Rock and the pavilion, which are the signature scenery of Jugeumsan Mountain, at the same time. Many people visit Jugeumsan Mountain to capture this scenery. It is especially spectacular during the season when azaleas bloom.

title: Junam Reservoir migratory bird habitat
description: Junam Reservoir Migratory Bird Sanctuary is a world-class migratory bird sanctuary that provides a healing space for visitors as a resort for birdwatching of various migratory birds and exploring the natural scenery encompassing Sannam, Junam, and Dongpan Reservoirs. It is also possible to use facilities such as the Ramsar Culture Center, Ecology Center, Bird Watch, and Junam Environmental School for free, and tour the Junam Reservoir area with an ecology expert guide. You can also see seasonal flowers created at Saedri Flower Road and Lotus Complex. The sunset and sunrise scenery are so beautiful that many people visit to see them.
address: Woljam-ri, Dong-eup, Uichang-gu, Changwon-si, Gyeongsangnam-do, Gyeongsangnam-do
priceDetail: Free

title: Jumunjin Fish Market
description: Jumunjin Fish Market, located in Gangneung-si, Gangwon-do, is a traditional market established in 1936 near Jumunjin Port, famous for squid fishing. This market is connected to various types of shopping malls, including a general market, dried fish market, and raw fish center. It is a fish market on the East Coast and a traditional market visited by many domestic and foreign tourists. We handle fresh marine products such as squid freshly caught on the East Coast, mackerel, pollack, saury, and crab, as well as a variety of dried fish, and can be purchased at a lower price than the market price. Another great attraction is that you can taste fresh raw fish with the flavor of the East Sea right away.

title: Juknokwon
description: Juknokwon is a bamboo forest that can be seen on the left immediately after passing Hyanggyo, which borders Gwanbangjerim Forest and Damyang Stream, the source of the Yeongsangang River. Damyang-gun created the Seongansan area with a dense bamboo forest of about 160,000 m2 and opened in May 2003. As you climb the stone steps one by one at the entrance to Juknokwon, you relax your stiff body, and the breeze blowing through the bamboo brings a sense of refreshment to your mind and body that are tired from everyday life. Also, when you walk through a dense bamboo forest while listening to the crunching sound of bamboo leaves, the feeling of receiving the energy of sunlight pouring through the green bamboo leaves with your whole body is also refreshing. In Juknokwon, bamboo tea grows wild by eating dewdrops falling from bamboo leaves. This is a place where you can relax your mind with a cup of bamboo tea after enjoying a bamboo forest bath. In addition, there is a 2.2km walking trail in Juknokwon where you can enjoy a bamboo forest bath. It consists of eight themed paths, including Unsudaetong-gil, Jukmagou-gil, and Philosopher's Path, and the trail begins from Juknokwon Observatory. From the observatory, you can see at a glance Damyang Stream, Damyang Gwanbangjerim Forest, which is made up of old trees over 300 years old, and Damyang's famous metasequoia tree-lined road. There is an ecological exhibition hall, an artificial waterfall, an ecological pond, and an outdoor performance hall, and lights have been installed in the bamboo forest so that people can take a walk at night.
